- **The rule of citations.** The key `"citations": true` — in `spec`, of the block `spec` of `tools/docs-check/budgets.json`; in another repository, of its `docs-budgets.json`, which the repository's own task sets and the template carries from the start — turns on the mechanical part of the rule of citations, which `tools/docs-check/citation-rule.mjs` holds. Outside the plan, the archives and the normative texts for authors, in a document, a comment of code, a `.proto` file and the description of a schema, it is an error:
  - a decision's number in any form — the repository's own, `spec`'s, another repository's, MathTrail's, a range —, but the number in an entry's own heading in its log and the next free number its opening names;
  - a citation of a section or a document — a numbered section of a document by its name, `раздел N` and `section N`, a document of `spec` by its file and the suffix, `RULES.md spec`, a document by its file and a heading in a parenthesis, `(RULES.md, How we work)` —, but a record of `sources` or `measurements`, this repository's or another's, and a section of a text outside the repository, right after its link or before «лицензии», `of` or `in`;
  - a dated attribution or amendment: a date beside the word «author», «автор», «amendment», «поправка», «decision», «решение», «answer», «ответ», «word» or «слово», four words between at most, in one clause; and an amendment to a decision, dated or not; the date a record was read names nobody and stands;
  - a task's number, `T` and digits, MathTrail's with its subtask, `T105.10`, a heading's too;
  - everywhere, the plan too, more than two citations in one parenthesis: the numbers of the registers and of the tables «В» and «Д», sections and tasks, a range one, counted in the parenthesis that holds them directly.

  The plan is RUN.md and `run/`, in `spec` also COORDINATION.md and the template's RUN.md and `run/`. The archives `docs/plan/` are not read; `spec`'s normative texts for authors — `format/`, `admission/`, `deployment/`, `legal/`, `consent-age/`, `export/` — are read only for the descriptions of their schemas, from which code is generated: their Markdown and the comments of their data, examples and vectors are the text for authors. The open questions О-, П-, Т- and the rows «В» and «Д» name open work and are no error. A key of each repository, as `comments`, so that a move to the tag does not turn red before the repository's own task; the block `repository` holds none. Whether a sentence still leans on what it once cited is the session's judgement and the review's.
- **An example of a citation** — `R03`, `R19` — is written in inline code, in a document and in a comment alike: `docs-check` reads no number in code.
- **`just new-repo-check`** runs the same mode on a copy; links to `spec` are checked by its submodule, and for a draft by `spec`'s working tree.

— *Why:*
- The documents of the other repositories were checked by hand, and a one-off script was lost with its session's folder; the check from the submodule needs nothing of the repository but `docs-budgets.json`.
- Reading the files git lists sees exactly the repository's documents, in any repository, the uncommitted ones too, and needs nothing on its side.
- The name as a suffix wherever a word boundary follows it: a trial on `spec` and eleven repositories found 113 places where a citation of another log was checked against the own one because such a number existed at home too, and this reading changes none of their sentences. Names of prose only at the end of a sentence caught natural sentences in every repository.
- 2 of 8 numbers of decisions sampled in comments were wrong, which no check saw (measurements 1.14). The switch is a repository's own so that its move to the tag does not turn red before the task that fixes its comments.
- The mechanical part of the rule of citations is what a pattern finds without judgement; the rest is the session's, and a key of each repository keeps a move to the tag green.

— *Rejected:*
- a justfile of its own in the template — before code, against the order in which the repositories get their parts;
- not checking the numbers in guillemets — the check would be blind to real citations in quotes;
- the tables «В» and «Д» checked only in the other repositories — one tool would hold two rules for identical tables;
- the path to the repository from the command line;
- `--exclude-standard` — the list would depend on the machine and the clone; parsing the repository's `.gitignore` by a rule of our own — a second rule beside git's; refusing a root without `.git` — `just new-repo-check` checks a draft, which has none;
- a sign after a repository's name to mark it a suffix — every author would have to remember it; a list of exceptions in `config.mjs` — a second rule beside the first; an error with a hint at each ambiguous place — 113 places, entries of logs and archives among them;
- a register of its own for the numbers of records of `docs/sources.md` — the check of sections already does it;
- a parser of each language for the comments — a dependency for each, where a scanner of comments and strings is enough; the comments checked in every repository from the tag on — red before its task;
- reading the string literals of code for citations — regular expressions and the tests' data hold numbers on purpose, and the messages are few enough for review.

— *Consequence:* `tools/docs-check/` — `main.mjs`, `config.mjs`, `citations.mjs`, `sections.mjs`, `registers.mjs`, `budgets.mjs`, `comments.mjs`, `citation-rule.mjs` and their tests; `repo-template/files/docs-budgets.json`; `docs/repositories.md`; `RULES.md`.

## Analyzer findings

**R33. An analyzer's finding that a change cannot close stays open, and its reason is recorded here.** As in MathTrail Canvas ([canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/tree/0901af0)). The findings of CodeQL and Scorecard come to the Security tab, those of SonarCloud to its project, and rule 12 of RUN.md closes them before a new task. The answer is given once, not on each scan, and the next reader tells an answered finding from a new one: a finding not on this list is new, and it is closed by a change. The list was compared with the first runs of CodeQL and Scorecard on `main` on 2026-10-20: `spec` — commit f2769e1, Scorecard score 6.6; `module-kit` — 254452e, 6.3. It is shared by all repositories with the shared checks: their template, devcontainer and author are the same.
- **Scorecard `Code-Review` and `Branch-Protection`** want approvals by a second person. The project has one author, and the ruleset of `main` does without approvals on purpose. Setting up a second account for the sake of the score is worse than the score itself.
- **Scorecard `Pinned-Dependencies`** is about the `npm install -g` of Claude Code in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`. The installation goes by exact version, and npm checks the archive against the hash that the registry publishes: that is the check available to a global installation.
- **`draft/` is outside CodeQL.** The loader of the single-file prototype `draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`, which a design tool built, is not the platform's code: the prototype does not ship, and the documents override it ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)). The `codeql.yml` of `spec` passes `draft/**` to the input `paths-ignore` of the shared `codeql.yml` of `.github`, and SonarCloud does not read it either; the analysis of `actions` still reads all workflows. The references to `.github` in the other shared checks — secrets, DCO and Scorecard — are raised by Dependabot.
- **Scorecard `CII-Best-Practices`** is closed by the OpenSSF Best Practices badge at the level passing. `spec` has it — project [15977](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15977) on bestpractices.dev, passing since 2026-10-27 (`badge_level` and `achieved_passing_at` in `https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15977.json`) —, and each repository with code and automated tests gets its own; until then the finding stays open in that repository (run/DEBT.md, Д34). If the alert of a repository with the badge is not closed by the next run of Scorecard on `main`, the finding is new (rule 12 of RUN.md). `spec` does not take silver and gold.
- **Pass with time:**
  - `Maintained` — the repositories are younger than 90 days;
  - `SAST` — in `spec`, some of the commits were made before CodeQL;
  - `CI-Tests` — some pull requests were merged before CI: in `spec`, CI checked 11 of 13;
  - `Fuzzing` — there is no code yet that parses outside input: `docs-check` reads the documents of the repository itself. Fuzz tests come with such code.

`Signed-Releases` and `Packaging` (−1) and `Contributors` (3 — one organization) give no alerts.

— *Why:*
- Rule 12 of RUN.md. A check that will be red for the whole life of a one-person project is not a defect, as in MathTrail Canvas ([canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/tree/0901af0)).
- `draft/` out of CodeQL, as it is already excluded from SonarCloud. The shared `codeql.yml` of `.github` has the input `paths-ignore` since v0.1.1: "Paths CodeQL leaves out of the analysis of javascript-typescript — draft/**, say" (the input's description at v0.1.10, read 2026-10-22). The first analysis of `main` without `draft/` closed its five alerts — `js/xss-through-dom` (high) and four `js/cross-window-information-leak` (medium) —, and a new prototype does not bring them.
- The badge: Scorecard gives 5 of 10 for passing, "passing badge: 5" (ossf/scorecard, `docs/checks.md`, `main` 1e241c4), and the alert threshold in the policy of scorecard-action is 5 too: `CII-Best-Practices: # passing score / score: 5` (ossf/scorecard-action, `policies/template.yml`, `main` 365df9f); both read 2026-10-26. Silver and gold give "silver badge: 7" and "gold badge: 10" (`docs/checks.md`, the same place, read 2026-10-27).
- Scorecard looks up the project by the repository's address: `url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/projects.json?url=%s", client.baseURL, repoURI)`, where `repoURI` is `https://` and the address (ossf/scorecard, `clients/cii_http_client.go`, `main` 1e241c4, read 2026-10-27). `https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects.json?url=https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec` returns project 15977 (checked 2026-10-27), as in canvas-api and standalone.

— *Rejected:* closing such findings with the mark "false positive" or "won't fix" — then a new finding of the same rule would disappear silently; leaving the prototype's findings forever, or fixing the generated code — a new prototype would bring them again; silver and gold for `spec` — passing closes the alert too, and silver also requires the criterion `access_continuity`.

— *Consequence:* `RUN.md`; `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## The development environment

**R34. An archive that `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` downloads is checked against the sha256 checksum written beside its version. A CI tool that a GitHub action or the runner image puts on the runner, and that there is nothing to pin with, is pinned as narrowly as its installer allows, and the run writes the exact version into its artifact or log.**
- **The checksum** is an `ARG` for each architecture, `amd64` and `arm64`, from the publisher's own list of checksums: `SHASUMS256.txt` of the Node release, `SHA256SUMS` of the releases of just and just-lsp, `gh_<version>_checksums.txt` of the gh release. The check runs before unpacking, and a wrong checksum stops the build. The checksum changes in the same change as the version: Dependabot does not see these versions, and they are raised by hand (`.github/dependabot.yml`).
- **No list of the publisher.** Where the publisher lists no checksums beside an archive, its `ARG` holds the sha256 of the archive as it was downloaded over HTTPS from the publisher's own address, for each architecture, with the date it was taken, and that the publisher lists none, in the comment beside it; a raise of the version takes the new sums the same way. The first such archive is Docker's static archive of the stage `orchestrator`, `docker-<version>.tgz` of `download.docker.com/linux/static/stable/`, whose folders hold no file of checksums (measurements 4.3). The sum still lets in no other archive once this one has been read; it cannot say that the archive read was the one Docker built.
- **The runner.** The rule of exact versions of `RULES.md` and the checksums are about what `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` and `devcontainer.json` install; the runner is outside them:
  - the runner image is set by a label — so the jobs of `spec` run too, `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml`);
  - the Android system image in the workflow `emulators.yml` of `canvas` is installed by `sdkmanager`: the action `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` is pinned by SHA, the emulator build by number, the image by API level, target and architecture, `system-images;android-36;google_apis;x86_64`, and the run writes the revision into an artifact, `sdk-installed.txt`. `sdkmanager` does not let one pin the revision: in the list of Google's repository this path has one entry — revision 7, the archive `x86_64-36_r07.zip` —, and its checksum is only SHA-1, `<checksum type="sha1">` ([sys-img2-4.xml](https://dl.google.com/android/repository/sys-img/google_apis/sys-img2-4.xml), read 2026-11-08). A new revision comes into CI by itself when Google releases it, and is visible in the run's artifact;
  - the rule reads the same way for what comes with the macOS runner image — Xcode, which the job chooses by version, and the iOS simulator runtimes.
- **The boundary** is that of a development or CI tool that never ships: such a tool only checks the platform, puts nothing of its own into a release file or an image, and NovaTrail does not distribute it. What goes into what ships is still pinned by exact version and checksum.
- **Revisit** if a new revision of the Android image brings down a run that passed on the previous one: then install the archive by a step of our own at the previous revision, with a sha256 checksum read once and checked against the SHA-1 of the list.

— *Why:*
- The checksum: an exact version does not prevent substituting the archive at the same address, while a checksum in the file itself lets in no other archive once this one has been read; this is how `.github` already checks the CI tools. The stage `toolchain`, in which the CI checks of each repository run, needs it no less. The checksums were checked on 2026-10-20 against the publisher's list, for the releases on GitHub also against the field `digest` of their API, and against the downloaded archives themselves.
- No list of the publisher: the license rules take the Docker client from Docker's static archive, and the stage takes the client alone.
- The runner: the rule is general, not only about Android. The image changes only when Google releases a revision, and the run reads it every time.

— *Rejected:*
- `npm ci` for Claude Code — the Scorecard finding about `npm install -g` stays open with its reason among the analyzer findings; an exact version without a checksum;
- the package `docker-ce-cli` of Docker's apt repository, whose sha256 its index `Packages` lists under the signed `InRelease` — another source of the Docker client than the license rules name, for a list that the build would not check against its signature either;
- the Android image's archive by the address and checksum from `sys-img2-4.xml`, bypassing `sdkmanager`: the checksum there is SHA-1, weaker than this decision's sha256, and instead of the action, an installation step of our own. The archives of past revisions are still served at their addresses — r05 and r06 answered 200 on 2026-11-08 —, but Google has no list that names them, and the sha256 checksum would have to be computed by us, not taken from the publisher;
- our own cache of the image, raised by hand, like the snapshot of the Ubuntu archive: the snapshots are a service of Ubuntu itself, while here NovaTrail would keep a copy of someone else's image itself, under terms about keeping a copy that nobody has read;
- an exception in the Hard rules of RULES.md: the rule there names where versions stand — an `ARG` of the Dockerfile and a literal of `devcontainer.json` —, and does not concern the runner, while each repository would take the exception with a new tag; the packages of `apt` take no exception either.

— *Consequence:* `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; `RULES.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## The task's review

**R35. A task's review is one round of `/code-review high`, and the executor may hand in a small change without a review.**
- Having fixed the round's findings, the executor does not repeat the review.
- Whether a change is small, the executor decides. The report says whether there was a review, and if not, why.
- The rule is written in rules 6 and 8 of the RUN.md of `spec`, of the template and of each repository, and for Codex in AGENTS.md.

— *Why:* «теперь всегда только 1 код ревью. Если изменения небольшие то код ревью в этом случае не проводится - это решает сам агент» ("from now on, only one code review, always. If the changes are small, there is no code review in that case — the agent decides that itself").

— *Rejected:* the former rule 6, «не больше двух кругов», where the second round ran if the first found something.

— *Consequence:* `RUN.md`; `repo-template/`; `AGENTS.md`.

## UI packages and samples

**R36. UI packages enter their consumer as web components, and the data types that the repositories share are taken from the releases of `spec`. Each package names its own elements; `canvas` has one element, `<novatrail-canvas>`, for every canvas kind, and the members below are the agreement of `canvas` and `app`, whose types are `CanvasElement` of `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas`.**
- **The element** takes data by properties, gives the work by methods, and tells what the learner did by events: a `CustomEvent` from the host, `bubbles` and `composed`, with a frozen `detail`, sent on the learner's own action alone, never on the consumer's assignment. It needs no framework, and each consumer chooses its own. Its Shadow DOM is open.
- **What it shows** — one at a time, another given while it shows one a `TypeError`, and `app` gives each segment of a lesson a new element:
  - `task`, the open view of a task, given before `history` and `marks`; a slot bound `zone` is a `TypeError`;
  - `paper`, a task from the learner's paper: its crop, which the element lays over a sheet as tracing paper;
  - `workedExample`, the open view of a lesson's segment `worked_example`, on a sheet the learner does not write on: `history` only empty, `marks` a `TypeError`, `exportWork()` and `filled` `null`, the pen alone.
- **`manifest`**, the open view of the module manifest: the element reads `module_format_version` — another version is a `TypeError` while the format is v0 —, `canvas.digit_height`, 32 without a manifest, and `languages.explanation`, the language of the statement and of a workbook's lines; a canvas setting it does not know is a `TypeError`. **`media`**, a function that gives a promise of a `Blob` for a picture's reference, its path from `media/`, asked once: the canvas goes to no network, and `app` gives the files of the device part that `api` serves. Until a file comes, its frame shows its `alt`.
- **The writing history:** the property `history`, a frozen array of history events, which the consumer gives back to open the sheet as it was — one the sheet could not have written is a `TypeError`, and the sheet stays —; and the event `historychange`, synchronous after each stroke, erasure, cut, clearing and undo, `detail` `{ events, from }`: a store whose length is not `from` has missed events and rereads `history`. `app` keeps the history and the submission context as they are, through JSON: rounded numbers break the digest and the crop's integers, and the element does not take the context back.
- **The work for checking**, `exportWork()`, a promise: on a sheet `{ png, submission }`, the crop and its context; on a workbook `{ cells, submission }`, `{ item, slot, png }` of each filled box in the task's order, each a crop as `canvas` cuts it at the manifest's digit height; on a task from paper `{ statement, png, submission }`; and `null` where nothing is to check — no stroke, no box filled, a worked example. The submission context — where the crop lies on the sheet, the stroke groups and the table "group label → stroke IDs", the crop's integers and the submission digest; on a workbook the table "box → stroke IDs" and the digest of every box of the page; on a task from paper the tracing paper's state too — is `app`'s: it stays on the device, and only the crops with their places leave it.
- **`filled`**, read-only: per item and slot, in the task's order, whether a slot holds a stroke `exportWork()` would take — a workbook's boxes, a sheet's one slot bound `anywhere` or `sheet`, a task from paper's one slot —, and `null` on a sheet of `choice` slots, with no task and for an example. An action changes it before its `historychange`, and a task or a history given changes it with no event. It is the exit condition `answer_slots_filled`.
- **`marks`**, the tutor's marks of one submission with its context, given after `task` and `history`: a mark names a slot by its place `{ item, slot }`, from 1, and its kind and place are held to `Mark` of `novatrail.api.v1`.
- **The tools:** `tool`, `"pen" | "eraser" | "select" | "hand"` — Select and the hand the element's own on every sheet the learner writes on, no tools of the format —, and `toolchange`, `{ tool }`; the settings of the pen, the eraser and Select's shape, `pens`, with `penchange`, which `app` keeps across one visit and gives to each new element. `undo()` and `clear()` are called by the element's own buttons, outside the agreement.
- **A task from paper's state:** `tracing`, `{ at, hidden }`, with `tracingchange`, and `grid`, `"dots" | "lines" | "blank" | "squares"`, dots as a task from paper comes, with `gridchange`, `{ grid }`. `app` keeps both and gives them back, which tells nothing; it keeps the grid across one visit's tasks, and a reload or a new visit starts with dots.
- **A worked example's demo:** `demoState`, `{ opened, hidden }`, `{ opened: 0, hidden: false }` as an example starts, and `demochange` on the learner's press of the element's "Next" or "Demo". `app` keeps the state and gives it back after the example; one the example cannot have is a `TypeError`.
- **The picture of a work**, `exportPicture()`, a promise of a PNG `Blob` with no condition, which `app` puts as `StoredWork.picture` by `PutWork` ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md)): the strokes the surface shows, each in its style, on white — the page, a sheet's or a workbook's with its draft, and the ink past it, right and down, the tracing paper where it lies counted whole —, a pixel a unit while it holds no more bytes than the page's 1000 × 1400, scaled down past that, its size in its PNG's header, within the limit of a stored work. A worked example's is its white page. Its size and colours are `canvas`'s.
- **The language** of the element's labels is its own attribute `lang`, not an ancestor's.
- **What `app` sets:** the style properties `--novatrail-canvas-accent`, the accent of the tool in use and of the focus ring; `--novatrail-canvas-glass`, the fill of the bar's glass; `--novatrail-canvas-top`, the offset, from the top of what scrolls the element, of the band in whose middle the bar stands; `--novatrail-canvas-pad-top` and `--novatrail-canvas-pad-bottom`, how far `app`'s own bars float over the element's top and bottom — the statement starts below the first, the sheet scrolls up past the second, and the bar's band ends above it —, each with the mockup's default; the boolean attribute `tools-hidden`, which takes the bar, and an example's row, out of sight and out of the accessibility tree, on a phone while the tutor's sheet is open; `statement-hidden`; and on a worked example its "Continue", a child `<button slot="actions">` in the named slot `actions`, after the element's "Next" and "Demo" in the element's row: "Continue" and what it does stay `app`'s.
- **The consumer's CSP:** the element sets the styles of its Shadow DOM by `adoptedStyleSheets`, a `CSSStyleSheet` with `replaceSync()`, with no `<style>` element or `style` attribute, and needs of the consumer's CSP only `img-src blob:`.
- **The types** are in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas`, written by hand; the package `canvas` registers the element in `HTMLElementTagNameMap` and its events in `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`.
- Later, with the text canvas, "Listen" on it is voiced by `app` on an event `speak`, by one speech synthesis for the whole app (Т-13). In the first slice there is no text canvas.

— *Why:*
- The packages have several consumers — `app`, the samples page, the site, the card of the MCP channel —, each with the framework its repository chooses. React 19 and Preact take the element by themselves: «React 19 adds full support for custom elements and passes all tests on Custom Elements Everywhere» ([React 19](https://react.dev/blog/2024/12/05/react-19#support-for-custom-elements)), «Preact fully supports Web Components» ([Preact, Web Components](https://preactjs.com/guide/v10/web-components/)); both read 2026-10-21. A new canvas kind is the platform's code: with one element for every kind, a new version of `canvas` brings it with no change to `app`.
- The Shadow DOM is open for the sake of styles: it isolates the styles and the DOM tree, not the code; third-party code still runs only in a sandboxed iframe.
- Each member is named here because it is a contract: without it in `spec`, `app` would learn it only from the package, and the types could not hold it on both sides. The events carry what is new, not the whole history; filling is a property, not a second event for one action.
- The canvas has no data of its own: the submission context, derived from the learner's work, is `app`'s and stays on the device. The crop's integers make snapping exact; the digest catches an accidental divergence, not a forgery.
- The labels are the package's own table, so that no consumer, the samples page among them, translates them.
- The CSP: `app` has `style-src 'self'`, and a `<style>` in the Shadow DOM is connected to the document — «A node is connected if its shadow-including root is a document» ([DOM](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/), Last Updated 19 October 2026) — and blocked: «If the Should element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy? algorithm returns "Blocked" … then return» ([HTML](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html), update a style block, Last Updated 30 October 2026); `replaceSync()` has no CSP step, «Let rules be the result of running parse a stylesheet's contents from text» (CSSOM, Editor's Draft 13 October 2026), held by a test of `canvas` under `default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; img-src blob:`. `ShadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets` is in Chrome since 73, Firefox since 101, Safari since 16.4 (`mdn/browser-compat-data`, `api/ShadowRoot.json`, commit a8813fc). All read 2026-11-02.

— *Rejected:*
- components of `app`'s framework — they would decide for `app` and carry the framework into the samples page; a mount function — each consumer would write the mounting and cleanup, and each framework a wrapper;
- the canvas voicing by itself — the rules for voices would live in two packages;
- the submission context in the canvas's memory — the canvas would get data of its own;
- this entry naming only the gist, the names and the composition left to `canvas` — the contract would have no record in `spec`;
- the labels given by `app` — each consumer would translate them;
- the whole history in `historychange`; filling in its `detail` or as an event of its own;
- the module's settings in each task's open view; `{ png, submission }` on a workbook, the boxes glued together; `png: null` for an empty box;
- `filled` by slot with `null` for `choice`; an example through `task`, or an element of its own; a demo led by `app` alone or by the element alone;
- `undo()`, `clear()` and `media` all in the agreement, or none of them;
- a `sha256` of the canvas's styles in `app`'s `style-src`, which each change of them would change; `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`;
- the bar as `::part(tools)` for `app` to hide by its own CSS — `app` could break the bar's accessibility; `app`'s "Continue" in a row of its own, or "Next" and "Demo" drawn by `app`;
- `exportPicture()` the package's own, as `undo()` — `app` would take its type from `canvas` unchecked.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s and `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `types/canvas/index.d.ts`.

**R37. UI packages are published to npm, in the scope of the organization `@altnovatrail`; for `canvas`, `@altnovatrail/canvas`. The same file that is signed in the GitHub release goes to npm, by a step of the shared `release.yml` of `.github` — through trusted publishing, with no long-lived token. The packages of `spec` — `@altnovatrail/spec` and, from line 0.7, `@altnovatrail/contracts` — go to npm together, by `spec`'s own `release.yml`, which carries the npm steps of the shared one.**
- The package is installed by an exact version and with no token, including by the authors of widgets from stage 4. Widget bundles are still pinned by hash in the module package.
- **Tied by the signature.** The version in npm is tied to the signed release by the signature of the file itself. The archive from the registry is the same bytes as the release file, and the consumer checks it against the bundle of the release file of the same name, and the `integrity` of the lock file against the checked bytes. The sum in the signed `SHA256SUMS` is not needed for this, but stays a release file of `canvas`.
- **The step of the shared release**, not a job of its own in each repository with a package. How it is built is decided by `.github`: the shared workflows are its own. What `canvas` asks of the step:
  - it runs on the runner, not in the `toolchain` stage of the caller: tokens do not go there;
  - Node and npm by an exact version and sum in the file itself, like cosign, no lower than npm 11.5.1 and Node 22.14.0;
  - it runs only if the caller named the package file: the author publishes the first version by hand, since a trusted publisher is configured for a package that is already in the registry;
  - `--access public` explicitly; with `publish: false` it publishes nothing;
  - on a rerun it takes the file from the release and checks the signature, does not publish a published version again but checks it by `integrity`; a version lower than the newest in npm it does not put under `latest`; on a refusal that `release-refusal` lets through, it publishes nothing.

  Whether the registry accepts provenance from a reusable workflow of another repository, the npm documentation does not say: the first publishing of `canvas` with this step checks it.
- **The packages of `spec`** are not published by the step of the shared release: that one cannot call `spec`. Their files are carried by `spec`'s own release, the author publishes the first version of each in npm by hand, and the publishing step through trusted publishing is `spec`'s own, in its `release.yml`: the npm steps of the shared `release.yml` of `.github` v0.1.10, carried into it word for word, except where `spec` is built otherwise, and one check beyond them:
  - **Which packages.** Each npm package of the release. The package name is not an input, and there is no step `npm-name`: the output `npm` of the step "Build the files" names the release's npm archives separated by spaces, and it also decides whether the npm steps run. The steps derive the package name from the archive's name the way npm pack names the archive of a package in a scope: `altnovatrail-<name>-<version>.tgz` — `@altnovatrail/<name>`; the check compares it with `name` in `package.json`. The output `contracts` sets the tag of the Go module of the contracts;
  - cosign is a step before the signing: the rerun needs it too;
  - Node is 24.22.1 with its npm 11.19.1, by the version and sum of the `.tar.xz` in the file itself, as in `.github`. This is not the Node of the `toolchain` stage, 24.21.0: that one came out before the security release 24.22.1 of 2026-10-20 ([nodejs.org/dist/index.json](https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json), read 2026-10-29). npm runs on the runner through the wrapper `npm-isolated` — without the user's and the project's settings and without scripts — and the OIDC token does not get into the container;
  - **the check** is before the signing and before the release: a bad package leaves no immutable release. It goes over each package, and a refusal of any one holds the whole release: there is neither a release nor packages in npm. The archive and its `package.json` are checked, then the package document from the registry by `?write=true`, then `npm publish --dry-run`. If the package is not in the registry, the run fails. The check's output is `plan`, a JSON array: the package, the archive, the `integrity` and what publishing does with it — `publish`, with the tag `previous` or without, or `skip`;
  - **publishing** is after "Verify the release" and before the check of the Go module: `npm publish --access public` of each package in turn, through trusted publishing. The outcome is decided by the registry, not by npm's exit code: npm may end successfully when the version is only prepared for publishing (staged), or fail on a version that came out ([npm/cli#9889](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/9889), open as of 2026-10-29). So the step then asks every 10 seconds for the documents of all the packages, within one shared limit of 20 minutes. A version is available when the package document has shown it and the registry serves its archive: a round, having seen the version in the document, asks for the archive, and a package is ready when the archive has come. A package on which npm failed is looked for three rounds, while the document has not shown it, and once it has, its archive is waited for until the shared limit. The archive of a package with another `integrity` or from someone else's address is not asked for at all: the check after the rounds rejects it. The step checks the `integrity`, the archive's address and the archive byte for byte against the release file; a failure of one package does not stop checking the others, and the step fails at the end. If the step does not get a version or its archive in the 20 minutes, its text says to rerun the job later: the rerun publishes what is not in npm, and the step "Check the npm package" finds what came out by `integrity` and does not publish it again;
  - a version that is already in npm with the same `integrity` is skipped. With another one, the run fails. Beyond `.github`, the run fails the same way on a number that npm already gave out and that was unpublished — the `time` of the package document remembers it: «Once `package@version` has been used, you can never use it again» ([npm/documentation](https://github.com/npm/documentation/blob/514e6c9e84ef5b29dd8e11b7e743ab573ba10a0b/content/policies/unpublish.mdx), commit 514e6c9, read 2026-10-29). If the release has already come out, the package is published by the next release, with a new number, and the message says so. If not yet, all the releases of the line stop, since each would take the same number, until `RELEASE_LINE` is raised, and the message names this. A number in npm without a release of `spec` can come only from someone else's publishing;
  - a version lower than the newest goes under the tag `previous`: without a tag npm 11 does not publish it — «Cannot implicitly apply the "latest" tag because previously published version … is higher than the new version» ([npm/cli v11.19.1](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.1/lib/commands/publish.js), `lib/commands/publish.js`, read 2026-10-29). The step counts the newest as npm does there: among the versions without a pre-release and without `deprecated`. So the placeholder `0.0.0-stage` that the registry set up with the package does not count;
  - a refusal of the Releases API that `release-refusal` lets through publishes nothing in npm: there is no release, and the release of the tip covers it;
  - a rerun of an already released commit publishes the file from the release, not one built anew. Each archive with its bundle is checked by `gh release verify-asset` — the attestation ties the file to the release and its commit — and by `release-verify`, from a new copy of the checkout of its own: a script from the copy is not run after its container. The cosign signature checked is that of the `release.yml` of `spec` on `main`, in this repository. `verify-blob` does not check the commit of the signing run: it is the tip of `main` at the start of that run, and a new run of the same commit — for example, CI run on it again — goes from a later tip;
  - a commit that is no longer the tip of `main` goes to npm too. npm's provenance names as its commit `GITHUB_SHA` — `gitCommit: env.GITHUB_SHA` ([npm/cli v11.19.1](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.1/workspaces/libnpmpublish/lib/provenance.js), read 2026-10-29) — that is, the tip, like the cosign certificate of its files, and its own commit is named by the release's attestation;
  - **the job's `timeout-minutes` is 85**: the 20 minutes of the npm wait and 5 for the second package — its dry run, publishing and `release-verify` on a rerun —, beside the rounds of the step "Verify the Go module", which outlast the 30 minutes while the Go proxy remembers its failure.

  The trusted publisher of each package is the repository `altnovatrail/spec`, the file `release.yml`, without an environment, with direct publishing: `npm trust github @altnovatrail/spec --file release.yml --repository altnovatrail/spec --allow-publish`, and the same for `@altnovatrail/contracts`. Staged publishing stays rejected, and direct publishing for a trusted publisher is turned on explicitly, by the flag `--allow-publish`: «Configurations created after Sep 03, 2026 are automatically set to allow `npm stage publish`, and you can choose whether to also permit direct publishing with `npm publish`» ([npm Docs, Trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers), page updated 2026-10-06, read 2026-10-29). The first versions have no provenance: the author published them by hand — 0.4.0 of `@altnovatrail/spec`, and 0.7.0 of `@altnovatrail/contracts` from the file of release v0.7.0, 2026-11-03, in the registry the same file, byte for byte.

— *Why:* the criterion — install by an exact version and with no token — is met only by npm. All read 2026-10-21:
- in npm anyone installs a public package in a scope: «Scoped public packages can be downloaded and installed by anyone», and a version does not change: «Registry data is immutable, meaning once published, a package cannot change» ([npm/documentation](https://github.com/npm/documentation/tree/4e8e03b978033529bf8f50d74305b29939eb022c), commit 4e8e03b, `downloading-and-installing-packages-locally.mdx` and `policies/unpublish.mdx`). An organization for public packages is free — «the "Unlimited public packages" free plan» (ibid., `creating-an-organization.mdx`). The organization `altnovatrail` was created in npm on 2026-10-21;
- from a reusable workflow npm checks the caller: «validation checks the calling workflow's name instead of the workflow that actually contains the publish command», and «The `id-token: write` permission must also be given to both parent and child workflows»; «Trusted publishing requires npm CLI version 11.5.1 or later and Node version 22.14.0 or higher» (ibid., `trusted-publishers.mdx`). OIDC needs no secret, so the step does not break the rule "shared workflows take no secrets";
- the publishing code is one for all the repositories with packages on the shared release, and the provenance certificate, by the Fulcio rule, names the shared `release.yml` in its SAN, like the cosign signatures.

The packages of `spec` in its own release, all three by the plan's recommendations:
- Node as in `.github`: the step stays a copy of the model, and the version is raised together with it;
- a version that is already in npm, and a refusal, as in `.github` and as `canvas` asked, above;
- a commit that is not the tip goes to npm: each version of line 0.4 is in npm, and the packages install the same version as the tag of the submodule `spec/`.

The wait of 20 minutes: the registry answers a publishing with `202` and «Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available» (its notice in the run of release v0.6.7, 41535725018, 2026-11-02): it checks the package first, and this «introduces a short delay between publishing and availability, typically around five minutes. It may take longer, up to 15 minutes or more, at peak times or depending on a package's content and size» ([GitHub Changelog, npm publish-time malware scanning, 2026-07-28](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-28-npm-publish-time-malware-scanning-and-dual-use-metadata/), read 2026-11-02). In 13 runs, from v0.5.3 to v0.6.6, the version appeared after 1–2.3 minutes, and for 0.6.7 after 6 minutes 9 seconds, and the step, which waited 5 minutes, failed, though the package came out. The npm steps of the shared `release.yml` of `.github`, from which these are copied, had the same limit of 5 minutes (2026-11-02).

Each package of the release, with one shared wait; the shared wait is not the plan's recommendation.

The wait for the archive, not by the executor's earlier proposal: release v0.7.2 (run 41576700224, attempt 1) failed on the step "Publish to npm": the document of `@altnovatrail/spec` showed 0.7.2 at 04:17:35 UTC, and the archive `https://registry.npmjs.org/@altnovatrail/spec/-/spec-0.7.2.tgz` answered 404 until 04:22:50 (the run's log and a reading every half minute, 2026-11-03). The step waited for the document alone, and downloaded the archive after — `curl --retry 3`, which does not retry a 404 without `--retry-all-errors`. Attempt 2 of the same run passed.

— *Rejected:*
- GitHub Packages — a token is needed even to install a public package: «You need an access token to publish, install, and delete private, internal, and public packages» ([github/docs](https://github.com/github/docs/blob/cca0c9d7299f760587d6601bd96acfd2f5cb8929/data/reusables/package_registry/authenticate-packages.md), commit cca0c9d, read 2026-10-21);
- only GitHub releases — npm 12 closes installing by a link by default: «As of npm 12 the default is `none`» for `allow-remote` ([npm/cli](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/ae98c62586b6fea44114f72e249e246a2981de70/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js), v12.2.1, commit ae98c62, read 2026-10-21), and each project would need `allow-remote=root`;
- a publishing job of its own in the `release.yml` of each repository — a copy for each repository with a package, and it needs a change to `.github` too: the shared `release.yml` has no outputs — neither the version nor a sign that the release came out;
- staged publishing — the author with 2FA approves each version, and the release again waits for a person, while it must come out by itself;
- publishing each version by hand; a long-lived npm token in the secrets — a shared workflow takes no secrets;
- for `spec`: the Node of the `toolchain` stage — it came out before the security release; 24.22.1 in the Dockerfile as well — a change to all the checks for the sake of a release step;
- a warning instead of a failure when the `integrity` differs — the version in npm would silently diverge from the release file;
- only the release of the tip goes to npm: an earlier commit would have a tag, and its version would not be in npm;
- the packages in turn, each with its own 20 minutes, and `timeout-minutes` 75 — the plan's recommendation: the body of the step would have stayed as before, but in the worst case the wait would have gone twice as long;
- a copy of the npm steps for each package: each change would go twice;
- a job with a `matrix` over the packages: the files checked in this job would have to be passed on as an artifact, and publishing waits for "Verify the release" of this job;
- `curl --retry-all-errors` up to five minutes after the wait, the executor's proposal after the failure of v0.7.2 — up to five minutes for each package beyond the 20, and `timeout-minutes` would have had to be raised to 70.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/README.md`; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

**R38. The CI of `tutor` takes the synthetic samples from a release of `canvas` at an exact tag and sum and checks that its eval runner reads them — with no AI calls and no key. Both sides check the sample file — the message `Sample` of the eval protocol, `novatrail.eval.v1` — by its `.proto` and the check of `spec`.**
- The synthetic data is a file of the same release of `canvas`, `synthetic-samples_v<X.Y.Z>.<…>`, as one archive, with a signature and a sum in `SHA256SUMS`. It comes out in the three compositions of the protocol's sample file — measurement, eval set and child — and the sample's ID is derived from the seed.
- **The schema.** The readers take the contract's code from the Go module and the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts` and read the file strictly. The rules that the descriptor does not hold — the composition by purpose, the history, the crops, the PNG chunks — are checked by the code of `spec`, and the CI of `tutor` and of `canvas` call it by a recipe through the submodule.
- This is a link of the kind "a CI tool at an exact tag", not a build dependency.
- The reverse link: the CI of `canvas` takes the open views of the measurement tasks from a release of `tutor`. There is no cycle in the build, as with `sim` and `learner-model`: each side takes an already released release of the other at an exact tag, and neither needs the other's code to build.
- **Who comes first.** The release of `tutor` with the file of measurement tasks comes out first: its release does not need the synthetic data of `canvas`. The CI of `tutor` gets the check of the synthetic data when the first release of `canvas` with it comes out, and from then on pins its tag. The release of `canvas` with the build of the page waits for the file of `tutor`, and the synthetic data comes out in the same release.
- **It waits.** The check of the synthetic data in the CI of `tutor` waits in the postponed epic E3 of `tutor`: the CI of `tutor` does not take the synthetic data of `canvas` for now, and the release of `tutor` with the measurement tasks, which comes out first, is not there for now. The measurement of AI reading was done without the synthetic data of `canvas`. The decision is not cancelled: when epic E3 of `tutor` comes back, so does it.

— *Why:* the test vectors of the protocol catch a change of the protocol, but not a divergence of `canvas` between releases of `spec`, and without the check the page and the runner would silently diverge. `tutor` is tested on synthetic strokes drawn by code anyway: the samples of `canvas` give them in the page's format. — *Rejected:* only the test vectors of the protocol in `spec`; no compatibility check. — *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## The license check in other repositories

**R39. The other repositories take the list of licenses and the check of an npm lock file by recipes of `spec`: `licenses-allowed` and `licenses-check-repo`. The check rejects a lock file without `packages`. An exception that accepts a license not from the list holds only a package that the lock file marks `dev` and of which nothing goes into any of the repository's deliverables — neither into an npm package, nor into a build, nor into a release file; a repository whose deliverable is a bundler's build keeps everything that the bundler embeds into it in `dependencies`, and `devDependencies` is for development and CI tools.**
- **The list.** `just -f spec/justfile licenses-allowed` prints the list of category A from `tools/licenses/config.mjs`, one SPDX identifier per line. This is an interface, like the release recipes: the layout of `config.mjs` can be changed without breaking the caller.
- **The check of an npm lock file** is `just -f spec/justfile licenses-check-repo <lock-file> [<exceptions file>]`, from the repository's root. The paths are its own: a path that leads out of it, the check rejects.
  - Each package of the lock file is checked against the same list and the same parsing of SPDX expressions as in `licenses-check` of `spec` itself.
  - The exceptions are the repository's own. This is JSON: an object of packages, each with `license` — what the lock file says of it, or `null` — and `reason`: why it is accepted and by which decision. There are no other fields, and a file of another form stops the check.
  - The exceptions of `spec` do not pass to another lock file. An exception that has nothing to accept in the lock file is an error, as in `spec`.
- **A lock file without `packages`** — lockfileVersion 1, such as npm 5 and 6 wrote — the check rejects, and so does `licenses-check` of `spec` itself; it does not read such a file as empty and answer "ok". «1: The lockfile version used by npm v5 and v6», and `packages` is «an object that maps package locations to an object containing the information about that package» ([npm Docs, package-lock.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json), read 2026-10-21).
- **Only `dev`.** An exception that accepts a license outside the list — an SPDX expression or a text that does not parse as one — holds only a package that the lock file marks `dev`: «If the package is strictly part of the `devDependencies` tree, then `dev` will be true». Such a package without `dev` is an error: the exception is for a tool that never ships. `devOptional` is not `dev`: «If it is both a `dev` dependency _and_ an `optional` dependency of a non-dev dependency, then `devOptional` will be set» ([npm Docs, package-lock.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json), read 2026-10-22), and a dependency of a package that ships may go out together with it.
- **`dev` and the deliverable.** The mark `dev` says which tree the package came from, not whether it goes into a deliverable: `canvas` embeds the data of the icon set at build time from a package in `devDependencies`. So the condition of the license rules, "never ships", is held by the mark `dev` and the exception's reason together: the check compares `dev`, and that nothing from the package goes into a deliverable is said by the reason and held by review.
  - **An app** — `app`, later `site` — keeps in `dependencies` everything that its bundler embeds, and in `devDependencies` only tools. Then `dev` in it again means "never ships", and an exception under `dev` accepts nothing embedded. `app` has already decided so: in `dependencies` are `react`, `react-dom`, `@altnovatrail/canvas`, later `skill-map`, and the package of the icon set, and its `ci-vuln` — `npm audit --omit=dev` — depends on the same boundary.
  - **An npm package** — `canvas`, `skill-map` — keeps in `dependencies` what its consumer needs, and a package whose data it embeds at build time — the icon set — in `devDependencies`: the consumer does not need it. Such a package has no exception. Where a package stands that only the repository's second build embeds — the samples page of `canvas` — is decided by `canvas` together with its build, by the same rule of exceptions.
- **Builds for platforms.** The same exception covers the packages that the tool itself names in `optionalDependencies` — this is how its builds for platforms come — as long as they too are `dev` and under the same license. Such a build without `dev` is an error with a reason of its own, and a package under another license is checked like any other. In `canvas`, one exception `lightningcss` covers in this way its 11 builds under MPL-2.0: on the lock file of `canvas` 88492c4 the recipe with it answers "ok — 115 packages, 1 exceptions", and without it names 12 packages.
- **An exception for `null` or for `SEE LICENSE IN <file>`** corrects what the lock file says, rather than accepting a license outside the list. This is how a lock file says that it has no license, or that the license is in the package's own file: «If you are using a license that hasn't been assigned an SPDX identifier, or if you are using a custom license, use a string value like this one» ([npm Docs, package.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json), read 2026-10-22). What license the package actually has, the reason says, and a person reads it. Such an exception has no condition of `dev`.
- **`licenses-check` of `spec` itself** does not carry the condition of `dev`: its `tools/` does not ship at all, and the packages in it are `dependencies`, and the lock file marks none of them `dev`.
- **Who calls.** The recipes run in the `toolchain` stage of the caller: Node is there. How `go.yml`, `typescript.yml` and `self-ci.yml` call them is decided by `.github`: the shared workflows are its own. The recommendation of `.github` is this:
  - `self-ci.yml` checks the copy of the list in `go.yml` against the output of `licenses-allowed`, not against a parsing of `config.mjs` as text;
  - the job `licenses` of the shared `typescript.yml` takes the submodule `spec` and calls `licenses-check-repo`. This is an exception to the checkout without a submodule: there the ban is held by the code that takes the files of `spec` from releases, and here the submodule gives the check's tool.

— *Why:*
- `go.yml` and `typescript.yml` of `.github` carry copies of the list, `ALLOWED_LICENSES`. The job "Workflows" of `self-ci.yml` checks them against `spec/tools/licenses/config.mjs`, reading the file as text, one quoted identifier per line (RUN.md of `.github`, commit b3ee1a8). This file had no interface, as `line.mjs` had none before the release recipes gave it one.
- The contract of the TypeScript wrapper has `ci-licenses` check each package of the lock file against this list, with exceptions by name. `spec` had such a check, but only for its own `tools/package-lock.json` and with its own exceptions. Without a recipe each TypeScript repository — `canvas`, `app`, `skill-map` — would write a script of its own, like canvas-api, and the rule would diverge across the copies.
- Only `dev`, by the executor's recommendation: the divergence was found in writing to `canvas`. The check of `canvas` is built this way and passes its CI, and `canvas` was to move to the recipe: without the condition it would lose the `dev` boundary in the move, and the exception `lightningcss` would become twelve names, which `canvas` rejected. The `dev` boundary carries the condition of the license rules, "never ships", from the reason that a person reads into the check itself.
- Nothing into a deliverable: `app` came to the same by itself (`main` of `app` 0849269). The rule is for everyone, not only for `app`: for `site` and for the second build of a package the deliverable is a build too.

— *Rejected:*
- the list as a separate data file that `config.mjs` reads too: the caller would again read an internal file of `spec`, only another one;
- the check as a release file of `spec` or an npm package: a release of `spec` carries files — each normative part with a version of its own as `<part>-<version>.tar.gz`, the Go module and the npm packages —, but the list of licenses and the check of the lock file are tools, not code, and the other repositories call them from the submodule;
- leave it as it is;
- no condition of `dev` on an exception; an open question while `canvas` keeps its own script — the rule would again live in two copies;
- the condition of `dev` for the exceptions with `null` and `SEE LICENSE IN` as well — then a shipped package whose license from the list lies in its file, not in the lock file, could not be taken;
- any text that does not parse as an SPDX expression, without the condition of `dev` — then a typo in a license would get around the boundary;
- a rule of `app` alone, without a rule in `spec` — `site` and the samples page would decide anew;
- a check of the exceptions against the bundler's manifest in `licenses-check-repo` as well — new code in `tools/licenses`, and each bundler has an input of its own;
- `app` has no exceptions for licenses not from the list — it would lose `lightningcss`, a tool that the license rules allow.

— *Consequence:* `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `tools/licenses/` — `config.mjs`, `main.mjs` and its tests.

## System packages in the devcontainer

**R40. A system package that `apt` installs in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is taken from the Ubuntu archive as of a date — from a snapshot alone, by a source of its own whose URI names the snapshot by its ID. The snapshot ID is an `ARG` beside the list of packages, and it is raised by hand, like a version.**
- **The source.** The `RUN` writes a source of its own into a folder of its own — `URIs: https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/<ID>/`, the suites `noble noble-updates noble-backports noble-security` and the components `main universe restricted multiverse` of the base image's `ubuntu.sources`, `Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg` —, gives `apt-get update` and `apt-get install` that folder alone, `-o Dir::Etc::SourceList=/dev/null -o Dir::Etc::SourceParts=<folder>`, with the list of packages, and removes it with the lists; `--snapshot` is not given. The ID is the `ARG` `UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT`. The base image's own sources stay as they are. Each package is then an exact version, the one that was in the archive at that moment, and the rule of exact versions in RULES.md is met without a version for each package.
- `apt` checks the archive's signature itself, as on any update.
- The snapshot is raised by hand, like a version that Dependabot does not see: when the list of packages changes and when the build fails after a new digest of the base image.
- The rule is about the packages of the Ubuntu archive. A package from another `apt` archive, which has no snapshots, brings a decision of its own.
- The Dockerfile of `spec` has no `apt` packages. `canvas` was the first to need the rule: 21 Chromium libraries on Ubuntu 24.04 and fonts.
- **RULES.md** words the rule of exact versions by this entry: a system package comes from a snapshot of the Ubuntu archive alone, from a source of its own whose URI names the snapshot by its ID, an `ARG` beside the list of packages, and not from the live archive; it does not name `--snapshot`.

— *Why:*
- `apt` does not pin versions itself, and the Playwright image by digest gives the browsers but not their system libraries: in the image those lie outside `/ms-playwright`.
- Snapshots are a service of Ubuntu itself: «The Ubuntu snapshot service makes it possible to see and use the Ubuntu archive as it was at any specified date and time», «Snapshots of the Ubuntu archive are available for any date and time after 1 March 2023» and «We intend to ensure snapshots are available for dates up to at least 2 years in the past, which we may extend if there is demand». Ubuntu 24.04 finds them by itself: «The apt included in Ubuntu 24.04 and later automatically detects when snapshots are supported for a repository». The order of the commands: «the apt update --snapshot [snapshot] command needs to be run immediately before the other apt commands», and «These commands will also fail if the snapshot format is incorrect or the snapshot does not exist» ([Ubuntu Snapshot Service](https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/), read 2026-10-21).
- Checked in a build. The Dockerfile of `canvas` on `main`, commit 88492c4 (pull request #18), installs the packages with `ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT=20261021T000000Z` and `--snapshot`. In CI run 39691386053 on this commit the `toolchain` stage built, and all 61 packages came from `https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/20261021T000000Z` (the log of the job "TypeScript / test", read 2026-10-21).
- The source of its own is for the speed of CI: `apt-get update --snapshot` fetched 67.6 MB, the indexes of the live archive and of the snapshot both, and `snapshot.ubuntu.com` gave from 259 kB/s (measurements 3.1); the source of its own fetches 33.6 MB, and from an empty state of dpkg both resolve the same 431 packages at the same versions; the same URI serves `arm64` (measurements 3.2).
- The wording of RULES.md: RULES.md is loaded into every session of every repository, and a hard rule that the template's own `RUN` breaks invites a session to put the flags back.

— *Rejected:*
- a version for each package, `package=version`: the Ubuntu archive does not keep all old versions, and the build will break when it removes them;
- the `toolchain` stage from the Playwright image by tag and digest: it has the libraries, but its user is `pwuser`, while the `devcontainer` stage of the template comes from `vscode`;
- an exception in Hard rules for `apt` packages;
- `--snapshot` with the base image's sources — the cost above;
- removing the base image's `ubuntu.sources` — a person's `apt` in the devcontainer would then read the snapshot alone;
- fewer suites or components — a smaller download, but then the resolution is no longer the base image's by construction;
- leaving RULES.md as it was until its next edit; leaving RULES.md to cite this entry.

— *Cost:* snapshots are promised «up to at least 2 years in the past», not forever. A snapshot that is no longer there will stop the build — then it is raised, like a version. — *Consequence:* `RULES.md`; `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile`; `docs/decisions.md`; `docs/measurements.md`.

## The modules of the first slice

**R41. The first slice is two modules of two subjects: olympiad maths 1–6 and short essays in English for any age.** The module of the check board stands beside them, not among them. Every task of each is solved on the sheet of a task from paper.
- **Olympiad maths 1–6** is the first module: the learner is a child, the canvas is a handwriting sheet, the answer is a number by hand or an option tapped on the tracing paper.
- **Short essays in English.** The canvas is a handwriting sheet, the essay is written by hand in free form. This is writing, not a language module: the explanations are in English, there is no target language. A module has one explanation language, and format v0 has no translations.
  - AI reads the essay — reading of handwriting — and assesses it by the author's criteria — assessment by a rubric. The learner gets feedback by the rubric, not a verdict.
  - Tasks with a key — for example, choosing the best first sentence — get a verdict.
  - The module is for any age, and the presentation style is by the learner's age. So an adult learner has a module of their own in the first slice, and the adult learner's account and the own key (О-4) stay in the slice.
- There are no third-party authors in the first slice, so both modules are official. The canvas of the slice is the handwriting sheet; there is no workbook and no text canvas in it.
- The screens of the prototype — a page of ten examples on fractions and the essay «My best day» — are illustrations, not content: the solving steps, the traps and the topics are written by `modules`.
- **Assessment by a rubric** is in the first slice. It is measured by the share of false alarms and by agreement with people's assessment. Whether feedback by a rubric affects the learner model is О-17, and it concerns the first slice.
- **An essay has no incorrect answers,** and so no hint ladder. "Hint" on an essay gives the task's techniques and its leading question, without AI and without the work, as before the first incorrect answer of a task with a key. The leak check has nothing to look for — there is no key — and the tutor must not write the essay for the learner: the feedback rule holds it, no more than three sentences and 80 words in English, and a quoted stretch of four words or more only the learner's own.
- **The path without AI** — a typed answer or a choice (О-5) — the first slice tries only with tasks with a choice.
- **An essay is the learner's free text.** Of an essay's attempt the server keeps how each submission ended and the marks of the criteria, not the text or the words of the feedback. To a learner under 18 a module gives made-up and general topics. A work, an essay too, is kept on the server only while the storage of the profile's works is on, off by default.
- **What the slice does not test:** the workbook and its box, which format v0 keeps; the solving steps, which the platform does not run; the text canvas, the check kinds "text" and "edit", and a language module where the target language is not the explanation language. Neither "text" nor "edit" is in format v0: an edit needs an edit binding, which v0 does not have, and signs and words written by hand are checked by a choice with the options in the check itself. The recommendation of an input field without autocorrect waits for a text canvas. A new canvas kind or check kind is an addition to the format, a minor version.
- The interface and explanation languages of the slice are О-2, which is open.

— *Why:* the slice follows the screens of the prototype ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)). The arguments are the plan's proposal:
- The main hypothesis — that AI understands the learner's free solution and reads the answer correctly — both modules test on handwriting: on a number on the sheet and on a whole text. The answers of Spanish — an edit and typing — a program would check without AI.
- Essays are the second subject and a path without a key: feedback by a rubric instead of a verdict, the author's order for skills with a rubric and the learner's work as their artifact. One module serves both a child and an adult, with a different presentation style and different AI routes.

— *Rejected:*
- Spanish A1 for adults. Its answers do not test AI reading, it needs a text canvas of its own — a kind of its own on the page markup, not a sheet — and the step "pronounce" waits for voice input (О-6). It stays a module for later;
- school maths of grade 3 on a workbook as a third module: the author's word removed it with the page of a workbook, so that every task of a module is solved on the one sheet of a task from paper; format v0 keeps the workbook, which the slice no longer tests;
- physics with a bench: it needs a widget, and widgets are stage 4;
- school maths alone — a sheet with fractions: the format would be tested on one subject.

— *Consequence:* `docs/decisions.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`.


## Normative texts

**R42. The normative texts for authors are in English and outside `docs/`. The module format lies in the folder `format/` at the root of `spec`: the schemas, the format text and the test vectors.**
- The normative texts are what an author writes a module by, and what the platform's code reads and checks it by: the module format, the widget protocol and the guides for authors.
- **The module format** is the schemas with descriptions, in JSON Schema 2020-12, the format text and the test vectors of the format.
  - **The format text** is the rules that a schema cannot express: a graph without cycles, the references and keys that `module-kit` checks, the meaning of the check kinds and of normalization, open fields, the format versions.
  - The test vectors are normative: an implementation that does not pass them does not conform to the format.
  - The examples show the format and test the schemas, but add no rules.
- The format is normative: what a module may and must contain and how the platform checks it is said by the schemas, the format text and the test vectors, and `docs/` describe it. A divergence is an error: the normative text decides it, and one change fixes it. The field names are the English terms of the glossary of `docs/concepts.md`, and a new or changed term goes there first; a decision changes by a rewrite of its entry.
- `docs/` stay descriptive. They are in English too, but for the epic archives `docs/plan/`, so the folder separates the roles, not the languages.
- **The folder.** `format/` holds the format text and the version number `format/VERSION`. The random generator and its test vectors, which `module-kit`, `engine` and `sim` share, lie in it — in the [format text](../format/README.md) and in `format/vectors/random/`: the generator belongs to the format version, though both `engine` and `sim` take it. Where the widget protocol and the guides lie is decided by epic E5. The language of all of them is this one.

— *Why:* a standard that "any author" writes by cannot be in Russian only, and the descriptive documents were then in Russian. RULES.md already requires the descriptions of schemas in English, and the format text beside the schemas is changed by the same change as they are. The code of `module-kit`, which carries out the format, is in English too. A separate folder is the plan's proposal: in `docs/` everything was then in Russian. The folder came before the schemas, with the format text and `format/VERSION`.

— *Rejected:*
- normative texts in Russian, like the documents: an author who does not read Russian could not read the standard;
- only the descriptions in the schemas, without a format text: the rules that a schema does not express would live in the descriptive `docs/`, in Russian;
- the format text in English in `docs/`: the folder would mix language and role;
- two languages with a translation: at each divergence one would have to decide which of them is normative.

— *Consequence:* `docs/decisions.md`; `RULES.md`; `RUN.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `CLAUDE.md`.

## The first code of stage 2

**R43. The first code of stage 2 is the review board of `tutor`, and the first code of `canvas` is the handwriting sheet, the element `<novatrail-canvas>`. The measurement of AI reading, put off until the author decided by the board's data, came back narrowed — Claude models and the course of writing — and is done; the samples page of `canvas` and what else needs samples of volunteers or children wait.**
- **The review board.** The author solves five fixed tasks by hand — sometimes with an error on purpose or illegibly. Claude models that the author chooses read the solution and assess it themselves: correct, an error in line N, or cannot read; GPT is not connected to the board. Under each answer the author marks whether the model is right, and the summary counts how often each is right. There is no program check on the board.
  - On the board the model reads and judges in one call, already knowing the key — what the product avoids by a reading without the key. The author's marks show how often the model "reads in" what is expected. This is an early signal, not the measurement's comparison: there is no reading without the key on the board.
  - The MVP needs nothing from `spec`: the board waits neither for the eval protocol nor for the module format.
- **Where.** The command `tutor-eval board` — the eval CLI of `tutor` — listens only on the local address 127.0.0.1 in the devcontainer, and the page opens in the browser on the author's computer. This is not a service: `tutor` still has no process of its own. The board has its own simple sheet, not the sheet of `canvas`.
- **Data.** The handwriting and the marks are only the author's own, an adult's. The pictures and the log lie with the author, outside git, and the models are called with keys for eval only.
- **The model's assessment on the board is what the board measures, not a verdict for a learner.** For the product a program delivers the verdict, and with no deterministic check there is no verdict. Whether to revisit this, the author decides by the board's data.
- **The measurement.** The large measurement — about 110 sheets and statistics — was put off until the board showed it was needed. On 2026-10-23 the board showed that Claude reads handwriting, and the same day the measurement returned — only on Claude models and with the main question: does the course of writing — the order of writing and erasing — help the model. The planning of 2026-10-25 narrowed it to this question — about 40 sheets, the judges Opus 5.5 · `high` and Haiku 5.5 · `low` with thinking and without. On 2026-10-26 the measurement was done: it showed no benefit of the course of writing. It returned no verdict by lines.
  - **The sheets** for it are in the format `tutor-sample`, not from the samples page of `canvas`: the author wrote sheet 1 on the board, and code drew 39.
- **`canvas`.** Its first code is the sheet, the element `<novatrail-canvas>`. The samples page, the synthetic samples and the build that opens from a file are epic E5 of `canvas`, «Страница образцов и большой замер»: they will be needed when a measurement needs samples of volunteers or children. The card of `canvas` in `docs/architecture.md` does not change: the crop by A3 stays a picture for the check in the product.
- **What still waits,** rather than being cancelled:
  - the release of `tutor` with the open views of the measurement's tasks for CI of `canvas` and the check of the synthetic data of `canvas` in CI of `tutor` — in the postponed epic E3 of `tutor`: the measurement done did not need them. The samples page and the synthetic data are described for a measurement on samples: when it comes back, so do they;
  - the measurements on the live handwriting of adult volunteers and on free writing — epic E4 of `tutor`.
- **Decided without the measurement.** What the measurement did not answer is decided apart from it: reading and analysis are two calls, reading is by two readers of one provider, the work is read only on the learner's action and a pause goes neither to reading nor to AI, and a hint on request gives the "givens and unknown" and the technique before the first incorrect answer and the current rung after it.

— *Why:*
- The board is what the MVP asks for: «на этапе MVP мне всего лишь нужно чтобы ты на канве показывал 5 статичных задач. Я сам буду их решать. Иногда специально ошибаться или писать неразборчиво. ИИ будет пытаться понять что я написал и выдавать свою оценку — решил правильно или с ошибкой. Далее я жму кнопку ИИ был прав или нет. Всё. Никаких проверок с твоей стороны не нужно вообще». It is recorded in `spec` because otherwise the card of `tutor` and the order of appearance in `docs/repositories.md` would name as the first code of the stage what was put off, and `canvas` would have built the samples page for a release of `tutor` that will not come for now.
- The sheet first: `canvas` replanned its E2 for the MVP, and the item of `tutor` and `canvas` in the order of appearance spoke of an order that `canvas` no longer had: the sheet and the samples page, before `modules` and `module-kit` and before `learner-model`, `engine` and `sim`, for the measurement of AI reading. Both this and the measurement put off waited for one decision, and are recorded in one change.
- The measurement done: `spec` called put off a measurement that had returned and was done.

— *Rejected:*
- to change nothing in `spec`, since the order of work is `tutor`'s business: the card of `tutor` and the order of appearance would name as the first code what is put off;
- to cancel what is decided of the samples page and the synthetic samples for that release: when the measurement comes back, so do they;
- to wait with the board for `api` and `app` or for the sheet of `canvas`: the author needs a simple board now;
- to keep the item of `tutor` and `canvas` until the decision by the board's data: it would speak of an order that does not exist;
- to remove the samples page from that item for good: this would decide for the author, and the author has not decided yet by the board's data;
- to change nothing once the measurement was done — the card of `tutor` and the item of `tutor` and `canvas` in the order of appearance would speak of an order that does not exist.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## Versions of `spec` and of the module format

**R44. The module format has a version of its own, MAJOR.MINOR, and a module is checked, built and executed by the version its manifest names. A new version of the format opens a new line of `spec`, and so do a new major package of a contract and a new version of each other normative part with a version of its own; only the format raises the major version of `spec`. While the format is v0, the platform reads only its current version, and from v1 the current major and the previous one; v0 leaves the window with the release of v1.**
- **Two versions.** The tag of `spec` is the version of the repository: of its documents, rules, recipes and release files. The module format version is the version of what a module may and must contain and how the platform checks it.
  - The number is written once, in `format/VERSION`, a place that does not change from version to version: a reader finds it before it knows the schema. The `$id` of each schema is a common prefix, this number and the file name.
  - A module names the number in the field `module_format_version` at the root of its manifest, a string that the schema gives the pattern MAJOR.MINOR, not one value; a module that names a version the reader does not read is rejected by the rule `manifest.format-version`. The attempt keeps the number.
  - The format version has no patch. An edit of the descriptions, examples and words of the format text that does not change the rules, and a test vector that pins what is already written, do not change the number: such an editorial change is named by the tag of `spec`.
- **The line of `spec`.** Each release is the next patch of the line, and a patch does not change the format version: in one line there is one format.
  - A pull request that gives the format a new version raises `RELEASE_LINE` in the same change.
  - `release-version` holds the link, by `tools/release/format-line.mjs`: another format version only higher and only in a raised line, a new major one only with a new major version of `spec`. A line whose releases carry one format version takes no other: the next version comes out in the next line opened.
  - While the format is v0, `spec` stays 0.x. Format v1 comes out with `spec` v1.0.0, and after that a major version of the format raises the major version of `spec` too.
  - **The other parts.** A line is opened, beside a new format version, by a new major package of a contract, `v2` or higher, and by a new version of each normative part with a version of its own: the admission table, `admission/`, the deployment configuration, `deployment/` (its first version, 1, opened line 0.11), the legal texts, `legal/` (from line 0.13), the table of the age of digital consent, `consent-age/` (from line 0.14), and the export format, `export/`. Another version of a part comes only higher than the previous one and only in a raised line. `release-version` holds each by a filter of its own in `tools/release/`: `contracts-line.mjs`, `admission-line.mjs`, `deployment-line.mjs`, `legal-line.mjs`, `consent-age-line.mjs` and `export-line.mjs`. There is no link of the major versions: only the format raises the major version of `spec`.
  - **The contracts** have no MAJOR.MINOR of their own: the version is the suffix of the protobuf package, `v1`, and the tag of `spec`.
