The code is in `tutor`, the same with which its eval measures models: so admission measures exactly what the platform will check. How words and sentences are counted is set by this code. The checks do not go into the module format: they do not depend on the module's data.
- **The language.** The word limit is measured for Russian and English. An explanation language that the measurement did not measure is checked without a word limit until a measurement in that language sets it: the platform is for any language, and one limit for all languages is too tight already for English. The other rules hold in any language.
- **The learner's gender.** The model does not get it. But in languages where the form of a word gives away gender — in Russian, the past tense and short adjectives about the learner, «ты нашёл», «ты прав» —, the tutor's words may call the child by the wrong gender.
  - The rule is for all of the tutor's words, not only for a hint: praise, an explanation and feedback give away gender the same way. The words are in forms without gender: «здесь всё верно», not «ты верно нашёл».
  - A program does not check this: by the forms of words there is no way without false alarms — «начала» is both a verb and a noun. The eval checks it: each capability that writes words to the learner has an item on gender in its eval set, and a model that gives away gender does not pass it.
  - `tutor`'s measurement of hints, by a rough search: in the Russian hints of the test, gender is given away by Opus in 0 of 102, by Haiku · `low` in 13, by Haiku without thinking in 37.

— *Why:* `tutor`'s recommendations. The form is a rule of the glossary, and for a program it is as simple to check as the leak, and a hint of three sentences or in another language would otherwise reach the learner. `tutor`'s options:
- the check does not depend on the module's data, so it is code of the platform, not a format rule;
- the word limit is by language, because modules are written in any language;
- the rule on gender is for all words, because «молодец, справился» gives away gender the same way as a hint.

— *Rejected:*
- form checks in the module format: the module gives them nothing;
- one word limit for all languages: it is too tight for English;
- leaving the form to `api` without a norm, or not checking it at all;
- the rule on gender only for a hint; a programmatic check of gender by a dictionary of forms.

— *Consequence:* `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `tutor`'s and `api`'s `docs/architecture.md`.

## Assessment by a rubric

**R71. Assessment by a rubric is measured by two measures. The main one is the share of false alarms: criteria that the AI called not met, though they are met. The second is agreement with people's assessment and Cohen's kappa for each criterion. At the rung "author" the target is set by `tutor`'s synthetic essays: the upper 95 % bound, by essay, of the share of false alarms on met criteria is at most 1 %. The target at the rung "full" and its eval set are set by the measurement of `tutor` on the essays of adult volunteers.**
- **The measurement of E4 of `tutor`:** 20 synthetic essays in English and a rubric of six criteria. The truth is the plan, without disputed cases. On the test, 15 essays with three repeats each:
  - Opus 5.5 · `high` has 0 false alarms of 197 assessments of met criteria, the upper bound of 95% over essays is 0.015, κ 1.00;
  - Haiku 5.5 · `low` has 1 of 198, κ 0.99;
  - Haiku without thinking has 2 of 198, κ 0.97.

  The measure is computed by a program and separates the models.
- **The target at the rung "author"** is the main measure on `tutor`'s synthetic set with the six criteria of E4: its upper 95 % bound, by essay, is at most 1 %. Missed "not met" and κ go beside it, without a target. The feedback is in English alone, as `english-essays` explains in `en`, until another language is measured. Until 2027-01-17 the entry `CallRubric` stands at "author" by the author's word, not by this target: the target is the rule of its run on Haiku 5.5 after that (run/DEBT.md, Д265).
  - On 300 synthetic essays in two calls, false alarms on met criteria: Haiku 5.5 · `medium` 2 of 1350, bound ≤ 0.005; Opus 5.5 · `high` 5 of 1347; Sonnet without thinking 12 of 1350, ≤ 0.014, by `tutor`'s measurement in its `docs/measurements.md`.
- **Why the target at the rung "full" is not by the synthetic data.** The synthetic data are even, and the criteria are without disputed cases, so a target by them would be too strict for live writing. Without a target there is no admission, so the target is needed before the first learner with essays.
- **The guide for authors** (epic E5). A criterion about capital letters on handwriting is disputable for c, o, s, u, v, w, x and z: only height tells their capital from their lowercase. Haiku's false alarms in the measurement are by the criterion "capitals and full stops", and one of them is of this kind: in essay 11, "One" was read as lowercase, since the capital O of the synthetic data is written as the lowercase one, only larger.

— *Why:* the recommendations of `tutor`. Feedback that does not see what was done confuses the learner just as "not yet" on a correct answer does.

— *Rejected:*
- leaving the measures open until the volunteers' essays: the measure is already there and checked;
- a target at the rung "full" now, by the synthetic data;
- the rung "author" as `tutor`'s eval had it, no false alarm and no missed "not met" on at least 30 met and 20 unmet criteria: each configuration had 2–12 on 300 essays, and only a set of about 10 essays would pass, with a bound of about 8–10 %;
- no rubric entry until the volunteers' essays: `api` starts an essay only where both of its capabilities are admitted, so `CallEssay` would give it nothing.

— *Consequence:* `docs/product.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `run/EPICS.md`; `tutor`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## Types of the module format

**R72. The types of `spec`'s normative parts are given by a generator of its own from their schemas, `tools/types`, for Go and, by the same model, for TypeScript, as the file `index.d.ts` beside the Go of each package. The Go module `spec` carries the types of the module format in the packages `types/formatv0` — the parts, the shared definitions, the canonical view, the inventory, the part list for the device, the index and the vectors — and `types/formatv0/open` — the open view of each part, under the same names; the package is named by the major version of the format. Beside them stand the types of the admission table, `types/admissionv0`, of the deployment configuration, `types/deploymentv1`, of the legal texts, `types/legalv3`, of the table of the age of digital consent, `types/consentagev1`, and of the export format, `types/exportv3`.**
- **The generator** is `tools/types/`, on Node, like the other tools of `spec`. It reads the schemas, the module layout and the version from `format/` with the same functions as `format-check`. The model, `model.mjs`, takes the shape of a value from the schema:
  - a type is at the root of each schema and at each `$defs`, in PascalCase and with `ID` instead of `id`: `task` → `Task`, `answer_slot` → `AnswerSlot`, `skill_id` → `SkillID`;
  - an object without a name of its own is named by the table `INLINE_NAMES`, in the words of the glossary: `Audience`, `Band`, `Languages`, `CanvasSettings`, `Author`, `Skill`, `RetiredSkill`, `Technique`, `Trap`, `RandomState` and five kinds of `…Draw`. The enumeration of a field is named by the object and the field: `CanvasKind`, `AnswerSlotBinding`;
  - the fields of an object come from its `properties`, its `allOf` and the branches of `if`/`then`/`else`. A field that the object always holds is required: it is in the `required` of the object or of its `allOf`, not of a branch;
  - a `$ref` beside which the keys only narrow the value is the type it refers to. A `$defs` that narrows a structure in this way is another name of the same structure: `WrittenCheck` is `Check`;
  - `pattern`, bounds, `not`, `contains` and conditions between fields are the business of the schema, not of the type.

  A shape that the model does not know is a generation error with a pointer to the place in the schema: two places of one name, an object without a name, a field to which the branches give different shapes. The generator understands the schemas of 0.1 as they are: the model has 101 types, and the open views are 24.
- **Go**, `go.mjs`:
  - a structure per object. A field that the object always holds is a value, and any other is a pointer, a slice or a map with `omitzero`. So absence and zero — an empty `alt`, `false`, 0 — are told apart, and a value is written back by the same JSON by which it was read;
  - `integer` is `int64`: the format's bounds of an integer, ±(2^53 − 1), fit in it. `number` is `float64`, and `["string", "null"]` is `*string`;
  - a string, an integer, a list or a map with a name of its own is a type of its own: `type SkillID LocalID`, `type Numbers map[TemplateName]int64`. The values of an enumeration are constants: `CanvasKindHandwritingSheet`;
  - the comment of a type names its place in the schema and repeats its `description`, and that of a field also its `default`;
  - there is no code in the packages, only types and constants: what is valid is decided by the schema, and `spec` is not the platform's library. Whoever reads a value from outside first checks it against the schema. The code that buf generates from the API contracts is not in `types/`: it lies in the nested module `contracts` and requires the protobuf runtime.
- **TypeScript**: the same generator gives `index.d.ts` beside the Go of each package, by the same model. The open view of a field and the place of a type, `openRefOf` and `placeOf` of the model, are shared by Go and TypeScript, and `just types-check` also checks the types with `tsc` by the same corpus.
- **The open view** is the package `open`: a structure for each type that the open view of a part reaches, with the fields marked `x-open`. A field is open if at least one subschema of its place marks it. On 0.1 this is the same as the rule by value of `tools/format-check/openview.mjs`: a field with the mark in a branch is either marked in a subschema that always applies too, or declared only in this branch. `open.Task` has no `check`, `template` and `solver`, but has `givens` and `unknown`; `open.Traps` is an empty structure. Strings, integers and enumerations `open` takes from `formatv0`.
- **The other parts.** The packages of the other normative parts have no open view:
  - `types/admissionv0`, from the schemas `admission/schemas`. The nested objects of the table's schemas are named by their `$defs`, not by rows of `INLINE_NAMES`. The package is only of major version 0 of the table, and for an `admission/VERSION` of another major version the generator writes nothing: it needs a package of its own;
  - `types/deploymentv1`, from the schemas `deployment/schemas`, only of major version 1 of its format;
  - the types of the legal texts, of the table of the age of digital consent and of the export format: each package is named by the integer version of its part and takes the place of the previous one, not standing beside it — `types/legalv3` from line 0.17, after `legalv1` of lines 0.13–0.14 and `legalv2` of lines 0.15–0.16; `types/consentagev1` from line 0.14; `types/exportv3` from line 0.18, after `exportv1` of lines 0.14–0.16 and `exportv2` of line 0.17.
- **The files are in the repository:** the Go module is built from the tag. `just types` writes them anew, and `just types-check` is the CI step "Types":
  - it compares them with what the generator would give, file for file;
  - it reads with its type, strictly, each value of `format/` that passes the schema, and writes it back. These are the examples, the part files of each module of the examples and vectors, the vectors themselves and the canonical view of each example of a whole module — 288 cases now. The open view of an open-view vector is read by the type `open`, and the part of the same vector with a closed field the type `open` must fail to read (`tools/types/corpus.mjs`, `tools/types/roundtrip`);
  - the corpus takes the values of `admission/` too — the table, the valid examples and the vectors — and those of `deployment/`, the valid examples and the vectors; the registry of `tools/types/roundtrip` knows each generated package;
  - the nested module `tools/types/roundtrip` takes `spec` from the working tree and requires no other modules.
- **The Go module** carries `types/`, and `tools/gomod` compares its files byte for byte, like `LICENSE` and `format/`. `go-check` checks `./...`, and the module still requires nothing; the vet and tests of `tools/types/roundtrip` are in the recipes `ci-lint` and `ci-test`, like those of all Go modules of `spec`, not in `go-check`. The components in Go take the types by the same tag as the format, with their move to a release of `spec`.
- **Versions in the window.** The package is named by the major version of the format: 0.2 changes its types, but not its path. With v1, `formatv1` stands beside `formatv0`, and with v2 the module is `/v2`, with `formatv1` and `formatv2` in it. How the module carries the previous major version of the format is still decided by the pull request that opens it.
- **The Go module gives no generator of randomness as code.** The format's normative functions of randomness are exactly Go's `math/rand/v2` and `hash/fnv`, and how to call them is decided by `module-kit`. The TypeScript types give none either.

— *Why:* all read 2026-10-29.
- **Three steps instead of one.** The generator with the Go types, the npm package with a publication step of its own and the shared Go checks are three rounds, and each is for one check, by RUN.md's rule on splitting a task larger than one review. The Go types come out at once, with the next tag, and `module-kit` and `sim` wait for them. The TypeScript types have no consumer while there is no npm package.
- **A generator of its own.** json-schema-to-typescript 16.0.0, quicktype 26.0.0 and go-jsonschema v0.24.1 do not understand `if`/`then`/`else`, `propertyNames` and `unevaluatedProperties`, and the schemas of 0.1 write unions through `allOf` and `if`/`then` — 24 times. A generator in Go would go into the module's zip or would be a second language of the tools, and 101 types by hand would diverge from the schemas.
- **Open views as a package.** Under the same names in `open`, the consumer gets the type of what the learner sees — `api` gives the open view of the manifest —, and a closed field cannot be read by them. The names `OpenTask` would double the length of one package.
- **Pointers with `omitzero`.** `omitempty` on writing would throw out the empty `alt` of a picture that only decorates, `false` and 0, and the consumer would not tell "not set" from zero.
- **Types of their own for IDs.** `type SkillID LocalID`, not an alias: the compiler will not let one confuse the ID of a skill with the ID of a task. Another name of a structure is an alias, since the narrowing of the schema does not change its shape.
- **Duplicates in SonarCloud.** The open view repeats the fields of the part, and the duplicates of new code would fail the quality gate, so `types/**` is in `sonar.cpd.exclusions`.

— *Rejected:*
- two steps — the types of both languages, then npm and `go.yml`; one step for all;
- a third-party generator; a generator in Go; types by hand;
- the open views in the same package under the names `Open…`; the package `formatv0/` at the root of `spec`, beside `format/`; a path by the full version of the format;
- values with `omitempty`;
- the generator of randomness as code in the Go module.

— *Consequence:* `tools/types/`; `types/`; `justfile`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `.sonarcloud.properties`; `tools/gomod/`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `README.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

**R73. The TypeScript types of the module format are given by the same generator, `tools/types`, by the same model as the Go types — flat, as in Go, as the file `index.d.ts` beside the Go of each package. The npm package `@altnovatrail/spec` carries them with no code and no dependencies and exports `./formatv0` and `./formatv0/open`, and from later lines the types of the element `<novatrail-canvas>`, of the other normative parts and the JSON of a workbook page, by the line of its version; the release of `spec` from the line 0.4 on carries it as the file `altnovatrail-spec-<version>.tgz`, with a cosign signature and under an attestation. Packages take it as a copy of their own by exact version. The first version in npm was published by hand, and each release then publishes its own.**
- **The TypeScript output** is `tools/types/ts.mjs`, by the model of the Go types without changes to it:
  - the names are the same as in Go. A structure is an `interface`: a field that the object always holds is required, and any other is `?:`, and so is a field of the schema's branches;
  - an enumeration is a union of strings, `type CanvasKind = "handwriting_sheet" | "workbook"`. A string, an integer, an ID, another name of a structure, a list or a map with a name of its own is an alias: `type SkillID = LocalID`, `type Numbers = Readonly<Record<TemplateName, number>>`;
  - `integer` and `number` are `number`, `["string", "null"]` is `string | null`. Everything is `readonly`, and lists are `readonly T[]`: these are data read from a module;
  - an empty open view is an object each field of which is `never`: an empty interface would accept any object, closed fields too;
  - a map by an enumeration key and a description that holds the end of a comment are generation errors;
  - the comment of a type and of a field is JSDoc from `description`, and that of a field also has `@defaultValue`;
  - there is no code: neither constants nor a generator of randomness. Declarations import with `import type`.
- **The npm package** is `tools/types/npm.mjs`. `package.json` is written by code, and the contents of the package are by the line of its version: in the line 0.4 the archive holds `package.json`, `LICENSE`, the package's README `tools/types/npm/README.md` and two `index.d.ts`, and nothing more:
  - `exports` are `./formatv0` and `./formatv0/open` with the condition `types`, and `./package.json`; `type: module`; neither `main`, nor scripts, nor dependencies;
  - `repository` is `git+https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec.git`: npm's provenance requires it to match the repository;
  - the version is the number of the release without `v`. It comes out with each release of the line, even when the types are the same;
  - the archive is built by `npm pack` of the Node that runs the tool, without the user's and the system's settings, with a cache of its own and without scripts, and is read back by `tar`.
- **What later lines add.** The lines are the constants of `tools/types/npm.mjs`, and the package of an earlier line stays the one it got:
  - from the line 0.5, `canvas/index.d.ts` — the types of the element `<novatrail-canvas>`, written by hand — and the export `./canvas`. The types of the element are with exact unions: "flat, as in Go" is a rule of the generator;
  - from the line 0.8, the types of the admission table, `./admissionv0` (`FIRST_ADMISSION_LINE`). The corpus of `tsc` imports only the packages of its values;
  - from the line 0.10, data — `format/page.json` and `format/vectors/pages/<case>.json`, the JSON of a workbook page —, exported, and their types are `Page` and `PageVector` in `formatv0`. The package still carries no code;
  - from the line 0.11, the types of the deployment configuration, `./deploymentv1`;
  - the types of the legal texts — `./legalv1` from line 0.13, `./legalv2` in its place from line 0.15 and `./legalv3` in place of both from line 0.17 —, of the table of the age of digital consent — `./consentagev1` from line 0.14 —, and of the export format — `./exportv1` from line 0.14, `./exportv2` in its place from line 0.17 and `./exportv3` from line 0.18.
- **The contracts** are not in this package: their TypeScript code comes out as an npm package of its own, `@altnovatrail/contracts`, with the runtime `@bufbuild/protobuf` in its dependencies, and `@altnovatrail/spec` stays without code and without dependencies.
- **The check** is in `just types-check`, the CI step "Types":
  - the package is built from the working tree and unpacked into a project that `tools/types/typescript.mjs` writes from the corpus of the Go types' roundtrip — a declaration per case, in one line;
  - `tsc` checks the project twice — under `nodenext` and under `bundler` —, with `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `verbatimModuleSyntax` and without `skipLibCheck`;
  - a case with a closed field stands under `@ts-expect-error`: if `tsc` accepts such a value, it fails;
  - `typescript` 7.0.2 is in `tools/package.json`.
- **The release file:**
  - from `FIRST_NPM_LINE`, 0.4, `tools/release/files.mjs` also names `altnovatrail-spec-<X.Y.Z>.tgz`, and `just release-files <commit> <folder> <tag>` builds it from the objects of the commit;
  - the signature and the check of the release are the same as for `format-0.1.tar.gz`;
  - the consumer checks the archive from npm with the recipe `release-verify`: the archive from the registry — against the bundle of the release file `altnovatrail-spec-<version>.tgz`, and the archive is bound to the tag by the `version` in its `package.json`.
- **The line 0.4** is opened by this change, and the format in it is still 0.1: the format's versioning allows the same format version in a raised line.
- **How packages take the types** — as a copy of their own by exact version:
  - `canvas` — in `dependencies`, since its `.d.ts` refer to the types of `spec`;
  - `app` — in `devDependencies`.

  The version is moved together with the submodule `spec/`, in one move to a tag, and the package is excluded from Dependabot `npm`, like the Go module.
- **A generator of randomness as code** the package does not give: how a widget gets the seed is decided by the widget protocol, epic E5 (Т-24).

— *Why:* all read 2026-10-29.
- **Two steps.** npm sets up a trusted publisher only for a package that is already in the registry: "Package must exist: The package you're configuring must already exist on the npm registry" ([npm Docs, npm trust](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/commands/npm-trust)). And a setting that has published nothing expires "48 hours after creation" ([GitHub Changelog, 2026-10-02](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-02-unvalidated-npm-trusted-publishing-configurations-now-expire/)). So first the release carries the package's file and the first version is published by hand, and the publication step comes as a step of its own, right after the setup.
- **Flat types.** One model and one corpus for both languages: what is checked in Go is checked in TypeScript too. Exact unions would require reading the branches of the schemas — their `required` and `not` — and giving names to the variants. The consumer narrows by itself, by a field: `slot.zone !== undefined`.
- **A copy of their own.** The package is declarations only, and two copies of it in a build cost nothing. TypeScript types are structural: two versions of one shape are one type, and a shape that diverged is a compiler error at the junction of `app` and `canvas`. With `peerDependencies` by exact version, each version of `canvas` would require exactly the version of `spec` that `app` has, otherwise npm refuses the installation, and a release of `spec` comes out on each change of `main`.
- **The line 0.4.** Which files the release carries is decided by its line (`tools/release/files.mjs`), as the files themselves came — from the line 0.3 on. A rerun of a release of the line 0.3 does not expect the package's file.
- **`tsc` by the corpus.** The check of a literal's excess properties is the same strict reading as `DisallowUnknownFields` in Go, and a missing required field `tsc` catches by itself. There are two module resolutions, since under `node16`, `nodenext` and `bundler` "TypeScript always matches the "types" and "default" conditions if present" ([TypeScript, Modules — Reference](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/reference.html), updated 2026-10-28), and `canvas` resolves modules as `NodeNext`.
- **TypeScript 7.0.2** is `latest`, under Apache-2.0, "a native port of TypeScript built in Go" ([Announcing TypeScript 7.0](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/), 2026-07-08); `canvas` has the same version. Its builds are the optional packages `@typescript/typescript-<platform>` 7.0.2, under Apache-2.0 and without install scripts, and the license check skips them.
- **`readonly` and aliases** — as in the temporary types of `canvas`. Brands for IDs are rejected: each value from JSON would have to be cast.
- **`release-verify` for the consumer.** The command `gh release verify-asset <tag> altnovatrail-spec-<version>.tgz -R altnovatrail/spec` checks less: the attestation does not bind the file to the commit.

— *Rejected:*
- one step together with the publication step;
- exact unions by a constant field and by the presence of a field;
- `peerDependencies` by exact version;
- the package in the line 0.3, by the content of the commit;
- brands for IDs; constants of enumerations and a generator of randomness as code in the package;
- a `.d.ts` file per schema: per Go package there is one file, and the `exports` point straight at it;
- the consumer's check by `gh release verify-asset`.

— *Consequence:* `tools/types/ts.mjs`; `tools/types/npm.mjs`; `tools/types/typescript.mjs`; `tools/types/npm/README.md`; `tools/release/files.mjs`; `tools/package.json`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `README.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s and `app`'s `package.json`.

## Types of the element `canvas`

**R74. The types of the element `<novatrail-canvas>` — the agreement of `canvas` and `app` — `spec` writes by hand, as the file `types/canvas/index.d.ts`, and the npm package `@altnovatrail/spec` from the line 0.5 on carries them and exports them as `./canvas`. They have no version of their own and no release file of their own. The tutor's marks are held to the message `Mark` of the contract `novatrail.api.v1`, and the test vectors of `canvas` are the eval protocol's.**
- **What is in the types** — the members of the element that `canvas` and `app` agree on:
  - `CanvasElement extends HTMLElement`:
    - the properties `tool`; what the element shows, one of three — `task`, the open view of the task `open.Task`, `workedExample` with `demoState`, the worked example of a lesson, or `paper`, a task from the learner's paper: the picture of its crop on a dotted sheet, with the pen and the eraser alone —; `manifest`, the open view of the manifest `open.Manifest`; `media`; `history` and, on a task from paper, `tracing` — where the tracing paper lies on the sheet and whether it is hidden — for reading and assignment; `marks`; and `filled` for reading;
    - the methods `exportWork()` and `exportPicture()`, the PNG of the strokes the surface shows;
  - the events — `ToolChangeEvent`, `HistoryChangeEvent`, `DemoChangeEvent` and `TracingChangeEvent`, and `CanvasEventMap` names them by their names;
  - the writing history — `HistoryEvent`, `Stroke` and `InkPoint`, as `canvas` records it; a stroke on the tracing paper is marked so, its points in the sheet's units from the tracing paper's corner, and moves with it;
  - the work for checking — `ExportedWork`, `ExportedSheet`, `ExportedWorkbook` with `ExportedCell`, and `ExportedPaper`: the crop without strokes, the PNG of the work and its context;
  - the submission context — `Submission`, `SheetSubmission` with `CropNumbers`, `Frame`, `Group` and `Box`, `WorkbookSubmission` with `Filling`, and `PaperSubmission`, a sheet's with the place of the tracing paper, `TracingState`;
  - the marks — `Marks`, `Mark` and `Anchor`: `FrameMark`, a frame round an answer slot or a box — on a workbook cell round the box and its strokes, round an empty box the box alone, a change of the frame that `canvas`'s decision log set before —, and `WavyLineMark`, the wavy line of a task from paper under a box, drawn over a light halo that keeps 3:1 against any page and named "Tutor's mark: where the mistake is" in the accessibility tree, and `VerdictMark`, the tick or the cross by each answer of a task from paper at the box its reading gave, over a white halo, which `app` makes from the verdict of the answer slot and no message `Mark` holds; `app` writes each mark's name;
  - `CellPlace`, `Filled`, `Tool` and `Media`.

  The unions are exact: a history event is told by `kind`, the work and the context by a key, and a mark by `kind`. The rule "flat, as in Go" of the format's types is a rule of the generator, and these types are written by hand, and there are none of them in Go.
- **What is not in the types:**
  - members of the element that the agreement does not name: `undo()` and `clear()` of `canvas`. If they become an agreement with `app`, `canvas` brings them as a row «в реестр spec»;
  - the place of the element in the DOM maps, `HTMLElementTagNameMap` and `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`. They are augmented by the package `canvas`, which registers the element: `interface GlobalEventHandlersEventMap extends CanvasEventMap {}`.
- **The file and the check:**
  - `types/canvas/index.d.ts` lies beside the generator's output. `just types` replaces only the generator's folders, and `just types-check` refuses if there is anything else in `types/`. The Go module carries this file in its zip, like the `.d.ts` of the format;
  - the declarations take the DOM types — `Blob`, `CustomEvent`, `HTMLElement` —, so the consumer's `lib` must include `dom`. The types of the format do not take the DOM, and the corpus is still checked without it;
  - the check is `tools/types/canvas.check.ts`. It holds a class of `canvas` that keeps the agreement, a synthetic history, contexts and work, the narrowing of the work by a key, and under `@ts-expect-error` everything the agreement does not allow — `undo()` and `clear()` among it. It turns a mark of the contract into a mark of the element by a full `switch` on the place and the kind, so a kind or a place that the contract adds without a type at the element breaks `tsc`. `tools/types/typescript.mjs` puts it into the project of `types-check` beside the corpus. `tsc` checks it under `nodenext` and `bundler`, with the DOM, against the package built by the line of the working tree.
- **The npm package** from the line 0.5 on also carries `canvas/index.d.ts`, and in its `exports` — `./canvas`. The contents of the package `tools/types/npm.mjs` takes by the line of its version, starting from `FIRST_CANVAS_LINE`, and the package of the line 0.4 stays as before byte for byte.
- **The version.** The types of the element have no version of their own, just as there is no file `<part>-<version>.tar.gz`: this is not a normative part with a version of its own, but declarations of a package whose version is the tag of the release. `canvas` and `app` take the package as a copy of their own by exact version, like the types of the format, and a shape that diverged `tsc` catches at their junction. A change of the types of the element requires no new line, and a new file of the package enters with a new line, as this one entered with the line 0.5.
- **The vectors of `canvas`** — the groups, the crops, the snapping and the boxes — are the vectors of the eval protocol, `contracts/vectors/eval/v1/`, as its messages, in `contracts.Vectors` and in the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`. The layout of a workbook page is a norm of the format, `format/page.yaml` and `format/vectors/pages/`, which `@altnovatrail/spec` carries as JSON. The types of the writing history stay the element's, and the protocol does not replace them: the element's history needs pressure, to draw the width of the pen's line, and a sample has none; how the element's history becomes a sample's is [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), in its rules that the device and the runner share.
- **How packages take the types** — by the same move to a tag as the types of the format:
  - `canvas` — a class with `implements CanvasElement` and the augmentation of the DOM maps;
  - `app` — the same types in `devDependencies`.

— *Why:*
- **By hand.** An event, a method and a promise are not JSON data, and a schema will not describe them. A schema of the data alone — the history and the context — would give two sources for one agreement, and the generator would need the DOM types, which it does not know.
- **The marks by the contract.** A mark's look and place are the contract's, and a program places it; the element draws it and `app` names it. The `switch` of the check keeps the two in step without a second schema.
- **The history is the element's.** The shape of the messages of protobuf-es — `$typeName`, and `case` with `value` for a `oneof` — is foreign to the element, and replacing its types with the protocol's would break `canvas` and `app`.
- **The vectors with the protocol.** Without the protocol's text and schemas they would be a copy of the files of `canvas`, and the protocol chooses the field and the threshold of snapping by its own data.
- **Without a version of its own.** The agreement of two packages that take `spec` by exact version is held by the compiler, not by the rule of lines. A version of its own would require a `VERSION` of its own, the rule "a new version is a new line" and a check in `release-version`.
- **A new file with a new line.** A rerun of the release builds the package by the list of files of the tip, from the objects of its commit (`release.yml`, the step "Build the files"). The commit of the line 0.4 has no file `types/canvas/index.d.ts`, and without binding the contents to the line such a rerun would fail. Checked on a trial commit: `release-files` built `altnovatrail-spec-0.4.1.tgz` of the commit v0.4.1 byte for byte the same as the release file.
- **The DOM maps are augmented by `canvas`.** If the package itself augmented them, and two copies of it with a diverged shape ended up in a build — at `canvas` and at `app`, each taking it as a copy of its own —, `tsc` would give the error TS2717 in the package's declarations in `node_modules`, where neither of them looks. Without this, a diverged shape is an error where `app` touches it. This is checked by a trial consumer with two copies of the package, and two copies of one shape do not interfere with each other either way.

— *Rejected:*
- the data by a schema, by the generator;
- one surface of the element, with the history and the context as opaque JSON;
- the types of the marks of `canvas`'s own, before the contract placed them;
- the vectors of `canvas` apart from the protocol — as they are or with schemas;
- the protocol's types of the history in place of the element's;
- a version of its own for the types of the element and a release file of its own;
- the types in the package 0.4.x by the content of the commit, rejected for the types of the format too;
- the augmentation of the DOM maps in the package of `spec`;
- the types of the element in the package `canvas`, as `canvas`'s decision log and its `docs/architecture.md` write: the agreement of `canvas` and `app` written down in `spec` would come out as types at only one side.

— *Consequence:* `types/canvas/index.d.ts`; `tools/types/canvas.check.ts`; `tools/types/typescript.mjs`; `tools/types/npm.mjs`; `tools/types/npm/README.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `README.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## The path of assessment by a rubric

**R75. Assessment by a rubric is two calls. The first is the reading of the essay: one reader, without the rubric, gives the text as it is written. The second is the assessment of the text read by the criteria of the rubric, without the picture: for each criterion — a justification and whether it is met, and one feedback on the whole essay. An essay that cannot be read does not reach the assessment: its submission ends "unreadable", and the learner rewrites the sheet.**
- **The path:**
  1. `app` sends the work — the crop of the handwriting sheet;
  2. `api` calls the reading of the essay. The reading gets the same as the reading of handwriting: the work, the open view of the task, the age category and the AI route. `tutor` checks the admission, and `api` gets the observation — the text read;
  3. `api` calls the assessment by the rubric with this text. `tutor` checks the admission again, and the model gives the assessments by criteria and the feedback;
  4. the feedback passes the leak check and the feedback rule and goes to the device. Feedback that does not pass is replaced by the phrase of `app` "no feedback this time", without a repeated call.

  These are two calls of the library `tutor`, not one with two requests inside: between perception and the rubric stands a program. Between the calls `tutor` stores nothing: the text lives in the memory of the request of `api`.
- **What the assessment gets:**
  - the text read — as data, not instructions;
  - the topic — the task statement;
  - the criteria of the rubric, in order;
  - the presentation style (О-23);
  - the module's explanation language, in which the feedback is written;
  - the age category and the AI route — for the admission.

  The picture does not go to the assessment, and a rubric has no key and no solution of the task.
- **An essay that cannot be read** does not reach the assessment, and the learner rewrites the sheet, as with "unreadable". But an item with a rubric has no verdict, and "unreadable" of an answer slot is a verdict. Such a submission ends "unreadable" — the sheet is empty or the essay cannot be read as a whole —, at the submission, not at an answer slot; the server keeps only the time and how the submission ended, and the learner rewrites the sheet and submits again or closes the attempt by "Done".
- **The data**, by `tutor`'s measurements in its `docs/architecture.md`. These are synthetic data and the rubric of E4 of six criteria:
  - on the 300 essays of the large run, for the four configurations together, the false alarms on met criteria are 26 with two calls and 28 with one, and the missed "not met" are 13 and 11. On the 15 essays of the run of two calls, for five configurations — 3 with two calls and 5 with one;
  - a separate reading keeps the learner's errors more exactly. Of 178 words with an error, read as written: Haiku 5.5 · `low` 167 against 155, Haiku 5.5 · `medium` 164 against 161, Sonnet 177 against 175, Opus 5.5 · `high` — 178 on both paths;
  - two calls cost $13.13 against $12.61 for 300 essays for the four configurations, 4% more, and the time is longer by 0–2 s, on the 15 essays.
- **The measure** is the main measure of assessment by a rubric, the share of false alarms, along the whole path, the reading and the assessment together: a false alarm from a wrong reading enters the main measure. The measurement on the essays of adult volunteers checks this path and measures one call beside it. If one call gives fewer false alarms, the question is returned to by a new decision.
- **One reader** reads the essay: two readers are for answer slots whose check gives a verdict, and a rubric has none.

— *Why:* a decided item must not stand open in the card of `tutor`, and the detailing of `api` needs the path and the data that go to the AI. The arguments of `tutor`:
- on the synthetic data, two calls are no worse than one by the main measure, the false alarms, and the cost and time are almost the same;
- the reading of handwriting is an AI capability of its own, with a prompt and an eval set of its own, as is the assessment by a rubric. Reading and analysis are arranged the same way, as two calls;
- the assessor does not see the picture: only the text read goes to it.

— *Rejected:*
- one call, as the measurement of E4 went: it merges reading and assessment into one capability, and on the synthetic data it has no fewer false alarms;
- waiting for the volunteers' essays: the item of the card would stay open, and the product's code would have nothing to rest on;
- writing nothing down.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md` — the card of `tutor`, with the assessment by two calls among what it does, the path of a task with a rubric, and what the learner sees when an essay cannot be read; `docs/privacy.md` — the criteria of the rubric and the text read without the picture; `docs/concepts.md`; `tutor`'s and `api`'s `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## The cross-repository plan

**R76. The other repositories' work toward the plan's goal is coordinated by the cross-repository plan, `COORDINATION.md` at the root of `spec`: its rules, in English, and «Порядок», in Russian — the goal in one line, then rows by the items of the order in which the repositories appear, in `docs/repositories.md`, each naming a task of a repository's RUN.md and the rows it waits for. The goal is the first slice with adults on the deployment `novatrail`, the tasks from the learner's paper among it. The coordinator names the next task, and the orchestrator runs an epic; the tasks across repositories of an epic that `spec` plans, as E11, are spec's table 1, not rows of the file, and the author leads each, not the orchestrator.**
- **The file** holds only the order. A row names a task of its repository's RUN.md, as "Txx `module-kit`"; for a task the repository has not written yet it gives that repository's session the text the file's rules set for such a task, and the session numbers it. A row whose tasks are all done, or that we do not do, is deleted and leaves «Зависит от»; numbers are never reused, each item names its next free one, and a deleted row is read in git. The file keeps no state, no closed rows and no task texts: the state is the coordinator's report, and the text a row's task is written from is in the task of `spec`, or the row «в реестр spec», that made the row. It has no registers «В» and «Д»: a question to the author is a row of the repository's table 3, `run/QUESTIONS.md`, and one across repositories goes to the registers О-, П- and Т-.
- **The items** follow the order of appearance in `docs/repositories.md`: `spec`; `.github`; `module-kit` and `modules`; `learner-model`, `engine` and `sim`; `tutor` and `canvas`, which go before items 3 and 4; `api`, `app`, `skill-map` and `infra`. Item 7, «все репозитории», is outside that order: a task that is the same in each repository, from one text, a row per repository. Its rows hold no part of the goal and do not wait for it, and a change of such a row that alters what a check proves — a package left out of `-race`, a gate split in parts — is that repository's decision. `site` takes item 8.
- **The goal**, the first line of «Порядок», is «Первый срез со взрослыми»: on `novatrail` adults from the US learn, each by a code of `api invite` of their own, from a phone, a tablet and a computer — handwriting, lessons, the engine and the tutor's words under the quota of platform AI, by epic E3 of `app`, and the tasks from the learner's paper. An account is created only by such a code, which the operator issues, and the one country is the US (`api countries allow`). Who learns there now, the rung, the facts declared and when the codes go to other adults are the log's decisions on platform AI on `novatrail` and on admission by eval (Д265); the codes are the operator's step, not a row. Outside the goal: children (Д240) and the checks on real devices. A row next to the goal, as the module of the check board, is one the goal does not wait for; what the goal holds, rows inside it bring.
- **The modules.** The module of olympiad maths names `adult` in its audience too: the platform offers a module only to learners of its age categories ([format text](../format/README.md), its rule on the manifest), and adults learn on the slice. The eleven tasks of the check board of `tutor` are an official module of `modules`, `novatrail/check-board`, beside the two modules of the first slice in `docs/product.md` and not among them: the author solves them on the path a learner takes, and its eval set checks each new tag of `tutor` once the eval runner is in CI of `modules`.
- **`module-kit` is the whole format:** a release that others take passes every test vector of the format it reads, with no departures, and the CLI binary that CI of `modules` takes has its signature checked.
- **The coordinator** is a session of `spec` that the author starts with «Что дальше по COORDINATION.md?». It reads the repositories on GitHub, read only, and the rows «в реестр spec» by `just inbox`, and names the next task — the first open row whose «Зависит от» is done —, its phrase and its container. It runs no task of another repository, changes none of their files, decides nothing for the author and commits nothing. Its rules are the file's own.
- **The orchestrator** carries the coordinator's role to the end: «Сделай эпик E…» in `.devcontainer/orchestrator/` runs each task of the epic in its repository's container and merges its pull request on green checks. Its graph is the epic's table 1 and the rows of «Порядок» it names; a task a repository has not written yet, the executor writes down from the orchestrator's text, by the file's rule for such a task. The file's rule that the coordinator runs no task of another repository, edits none of their files, decides nothing for the author and commits nothing binds the coordinator alone.
- **An epic of tasks across repositories** that `spec` plans, as E11, keeps its tasks in spec's table 1, each naming its repositories, and has no rows in the file. It is not run by «Сделай эпик E…»: its tasks run one at a time, each one session the author leads in the orchestrator's container, on one branch of one name in each repository.

— *Why:* the work goes by the order in which the repositories appear, not by the thin slice; the slice holds handwriting, not a single choice of an option, and lessons, not a list of tasks. A separate file is not the "one shared plan for all the repositories" rejected when each repository got a RUN.md of its own, which would mix the order of work of twelve repositories: the tasks and the order within a repository stay in its RUN.md, and the file names only which task waits for which. Without it the order between repositories would live in the chat history, not in files, where what the next task needs must live; a goal gives the rows their end, since several repositories go toward it at once and the deployment waits for their releases.
- The rows are deleted, not kept: the coordinator read 73 KB a run, three quarters of it closed rows and state, and git keeps every cited row readable.
- A task the same in every repository reads best in one item; in the items of the order of appearance it would be spread over six tables.
- A phone: the app is to work on one, and the reflow to 320 CSS px that the accessibility standard of the UI packages requires anyway (WCAG 1.4.10) brings it near.
- The check board judges a solution by a model and asks the author whether the model was right: only a module goes the platform's own way, and `api` serves only packages that the chain from the signed index of a release of `modules` holds. Its tasks are solved on the sheet of a task from paper, a model judging them there too, as it judges a task from paper.
- When the AI reads the work of others than the author is the frame of the slice, not a detail of one repository: a question that concerns more than one repository belongs in `spec`.
- Each code task of E11 writes and checks every repository it touches in one session: the epic's order is its table 1, and rows would restate it.

— *Rejected:*
- the thin slice: first only a choice of an option, without AI and the engine, with `api` and `app` before `learner-model`, `engine` and `sim`; in the slice only a choice of an option, keyboard input in format 0.2, or a choice beside a scratch sheet that is not read;
- a list of tasks the learner chooses from, or tasks from `api` in the order of the graph; a slice without sign-in;
- the whole port of standalone before the first app; a learner of `under_13` on a module without `adult` — the category would be wrong;
- the cross-repository plan as an epic of spec's RUN.md, as the draft proposed, or as `docs/coordination.md`: `docs/` holds the platform's descriptive documents, and the plan is at the root, like RUN.md;
- no goal, the file leading open rows alone: the order between repositories would live in no file;
- closed rows kept in the tables with `[x]`, or moved to an archive file of their own;
- the full texts of the rows' tasks in the file: over its budget of size;
- the look of the slice, by the interface mockup, by rows next to the goal, which would then hold a phone and a look that no row brings; the slice only for a tablet and a computer;
- the rows of item 7 in the items of the order of appearance; for the speed of CI, an image of the stage published in GHCR, the option the shared CI checks left for a long build: the stage builds in 25–36 s with Go and loads from the cache in 13–36 s (measurements 3.1), and NovaTrail publishes no image;
- the module of the check board hidden from the catalog — a field of the manifest, a format change with `api` and `app` after it —, or a local unsigned package for `just dev` of `api`, which breaks the chain of digests from the signed module index and gives no eval set;
- a deployment without conditions: anyone with a Google account could learn;
- who the AI reads decided only in the documents of `tutor` and `api`; a deployment fact "the models are admitted at the rung `full`": a fact is what the operator declares of its agreements with a provider, not who learns, the rungs are `tutor`'s list ([`admission/`](../admission/README.md), its deployment facts and its admission function), and a new fact is a new version of the table;
- the operator's bucket only with the children: the samples and forms of adult volunteers come to it (Д156); a rollout of `app` with an `api` older than the one that serves what it shows, the titles and the quota's share then silently missing;
- for the synthetic child of `just dev-app` of `api`, `app` making the child — only the operator's command in `api`'s container confirms a consent —, or a workbook module for adults in `modules`, a module for a test alone;
- in the order to the first app: E3 of `spec` whole, with the age of consent and the export format; `module-kit` as a subset of the format that rejects the rest, or modules checked by a recipe of `spec`, a second owner of the format's semantics beside `module-kit`; the first release of `modules` only with the gate of `sim`; the check of the signature only by the first deployment, or after a release of `module-kit` with code — the recipe would come after `modules` moved to a tag, and a second move would follow; two moves of the repositories to a tag of `spec` where one does; a pause for E7 `canvas` and E1 `tutor`.

— *Consequence:* `COORDINATION.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `RULES.md`; [docs/README.md](README.md); `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/EPICS.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## The check of a release's signature

**R77. The signature of a NovaTrail release file is checked by one recipe of `spec`, `release-verify`, on sigstore-js, where the file enters NovaTrail, and it checks everything the certificate names: who signed, by whose call, on what branch and from what commit. A file of a shared release is signed by the shared `release.yml` of `.github` at the SHA of its release no lower than v0.1.7, on the history of its `main`, and a file of `spec` is bound to its tag by its content. The library `module-kit` does not check signatures: it trusts a package by the chain of digests from a pinned index.**
- **A file of a shared release** is a release file of any NovaTrail repository except `spec`, with the tag T. The check passes only if everything matches:
  - the bundle `<file>.sigstore.json` is a Sigstore v0.3 bundle with one Fulcio certificate. The signature matches the bytes of the file, the certificate the Fulcio chain, and the transparency log entry and the timestamp the Sigstore root of trust;
  - the issuer, Issuer (`1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.8`), is `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`;
  - who signed. The SAN and the Build Signer URI (`…1.9`) are `https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/.github/workflows/release.yml@<S>`, where S is the SHA of a commit, 40 characters, and the Build Signer Digest (`…1.10`) is the same S. S is the commit of a tag `v*` of `.github` no lower than v0.1.7, and it lies on the history of `main` of `.github`. "No lower than v0.1.7" is checked by history, not by the name of the tag: the commit of the release v0.1.7, 0acbf75, lies on the history of S. A branch or a tag instead of a SHA does not pass;
  - by whose call. The Source Repository URI (`…1.12`) is `https://github.com/altnovatrail/<repository>`, and the Source Repository Owner URI (`…1.16`) is `https://github.com/altnovatrail`. The Source Repository Identifier (`…1.15`) and the Owner Identifier (`…1.17`) are the numeric IDs of this repository and of the organization `altnovatrail`, 344507087. The Build Config URI (`…1.18`) is `https://github.com/altnovatrail/<repository>/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main`;
  - on what branch and where. The Source Repository Ref (`…1.14`) is `refs/heads/main`, the Runner Environment (`…1.11`) is `github-hosted`;
  - from what commit. The Source Repository Digest (`…1.13`) and the Build Config Digest (`…1.19`) are the commit of the tag T of the same repository. The shared release signs only the commit of its run, so this is also the commit from which the files are built.

  Not checked are the Build Trigger (`…1.20`) — a release lawfully goes both by `workflow_run` and by the button, `workflow_dispatch` —, the Run Invocation URI (`…1.21`) and the Source Repository Visibility At Signing (`…1.22`): they say nothing about trust. Nor are the deprecated fields `…1.1`–`…1.6` checked: Fulcio still issues them, but has declared them deprecated.
- **A file of `spec`** is signed by the own `release.yml` of `spec`. The same is checked, except the caller and the commit:
  - the SAN, the Build Signer URI and the Build Config URI are `https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main`;
  - the Source Repository URI, the Source Repository Owner URI and both IDs are `spec`; the branch and the environment are the same.

  The Build Signer Digest, the Source Repository Digest and the Build Config Digest are not checked: they name the tip of `main` at the start of the run.

  The Source Repository Digest names the tip of `main` at the start of the run, and `spec` also releases a commit that is no longer the tip. So the file is bound to the tag T by its content:
  - `format-<version>.tar.gz`, `admission-<version>.tar.gz` — the admission table —, `deployment-<version>.tar.gz` — the deployment configuration —, and `legal-<version>.tar.gz`, `consent-age-<version>.tar.gz` and `export-<version>.tar.gz`, each of the last three with an integer version — the commit that `git archive` writes into the archive's header, and `git get-tar-commit-id` reads, is the commit of the tag T;
  - `altnovatrail-spec-<version>.tgz` and `altnovatrail-contracts-<version>.tgz` — the `version` in its `package.json` is T without `v`; `name` there, in both packages, is the one that names the file. `release-verify-npm` takes `@altnovatrail/contracts` from the release of `spec`: a package that comes out in a release not of its own repository is named by `RELEASED_BY` in `tools/release/verify.mjs`.

  A new kind of file of `spec` names its binding in the task that introduces it.
- **The list of releases of `.github`** the check reads from GitHub at the moment of the check, through git, without the REST API and without a token: the tags `v*` by `git ls-remote`, the history of `main` from the same repository. A new release of `.github` is good at once, without a release of `spec` and without a move of the consumers to a tag.
- **The minimum is v0.1.7:**
  - from v0.1.6 on, the shared release requires the caller's submodule `spec` to stand on a tag, and checks the sum of the script of `spec`;
  - from v0.1.7 on, the recipes of `spec` run in a copy of the checkout, and their containers do not change the `.git` that the runner reads.

  Releases below the minimum do not pass. `module-kit` `v0.1.0`, signed by v0.1.4, the rule rejects: nobody takes its CLI template, and the first release of `module-kit` with code will come out on a shared release no lower than the minimum. Only a change of this entry can raise the minimum. It names what to do with the files already released that the new minimum cuts off, and with the cumulative index of `modules`, whose previous index is signed below the new minimum.
- **The condition of the check** is immutable releases and a ruleset of the tags `v*` with the rules `update`, `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`, without bypass; at `spec`, of the tags `contracts/v*` too. They are needed at `.github`, at `spec` and at each releasing repository: a repository turns them on before its first release.
  - Checked 2026-11-01 by the GitHub API. `immutable-releases` is `enabled: true` at `.github`, `spec` and `module-kit`, and their rulesets are 25452244, 25426896 and 25559103. All releases of `.github`, v0.1.0–v0.1.11, are immutable, and the tags v0.1.4–v0.1.11 lie on the history of its `main`. Checked 2026-11-02 by `gh release view`: the releases of `.github` v0.1.12 and v0.1.13 are immutable too, and v0.1.13 is the commit 09443e1 on its `main`; the release `tutor` v0.1.0 is immutable too.
  - The check does not read these settings: it is a standing condition, like the ruleset of the tags of `spec`, and it is checked by the task that changes the settings.
  - The ruleset does not restrict the creation of tags. A tag of `.github` on a commit outside `main` the rule rejects by the history of `main`. A tag of the caller, set by hand on an already released commit, carries the same signature of the same bytes. That only the release sets tags is held by the rule that nobody sets tags by hand, in `spec` and in the shared release of `.github`, not by a setting.
- **The check trusts the tags of `spec` too.** The SHA of the release of `.github` does not pin all the code that ran with the right to sign: the script `spec/tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` comes from the caller's submodule, on a tag of `spec`, which the shared release checks since v0.1.6. The script is NovaTrail's code on an immutable tag, and it is pinned by the caller's commit — the Source Repository Digest —, like an action by SHA. The condition is immutable releases and a ruleset of the tags of `spec`, and `spec` meets it.
- **Where it is checked** — where the file enters NovaTrail. From then on it is held by the digest that whoever checked pinned:
  - CI of `modules` and `canvas` — the CLI binary of `module-kit` from the release, by exact tag and before the first run, not `go install`;
  - CI of `tutor` — the archive of the synthetic data of `canvas`;
  - `app` and `canvas` — npm packages, in CI of the pull request that changes the version in the lock file. The archive from the registry is checked against the bundle of the release file with the same name — these are the same bytes —, and the `integrity` of the lock file against the checked bytes. From then on the version is held by `integrity`;
  - the release of `modules` — the index of the previous release, before the new one is built, in the step of the shared `release.yml` on the runner that gets it, not in the recipe `release-files`;
  - CI of the pull request of `api` that pins a release of `modules` and its index — this index. The pull request is the anchor of trust, and from then on trust goes by the chain of digests: index → inventory → parts → files;
  - code not in Go that takes the format as the file `format-<version>.tar.gz` — on download;
  - the rollout of `infra` — the rule and the recipe for the release files it installs: the deployment of `infra` takes a service's binary and `Dockerfile` from its release and checks them with `release-verify`, and the rollout of the build of `app` checks the archive's signature.
- **One implementation** — the recipe `release-verify`. Everyone takes it by the tag of the submodule `spec/`, like `release-version`:
  - **the tool is sigstore-js** in `tools/`, by the exact versions of `tools/package.json`, which Dependabot raises: `@sigstore/verify`, `@sigstore/bundle`, `@sigstore/tuf` and `@sigstore/protobuf-specs` — on 2026-11-15 `@sigstore/verify` 4.1.3, `@sigstore/bundle` and `@sigstore/tuf` 5.0.1, and `@sigstore/protobuf-specs` 0.5.2. To the other repositories the packages come with `tools/` of the submodule `spec/`, and Node 24.21.0, which they need (`engines` — `^24.15.0`), is in the stage `toolchain` of all thirteen. The recipe reads the certificate's fields from `identity.oids`, which `Verifier.verify` returns for a certificate checked together with the bundle. The licenses — Apache-2.0, MIT, and BlueOak-1.0.0 of `minimatch` — are in the list of allowed licenses, and there are no exceptions;
  - **the timestamp** — at least one RFC 3161 timestamp: by default the check also counts the time of the Rekor entry as a timestamp, and this entry names the timestamp separately. The rest is by Sigstore's default: the certificate's chain to Fulcio and its SCT, a Rekor entry with an inclusion proof, each timestamp and the signature of the bytes, at least one of each;
  - **the root of trust** the recipe reads by TUF from `https://tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev` on each run, into a new cache, from the root that comes with `@sigstore/tuf`. If the network or Sigstore does not answer, the file is rejected: the recipe has neither a former cache nor a copy of the root;
  - **numeric IDs** — the table `tools/release/repositories.mjs`: the organization and thirteen repositories, by `gh api` 2026-11-01. A new repository is entered in it by the task of `spec` that sets it up;
  - **git.** The recipe calls git without the caller's `GIT_*` variables, without its global and system settings, and in an empty folder of its own. Otherwise `insteadOf` would divert the address, and the checkout's `.git/config` carries a token in `http.extraheader`. From the output of `ls-remote` only references with the exact name are taken: the pattern is matched against the end of the name, and a branch `x/refs/tags/v1` would pass for a tag. An annotated tag is unwrapped by the pattern `^{}`. The history of `main` of `.github` is a clone without trees, `--filter=tree:0`, and a commit that is not in it is not fetched (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`);
  - **arguments.** `just release-verify <repository> <tag> <file> [<bundle>]`: the bundle by default is `<file>.sigstore.json`, and paths are from the caller's folder. The npm mode is `just release-verify-npm <lock-file>`, the whole lock file of version 2 or 3. Each package `@altnovatrail/*`, under its own name or under an alias, is taken by `resolved` — the registry's address for this version; any other is rejected. The recipe takes the bundle from the release of the package's repository by its tag and checks the archive as the file `altnovatrail-<repository>-<version>.tgz`, and then `integrity` by the checked bytes. A link to a folder, `link`, is never a release file: the recipe names it and skips it;
  - **the tests** run without the network, on real files with their bundles — `spec` v0.5.6, `LICENSE` of `module-kit` v0.1.0 and `SHA256SUMS` of the release `tutor` v0.1.0 — and on a copy of the root of trust. The check compares the validity periods of the certificates and keys with the bundle's timestamps, not with today, and the copy does not age. `module-kit` v0.1.0 is checked with a minimum that the test sets. `SHA256SUMS` of `tutor` v0.1.0, 93 bytes, was signed by the shared `release.yml` of `.github` v0.1.11, and the release was published 2026-11-01: the test accepts it at the real `MINIMUM`, v0.1.7, and holds it to its repository and tag; live, `just release-verify tutor v0.1.0 SHA256SUMS` answered the same — "signed by the shared release.yml of .github v0.1.11" (2026-11-02).
- **`module-kit`** does not check signatures: its library does not go to the network. It checks a package by the chain of digests from the index that the pull request of `api` pinned.
- **The rerun path of the shared `release.yml`** checks the package archive with the recipe `release-verify` from the caller's submodule `spec`, not with `cosign verify-blob`, from v0.1.13 on, and so checks the SAN by this same rule: only `@<SHA>` of a release of `.github` no lower than the minimum, without branches and tags. `spec`'s own `release.yml` on a rerun calls the same recipe.

— *Why:* the certificates were read 2026-11-01 from the bundles of the files of the releases `module-kit` `v0.1.0` and `spec` v0.5.5.
- **Both the SAN and the caller.** The shared workflow is public. The SAN alone would let through a signature of someone else's call, and the caller's details alone a signature not of the shared workflow. The SAN names `job_workflow_ref`, and the caller's workflow is named by the Build Config URI ([Fulcio, OIDC usage](https://github.com/sigstore/fulcio/blob/a699382/docs/oidc.md) and [OID information](https://github.com/sigstore/fulcio/blob/a699382/docs/oid-info.md), commit a699382, read 2026-10-20). For `module-kit` `v0.1.0`, the bundle `module-kit_v0.1.0_linux_amd64.sigstore.json`:
  - the SAN and the Build Signer URI — `https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/.github/workflows/release.yml@11435dbe61d3d4885c9a8dd30686e8111e26cabb`, that is, the release v0.1.4;
  - the Build Config URI — `https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main`;
  - the Source Repository Digest and the Build Config Digest — 7e0144a, the tag's commit;
  - the Source Repository Ref — `refs/heads/main`, the Source Repository Identifier — 1425817249, the Owner Identifier — 344507087, the Runner Environment — `github-hosted`, the Build Trigger — `workflow_run`.

  For `spec` v0.5.5 the SAN, the Build Signer URI and the Build Config URI are its `release.yml` on `refs/heads/main`, and the Source Repository Identifier is 1424771727.
- **The caller's branch and file.** The trial #33 of `.github` on a pull request signed files, and its entry lies in Rekor in the open: the SAN — `…/release.yml@refs/pull/33/merge`, the Build Config URI — the trial workflow, the Build Trigger — `pull_request`. The rule rejects a signature of a run not on `main` or not from the caller's `release.yml`.
- **Its own parsing of the certificate.** cosign's flags `--certificate-github-workflow-*` compare deprecated fields: `--certificate-github-workflow-sha` — `1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.3`, and `--certificate-github-workflow-ref` — `…1.6` ([cosign v3.1.4, `pkg/cosign/certextensions.go`](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/v3.1.4/pkg/cosign/certextensions.go), read 2026-11-01). And Fulcio writes: "GitHub Workflow specific OID extensions have been deprecated in favor of provider generic extensions starting from 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.8" ([OID information](https://github.com/sigstore/fulcio/blob/a699382/docs/oid-info.md), read 2026-11-01). The Build Config URI and the numeric IDs cannot be compared by flags at all. So they are compared by a parsing of the certificate — the one checked together with the bundle.
- **Numeric IDs.** A repository's address changes with a renaming, and its ID does not: the ID also tells apart a repository created anew under the former name.
- **The release's SHA, not the tag.** The caller pins the shared workflow by SHA, and the SAN ends in `@<sha>`. Any SHA would let through a commit of `.github` that did not come out as a release. A list from GitHub at the moment of the check does not require a release of `spec` for each release of `.github`, and Dependabot raises the pin in the callers by itself.
- **The history of `main`, not the release flag.** Through git the list is read without a token and without the REST API's limit: "The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour", and it is counted by the address the request came from ([GitHub Docs, Rate limits for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api), read 2026-11-01). And the flag of an immutable release would not close the gap of tag creation: a release on a commit of a branch without review is immutable too.
- **The minimum.** The checker need not compare the submodule itself, since the shared release compares it. But only the shared release from v0.1.6 does so, and the runner's `.git` is protected from containers only from v0.1.7.
- **The content of a `spec` file.** The attestation of an immutable release links the bytes with the release, not with the commit: a release created by hand may carry the real bytes of another version. And it needs `gh` with a token, and tokens do not go into the container of the stage `toolchain`.
- **A recipe of `spec`, not of `module-kit`.** A CLI will not check its own binary before it runs, and `canvas`, `tutor` and `app` would install `module-kit` for the sake of one check. A signature also in the library would be a second implementation, and the two would diverge. And `api` does not need the signature at work: the anchor of trust is the pull request that pins the index.
- **Now, by `v0.1.0`.** The signature of a release of `module-kit` with code is built the same way: the same shared `release.yml`, the same fields. The rule and the recipe come out before the repositories move to line 0.6, and each takes them by the same single move.
- **sigstore-js, not cosign.** It comes to every repository with `tools/` of the submodule, and it returns the certificate's fields already parsed. Sources, read 2026-11-01: the npm registry — the packages' versions, licenses and `engines`; the source code of `@sigstore/verify` 4.1.2 (`dist/verifier.js`, `dist/key/index.js`) and of `@sigstore/tuf` 5.0.0 (`dist/index.js`, `dist/client.js`).
- **The IDs in a table of `spec`.** Read from GitHub at the check, a repository created anew under the former name would return its new ID, and without a token the REST API gives 60 requests an hour.

— *Rejected:*
- the SAN only; the caller only;
- cosign's flags only, without the Build Config URI and the numeric IDs;
- cosign in the stage `toolchain` of each repository: an edit of every Dockerfile with a sum for each architecture, its own parsing of DER for the fields, and `--trusted-root` for tests without the network;
- a list of the releases of `.github` in a file of `spec`: each release of `.github` would wait for a release of `spec` and for the consumers' move;
- the immutability of a release of `.github` by the REST API at each check, alone or together with the history of `main`: it needs a token, anonymous requests have a limit, and it does not close the gap of tag creation;
- any release of `.github`, without a minimum;
- the attestation of a GitHub release for `spec`'s files;
- the numeric IDs read from GitHub at the check; the ID as an argument — each consumer would have a copy of its own;
- a package per call of `release-verify-npm`: a new package is easy to miss;
- a signature also in the library `module-kit`; a command of the CLI `module-kit`; a check of its own at each consumer;
- waiting for the first release of `module-kit` with code: the recipe would come out after `modules` moved to line 0.6, and a second move would be needed.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `format/README.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `justfile`; `tools/package.json`; `tools/release/verify.mjs`; `tools/release/repositories.mjs`; `tools/release/test/fixtures/tutor-v0.1.0/`; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; `.github`'s `.github/workflows/release.yml`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## Interface icons

**R78. The icons of the UI packages are one set of the Iconify catalog, Material Symbols, in the style Rounded: outlined, and what is selected — filled. Each UI package takes the set's package `@iconify-json/material-symbols` itself, by exact version, and builds in at build time only its own icons: the device does not call the Iconify API. `canvas`, `skill-map` and `app` build them in by a script on `@iconify/utils` and raise the set together and on purpose, not by Dependabot. The caption beside an icon is always visible and is the button's name, but on the closed list of buttons that show an icon alone. Which icon has which value is said by the table of icon values in `docs/architecture.md`.**
- **The set** — Material Symbols, the prefix `material-symbols`, the author Google, the license Apache-2.0 from the list of allowed licenses. The set is one, without a fallback. A button for a value that the set lacks holds by its caption alone until a change of this entry names an icon; a second set also comes only by a change of this entry. So it is now with the protractor, a tool of the canvas: it is in none of the four candidate sets.
- **The style** — Rounded. A button's icon is the outline, `<base>-outline-rounded`. The selected option of a choice — "Pen" or "Eraser" — and a mode turned on are the same icon with a fill, `<base>-rounded`. The fill does not replace the state: a screen reader is still told it by ARIA — `aria-checked` on "Pen" and "Eraser", `aria-expanded` on "Demo". For line icons — arrows, "Undo" — the outline and the fill are the same.
- **How the icons get into the build:**
  - the set's package `@iconify-json/material-symbols` a UI package takes by exact version. In a package that comes out in npm — `canvas` and `skill-map` — it stands in `devDependencies`: the consumer does not need the set's data, since the icons are already built in. In `app` it stands in `dependencies`, like everything its bundler builds in. The license check sees the set as any dependency, and Dependabot does not raise it: each of the three ignores the package in its `dependabot.yml`;
  - `canvas`, `skill-map` and `app` raise the set's package together and on purpose, and a new version may draw an icon differently. Each raise is a row of COORDINATION.md: `canvas` and `skill-map` come out with the new version, then `app` takes both with its own set at the same version, so that one value looks the same on one screen;
  - the build builds in only the icons that the package takes. By what — the package decides: by a plugin of its bundler, for example unplugin-icons, or by a script on `@iconify/utils`. `canvas`, which only `tsc` builds, `skill-map` and `app` build them in by a script on `@iconify/utils` at build time. `unplugin-icons` with `compiler: 'jsx'` does not suit a UI package on React: it requires `@svgr/core`, and that, through `@babel/core`, pulls `caniuse-lite` under CC-BY-4.0, which is not in the list of allowed licenses. A package does not turn on unplugin-icons' auto-install of sets, `autoInstall`: the set comes from the lock file, not by an import;
  - at run time — not one request to `api.iconify.design` or to another Iconify API. Iconify's components that go there for icons — `@iconify/react`, `iconify-icon` and the like — the packages do not take.
- **The license.** The check of the lock file by `spec`'s list of licenses reads the license of the set's package — `Apache-2.0`, from the list. The set's icons go into the build even when the set's package stands in `devDependencies`. So no exception is written for it in `licenses-check-repo`, not even under `dev`: the boundary `dev` of the license check is for tools that never ship anywhere. If a new version of the set changes the license to one not from the list, the check will reject it, while an exception under `dev` the check would let through: this rule is held by review, not by code. A repository whose deliverable is a bundler's build keeps everything that the bundler builds in in `dependencies`.
- **The notice:**
  - Apache-2.0 requires giving the recipient a copy of the license: "You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License" ([the set's LICENSE](https://github.com/google/material-design-icons/blob/10ecc14/LICENSE), section 4(a)), as for a module's required `LICENSE`. It is carried by the `LICENSE` of the NovaTrail package itself: it is the same text of Apache-2.0, NovaTrail's license. The set has no `NOTICE` file, so there are no notices from it to carry, and there is no copyright line of Google in the license text either;
  - beyond that, the package names the set in its `NOTICE`: Material Symbols, Google, Apache-2.0, the address `google/material-design-icons` and the version of the set's package. The packages `@iconify-json/*` have neither `LICENSE` nor `NOTICE`, and without this line one cannot learn from the build where the icons come from. `NOTICE` goes into the package's npm archive, and in `app` into its build, together with the notices of everything else built into it.
- **Accessibility:**
  - an icon's SVG is with `aria-hidden="true"` and without `<title>`. The button's name is the caption from the package's table of captions;
  - the caption beside an icon is always visible, in each UI package, and the button's name is its text (sources 3.13). The icon stands beside the caption, not instead of it;
  - outside that rule is the closed list of buttons that show an icon alone, which the accessibility standard of the UI packages keeps: such a button shows its icon alone, and its caption from the package's table of captions is its accessible name, in `aria-label`;
  - an icon's color is `currentColor`: in forced colors mode it takes the system color of the button;
  - the translations of captions go by the shared rules of translations of the UI packages.
- **The table of values** — in `docs/architecture.md`:
  - one value is one icon, and one icon is one value, like a term of the glossary. Buttons with one value in different packages look the same, and an icon from the table does not stand on a button with another value;
  - the first rows are the buttons of the row of `canvas` (`src/element/labels.ts` of `canvas`, `main` e90e210): the task screen of `app` shows them. The row "next" names only `canvas`;
  - the button of the lesson player of `app` "Continue", to the next segment, is a value of `app` of its own, not "next" of the table: `app` chooses the icon for it from the set itself, not from those in the table, and records it in its `docs/architecture.md`;
  - the values of `app` in the closed list of buttons with an icon alone — back, close, the previous and the next task (‹ ›), the speaker of voicing, Help and the tutor's button — are values of `app` of its own: it chooses their icons from the set itself, not from those in the table, and records them in its `docs/architecture.md`; so ‹ › do not take `arrow-forward` of the value "next";
  - the five states and the two marks of the skills are in the table: the map of `skill-map` and the module card of `app` show them;
  - a value that a second package needs enters the table as a row «в реестр spec». An icon for a value that only it has a package chooses from the set itself — not from those in the table — and records it in its `docs/architecture.md`. If it already stands at another package for another value, both values enter the table by the same route;
