  - an icon whose direction goes along the line — "Next", "Undo", the hidden "Demo" — is mirrored in a right-to-left line. Which icons are so, the table says.
- **What the entry does not concern:** the pictures of content — these are the module's media files, and their rule is the module format; the icons of widgets — a widget is foreign code in the iframe sandbox.

— *Why:* the set and the style — by their look in the catalog. The sources below were read 2026-11-02.
- **One set.** The set is shared: otherwise one button would look different in `app` and in the canvas, and each package would decide the license and the way of delivery itself.
- **No requests at run time.** "Iconify icon components do not bundle icon data. They load only data for icons used on currently viewed page at run time", "Component requests data for icons from Iconify API", and among the drawbacks — "Requires access to Iconify API, making it unusable for offline applications" ([Iconify, Icons on Demand](https://iconify.design/docs/icon-components/)). A request from the learner's device would give its IP address to a third party that is not among the platform's external services, and an IP address is personal information under COPPA (sources 3.1). The UI packages themselves are not loaded at run time either.
- **Building in without the network.** "Not using any frameworks, but want to automate the build process? Iconify Utils offers easy to use functions that generate SVG", and "All icons in Iconify packages pass very strict validation, so they do not contain any potentially harmful content, such as scripts and external resources" ([Iconify, SVG](https://iconify.design/docs/usage/svg/)). unplugin-icons has "On-demand - Only bundle the icons you really use, while having all the options", and the auto-install is "Option C: Auto Install (Experimental)", by default `autoInstall: false` ([README](https://github.com/unplugin/unplugin-icons/blob/v24.0.0/README.md), tag v24.0.0). The licenses of unplugin-icons 24.0.0 and `@iconify/utils` 3.1.7 are MIT (the npm registry).
- **The set and its license.** `@iconify-json/material-symbols` 1.2.97 of 2026-10-28 has `license` — `Apache-2.0`, and `info.json` names 15,761 icons, the author — Google — and the license. There are nine files in the package, and neither `LICENSE` nor `NOTICE` is among them (the npm registry and jsDelivr). `google/material-design-icons`, commit 10ecc14, has at its root a `LICENSE` with Apache-2.0 and no `NOTICE`, and the README says: "We have made these icons available for you to incorporate into your products under the Apache License Version 2.0" and "We'd love attribution in your app's *about* screen, but it's not required".
- **Coverage.** The set has icons for the canvas tools — the pen `ink-pen`, the eraser `ink-eraser`, the ruler `straighten`, the calculator `calculate`, the keyboard `keyboard`, the microphone `mic` — and for all the buttons of the row of `canvas`, each in all six styles. A protractor is in no candidate — neither in Material Symbols nor in Lucide, Tabler and Phosphor. The catalog's search finds this tool only in small sets: iconoven, iconmind, matita and energy-icons (`api.iconify.design/search?query=protractor`).
- **Each package — itself.** The set's package gives data, not code, and a copy of its own in each package ties nothing. A shared package of icons would require a new repository, and a new icon its release and the consumers' move to a version. The table in `spec` gives the same unity without this.
- **The set's package, not copies of SVG.** Its license is compared by the check of the lock file, and its version is a number in the lock file that a raise changes; neither of them sees copies of SVG.
- **A script in `app` too.** The way of `app` is the same as that of `canvas` and `skill-map`, because `unplugin-icons` with `compiler: 'jsx'` pulls a license not from the list.
- **"Continue" is not "next".** The button to the next segment of the lesson player is "Continue", told apart from the element's "Next", which opens a part of the demo. On the screen of a worked example both buttons are visible at once and do different things, and one icon would confuse the learner.
- **The closed list.** The icons of the list are those whose meaning a learner reads without a word, and a value of one package needs no row of the table; the states become shared when `app` draws them on its card.
- **A raise together.** `skill-map` 0.1.13 and newer build with 1.2.99 and `canvas` 0.3.29 with 1.2.98, so `app` could take only `skill-map` 0.1.12. The set comes out every two or three days, and a Dependabot pull request that raises it fails in `canvas`, whose `icons --check` wants the icons and `NOTICE` written anew. One raise of `canvas` to 1.2.99 closes the gap, and a raise made together keeps the packages from parting again.

— *Rejected:*
- Lucide (ISC), Tabler (MIT) and Phosphor (MIT) — the other candidates; the choice is by look;
- the styles Outlined and Sharp; always the outline; always the fill;
- a main set with a fallback;
- Iconify's components and its API at run time, including an instance of the API of our own;
- SVG copied into the package's repository together with the set's license;
- a shared package `@altnovatrail/icons` — a new repository, a change of the list of repositories and a release of its own;
- an export `./icons` in `@altnovatrail/spec`: the package would stop carrying declarations alone, and a new icon would wait for a release of `spec` and for the packages' move to a tag;
- only the set and the rules, without the table of values: the packages would draw one button with different icons;
- a guard in the code of `licenses-check-repo` that would reject an exception for `@iconify-json/*`: it would close one set of icons, and the general case would stay without a record;
- `unplugin-icons` with `compiler: 'jsx'` in `app`;
- "Continue" with the value "next" and its icon;
- captions beside every icon; a row of the table for each value of `app` in the closed list;
- catching up now without a rule: the packages part again at the next raise;
- a row of COORDINATION.md for each version of the set — one every few days;
- the same paths of the icons instead of the same version: a check of its own in `app`, while the packages raise the set apart.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/concepts.md` — "icon" and "icon set"; `docs/repositories.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `canvas`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s `NOTICE`; `skill-map`'s `NOTICE`; `app`'s `NOTICE`; `app`'s `docs/architecture.md`; the `dependabot.yml` of `canvas`, `skill-map` and `app`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## The template's kind `typescript`

**R79. The template's kind `typescript` carries a stage with browsers for tests, one for each engine CI checks, and the Biome extension. A copy of this kind gets, at the end of the stage `toolchain`, Chrome Headless Shell, WebKit and Firefox from the Playwright image by tag and digest and their system libraries from a snapshot of Ubuntu, and in VS Code the extension `biomejs.biome` and Biome as the default TypeScript formatter.**
- **How it is built:**
  - a kind in `repo-template/kinds.json` is an object with five keys: `extensions` — VS Code extensions; `settings` — VS Code settings; `toolchain` — a file in `repo-template/kinds/` whose lines go at the end of the stage `toolchain` of the Dockerfile, before the heading of the stage `devcontainer` and its `FROM`; `devcontainer` — a folder in `repo-template/kinds/` whose `Dockerfile` lines go into the stage `devcontainer`, before the step of Claude Code, and whose other files the copy gets in `.devcontainer/` as they are; `claudePlugins` — the folders of `claude-plugins/` that `new-repo` names in `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` of `containerEnv` of the copy's devcontainer. The recipe stops at a key it does not know, at a value of the wrong type, at a file outside `kinds/`, at a setting that `spec`'s devcontainer already has, and at a place in `spec`'s devcontainer that it did not find exactly once. A kind written as a list of extensions, as before this entry, the recipe still reads: `just new-repo` builds a copy from the template of the latest tag, and at `v0.6.2` the kind is still a list;
  - the kind `typescript` has `biomejs.biome@3.8.1`, the setting `"[typescript]": { "editor.defaultFormatter": "biomejs.biome" }` and the file `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile`. The kinds `go` and `docs` have no stage `toolchain`; `go` still has the Go extension, and gives gopls in the stage `devcontainer`;
  - the file's lines: Chrome Headless Shell of revision 1254, WebKit of revision 2388 and Firefox of revision 1572 from `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.65.0-noble` by digest `sha256:9beb546099e11f52d62e505537914870e01a67e0e6b00ae41da4775324e73dbe`, each by a `COPY` of its own into `/ms-playwright`; `ENV PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright`; and the system libraries of all three — the lists `chromium`, `webkit` and `firefox` for Ubuntu 24.04 in Playwright's `nativeDeps.ts` at v1.65.0, each package once — with the fonts of its list `tools`, all but `xvfb`, 78 packages from the snapshot `20261021T000000Z`, by the rule of the Ubuntu archive's snapshot. The image's version is that of `playwright` in the copies, 1.65.0, as in `skill-map`. The stage of a copy of the kind `typescript` matches the template's line for line, and only the comments differ;
  - the revisions are what `browsers.json` of the tag v1.65.0 names, and the image holds `/ms-playwright/webkit-2388` and `/ms-playwright/firefox-1572` (measurements 2.1); the revisions 2370 and 1555 of WebKit and Firefox are those of 1.64.1, not of this image. `COPY` takes a folder's contents and not the folder, so each browser has a `COPY` of its own, and the test of `new-repo` holds the three to one image and to their `ARG`s. All 78 packages are in the snapshot for `amd64` and `arm64`, and the stage needs no new one (measurements 2.1). Without the fonts of `tools` WebKit gives inline elements a height of 0 (measurements 2.1);
  - the decisions the file's comments cite, if any, are `spec`'s decisions, and the recipe gives them the suffix `spec`, as in the whole Dockerfile.
- **Who raises the versions.** `spec` raises the image's tag and digest, the three revisions and the snapshot in the template, together and by hand, and a copy gets them by its move to a tag. Dependabot does not see them: the image stands in `COPY --from`, not in a `FROM` line. A repository that needs a new `playwright` sooner raises them all in its Dockerfile — in the pull request that raises the package, as `canvas` does — and writes a row «в реестр spec». Until its move to a tag with the new template, its Dockerfile is no longer the recipe's output, and its decision names this.
- **The browsers' terms.** Chrome Headless Shell is a build of Google Chrome for Testing under Google's free terms. WebKit and Firefox are Playwright's builds (sources 7.7, read 2026-11-13). WebKit "is open source software with portions licensed under the LGPL and BSD licenses": the texts webkit.org gives are LGPL-2.0-or-later and BSD-2-Clause. Its build, the bundle of WebKitGTK with Playwright's patches, holds no license file, and the libraries it bundles are under LGPL-2.0 (libsoup), BSD-3-Clause (libjxl, libbacktrace) and MIT (brotli). Firefox says of its build: "All of the source code to this product is available under licenses which are both free and open source", most of it under the MPL 2.0, and Playwright's agent Juggler in it is under the MPL 2.0 too. Every one of these licenses is approved by OSI. Firefox's list of licenses also names "Disconnect.Me License - Creative Commons BY-NC-SA-4.0", which OSI does not approve and which is not free for everyone; but that is the license of a list of trackers that the build neither carries nor fetches: Playwright's settings turn tracking protection off and point Remote Settings at a dummy. So the three are development and CI tools that never ship, Chrome Headless Shell under free terms and WebKit and Firefox under OSI-approved licenses, and **this entry is the decision that brings them into a copy of the kind `typescript` and names them as exceptions**: Chrome Headless Shell; WebKit under LGPL-2.0-or-later and BSD-2-Clause, with its bundled libraries; Firefox under MPL-2.0 — in the stage of the kind `typescript`, and nowhere that ships. Both bounds of such a tool hold. NovaTrail distributes none of them: the stage `toolchain` is built from the Dockerfile, CI takes its image from the GitHub Actions cache, by a key with the sha256 of `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, and builds it only on a miss, while releases always build it; the cache gives the stage to no one, and it is published nowhere. Where the cache already stands is held by Д146. And the platform is built, run and deployed without them. A repository of the kind `typescript` names the three, citing this entry.
- **What is new against the rejection in the decision on licenses.** It rejected only OSI licenses — tests in WebKit or in Firefox in place of Chromium —, for which the wrapper's contract and the stage of `canvas` would change, as a route nobody had tried. The route has been tried: `app` ran its 331 tests in the browser and the 10 of its built page in WebKit 27.2 and Firefox 157 of Playwright 1.64.1, with their libraries from the same snapshot, by `app`'s measurement, and WebKit showed what Chromium does not — a Blob that IndexedDB of an ephemeral session does not write, `forced-color-adjust` it lacks, and the name of a language with a capital letter, which `app` fixed in code. And the two do not replace Chrome Headless Shell: they stand beside it, the wrapper's contract keeps Chromium, and what was rejected stays rejected. Since the executor runs the checks without the author, the three engines in CI are the check of the engines in place of devices.
- **The default formatter** is the executor's proposal. The formatter setting exists in `canvas` and in the plan of `app` ("the stage `devcontainer` — the extension `biomejs.biome` and the default TypeScript formatter", in `app`'s `docs/architecture.md`). Without it in the template, each repository would again add it by hand.
- **Who gets it.** `canvas`, `app` and `skill-map` take the stage from the recipe by their move to a tag, add projects of Vitest on WebKit and Firefox, and name WebKit and Firefox as they name Chrome Headless Shell; `.github` names the browsers of its wrapper's contract — Д217. The Dockerfile of `canvas` becomes the recipe's output again, and its decision then says that the lines came from the template; `skill-map` drops its difference from the template. `skill-map` gets the stage and Biome by the same route, at its move to a tag. The Dependabot comment, `docs/repositories.md` and the template's README name the three browsers.

— *Why:*
- The stage was put off until "a second repository on TypeScript takes up tests in the browser". `app` is the second: its screens with the element `<novatrail-canvas>` run in Chromium, and the canvas element does not work in DOM emulators. Without a shared stage the same lines — the image, the revisions, the `apt` packages and the snapshot — would live in two copies, and each move to a tag would carry the recipe's edits into the Dockerfile by hand: in `canvas` it was already so. Biome was chosen by both repositories on TypeScript that have a decision on the linter: `canvas` and `app`. The extension's version is the latest stable, 3.8.1 of 2026-10-24: `canvas` has 3.7.1, and `app` in its plan 3.8.1. Later versions in the gallery are pre-releases, with numbers of the form `2026.10.241124` (the VS Code Marketplace gallery API, `extensionquery` for `biomejs.biome`, read 2026-11-02).
- Playwright 1.65.0: without it each copy of the kind `typescript` keeps Dependabot's pull request for `playwright` 1.65.0 red until it raises the image itself: Dependabot reads only `FROM` lines, and this image is not in such a line. Verified 2026-11-11: `https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/playwright/manifests/v1.65.0-noble` answers with an image index with `Docker-Content-Digest` `sha256:9beb5460…`; `packages/playwright-core/browsers.json` at the tag v1.65.0 names for `chromium-headless-shell` `"revision": "1254"`; the list `chromium` for `ubuntu24.04-x64` in `packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/nativeDeps.ts` at the tags v1.64.1 and v1.65.0 is one and the same, 21 packages.
- Three engines: without WebKit and Firefox in the stage an edit of CSP, of storage or of a screen breaks them unnoticed, and nobody checks the engines on devices by hand. One copy of the stage in the template is this entry's own argument against two copies.

— *Cost:*
- The stage with the browsers also goes to a copy that does not test in a browser. With Chrome Headless Shell alone, the step "Toolchain image" of `canvas` took 57–67 seconds in each of five jobs, and without the browser 18. All the required checks of such a copy also depend on MCR and on `snapshot.ubuntu.com`. `skill-map` gets Biome before its decision on the linter; if it chooses another linter, its decision will remove the extension and the setting and name this a difference from the recipe.
- WebKit and Firefox (measurements 2.1): the two folders take 595 MiB, and the packages, 341 instead of 61, about 203 MB to download instead of 50 MB and 729 MB on disk instead of 216 MB. The entry of the image in the GitHub Actions cache grows from 554 MiB to about 0.95 GB, by estimate. `canvas` already fills the cache's "10 GB per repository" with 18 entries of the stage, of `main` and of pull requests, and GitHub then deletes entries "in order of last access date, from oldest to most recent" ([Dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching); sources 6.4); at the new size about ten fit, so the entry of `main` is evicted sooner, and each miss builds the stage anew, longer than before, from MCR and `snapshot.ubuntu.com`. The fonts of `tools` change the default font: `fc-match` names WenQuanYi Zen Hei for `sans-serif`, not Liberation, and Chromium of a copy renders with it too, so a test that measures text may see other numbers at its move to the tag. A copy that starts only Chromium — `skill-map` until it adds projects of WebKit and Firefox, and any copy that does not test in a browser — carries the two browsers unused; whether `skill-map` tests on three engines is its own decision (Д217).

— *Rejected:*
- each repository keeps its own copy of the stage, like `canvas`: two copies and two raises by hand;
- only the Biome extension, and the stage when a third repository takes up the browser: the stage was put off only until the second;
- a shared image with the browser for all repositories: it would have to be published, and NovaTrail does not publish an image with Chrome for Testing;
- waiting with Playwright 1.65.0 until `spec` itself or another copy needs a new `playwright`: `canvas` and `app` have the same kind and the same Dependabot;
- WebKit and Firefox only in `app`, by a difference of its own from the template, as in MathTrail Canvas ([canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/tree/0901af0)): `canvas` has the canvas element and its styles too, and a second copy is what this entry rejects;
- runs in WebKit and Firefox by hand at each move to a tag, as `app` once ran them: the author walks nothing by hand;
- Playwright's fonts without the CJK and emoji fonts, to keep Liberation the default: the list `tools` is what Playwright's own image and `install-deps` give, and a shorter one is a route of our own nobody has tried.

— *Consequence:* `repo-template/kinds.json`; `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile`; `tools/new-repo/devcontainer.mjs`, its functions `readKind` and `editDevcontainer`, and the test of `new-repo` in `just new-repo-test`; `repo-template/README.md`; `.github/dependabot.yml`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `docs/measurements.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s, `app`'s and `skill-map`'s `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; `canvas`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `.github`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## The learner model on the server

**R80. The learner model lives in the platform's database — the database of `api`. What is stored is an append-only log of evidence, and it is the source of truth, while the skills' state is a cache marked with the version of `learner-model`, the pinned release of `modules` and the window of format versions of `api`. `api` gives `learner-model` the log and the graphs, and `learner-model` transfers progress by `retired_skills`. The engine choice also stores the release of `modules` and the number of the log's last evidence by which it was made.** `api`'s own `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/architecture.md` hold the details.
- **Where the model lives** — in the database of `api`. Several devices and several learners of the account and a subscription work with it, and the engine computes on the server, as Т-10 recommends. The export is in an open format, the normative part `export/`: a ZIP of the manifest of `app`, `api.zip` and the files of the device, and from version 3 also the stored works as files of their own.
- **What is stored:**
  - evidence — one per finished attempt, with three exceptions that give none: an attempt of a task with a rubric, in the first slice (О-17); an attempt that the learner left or abandoned, if there were no wrong answers in it; and an attempt of a lesson that the end of its run "not suitable" closed, if there were no wrong answers in it. With wrong answers the outcome of the last two is "left unfinished". The attempt itself remains a row with a close reason, and an adult sees it in the progress. A run ends "not suitable" when the lesson or its task stopped suiting the profile, and its open attempt is closed with the same reason. What is in evidence and how much it weighs is decided by `learner-model`, and `api` stores it as it is; whether the weight needs the fact "a segment of a lesson" — the attempt knows its run and the segment place — is decided by `learner-model` too;
  - the log is only appended to. The recomputation cuts off evidence on a version that the module index marked `wrong_key`, and the rows remain. The log is deleted only whole — with the profile or by the time limit;
  - the skills' state is a cache marked with the version of `learner-model`, the pinned release of `modules` and the window of format versions of `api`. It is recomputed from the log when any of the three changes or a version is withdrawn because of `wrong_key`. New evidence is appended to the cache without recomputing the whole log.
- **The condition for `learner-model`** is one: the state appended by new evidence matches the one recomputed from the log. If it does not match, the cache is recomputed whole. If `learner-model`'s design of the model decides otherwise, the question of what is stored returns.
- **The boundary of the transfer of progress** between `api` and `learner-model`. `api` cuts off the evidence of `wrong_key` and gives the profile's log and the graphs of the current versions of the log's modules with `retired_skills`, in the types of `learner-model`, which sets the graph's types, and `learner-model` does the transfer. Beside the appending condition, the transfer holds these conditions:
  - a module's skill that is neither in `skills` nor in `retired_skills` of the current version goes to no skill, without an error;
  - an anchor skill `core.<name>` goes as it is if the vocabulary of some format version in the window of `api` knows it, and otherwise to no skill; the trap's skills, if the evidence carries them, go by the same rules;
  - in the cache there is only what the log, the graphs of the log's modules and the version of `learner-model` set. The starting point of skills without evidence and the mastery of an anchor skill by the learner's module skills `learner-model` computes on reading, without writing to the cache;
  - evidence carries everything the recomputation reads — the task's band and difficulty, the number of options, the key's provenance, the trap's skills — and the recomputation opens no packages of former versions: with a change of the window they leave the image;
  - a snapshot of the state, if there is one, is valid only under the same mark of the cache, and the transfer does not apply to it.
- **The engine choice** stores what `docs/architecture.md` names for it, its time among them, and also the release of `modules` and the number of the log's last evidence. Without them a repetition from the log does not know which prefix of the log to take and which withdrawal marks were in force then.

— *Why:*
- A change of algorithm recomputes the state from the log rather than carrying over the old one. The engine choice is repeated from the log, and by it too the model is recomputed without the evidence of `wrong_key`. The cache is needed so that the engine choice after each attempt does not recompute the whole log.
- The window in the mark: the window moves even with the same release of `modules` — with a new version of `api` —, and the current versions of the log's modules, their graphs and the transfer by `retired_skills` depend on the release and the window. Without the window the mark would not change, while the graphs under it would, and the appended state would silently diverge from the recomputed one.
- A lesson's attempt closed "not suitable" is, for evidence, like a left one, and not "unchecked": if `learner-model` gave it zero weight, the wrong answers before the end of the lesson would be lost — the same argument as for leaving.

— *Rejected:*
- a family's file — for example, in Google Drive, as in standalone. There the file was the truth, but writes went without a condition — "Whoever uploads last wins, silently" — and an emptied Drive trash erased a profile without a copy ([`docs/architecture/05-storage.md` of standalone@42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/42b4408/docs/architecture/05-storage.md));
- the device: the engine computes on the server (Т-10), and each device would have a model of its own;
- deciding now only where the model lives, and what is stored after `learner-model` designs the model: the condition for `learner-model` is one, and with another design the question returns anyway;
- leaving the boundary of the transfer to `learner-model`'s design, with `api` adjusting: `api` builds the log and the graphs earlier, in its own tasks, and without a boundary the recomputation might need packages of former versions that are no longer in the image;
- `api` does the transfer, translating the IDs in the evidence: the skills' IDs are part of the evidence type, and the type is set by `learner-model`, while `api` stores it as it is;
- the window as a detail of `api`, with the mark named without it: the mark would diverge from this entry's own transfer, where an anchor skill goes by the vocabulary of a format version in the window of `api`.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `api`'s `docs/architecture.md`.

## The inbox of `spec`

**R81. The session of `spec` finds the rows «в реестр spec» of the other repositories itself: the recipe `just inbox` reads on GitHub table 3 of each, its `run/QUESTIONS.md`, and compares it with table 5 of `spec`, `run/INBOX.md` — which rows are already recorded and where, and which recorded ones have changed since, by a fingerprint. It runs, with its triage, on the author's word or once every task of the current epic is done, not before each task. A row counts as arrived when it is on `main` of its repository, while the rows of open pull requests are "on the way", and they are recorded only on the author's word. There is no new channel, and the author no longer carries rows. The recipe also names the monthly measurement of tokens and the quarterly check of Claude Code's changelog once they are due.**
- **How it works.**
  - A repository's session writes a row as it did — into table 3 of its plan, `run/QUESTIONS.md` — and its question opens with the mark «В реестр spec», by the shared rule of `RULES.md` on what a repository has for `spec`. The recipe recognizes the mark regardless of case and only at the start of the question: the same words further in the text are not the mark.
  - `just inbox` reads through `gh` the `run/QUESTIONS.md` of each repository from `tools/release/repositories.mjs` except `spec`: on the commit of `main` and in each open pull request that changes the file. It reads table 3 of a repository under its heading «Table 3.» alone, and table 5 of `spec` under «Table 5.»; the mark stays «в реестр spec». It prints four lists: new rows on `main`; "on the way" — rows that a pull request adds to its base; rows of table 5 that the source no longer carries — they may leave it; rows of table 5 whose rows on `main` of the source have changed since they were recorded.
  - `main` without `run/QUESTIONS.md` is a repository that cannot be read; a pull request that leaves the file alone adds no rows; one whose merge base has no such file is a problem — what it adds cannot be told, and it is to be rebased.
  - The session of `spec` triages the rows the recipe prints by the rules at the start of `run/INBOX.md`: what the author has already decided it records, and the rest it brings to the author with options and a recommendation. A recorded row goes into table 5.
  - **When.** `just inbox` and the triage run only on the author's word — «Разбери входящие» — or once every task of the current epic in table 1 of RUN.md is done, before the next epic is chosen; not before each task. A row «в реестр spec» therefore waits on `main` of its repository until the next triage; what a task of `spec` needs from another repository sooner, the author asks for.
  - The answer reaches the repository, as before, with its move to a tag (the «Д» rows of table 4).
  - What is not a question needs no route of its own: what a repository took by a move to a tag is seen by its submodule, and its tasks by its RUN.md.
- **The fingerprint** is the first 12 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the rows of the source's table 3 in the order of their numbers: a row's cells, each with its whitespace collapsed, joined by " | ", and the rows joined by a line break (`fingerprintOf` in `tools/inbox/inbox.mjs`). It is of the cells alone: an edit of any word of a row — the question, the options, the recommendation — changes it, while the row's place in the file, the file it stands in and Markdown marks do not. The fingerprint is one per row of table 5, not per number: a row of table 5 names several rows of the source, and the column stays short.
- **A changed row** is a row of table 5 at least one of whose rows is on `main` while their fingerprint is not the one recorded, or is not recorded at all, "—"; the recipe prints it with the new fingerprint and the place of the rows at the source. The session rereads them, records what was added as a new row, and puts the fingerprint into table 5. When some of the rows have left the source, the fingerprint of the remaining ones is different too, and the recipe names the row both among the changed and among the gone. A changed row is not an error, and the recipe ends with code 0; a fingerprint that is not 12 hexadecimal digits is an error of table 5, like an unread row. The rows "on the way" have no fingerprint: they go into table 5 only on the author's word.
- **What is due.** `just inbox` also prints, as lines `due: …`, the monthly measurement of the sessions' tokens and the quarterly check of Claude Code's changelog, once the date of the line `Next measurement: by …` or `Next check of Claude Code's changelog: by …` of measurements 1.9 has come; a missing or doubled line is a problem, exit 1. It reads the working tree, not GitHub.
- **The first run**, 2026-11-02. 12 repositories were read: 40 rows on `main`, 0 on the way. 29 of them had been recorded, and they went into table 5 — by the «Д» rows and the start of table 3. There were 11 new: four of `api`, six of `app` and one of `canvas`. While the task ran, one more came to `main` of `.github`, and the next run found it. The errors of the trials that the recipe no longer makes:
  - without the condition "at the start of the question" it took a row of `module-kit` — a question about the order of its tasks, where «в реестр spec» stands in the recommendation;
  - without comparison with the pull request's base — 38 rows from old branches of Dependabot, recorded long ago. The base is the common ancestor of the branch with `main`, not the pull request's `base.sha`: otherwise an old branch would bring back rows that `main` has closed since;
  - a row recorded from a pull request on the author's word it does not name as gone while the pull request is open; a failure of one repository or pull request does not stop the run, and it reads the lists page by page.
- **The first fingerprints** were taken 2026-11-04 from `main` of the sources. Since the commits at which `spec` recorded the rows, three rows of `api`, one of `module-kit` and two of `modules` had changed, and the same day they were compared: there were no new requests to `spec` in them.

The edit of `RULES.md` reaches the other repositories with their move to a tag, but the recipe does not wait for it.

— *Why:*
- The rows already lie in the tables 3 of the other repositories, where `RULES.md` has every repository write what it has for `spec`, and the coordinator of the cross-repository plan already reads their plans on GitHub: all that was missing was that the session of `spec` read them itself. Nothing changes for the other repositories — neither their plan's rule that a session acts outside its repository, `spec` included, only after a warning and the author's confirmation, nor the order of their move to a tag — and the recipe works at once, on any tag of theirs. The record is one, in the repository's file, as the rule that a project's context lives in the repository's files requires. A row on `main` the author has already reviewed, while before the merge it may change, so the rows of pull requests are only "on the way".
- The fingerprint: comparing rows only by their numbers, the recipe did not see additions to recorded ones — additions of `api` to four of its recorded rows and an edit of a row of `modules` went through, and only the third inbox triage of 2026-11-02 found them, by reading the rows whole.
- The lines `due: …`: the recipe already runs at each triage.
- `run/QUESTIONS.md` and «Table 3.» alone: every other repository keeps the plan's tables in `run/` and in English, and a merge base with no file would hide what a pull request adds.

— *Rejected:*
- issues in `spec` that the sessions of other repositories open: the rule would reach them only with a move to a tag, the row's text would live in two places, their plan's rule that a session acts outside its repository only after a warning and the author's confirmation would need an exception, and issues are public. The inbox would be only the issues of the author's account, and the author's answer by that account cannot be told apart from a session's record;
- Discussions in `spec`: the same, and the `gh` commands for them in version 2.101 are in preview, and a pull request does not close a discussion;
- messages between sessions of Claude Code: two sessions are needed at once, a message is not kept and does not get into files, and an exchange between different devcontainers is not verified. On 2026-11-02 `ListAgents` did not see other sessions;
- an inbox file in `spec` that the other repositories add to by pull requests: a session would change `spec` not from within it, which `RULES.md` forbids;
- only `main`, without the rows of pull requests: the author would wait for the merge where the answer can be prepared earlier, as with two rows of `.github`;
- `main` and pull requests on an equal footing: a row recorded from a branch could diverge from the one that gets merged;
- a rule in `RULES.md` and in the template of RUN.md that an addition to a recorded row goes as a new row with its own number — it would be held by hand in twelve repositories, while the recipe sees the edit itself; changing nothing — the triage would reread each recorded row whole at each run;
- the triage before each task;
- a merge base with no `run/QUESTIONS.md` counting as no rows — a row `main` closed since would come back as new.

— *Consequence:* `tools/inbox/` and its tests; `justfile`; `RUN.md`; `run/INBOX.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `RULES.md`; `repo-template/files/RUN.md`; `repo-template/files/run/QUESTIONS.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## Showing the solution and a hint on request

**R82. No task shows its solution by a button: there is no "Show the solution", on a task of a module or on a task from paper, at any rung and for every age category. A grown-up gets the solution only by asking the tutor in grown-up mode, behind the PIN. "Hint" before the first wrong answer gives "givens and unknown", the task's technique and its leading question, and on a task from paper the first rung of the ladder that its Check gives, by the same call on the work as it stands; after it the words of the current rung once more, without AI; "explain differently" gives the same rung in other words, one AI call per rung, without the work. An attempt left or abandoned with wrong answers has the outcome "left unfinished".** On a task from paper the words come with the Check: its one call gives the tutor's words, a ladder of 2 or 3 rungs and the place of the first mistake, with no second call; "explain differently" is a call of its own, by the model's hidden solution, and every call goes by the cascade of models of a task from paper. `api`'s side is detailed in its `docs/architecture.md` and its `docs/decisions.md`.
- **The ladder:**
  - a wrong answer is a submission in which at least one answer slot got "not yet". "Unreadable" and "unchecked" give no rung: they are not the learner's mistake;
  - the k-th wrong answer gives rung k while k is at most three, whether the tutor's panel is open or not. From the fourth there is no new rung and no AI call for a rung's words: the words of rung 3 stay, and Hint and "explain differently" work as below. To a child the program offers to call an adult, and to an adult learner nothing more. "Call an adult" is the interface of `app`: `api` notifies no one. Whether a child who solves with the panel closed has passed the ladder is О-26;
  - the rung's answer slot is the first "not yet" slot in order in the submission that gave the rung — items by place, slots by order in the item —, chosen by the program; the rung's words, "explain differently" and the fallback text speak of it. From the fourth wrong answer it stays rung 3's;
  - the ladder is per task, not per item: four submissions with a mistake end the ladder of a task of several items whole.
- **No showing.** The key and the task's solution go to the device only once the attempt is closed by a correct answer or by "Done"; a left, an abandoned and an "unchecked" attempt give no key, and the model's hidden solution and answer of a task from paper never go to it. The request `ShowSolution`, the close reason "solution shown" and the profile's setting "ask before showing" stay in the contract, unused: no attempt closes so.
- **Grown-up mode** is no rung: the grown-up asks the tutor, behind the PIN, and the solution it writes on the sheet is the drawing's own, made at that request; the attempt stays open, its outcome does not change, and on a task of a module an attempt it acted on gives no evidence.
- **A hint on request** sends no work, and the rung grows only with wrong answers:
  - before the first wrong answer — "givens and unknown", which `app` shows from the task's open view, and the task's technique and its leading question, when it has one, which `api` gives; without AI. The leading question is no rung and changes no fallback text;
  - before the first wrong answer on a task from paper, which has no module and so none of the three — the first rung of a ladder: Hint before the first Check sends the work as it stands, by the Check's call, and shows the ladder's first rung, with no verdict and no wrong answer counted; with nothing written the model answers `no_answer` and gives the ladder from the statement alone. The attempt keeps the ladder, and Hint gives its rung again without AI. A rung that names the model's hidden answer, or none that comes, gives the platform's opening question, "What do you already know here, and what do you need to find?", in the language of the interface, which is kept nowhere. It is no rung of the attempt, and "explain differently" is not offered on it;
  - after a wrong answer — the current rung's words that the attempt keeps, without AI, or the rung's fallback text when there are none. Words not asked because the tutor's panel was closed are asked once, by AI and with the work, when "Hint" opens the panel; on a task from paper they came with the Check, and none is asked later;
  - the rung's words on a task from paper are rung k of the ladder that the latest Check gave, its last when it has fewer, its first after a Check with none counted, without AI, in the language of the screens `app` shows; the rung's task is the first "not yet" slot, as above. Their fallback text, which no module gives, is the platform's template of the rung, in English and Russian. "Explain differently" on a task from paper, `hint`, gets the task's crop as printed, the rung, the model's hidden solution and answer that `api` keeps and the questions before, without the work. Every call of a task from paper that gives words — the Check and "explain differently" — is the cascade of the calls of a task from paper, Haiku, Sonnet and Opus of one provider in turn, admitted at the rung "author", the author's word, until 2027-01-17;
  - on a task with a rubric, an essay, which has no wrong answers and no ladder — what it gives before the first wrong answer: the techniques and the leading question, without AI and without the work. A task that names neither gets the empty answer, and `app` says there is nothing to hint; the button stays, since the techniques are closed and the device does not know them before it asks;
  - "explain differently" — the same rung in other words: one AI call per rung, within the quota; the model gets what it gets for the rung's words, except the work. Words that did not come or did not pass the leak check and the form check become the rung's fallback text. In the mode without AI (О-5) it is not offered;
  - every call for the attempt's words, of a rung and of "differently", gets the previous questions of the task, so as not to repeat them;
  - a hint exists from the start of the task.
- **"Show where"** is the profile's hint mode. With it on, after "Not yet" on a task from paper the tutor's mark is a wavy line under the place of the first mistake, drawn from its box on the picture of the work, which the Check gave; with "Questions only", and with a fallback text, the words alone. The line stands beside the words in the tutor's panel, and goes with other work, the tracing paper moved, or another Check. A task of a module keeps its frame in either mode.
- **Evidence** is the facts of the attempt, not the model's conclusions; what it carries is `learner-model`'s, and an attempt of a task from paper gives none, nor one of a task of a module that grown-up mode acted on, its verdict still shown. The outcome goes by the wrong answers; the request and "explain differently" do not change it. "Left unfinished" is the outcome of an attempt the learner left by beginning another, or abandoned, with wrong answers; without them it gives no evidence. Beyond the outcome the evidence carries:
  - the traps the program found by the trap values, not the candidate traps of reading;
  - for each item, those correct to the end too: whether it was submitted, the reasons of its submissions without a verdict, the first verdict and the number of wrong answers before the submission that gave it, the verdict at the end and the number of wrong answers before the first "correct";
  - the task's technique on request, and the leading question on request in its own field of the schema of `learner-model`, apart from the technique;
  - how many times the learner asked "explain differently";
  - whether the solution of this task went to the profile's device earlier, after a correct answer. A template has no such fact: a new attempt gives new numbers. The solution of a task with a rubric, open after "Done", is a sample, not a key: it counts neither here nor in the summary of issues;
  - everything else the model reads, and not the lesson's segment.

  That the learner saw "givens and unknown" is not recorded. The weights of the outcome and of each fact are `learner-model`'s.
- **The engine** does not give as the next task a task with a key — not a template — whose solution has gone to the learner's device; how long after it may, `engine` decides, and a task with a rubric it reads by its own rule.

— *Why:*
- the recommendations of `api`, which repeat that of the product's question on a hint on request;
- no showing: the author's word — one canvas of solving, whose tutor never gives the learner the answer; a grown-up who wants the solution asks for it in grown-up mode, on the sheet where the child works, and that attempt counts for nothing;
- the fourth wrong answer, as in MathTrail Canvas, where the ladder came from: there the analysis went on for at most three wrong answers ([canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/tree/0901af0)), and from the fourth `app` offers a child an adult's help. So the child first tries the simpler case of rung 3;
- "differently" once per rung and without the work: at most three calls per attempt beyond the rungs' words, and of what is kept `docs/privacy.md` lets only the previous questions go to the AI;
- "left unfinished", not "not solved": a task left is not a task judged unsolved, and one term means one thing. Leaving without wrong answers does not move the model, like a skip in mathtrail-standalone, where punishing a skip punished an accidental tap ([standalone@42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/tree/42b4408));
- the evidence holds facts, not conclusions: "the item is blank" or "not solved" would be read by one version of the weight rule, submissions, verdicts and wrong answers by the next too. Without the first verdicts the model would not tell a page nine items of ten correct at the first submission from one correct only after hints. `api`'s attempt stores the verdicts, traps and wrong answers anyway: no new data of the learner. The lesson's segment changes no weight and has no reader;
- the technique on request, by `GetHint`; `BeginStep`, which gave it at a solving step, stays in the contract, unused. The learner sees the solution after a correct answer too, so the fact covers both. "Givens and unknown" are open, since they do not hint at the way: a record would say nothing;
- the leading question suggests the way, so it is closed and recorded. Its own field: the log of evidence is append-only, and a question in the technique's field would mix two facts for good, beyond recomputation;
- "Hint" on an essay: no new AI call and no new data; an essay is helped by the technique — the plan of a text from the module's author —, and the rubric's feedback comes after the submission anyway;
- a sample, not a key: the learner saw no key that a repeat would give away;
- a task from paper: the model's hidden solution never leaves the server, and the learner solves it themselves; the wavy line shows where without touching the learner's strokes. Its hints are the Check's: a page has no author's question, one question of the program for every task says little, and a ladder that comes with the verdict needs no second call to read the work again; kept, so Hint again costs nothing. The hidden answer guards them as a key guards a rung's words — a guard, not a proof, as the leak check of a module's hints is.

— *Rejected:*
- "Show the solution" by a button on a task of a module — to an adult learner from the start of the attempt, to a child from the fourth wrong answer behind an adult's setting "ask before showing", closing the attempt as "solution shown" —, or on a task from paper by the model's hidden solution: the author's word, one canvas whose tutor never gives the answer, and grown-up mode gives a grown-up the solution on the sheet;
- "skipped, the rating does not change", as the prototype: a skip with wrong answers is "left unfinished", without them no evidence;
- every request raising the rung, as the analysis of the product's question on a hint on request had it: the learner would reach the solution without trying;
- "explain differently" without a limit and with the work of the last submission: the quota would go on presses, and the device would keep the work to send again;
- deciding the hint on request after a measurement of "differently" in `tutor`: that is an eval of the hint, not a condition of the decision;
- a left or abandoned attempt "unchecked", like an attempt `api` closes as "unchecked": if `learner-model` weighs "unchecked" zero, the wrong answers before leaving are lost to the model;
- leaving without wrong answers as "left unfinished" too: mathtrail-standalone rejected the same ([standalone@42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/tree/42b4408));
- recording that the learner saw "givens and unknown", or that they asked "Hint" before the first wrong answer: the first says nothing of the way, the second has no reader until `learner-model` asks for it;
- the model's conclusions in the evidence, "which items were blank" or "not solved", instead of "whether the item was submitted"; the lesson's segment in the evidence;
- the leading question in the technique's field; a field of it in a contract of `spec`: the evidence is no contract of `spec`;
- on an essay, no "Hint", only "Done"; the tutor's question by the rubric's criteria — an AI call with the work, a new capability and its eval set; no button where the task names no technique — a new open field of the format or the contract to say whether a hint exists;
- a day's pause of the engine after "Done" with a solution;
- before the first wrong answer on a task from paper, a question of the program without AI, alike for every task, and an empty answer, "nothing to hint"; the words of a task from paper by Opus 5.5 · `high` alone, as the hint of a module, or by Haiku alone; on a task from paper, the words of each rung and the place of the mistake by a call of their own after the Check, as on a task of a module — a second call that reads the work again;
- the wavy line in the mode "Questions only", or kept across other work, whose strokes it may no longer underline.

— *Consequence:* `docs/product.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `format/README.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `tutor`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## Contracts: protobuf, buf and Connect

**R83. `spec`'s contracts are proto3 files in `contracts/`, packages `novatrail.<part>.v1`, by buf's rules `STANDARD`, `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC` and with the compatibility `FILE` against the previous release of `spec`. A field's name in JSON is its proto name, snake_case. A contract's version is the package's suffix and the tag of `spec`, and a breaking change — of the wire, of JSON or of the meaning — is a new package and a new line of `spec`. The code from the contracts is generated by `spec` and comes out in its releases from line 0.7: in Go, the nested module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts`, tagged `contracts/<tag>`, in TypeScript, the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`, which the release publishes to npm. `app` and `api` talk over Connect, binary protobuf on the wire.**
- **Layout.**
  - The folder `contracts/` at the root of `spec`, as `format/`. The normative text is `contracts/README.md`, in English, as are the comments in the `.proto` files.
  - A file is `contracts/novatrail/<part>/v1/<name>.proto`, its package `novatrail.<part>.v1`: the path from `contracts/` repeats the package's name, as buf's rule `PACKAGE_DIRECTORY_MATCH` requires. The prefix `novatrail` makes the packages' names unique in the world, and the Go FAQ requires that of every declaration that gets into a Go binary.
  - `buf.yaml` of version 2 is at the root of `spec`, with one module, `contracts`, and without `deps`: buf takes dependencies only from the Buf Schema Registry, and the build must not depend on a service outside the repository.
  - A package whose rules a program executes has test vectors, `contracts/vectors/<part>/vN/<case>.json`. A package may have examples too, `contracts/examples/<part>/vN/<case>.json`: messages of the package, written in the package's JSON, which the check holds to the package's rules. `novatrail.eval.v1`, the eval protocol, has both, and the runner's report is a file of its own in it, `report.proto`. In a package whose examples show more than one message, the case names the message: in `novatrail.eval.v1` an example `report-<case>.json` is a runner's report, the others are sample files.
  - `contracts-check` knows the vectors, the examples, `contracts/vectors.go` and its test in the layout. A vector of a package that does not exist, or whose vectors the check does not run, is an error, and so is an example of a package that does not exist, or whose examples the check does not read; so is the package `novatrail.eval.v1` without vectors, without examples, or without examples of both a report and a sample file. A file in `contracts/` that the recipe does not know is an error, as in `format-check`.
  - Each service of `novatrail.api.v1`, the contract `app` ↔ `api`, is in a file of its own, and buf's code of the services is `novatrail/api/v1/apiv1connect/`. The package has no vectors: its rules are what `app` and `api` do. The files of a package's device part are no method: [contracts/README.md](../contracts/README.md) writes the form of their path and the answers, because `.proto` does not express them.
- **buf's rules.**
  - `buf lint`: the categories `STANDARD`, `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC`, without `except` and with `disallow_comment_ignores: true`, so a comment in a file does not lift a rule. `COMMENTS` requires a comment on every element, as the format's schemas require a `description` on every property. `UNARY_RPC` forbids streams: the tutor's words come whole, and there is no real-time channel in the first slice (Т-25). The rule `PROTOVALIDATE` is empty: protovalidate's constraints need the module `buf.validate` from the BSR, and the contracts do not take them.
  - `buf breaking`: the category `FILE`, against the previous release of `spec` by its git tag — the newest tag `v*` in the history of HEAD other than the tag of HEAD itself. When the working tree changes `buf.yaml` or `contracts/`, what it will commit comes after HEAD, and the tag of HEAD itself may be the previous release: the recipe sees the changes by `git status --porcelain -- buf.yaml contracts`, together with the files git does not know yet (`previousRelease` in `tools/contracts/buf.mjs`). In CI this changes nothing: the commit of a pull request carries no tag, and its working tree is not changed. The recipe lays out the release's `buf.yaml` and `contracts/` with `git archive` into a temporary folder, and buf compares against it. A previous release without `.proto`, as for the first release with a package, gives nothing to compare with, and the recipe refuses a shallow clone, as `release-version` does. The history of `spec` holds every release, and only `release.yml` sets a tag.
  - **Beyond buf** the recipe holds what [contracts/README.md](../contracts/README.md) requires and buf lets through: `syntax = "proto3"`, without editions and proto2; not one `json_name`: the source info of buf's image names it even when the name matches the default one; not one unsigned type; the prefix `novatrail.` and the path `contracts/novatrail/<part>/vN/<name>.proto`, where N is from 1, without `alpha` and `beta`; `buf.yaml` exactly as above, and `buf.gen.yaml` with local plugins, output into `contracts/`, without `inputs` and `clean`. While `buf.yaml` or `buf.gen.yaml` break this entry, buf is not run: it could go to a service outside the repository. Without a `.proto` the recipe does not call buf, and its tests try buf itself, on trial `.proto` files. `optional` where "none" and zero differ, and `int64` only above 2³¹ − 1, are rules of meaning, and review holds them.
  - A method's idempotency level is decided before its service's first release: the rule `RPC_SAME_IDEMPOTENCY_LEVEL` catches a change of the level. The four methods of `PackageService` have the level `NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`: `app` takes the open views by the package digest with Connect GET, without a token and headers. No method of `AttemptService`, `AccountService`, `ModuleService`, `LearningService` or `ProgressService` has it: they have the default level.
- **The recipes.** `just contracts-check` checks, `just contracts` writes buf's code beside the files, `just contracts-check-test` runs the tests of the check, as `types` and `types-check` do.
- **Fields.**
  - Names are the glossary's terms in English, in snake_case, and a repeated field is in the plural (protobuf's style).
  - Integer places and crops are `int32`: an `int64` is a string in JSON and a `bigint` in TypeScript. There are no unsigned ones. `int64` is only for a value that can be greater than 2³¹ − 1, the greatest `int32`.
  - An enum's zero value is `<NAME>_UNSPECIFIED`, and it has no meaning. A field and an enum value are not removed from a package (version, below): what is not needed stays, with a comment saying so, and the next major package does not take it.
  - The values and IDs of the module format — `handwriting_sheet`, a task's ID — stay `string`, not a proto enum: otherwise one value would have two spellings.
  - `optional` is on a simple field where "none" and zero differ, as absence differs from a zero value in the format's types. "One of" is `oneof`. PNG is `bytes`, and in JSON it is a base64 string. Time is `google.protobuf.Timestamp`, in JSON an RFC 3339 string.
  - The format's open view, a JSON Schema value, goes as the message `OpenView`: the bytes of the format's JSON with `module_format_version` beside them, as the solution of a task goes in the contract `app` ↔ `api`.
  - The enum of the engine's reason codes, `ReasonCode`, lies in `cause.proto`, beside the engine choice, although only the progress, `progress.proto`, carries it: if `EngineChoice` needs a code field too, the enum will not have to be moved, and `buf breaking` of the category `FILE` counts a move between files as a removal. The engine choice and the run's end lie in `cause.proto`: the refusal's data carry them, and a file that imports `cause.proto` cannot itself be imported by `cause.proto`.
- **Names in JSON.** A field's name in JSON is its proto name, snake_case, as in the module format.
  - A JSON writer — of a sample file, of a file of `spec`, of the Connect codec — turns on `UseProtoNames` in Go (`protojson`) or `useProtoFieldName` in TypeScript (protobuf-es).
  - The option `json_name` is forbidden in the contracts. A reader accepts both spellings, as ProtoJSON requires.
- **Syntax** is `syntax = "proto3"`, and simple fields where presence matters are `optional`. The Go code is the Open API, the default for proto3. Moving to editions is possible later, by a decision of its own: the wire and JSON do not change by it.
- **Version.**
  - A contract has no MAJOR.MINOR version of its own. The version is the package's suffix, `v1`, and the tag of `spec` in which the file came out. buf's rule `PACKAGE_VERSION_SUFFIX` does not let a package `v0` through.
  - Within a package a change only adds, and `buf breaking` `FILE` holds this. Such a change comes out in any release of the line.
  - A change of a contract's meaning breaks the package even though buf does not see it: another meaning of a field or of an enum value, another rule by which a part of the platform reads a message — whatever gives another result on the same message. `buf breaking` sees only the wire and JSON, so review holds this. A new enum value or a new field that does not change the meaning of the former ones is an addition.
  - A breaking change is a new package, `v2`, beside `v1`. A package `vN` with N from 2, beside `v(N−1)`, opens a new line of `spec`, as a new version of the format does, and `release-version` refuses a new major package without a new line (`tools/release/contracts-line.mjs`). The first package `v1` of a new part does not open a line.
  - `api` keeps two major packages, the current and the previous, as the platform reads the format's current and previous major version, and `app` reads the package of its build. Within a major package an old build of `app` works with a new `api`: both sides of Connect skip unknown fields, and a new enum value reaches it as a number on the binary wire (the transport, below).
- **The Go code** is the nested module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts`, with its own `go.mod` in `contracts/`.
  - The generated `.pb.go` and `.connect.go` lie in the repository beside their `.proto`. `just contracts-check` checks that they match what buf generates, as `just types-check` checks the format's types. buf's code is not in the Go coverage: `codecov/patch` would count every generated line as uncovered.
  - Beside buf's code the module carries the package `contracts`, written by hand: `contracts/vectors.go` embeds the test vectors as `contracts.Vectors`. The package has no dependencies beyond the standard library, so the module requires only the runtime of protobuf and Connect, `google.golang.org/protobuf` and `connectrpc.com/connect/v2`, at exact versions; Connect is a direct dependency, for the code of `protoc-gen-connect-go`. The examples the module carries as files, without an `fs.FS` of their own: `tutor` and `canvas` read them from the submodule `spec/`.
  - The module's tag is `contracts/vX.Y.Z`, with the number of the tag of `spec`.
  - The root module of `spec` still requires nothing: with the `go.mod` in `contracts/`, the nested module is not in its zip. `go-check` checks the zip of the module `contracts` through `tools/gomod`.
- **The TypeScript code** is the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`: JavaScript code and declarations, without JSON types. In `buf.gen.yaml`, `protoc-gen-es` has `target=js+dts` and `import_extension=js`.
  - The package is built by `tools/contracts/npm.mjs`, which shares its packing with `@altnovatrail/spec`, `tools/npm-package.mjs`:
    - the files are `LICENSE`, the README `tools/contracts/npm/README.md` and every `_pb.js` and `_pb.d.ts` under `contracts/` of the commit, without the prefix `contracts/`;
    - `exports`: one per code file, by the file's path, as a Go package's path without the module's prefix: `./novatrail/observation/v1/observation_pb.js` with the declarations beside; `type: module`, `sideEffects: false`, `files: ["novatrail"]`;
    - the dependency is `@bufbuild/protobuf` at the exact version from `tools/package.json` of the commit, where it is a direct dependency, and the same as that of `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es`: otherwise the package does not build;
    - the version is the tag without `v`, `repository` is `spec`, as for the types package.
    - Dependabot raises `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` and `@bufbuild/protobuf` as one group `bufbuild`, the major version too: separately the package would not build in each pull request.
  - The package carries the test vectors of the packages whose rules code in TypeScript executes — the rules of the device and of the runner, `vectors/eval/v1/<rule>.json`, which `canvas` executes —, and exports each by its path. The observation's vectors are not in it: TypeScript gives no verdicts. The package's contents follow the tree, as buf's code does, so the package of a commit without these vectors stays the same byte for byte, and no new line is needed.
  - **The TypeScript check.** `just contracts-check`, when the code matched what buf writes, builds the package from the working tree and installs it into a trial project beside the runtime of the same version. `tsc` of `tools/` takes every message of every file — create, write in binary form and in JSON with proto names, read — under `nodenext` and `bundler`, as strictly as `types-check`, with `skipLibCheck: false`, and Node takes every message empty and with a value in every field — a member of every `oneof`, an element of every list and `map`, nested messages —, reads it back from the binary form and from JSON of both spellings, and checks that JSON with `useProtoFieldName` names every field, nested ones too, by its proto name (`tools/contracts/typescript.mjs`, `tools/contracts/contracts.check.mjs`). Node also reads, with the package's code, every message of every vector the package carries. The check is generated from the package's declarations, so every contract is checked alike.
  - `@altnovatrail/spec` stays declarations only. The mark's type in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` is written by hand, as the element's types are, and `tools/types/canvas.check.ts` converts the contract's `Mark` into the element's `Mark` with an exhaustive `switch`; the recipe `types-check` installs beside it the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts` of the working tree and the runtime of protobuf-es.
- **The release.** The contracts come out in the releases of `spec` from line 0.7, `FIRST_CONTRACTS_LINE` in `tools/release/files.mjs`: what a release carries is decided by the line of its commit, and a rerun of an old release builds the files it got.
  - A release carries the npm package, `altnovatrail-contracts-<version>.tgz`, signed as the types package is, and publishes it to npm by the same step as the types package, with a trusted publisher in npm. The first version was published by hand from the release file: a trusted publisher of npm is set only on a package that is already in the registry, and a setup without a publication expires after 48 hours.
  - **The binding of the file**: `altnovatrail-contracts-<version>.tgz` is bound to the tag, as the types package is — the name and the tag agree, `spec` has the tag, `version` in `package.json` is the tag without `v` —, and `name` in `package.json` of each of the two packages is the one that the file names. A consumer checks it with `release-verify-npm`, which takes `@altnovatrail/contracts` from the release of `spec`: the archive at the registry's address `…/@altnovatrail/contracts/-/contracts-<version>.tgz`, the bundle from the file of the same name in the release of `spec` of the same tag (`RELEASED_BY` in `tools/release/verify.mjs`).
  - **The tag of the Go module** is set by the step "Tag the Go module of the contracts" of `release.yml` after "Verify the release", once the release is out and checked: `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs` with the job's token, a lightweight tag, as with `gh release create`, on the release's commit. A rerun sets the tag if it is not there, does nothing if it is on the same commit, and fails if it is on another: such a tag was set by hand. "Verify the Go module" checks this module too, through the proxy.
  - **The ruleset "v-tags"** holds `refs/tags/contracts/v*` too: moving, deleting and force push are forbidden, with no bypass. It does not restrict creation.
- **The transport** `app` ↔ `api` is Connect, and the contract chooses it: the services' stubs are born in `spec`, and the client must match the server.
  - The server is connect-go v2 in `api`, the client connect-es in `app`.
  - Calls are unary only.
  - On the wire `app` ↔ `api` is binary protobuf, and `app` turns it on explicitly. The server accepts JSON too, for debugging, with proto names: its JSON codec is `protojson` with `UseProtoNames`. A Connect server accepts gRPC and gRPC-Web too.
- **The plugins and buf** are local, at exact versions; there are no remote BSR plugins, whose version may be "latest":
  - `protoc-gen-go` and `protoc-gen-connect-go` by `tool` directives in `contracts/go.mod` itself, and `buf.gen.yaml` calls them with `go -C contracts tool …`;
  - `protoc-gen-es` at an exact version in `tools/package.json`;
  - `buf` itself as an `ARG` of `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, in the stage of the toolchain, the release's binary without an archive, with a checksum for each architecture from its release's `sha256.txt`, checked against the field `digest` of the GitHub API and against the files themselves. With the Dockerfile it comes into the copy of every repository, as Go does, and in a copy without contracts it is not used.

  The versions stand in those files. The licenses: buf Apache-2.0, `google.golang.org/protobuf` BSD-3-Clause, `connectrpc.com/connect/v2` Apache-2.0, `@bufbuild/protobuf` and `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` Apache-2.0 and BSD-3-Clause, `@connectrpc/connect` Apache-2.0: all of the ASF's category A. There is no version of buf in the generated code — `protoc (unknown)` —, so raising buf does not change the code, while raising a plugin changes the headers, and the pull request of the raise runs `just contracts`.

— *Why:*
- **One type per process.** `tutor`, `module-kit` and `api` exchange the observation in one process, and it must have one type. The Go FAQ: "When a single .proto file is generated into two or more Go packages and linked into the same Go binary, it conflicts on every Protobuf declaration in the generated Go packages", and "Starting with v1.26.0 of the google.golang.org/protobuf module, a hard error will be reported when a Go program starts up that has multiple conflicting Protobuf names linked into it" (protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq, read 2026-11-02). Code generated at each consumer would not start this binary. `api`'s card in `docs/architecture.md` too expects the contract as generated packages from the releases of `spec`.
- **A nested module.** The generated code imports the protobuf runtime (`protoreflect`, `protoimpl`), and the root module of `spec` requires nothing. The nested module's tag: "each tag name must be prefixed with the module subdirectory, followed by a slash" (go.dev/ref/mod, read 2026-11-02). Of the two arguments against a Go module in a subfolder for the format — a second kind of tags and a copy of `format/` inside —, the cost of the tags is accepted, and here nothing needs copying: the `.proto` files lie in the module itself.
- **An npm package of its own.** protobuf-es code takes a runtime too: `import { fileDesc, messageDesc } from "@bufbuild/protobuf/codegenv2"` (`packages/protobuf-example/src/gen/example_pb.ts` @v2.16.0). And `@altnovatrail/spec` is declarations only, without dependencies. connect-es does not work without the descriptors, so types alone are not enough.
- **The rules.** The version suffix: "The last component of a package must be a version of the form v\d+ … where the numeric parts are at least 1" (buf.build/docs/lint/rules, read 2026-11-02). Compatibility: "If you don't know which to pick, start with FILE (the default)", and "you should use FILE to protect all generated languages" (buf.build/docs/breaking/rules, read 2026-11-02): the contracts generate code in two languages.
- **The previous release by its git tag**: the history of `spec` holds every release, so no file of a release and no network is needed. The tag of HEAD counts when the working tree changes the contracts: otherwise a working tree on the commit of a release would compare its change with the release before it, where a file it changes may not exist yet, and a change that breaks the package of the last release would pass the local check and be caught only by CI of the pull request.
- **Without a `.proto`** buf refuses — "Module "path: "contracts"" had no .proto files" —, and this is "Working as intended" ([bufbuild/buf#175](https://github.com/bufbuild/buf/issues/175), read 2026-11-02).
- **The Go plugins in `contracts/go.mod`**: one pin holds the generator and the runtime, and one Dependabot entry raises them together. This adds no modules: `cmd/protoc-gen-go` is a package of `google.golang.org/protobuf`, and `cmd/protoc-gen-connect-go` v2.0.2 imports only connect and protobuf (read 2026-11-02).
- **Names in JSON.** "Parsers accept both the lowerCamelCase name (or the one specified by the json_name option) and the original proto field name. This allows for a serializer option to choose to print using the original field name … and have the resulting output still be parsed back by all spec parsers" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json, read 2026-11-02). So a field has one spelling — in the format, in `.proto` and in JSON —, and a sample file is of the same style as the module.
- **Without JSON types.** `json_types=true` gives types `…Json` with lowerCamelCase names, a JSON that the contract's writer does not write by this entry, while `toJson` with `useProtoFieldName` gives a `JsonValue` anyway, not a type `…Json` (protobuf-es 2.16.0, `to-json.d.ts`), and `fromJson` accepts a `JsonValue`.
- **`optional`.** "We recommend adding the optional label for proto3 basic types by default" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/field_presence, read 2026-11-02).
- **Integers.** "ProtoJSON serializers emit int64s as strings to ensure no precision loss will occur on large int64s by any implementation" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json). The fractions 0–1000 and the integer crops fit in `int32`, and in JSON they are numbers.
- **Connect.** "Connect also offers direct support for the gRPC-Web protocol used by grpc/grpc-web, without relying on a translating proxy like Envoy", and Connect's own protocol "works over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3" (connectrpc.com/docs/introduction, read 2026-11-02). Both sides skip unknown fields: connect-go v2.0.2 — `DiscardUnknown: true, // Ensure difference schema versions unmarshal.` (`connectproto/connectproto.go`), connect-es 2.3.0 — "In connect-es, unknown JSON fields are ignored by default" (`packages/connect/src/protocol/serialization.ts`).
- **Binary on the wire.** Binary protobuf carries a new enum value to an earlier build of `app` as a number: a proto3 enum is open. In JSON the server writes the value's name, and connect-es skips an unknown name — protobuf-es's `ignoreUnknownFields` "ignores unknown fields in parsing, as well as unrecognized enum string representations" (`packages/protobuf/src/from-json.ts`, protobuf-es v2.16.0, read by `api` 2026-11-02) —, and the field is read as empty: a new close reason would look like "the attempt is open". So the promise that an earlier build works with a new server within a major package holds only on the binary wire. connect-web sends JSON by default — "By default, connect-web clients use the JSON format" (`packages/connect-web/src/connect-transport.ts`, connect-es v2.3.0, read by `api` 2026-11-02) —, so `app` turns on binary explicitly.
- **Line 0.7.** v0.6.7 already carries `observation.proto`, and its release has no package file; a rerun of it must build the files it got.
- **The tag of the Go module.** "Each tag name must be prefixed with the module subdirectory, followed by a slash" ([Go Modules Reference](https://go.dev/ref/mod), read 2026-11-02).
- **The first version by hand.** Since 2026-10-02 npm creates a new package too — "You can now create a new npm package with `npm stage publish`" —, but "using a local session or a granular access token, including a stage-only token", and a trusted publisher is set up "after package creation" ([GitHub Changelog, 2026-10-02](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-02-npm-staged-publishing-now-supports-creating-new-packages/), read 2026-11-02). Publishing to npm takes no token and no staged publishing, so the first version of a new package is published by hand.
- **The TypeScript check**: the code of protobuf-es works under TypeScript 7: the check takes every message under both resolutions without errors, and Node runs them. In `types-check` it would not run on a change of `.proto`, which ends with `contracts-check`.

— *Rejected:*
- a folder `proto/`: a name by the technology, not by the role; the contracts inside `format/`: two normative parts with different versions in one folder and one archive;
- `STANDARD` without `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC`, and the soft `BASIC`, `WIRE_JSON` and `PACKAGE`: without a version in the package's name, without `_UNSPECIFIED`, and `WIRE_JSON` does not protect the generated code;
- `buf breaking` against a release file checked by `release-verify`: the contract has no version of its own, `verify.mjs` knows no binding of such a file, `release.yml` lets through only `<part>-MAJOR.MINOR.tar.gz`, every pull request would go over the network to GitHub and Sigstore, and the releases before line 0.7 have no such file; never comparing with the tag of HEAD and comparing by hand: the local check would let through what CI catches;
- only buf and the comparison of the code: buf would let `json_name`, editions and a weakened `buf.yaml` through silently;
- a recipe `buf-check`: a name by the technology, as the folder `proto/`;
- the Go plugins in a module of `tools/`, `tools/contracts` or another: the versions of protobuf and connect would stand in two `go.mod`, and the check would have to keep them equal;
- lowerCamelCase names in JSON, ProtoJSON's default: a field has two spellings; `json_name` on every field: a duplicate of the name, easy to forget;
- JSON types in the npm package: the types would describe a forbidden spelling;
- for the open view, protobuf messages of its own — a second schema beside the format's —, and `google.protobuf.Struct` — without types, and numbers are `double`;
- Edition 2023 and 2024: 2024 gives the Opaque API in Go by default, while publishers of generated Go code are advised the Hybrid one (go.dev/blog/protobuf-opaque, 16.12.2024), protoc-gen-go v1.36.12 goes no further than 2024, and every generator knows proto3;
- a MAJOR.MINOR version of its own, as the format has: a new line for each step of the first contracts, and STANDARD does not let a package `v0` through; `v1alpha1` until the first app: buf would not catch the renaming of a field, and sample files are kept long;
- a change of meaning in any release of the line: an old observation in the database would be read by the new rule with no sign of the version;
- the examples as vectors `contracts/vectors/eval/v1/`: a vector holds a rule that a program of another repository executes, while an example shows a message whole and is checked by the code of `spec`, by which the other repositories check theirs too;
- the code in the root module of `spec`: the root module would require the protobuf runtime, and every consumer of `spec` in Go would get it; the code at each consumer: a conflict of the protobuf registry in the binary of `api`; a generator of our own without a runtime, as `tools/types`: our own implementation of ProtoJSON and no Connect stubs, while connect-go requires `proto.Message`;
- the TypeScript code in `@altnovatrail/spec`: it would no longer be declarations only, without dependencies; generation at `app` and `canvas`: two generators whose versions may diverge; declarations only: connect-es does not work without descriptors;
