- in the npm package, the pattern `./novatrail/*`: any file of the folder would go out; an `index.js` of our own per protobuf package: code of `spec` on top of `protoc-gen-es`;
- the TypeScript check in `types-check`: a change of `.proto` ends with `contracts-check`;
- the file and the publication step of the npm package as one piece of work with two pull requests: more than one round of checks; the npm package after the first contract of `app` ↔ `api`: `app` needs the observation in TypeScript;
- the package and the tag from the line that the next version of the format opens: the path of the release would not be tried until then; a sign by the commit's content, without a line: what a release carries would no longer be decided by its line, and renaming the file would break the reruns of old releases;
- the tag of the Go module before the release: a failure of the release would leave a tag without a release, and the ruleset does not let it be deleted; an annotated tag object: Go does not need it;
- gRPC-Web: the browser needs a proxy, Envoy by default; HTTP of our own with protobuf bodies, as in MathTrail Canvas ([canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/tree/0901af0)): there are no stubs, and the contract does not check the transport; choosing the transport in the detailing of `api`: the stubs are born in `spec`, and the client must match the server;
- JSON on the wire: a new enum value would be read as empty by an earlier build, and a crop of the work in JSON is a base64 string, a third longer; JSON with numbers instead of the enums' names: the names would not be readable even in JSON.

— *Consequence:* `contracts/README.md`; `contracts/`; `buf.yaml`; `buf.gen.yaml`; `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; `justfile`; `tools/contracts/`; `tools/npm-package.mjs`; `tools/package.json`; `tools/types/canvas.check.ts`; `tools/release/files.mjs`; `tools/release/contracts-line.mjs`; `tools/release/verify.mjs`; `tools/gomod/`; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; `.github/dependabot.yml`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## Own key

**R84. An own key lies on the device only if the key's owner decided so on this device — in the database of their profile —, and otherwise only in the tab's memory while their profile is open; on the server, only in the request's memory. The key and its provider come with every request of the owner profile that calls AI, the provider without the key with every request whose answer or refusal may give an engine choice, and `api` accepts either only with a profile of the category `adult`. The owner profile on an account that has a profile of another category is opened by the same PIN as the section for adults, and a hidden page closes it after a period that an adult sets on this device. The providers' terms allow giving the key to `api`.** `app`'s and `api`'s sides are detailed in their `docs/decisions.md`.
- **Where the key lies.** On the device, only by the key's owner's mark "Keep on this device", separate for each device: only they know whether the device is shared. Without the mark the key lives in the tab's memory while the owner profile is open. There is no encryption in the browser: whoever holds the device can get at a key saved on the device, and `app` says so plainly, and the damage is held by the key's limit and lifetime at the provider. On the server, only in the request's memory, not in the database and not in the logs. The key is not in the export: the export is the learners' data, and the key is a secret of the key's owner.
- **With which request.**
  - The key and its provider go with every request of the owner profile that calls AI: with the work for reading, with the rung's words and with "explain differently", which sends no work. `app` names the provider without the key at the start of the attempt.
  - The provider without the key, `own_key_provider`, goes with every request whose answer or refusal may give an engine choice, though it calls no AI — `ChooseNext`, `OpenLesson`, `GetLessonRun`, `CompleteLesson`, `ShowSolution` and `Done` —, so that `api` judges by it whether the AI that checks a task is closed on this route, and a choice gives nothing that the beginning of an attempt on the same route would refuse. `SubmitWork` names the route by the provider of its `own_key`, or by `own_key_provider` when it sends no `work`, which AI would read: a task that a tap checks sends no key. A submission with `own_key_provider` beside `work` or `own_key` is refused `invalid_argument`. `BeginAttempt` names it by its own.
  - With a request of a profile of a category other than `adult`, `api` accepts neither the key nor a provider, checks this itself, and refuses `CAUSE_KEY_NOT_FOR_PROFILE` (О-4).
  - A provider's refusal by a limit is the outcome "limit reached" with a cause, a refusal of the key itself — wrong or revoked — is an outcome of its own, and neither moves the call to platform AI without an action of the key's owner.
- **Connecting.** `api` checks the key through `tutor` — it does not go to providers bypassing `tutor` — by a request without the learner's content, on behalf of the owner profile: the key is accepted, wrong, the key has no rights, or the provider is closed for the profile.
  - A check beyond the checks `api` lets an account make in a sliding window is refused `CAUSE_KEY_CHECKS_EXHAUSTED`, code `resource_exhausted`, with no call and with when the next check opens, `Refusal.next_key_check`; `api` holds the number and the window (Д247).
  - The providers open to an own key for the profile are named by `api`, `ListOwnKeyProviders`, and `app` does not build them in: those whose own key `tutor` admits at the profile's category for one kind of call of `api` at least, by the admission table and the models admitted at the deployment's rung, so that a provider out of the list is "provider closed" with no call.
- **The owner profile on a shared device** is behind the same PIN as the section for adults, at every opening, if the account holds a profile of a category other than `adult`. Without such profiles, without a PIN. The PIN is a barrier of the interface, and `api` holds its hash and counter. It closes by itself:
  - by "Switch learner" and on reload;
  - after a period of a hidden page that an adult sets on this device: 5 minutes by default, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. There is no "Do not close" among the periods.
- **The providers' terms.** They allow giving an own key to `api`. At Anthropic, API keys of individuals too go by the Commercial Terms, there is no clause about passing a key in them, and the help page directly describes a key in third-party tools: "when you upload your API key to third-party tools … you are giving the developer of that tool access to your Claude Console account" (sources 2.3). At OpenAI, the Services Agreement is a contract "between the organization agreeing to these terms", §3.1 says "Customer will not share Account access credentials or individual login credentials between multiple users", by §3.3(g) one may not "buy, sell, or transfer API keys from, to, or with a third party", and an End User is also the one "who accesses the Services under Customer’s Account" (sources 2.2). There is no direct ban on a key in a third-party service in it.

— *Why:*
- the providers advise keeping a key on the server: OpenAI, "Don’t share it with others or expose it in any client-side code such as browsers or apps", Anthropic's SDK for the browser, "Any user with access to the browser can potentially inspect, extract, and misuse these credentials" (`app`'s `docs/sources.md`, checked 2026-11-02). But the platform's server stores no own key, so the key is on the device, by default only in memory, and in the database where an adult learns alone and decided so themselves;
- the key comes with every AI call: otherwise "explain differently" of the key's owner would go through platform AI, at its quota and under its contracts, not under the terms the key's owner accepted with the provider;
- the provider comes with every request that may give a choice, not with `ChooseNext` alone: a choice comes in `next` and at the end of a lesson run too, and on the route of platform AI an owner whose quota is spent would get there only tasks by tap, or "nothing to give" with the quota;
- the check at connecting is so that a typo in the key is found on the page where the key is entered, not at the first hint. With the cause of exhausted checks `app` tells the owner when to try again rather than "it did not work", and by the list it offers no provider whose key the check always finds closed;
- the PIN of the owner profile does not wait for the question of for whom an own key is: that decides who gets a key, not how it lies on a shared device, and a key is only ever on a profile `adult` anyway;
- the period of a hidden page: closing for protection is a time limit by WCAG 2.2, 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable, level A: "if a time limit is included in order to address security concerns, it would be considered to have been set by the content" ([Understanding 2.2.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable.html)). The criterion allows turning the limit off — "Turn off" — or changing it "over a wide range that is at least ten times the length of the default setting" ([WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/)); both quotes were read 2026-11-02. 60 minutes is twelve default periods, so 2.2.1 is met without turning off. Only the adult knows whether the device is shared: the same argument as for the mark "Keep on this device";
- the providers' terms: Anthropic directly describes such a path, and OpenAI does not directly forbid it.

— *Rejected:*
- the key always on the device: on a shared tablet it would always lie there, against the providers' advice;
- the key on the server, encrypted: the server would hold a secret of every key's owner, and the platform's server stores no own key;
- the key only with the work: "explain differently" of the key's owner would go through platform AI;
- the provider with `ChooseNext` alone, with a rule that `app` asks `ChooseNext` again after "nothing to give": it would not see a pool narrowed to tasks by tap; `ChooseNext` alone, with the rest as a debt;
- no check of the key: a wrong key would be found at the first call;
- for exhausted checks, a cause with no data, as `CAUSE_TOO_MANY_CONSENTS`, or no cause, `app` reading the refusal by its code; the list of providers by the cell `own_key` of the admission table alone;
- the owner profile on a shared device left open until it is decided for whom an own key is (О-4): that decides who gets a key;
- "Do not close" among the periods: a child on a shared tablet would stay in the owner profile, on the AI routes for adults and on the owner's own key, and this PIN is what closes them off from the child; a fixed period, with 2.2.1 as a declared nonconformance of `app`: the platform's accessibility standard would be held with a reservation that can be done without;
- the providers' terms as a question to a lawyer before the code of the own key, a question of its own or one beside the own key of minors, with the own OpenAI key closed until the lawyer answers: the terms as quoted above allow the passing.

— *Does not decide:* for whom the own key is, О-4, beyond its being closed to a learner under 18 at every provider; which providers the admission table opens to an own key; how `tutor` checks the key.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `tutor`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## The deployment configuration of `app`

**R85. The format of the deployment configuration file of `app`, `/deployment.json`, is a normative part of `spec`, [`deployment/`](../deployment/README.md), built as the AI admission table: its own text in English, a version of its own, an integer, a JSON Schema 2020-12 schema at the permanent path `deployment/schemas/deployment.schema.json`, examples, reading vectors and a check of its own, `just deployment-check`; a release file `deployment-<version>.tar.gz`, signed and attested, which `release-verify` accepts; `spec.Deployment`, an `fs.FS` in the Go module, and the types package `types/deploymentv1` for Go and TypeScript. The build of `app` carries a copy of the file's schema from the release of `spec` it stands on, and the rollout of `infra` checks the file by the schema of its `spec/` submodule and by the schema of the build. The CSP template `csp.json` and the layout of the build's archive are a contract of the build of `app`, not of the part.**
- The file is written not by those who read it: on the platform, by the rollout of `infra` from the rollout list, in a self-hosting copy, by its operator, and `app` reads it. Version 1 is the format `app` named first, without changes: `format`, `api` and `signIn`.
- **Versions.** The version is an integer, in `VERSION` and in the field `format` of the file itself, the first is 1. Any change of the form gives a new version: `app` rejects an unknown field. A new version, as with the admission table, opens a line of releases of `spec`, and version 1, a new kind of release file, opened line 0.11, as the admission table opened its own, while the module format kept its version. The build of `app`, by the copy of the schema it carries, names the version it reads. The rollout refuses a build of another version, naming both: then `infra` moves to the tag of this version in a task of its own.
- **Reading vectors.** A case is a file, the origin where `app` is open, and what the reading gives: the file is accepted, or the step that refused it — the schema or a rule — and the paths of the fields. The reading is first the schema, then two rules that the schema cannot express: `deployment.api-origin`, `api` equals its own origin as the URL Standard writes it, and `deployment.loopback`, `http` for `api` only when `app` itself is open on loopback. By the vectors `app` checks its code, and `infra` its check.
- **The fields' names** are those of `app`'s first format, in camelCase: in `signIn` these are the keys of the configuration object of a Firebase project, which the operator copies from the console, and `app` gives to the SDK as they are. The snake_case rule of the schemas' conventions is lifted from the file's schema, but not from the vector's schema.
- **The types** are Go and TypeScript, by the same generator as the other parts' types, `tools/types`.
- **The build's contract.** It is written in `app`'s `docs/architecture.md`, and `app` brings a change of the form or of the layout as a row «в реестр spec» before the release that carries it:
  - `csp.json` is an object "directive → string of sources" with the places `{api}` and `{authDomain}`;
  - at the archive's root are `index.html`, `assets/`, `deployment.schema.json`, `csp.json`, `NOTICE` and `LICENSE`, without a `deployment.json` of its own, as the rollout of `infra` reads them; the site serves `NOTICE` and `LICENSE` at `/NOTICE` and `/LICENSE`. Of the layout the part names one thing, `deployment.schema.json` at the archive's root. The rollout does not reject extra files and deploys them all (`infra`'s `tools/deploy-check/check.mjs`), and it can check that `NOTICE` and `LICENSE` are there at its move to a tag (Д208).

— *Why:*
- shared formats live in `spec`, and a contract type held by one side is rejected: the file has a second reader in code, the rollout of `infra`, and writers other than `app`, and a self-hosting operator looks for the normative text in `spec`;
- the part came with the first code of the rollout, before the first deployment: before that code `app` alone read the file, and the schema in its signed build had nothing to diverge from;
- the permanent path of the schema: by it the check of `infra` finds the schema in its submodule, as it finds the schemas of the admission table;
- `csp.json` stays in the build: it follows the build's code, not the contract between whoever writes the file and whoever reads it. An object is the most direct writing of the "one table of directives" of `app`'s design, and the rollout rejects another form both at the check of a pull request and at the release;
- `NOTICE` and `LICENSE` at the archive's root: the Vite bundle does not keep the packages' license comments, and without `NOTICE` the archive and the site would distribute the code of React, Firebase, `canvas` and others without the notices that Apache-2.0 §4(d), MIT and ISC require (sources 7.5); a copy of the archive taken on its own carries them itself.

— *Rejected:*
- the part before the code of the rollout, as a task of an early epic: a new normative part for a file that only `app` read, and every new field would wait for a release of `spec`;
- the format forever in the documents of `app`: the contract would be held by one side, and a self-hosting operator would look for the normative text in the documents of one repository;
- the schema in `format/`: it has another reader and a version of its own;
- the schemas of all versions in the part, so that a rollback of the build of `app` does not wait for `infra`: the builds of `app` and `api` are pinned together;
- only examples by the schema, without reading vectors: the loopback rule would stay words, and each side would write its own cases;
- the CSP template in the part: every change of the scripts of `app` would wait for a release of `spec`; a schema of the form of `csp.json` in the part, without the template's content: a new version of the format and a new line of `spec` for what one rollout reads, and a change of the form would wait for a release of `spec`; the whole layout in the part's text: a description without a reading rule, and the part has another subject; another form at `app` and a change of the rollout to suit it: the rollout's code already exists;
- only TypeScript types: an exception in the generator for one part;
- version 1 in a patch of line 0.10: `verify.mjs` and the line's rule would have to be taught to accept a new kind of file in a patch;
- snake_case fields: `app` would translate the names into Firebase's keys, and the console's object would not do as it is;
- `NOTICE` and `LICENSE` beside the archive in the release, or only on the legal pages of `app`: a copy of the archive without them.

— *Consequence:* `deployment/README.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/architecture.md`; `infra`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## Observation

**R86. The observation is the contract `novatrail.observation.v1`. For each answer slot whose answer AI reads, it carries the value as written, or why there is no value, and for a slot `anywhere` also the box of the final answer. In the reading mode `pair` `module-kit` joins two readings into one, by the slot check, and gives the verdict by the joined observation; in the mode `single` it gives the verdict by the one observation, without the join. The module format does not change by this. The reading request and the analysis response are types of `tutor`, and a change of the contract's meaning is a new package. The test vectors of the observation are JSON files without a schema of their own: `spec`'s checks compute them by a second implementation, and `module-kit` takes them as `contracts.Vectors` of the Go module of the contracts.** [The contracts text](../contracts/README.md) and `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation.proto` are normative.
- **What is in the observation.** The message `Observation` is the slots whose answer AI reads, each once, in the task's order. On a handwriting sheet these are the slots `anywhere`, `zone` and `sheet`, on a workbook every box. `tutor` takes the boxes from the open view, and gives an empty one as empty without calling the model: the work holds only the filled ones. A slot has its place, `{ item, slot }` from 1, and one of two: `value`, as written, or `unreadable`: blank, illegible, ambiguous, no final answer, several final answers. AI does not read a tapped choice, and it is not in the observation: `api` gives `module-kit` the option the learner chose beside the observation.
- **What the reader gives.**
  - A value only if it is visible in the writing itself, as in MathTrail Canvas ([canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/tree/0901af0)), and as written: the check kind normalizes it. A vertical fraction is written in a line.
  - "Ambiguous" is a mirrored digit, a value of which the reader sees another reading, and a value that it cannot show in the writing.
  - The reader knows nothing of the slot check: neither the kind nor the options of a handwritten choice. The answer's form is named by the task statement, and options among which the key stands would hint at the answer, as the key would.
- **The place:**
  - for a slot `anywhere`, the box of the final answer on the crop in whole thousandths, `CropBox`, if the reader named it and it is valid;
  - for a zone and a box, the slot itself;
  - a group label only if group boxes go with the work (Т-31).
- **Joining**, in the mode `pair`. Slots with a verdict have two readers, and `tutor` gives the observations of both or a call outcome, never one. `module-kit` joins them slot by slot:
  - values agree when the slot check compares them as equal, as a value with a trap, and gives them one verdict; then the value is that of the pair's first reader. A predicate compares the integers read;
  - equal reasons give the same reason, and everything else gives "ambiguous";
  - a value that the check kind normalizes to empty is joined as "blank", and a joined reason has no box;
  - an invalid observation is as an AI failure: there is no joined one, and every slot that AI reads is "unchecked". A reason that the release of `module-kit` reading the observation does not know is invalid too.

  An essay is read by one reader, and there is nothing to join.
- **The mode `single`.** `tutor` gives one observation, of a slot with a verdict too, and `module-kit` validates it and gives the verdict by it without the join.
- **The verdict** is by the joined observation, or in `single` by the one observation, as a whole.
  - A value gets the format's verdict, with a reason and a trap, by the module format's checks.
  - A reason without a value gives `unreadable` with the reason of its name: `blank`, `illegible`, `ambiguous`, `no_final_answer` or `several_final_answers`. The reason `notation` remains the format's.
- **The call outcomes are not an observation.** An AI failure, a limit, "not admitted" and a refusal of the own key give the slots that AI reads "unchecked". If one reader of the pair failed, there is no observation at all.
- **What `api` stores** is the joined observation, or in `single` the one reader's, and the tapped choice: by them the same release of `module-kit` repeats the verdict. The readers' observations, the writing parts and other readings are not stored. The server has no observation of an essay: of an attempt of a task with a rubric it keeps how each submission ended and, for feedback, the mark of each criterion and the source of the words, and neither the text of the essay, nor the justifications, nor the words of the feedback.
- **The format does not change.** It judges the read value, and what makes a slot "unreadable" before the check kind its text already assigns to the observation. The module format's text on checks refers to the contract: an editorial change. The rules about a vertical fraction and about a mirrored digit are rules about the reader, and change no version of the format.
- **The reading request and the analysis response are types of `tutor`.** Only `api` and `tutor` exchange them, and `api` calls its library anyway.
  - The open view in the request is the format's type `open.Task`; in protobuf an open view goes as the contracts carry it, the bytes of the format's JSON with `module_format_version` beside them.
  - The analysis gives the box of the first error or nothing, and a trap from the block or nothing. The box is the same message `CropBox`, and `api` gives it as a mark without conversion.
  - The candidate trap and the place of the first error are not in the observation but in the response of the analysis, which sees the key.
- **The version of the meaning.**
  - A new value of a reason or a new field is an addition to `v1`. So is the mode `single`: on the same messages the join and the verdict give what they gave.
  - A change of the meaning of a field, a value or a rule of the observation in [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md) — whatever gives another result on the same message — breaks the package: a `v2` and a new line are needed, as with a major change of the format.
  - `buf breaking` does not see this, and review holds it.
- **The test vectors** are `contracts/vectors/observation/v1/<case>.json`. They hold the task's items, the readers' observations with a validity flag, the taps and the joined observation with verdicts, and for an essay the outcome of the submission.
  - **JSON, not YAML.** An observation in a vector is proto3 JSON with proto names, and with it the whole file. The contracts text's rules of JSON already name "a file of `spec`" as a writer of the contract's JSON. `module-kit` reads a vector through `encoding/json` and `protojson`, without YAML. JSON has none of YAML's type traps: `8.` and `0.5` stay strings. An observation is written as `toJson` with `useProtoFieldName` and `alwaysEmitImplicit` or `protojson` with `UseProtoNames` and `EmitDefaultValues` writes it — with every field, zeros too. A reason that the package does not have is written as a number.
  - **No schema of its own.** The type of the observation is described once — in `.proto`. It is held by a strict `fromJson`, and the writing by a comparison with `toJson`. The canvas and the items are held by the format's schema, `task.schema.json`: `#/properties/canvas` and `#/$defs/item`. The task's rules that are seen by the slot check are held by `slotBreaches` of `format-check`. The keys of the file and of a case are held by the check's code, and the file is described by the test vectors of the observation in [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md).
  - **`contracts.Vectors`.** The vectors lie in `contracts/`, so they are carried by the Go module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts` at the tag `contracts/vX.Y.Z`. `tools/gomod` already requires every file of `contracts/` in its zip. The package `contracts` at the root of the module — `contracts/vectors.go`, written by hand, — embeds `vectors/` with the directive `//go:embed all:vectors`, as the package `spec` embeds the format, and requires nothing beyond the standard library. Its test checks that what is embedded matches the files on disk. It also reads each observation of each vector with `protojson` and compares the writing back: this shows that Go takes the vectors the same way as protobuf-es.
  - **The descriptors of buf's image.** The code `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation_pb.js` imports `@bufbuild/protobuf/codegenv2` by a bare name, and from `contracts/`, where there is no `node_modules`, this import does not resolve. So the registry is built from the image of `buf build`, which `contracts-check` builds anyway. For this the image is read with `fromJson(FileDescriptorSetSchema, …, { ignoreUnknownFields: true })`, since the image file has a field of buf beyond `FileDescriptorProto`. The well-known types, which an image without imports omits, are taken from the runtime. The descriptor is the same as the one embedded in the code, and the same recipe compares the code. The check runs in its own process and is part of the coverage.
  - **What the check computes** — `tools/contracts/observation.mjs`:
    - the validity of an observation by [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md). An invalid observation of a vector breaks one condition, so that it is seen which;
    - the join. Values join by `readingOf` of `tools/format-check/verdicts.mjs`: it gives "blank", the normal form outside the notation, or what the check compares by, with the verdict. It is separate from `comparableOf`: a value outside the notation may, after normalization, match its notation's writing, as `1/100000000000000` matches `0.00000000000001`;
    - the verdicts of the slots and of the item and the outcome of an essay. The verdict of a predicate on a value in the notation is taken from the vector, as with the format's verdict vectors, while the join of predicates is computed in full: a predicate compares integers;
    - that the vectors together give each reason of the contracts text's table of reasons in a joined observation, each check kind, an invalid observation and a tap. A reason that is not in the table the check refuses until a change adds it.
  - **Where the contracts text could be read two ways, the vectors pin one reading**, and the text says it: an editorial change, since each says what the text already implied. The vectors hold each to one reading until `module-kit` has come out with the join; later an edit would be a new meaning and `v2`:
    - an extra slot — `choice` or a place that the task does not have — makes the observation invalid: "and no other";
    - white space is the Unicode property White_Space of the raw value, as in the module format's normalization of a number: U+0085 is white space, U+FEFF is not;
    - a value that the kind normalizes to empty is `UNREADABLE_BLANK` even before the join: with `UNREADABLE_BLANK` and with such a value it gives `UNREADABLE_BLANK`, and with a value or another reason — `UNREADABLE_AMBIGUOUS`;
    - "the same once normalized" is the module format's seven steps of a number, with units, and a choice's normal form in lowercase. So `7²` and `7³` join: both are 7 and U+FFFD;
    - an invalid observation does not touch the taps: a slot `choice` gets the verdict of the option, and the item is made of all its slots.
  - **Pitfalls.**
    - `fromJson` refuses an unknown field and an unknown name of a reason, but accepts `answerSlot` in lowerCamelCase. So the proto names are held by the comparison with `toJson`.
    - `{"value": "x", "unreadable": null}` protobuf-es refuses, while Go accepts. The comparison with the writing does not let such a vector through.
    - The format's verdict vectors `module-kit` reads with Go types generated from the schemas. The observation vectors have no schema, so `module-kit` writes its own structure: the items in `formatv0`, the observations through `protojson`. The module `contracts` cannot give this type: it would require the module `spec`, and `go-check` lets in only protobuf and Connect.
  - The outcomes of a call are not observations, and the vectors hold none.

— *Why:*
- **The join is `module-kit`'s.** Normalization is its own, and comparing by verdict is possible only with the key. In `tutor`, the reading path would get the slot checks together with the keys, and reading goes without the key. The join is a rule, not perception, and its place is in the deterministic core. The eval of `tutor` compares the same way: "their values, read as the check of the kind number reads them, and their verdicts are one" (`internal/report/reading.go` of `tutor`, `main` be607e5, read 2026-11-02).
- **Comparing by the check, not by the text.** "0.5" and "1/2" under `number` are one value, and "3 / 4" and "3/4" are one notation: by the text they would go to "unreadable" with no gain. One verdict is needed because the check compares "2/4" and "1/2" equal, while under `form: reduced` their verdicts differ.
- **Without the writing parts and the other readings.** The check needs only the values, and the analysis does not get the observation. With the parts, `api` would keep the learner's writing of the solution whole, "while the profile lives", and minimization does not allow this. The other readings are already expressed by the reason "ambiguous".
- **The format is not touched.** The type of the observation is described once — in `.proto`, while in the format's vectors it would have to be described by JSON Schema as well. A new format version would require a new line and a move of all the components, though not one module changes.
- **The types of `tutor`.** A contract is needed where a type is shared by two repositories that do not call each other: the observation goes from `tutor` to `module-kit`. The reading request and the analysis response go only between `api` and the library of `tutor`, and the place in them is from the contract.
- **A version of the meaning.** The verdict is repeated from the observation kept, and an edit of the join rule would change it on the same messages with no sign in the package.
- **The vectors without a schema.** A schema of a wrapper would describe the observation a second time, or only as `object`; the format's schema and the check's code already hold the rest.

— *Rejected:*
- format 0.3, where the format's verdict is given from the observation, and the verdict vectors carry the reasons and two readings. That is a new line 0.7, ~140 files of `module_format_version`, new digests of the vectors of packages and indexes, and the type of the observation would be described twice;
- a rule in the format text without a new version: new reasons for "unreadable" are a new value of the list, and in v0 that is the next 0.y;
- the join in `tutor`, as `tutor`'s `docs/architecture.md` proposed: normalization and the key are `module-kit`'s;
- the join by the text after normalization — stricter with no gain;
- the writing parts in the observation, as `tutor`'s `docs/architecture.md` proposed, and the other readings, which `api`'s `docs/architecture.md` wanted to keep;
- the reading request and the analysis response in the contract: the open view in protobuf and the analysis response would be fixed in `spec` before `tutor` and `api` built them;
- an edit of the meaning within `v1`: an old observation in the database would be read by the new rule with no sign of the version;
- YAML for the vectors, like the format's vectors: rules of the format's YAML would be needed, and the observation would have to be rewritten in YAML;
- a JSON Schema of a wrapper in which the observation is just `object`: under `contracts/` second schemas with their own conventions would appear, and the reference to the format version would have to be raised with each of its versions;
- reading the vectors from the submodule `spec/`: code takes `spec`'s files from its releases;
- a release file of its own, `observation-vectors-<version>.tar.gz`: the contracts have no version of their own beyond the package, and a new kind of release file is a new line;
- running the vectors in a trial project, like `tools/contracts/typescript.mjs`: then they would wait for the build of the npm package and would run in a child process;
- a comparison of the vectors with the previous release: an edit of their meaning is held by review, since a byte-for-byte comparison would not let through even a new format version that changes the form of an item.

— *Consequence:* `contracts/README.md`; `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation.pb.go`; `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation_pb.js`; `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation_pb.d.ts`; `contracts/vectors/observation/v1/`; `contracts/vectors.go`; `contracts/vectors_test.go`; `tools/contracts/observation.mjs`; `tools/format-check/verdicts.mjs`; `format/README.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `README.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `RUN.md`; `COORDINATION.md`.

## A task with a rubric

**R87. A submission of a task with a rubric ends with feedback, "unreadable" or "unchecked" — not with a verdict, and the attempt is closed by the learner's "Done", and then the task is solved. Of such an attempt the server keeps how each submission ended, and for feedback the mark of each criterion, "met", "not met" or "not assessed", and the source of the words; it keeps neither the text of the essay, nor the justifications, nor the words of the feedback.** `api`'s `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/architecture.md` hold the details and the arguments of `api`'s side.
- **The submission end:**
  - feedback — the assessment returned at least one criterion with a mark;
  - "unreadable" — the sheet is empty or the essay cannot be read as a whole, and it does not reach the assessment;
  - "unchecked" — an AI failure, an exhausted quota, "not admitted", a refusal of the provider by a limit, a refusal of the own key, or an assessment without a single criterion with a mark.

  "Unreadable" and "unchecked" mean the same as the verdicts of the same name: this is not the learner's error. But they stand at the submission, not at the answer slot and the item: an item with a rubric has no verdict. The three ends have no common name: "result" in the glossary already means both feedback and the end of an attempt. Normative for the observation is [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md).
- **"Unreadable" — only for the essay as a whole.** One illegible word does not send the whole essay to rewriting — the same argument as for one reader of an essay. How a reader gives such a word is Т-37: the reading prompt of `tutor` has not yet measured the outcome "unreadable", and the synthetic data are all legible, as `tutor`'s `docs/architecture.md` records.
- **Feedback that did not pass** the leak check or the feedback rule is replaced by the phrase of `app` "no feedback this time", without a repeated call. This is not the neutral phrase of an AI failure: there was an assessment, only the words did not pass. The marks are recorded then. A criterion that is not in the model's answer or that is named twice is "not assessed", and the call is not repeated either: this is the answer to the question that `tutor`'s `docs/architecture.md` left to `api`.
- **"Done"** is a learning action of the learner, after at least one submission, however it ended; before that — the refusal "no submission". Until "Done", the attempt is open for rewriting: the learner edits the same sheet and submits it again, and each submission is again two calls and its own quota. "Done" after "unreadable" or "unchecked" is the way out for a learner whose essay cannot be read, and for one whose quota ran out. An attempt closed by "Done" gives no evidence (О-17), and the lesson's segment ends with it.
- **The task is solved** when its attempt is closed by "Done". Then its criteria and its solution, if the task has one, are open. The solution that "Done" opens is not a solution that went to the device in the summary of issues, and the engine does not pause the task for it. The adult sees the marks in the progress, and the learner sees feedback, not an assessment. Feedback does not go to the learner model (О-17), and "what to develop" for tasks with a rubric the progress reads from the marks, not from the model.
- **What is kept:**
  - for a submission — the time and how it ended;
  - for feedback — the mark of each criterion by its number in the rubric, and the source of the words: the model or the phrase "no feedback";
  - the crop of the sheet, the text read, the justifications and the words of the feedback are neither in the database, nor in the caches, nor in the logs: they live in the memory of the request, and what was read and the feedback also on the device, with the essay. The server has no observation of an essay;
  - the text of the essay — only as an artifact at the account owner's choice.
- **The words of the marks** are "met", "not met", "not assessed", as in the assessment by a rubric and its measures, not "yes" and "not yet": "not yet" is a value of a verdict.

— *Why:* the assessment by criteria is needed by the progress — what to develop —, and the text and the words are not. Repeating feedback from the observation is not needed: the deterministic core repeats a verdict from what is kept, and feedback has none. Otherwise the server would hold the essay without the owner's choice, contrary to what `docs/privacy.md` promises. "Done", not the first feedback: rewriting is a part of writing, and a rubric has no showing of the solution, with which an attempt of a task with a key ends. To the adult the marks say what to work on, and the criteria the author can name in the task statement anyway. A solution open after "Done" is a sample, not a key: the learner saw no key that a repeat would give away.

— *Rejected:*
- keeping everything, as for any attempt: the text read, the words of the feedback and the assessment; keeping only the fact of the attempt;
- closing the attempt with the first feedback: in a lesson it would then be impossible to rewrite, and feedback lost in the network or that did not pass the rule could not be returned;
- repeating the assessment when the feedback did not pass the rule, and the neutral phrase of an AI failure instead of "no feedback";
- the rubric's criteria are always closed, and the marks are only in the export: the progress would have nothing to show;
- after "Done", the criteria with marks to the learner: that is an assessment, not feedback;
- "yes" and "not yet" as the words of the marks: "not yet" is a value of a verdict.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `format/README.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## The format's Starlark

**R88. All of the format's Starlark — the predicate of a check, the template expressions and the solver — runs in one dialect: go.starlark.net at version `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d` with the options `syntax.FileOptions` of standalone's solvers, and the built-in names are the 33 names of its `starlark.Universe`, by a list. The steps of the limits of the predicate and of the solver are counted by this version, and the computation stops when the count reaches the limit. The version of go.starlark.net is a part of the format: raising it is a new format version. Text — format 0.3, from line 0.9 of `spec`.** `module-kit`'s side is in its `docs/decisions.md`.
- **The version** is `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d`, commit 4f4267fb140d of 2026-10-21: on 2026-11-04 it is still the latest, and go.starlark.net has no tags (google/starlark-go, the GitHub API, read 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-04). It is pinned by `module-kit` and excluded from Dependabot. Raising the version is a new format version: while the format is v0, the next 0.y and a new line of `spec`.
- **The step count** of this version is by 10 on entering a function, after each call, on each back edge and after `load` (`starlark/interp.go`, lines 72–78, 289–293, 390–393, 536–540, 614–617 and 696), not by 1 per instruction, as at 89a6a09411d5, the version of standalone ([standalone@42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/tree/42b4408)), where the same file counts so at line 109. The limits are 1,000,000 steps for the predicate and 100,000,000 per template for the solver. On standalone's solvers the median ratio of steps, new count / old, is 0.96, the heaviest is 2,725,355 steps against 2,413,617, and an iteration of an empty loop is 10 steps against 6 (`module-kit`'s measurement of 2026-11-02, in its `docs/decisions.md`). The format text does not repeat the count in words, but says by an example that the versions count differently.
- **The limit** — the predicate runs on a thread of its own with `Thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps(1000000)`, and the solver on a thread with `Thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps(100000000)`: the computation stops when the count reaches the limit. This is how go.starlark.net of both versions compares — `thread.Steps >= thread.maxSteps` (`starlark/interp.go`, lines 702–705 at 4f4267fb140d and 109–110 at 89a6a09411d5).
- **The dialect** is one for all of the format's Starlark: `Set`, `While`, `TopLevelControl` and `GlobalReassign` are on, `Recursion` is off, `load` is forbidden, `print` writes nothing. The predicate and the template expressions run in it too, and for an expression only `Set` and `Recursion` of the options matter. The built-in names are the `starlark.Universe` of this version, 33 names, by a list in the format text: `None`, `True`, `False`, `abs`, `all`, `any`, `bool`, `bytes`, `chr`, `dict`, `dir`, `enumerate`, `fail`, `float`, `getattr`, `hasattr`, `hash`, `int`, `len`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `ord`, `print`, `range`, `repr`, `reversed`, `set`, `sorted`, `str`, `tuple`, `type` and `zip` (`starlark/library.go`, lines 39–73). The rule `task.predicate-expression` names the built-in names of the dialect, not "Starlark's built-in names", and lets in the names that an expression binds itself, such as the variable of a list comprehension.
- **The vectors at the boundary** of the predicate's limit and of the solver's budget are a measurement on this version. The vector `task.template-solver/past-the-budget-of-the-template` is a loop of 2,000,000 iterations: on this version a call of `solve` takes about 20,000,000 steps, a share of the budget, and 64 instances together go far beyond it. With 10,000,000 iterations one call took 100,000,040 steps, the whole budget, and the vector would no longer show that the budget is the template's (`module-kit`'s measurement). How many steps a call takes is computed by the CI of `module-kit`: the CI of `spec` has no Starlark.
- **Template expressions** call no functions and hold no loops: their steps are bounded by their length, and they have no step limit. "No more steps than it has tokens" would be wrong under both counts: the expression `a` has one token but two instructions, a load and `RETURN`, and under the new count any expression takes 10 steps on entering a function.
- **The clock and concurrency** are not the format: the clock is `module-kit`'s, and how many computations run at once `module-kit` leaves to the caller; the format text says so.

Normative — format 0.3, from line 0.9 of `spec`: the [format text](../format/README.md), its rules on the versions of the format, checks, templates and solvers, the rule `task.predicate-expression` and the vectors at the boundary of steps, `past-the-budget-of-the-template` among them.

— *Why:* the primary sources were read on 2026-11-02.
- The format's limits are set "as go.starlark.net counts them", and the count changed on 2026-10-05, pull request #663, commit de228787c8fb: "We only need to increment the step counter and check for cancellation in loops (back edges) and calls" and "Clients may need to adjust their SetMaxSteps parameter to taste. (Let us know if you think our scale factor is way off.)". Without a version, two implementations of the format would diverge on one module, and a template near the boundary of the budget would pass in one and get a refusal in the other. So the version is a part of the format: the step limit and the dialect are a major edit.
- The latest version, not standalone's: on standalone's solvers, by which the budget was calibrated, there is almost no difference, for predicates the new count is no more expensive — a simple predicate is 20 steps against 19 —, and the panic of `set([1]).difference()` is fixed in it (#672, commit 4f4267fb140d). The predicate's limit was chosen by judgement, not by a measurement: "an expression of one number does not need 25,000,000 steps".
- One dialect: for an expression it coincides with the Starlark specification that the [format text](../format/README.md) refers to. In it `set` is a built-in function, and "It is a dynamic error for a function to call itself or another function value with the same declaration" (bazelbuild/starlark, commit c0af0ea03d, `spec.md`, lines 3595 and 1419, read 2026-11-02). With `Recursion: false`, go.starlark.net catches recursion through `lambda` too: "We look for the same function code, not function value, otherwise the user could defeat the check by writing the Y combinator" (`starlark/interp.go`, lines 37–45). With `Recursion: true` the depth is bounded too — 100,000 frames (#619, the same file, lines 25–34) —, but the README promises of it only "enough in most cases": recursion turned off is an argument of one dialect and of the specification, not of a single protection of the stack.
- The list of names: "Starlark's built-in names" would be those of the bazelbuild specification, which has no `chr` and `ord`, while go.starlark.net has "The `chr` and `ord` built-in functions are supported" (`doc/spec.md`, line 4349). The list of `Universe` with them needs no filter in `module-kit`, and standalone's solvers ran with these names. None of the 33 names brings in randomness or reads the clock, so a computation repeats on the same inputs.
- The limit "reaches": this is how go.starlark.net itself stops a thread, and `module-kit` passes it the format's number as it is.

— *Rejected:*
- standalone's version, 89a6a09411d5, by an editorial change in 0.2 — the budget and the vector are calibrated on its count: the format would pin an old interpreter with the panic of the methods of `set`, and raising it would become a new format version anyway;
- a version without a name, like the Unicode version of normalization: there the vectors hold characters that all versions since 15.0 normalize the same way, while steps have no such common core — an iteration of a loop costs 6 steps on one version and 10 on another;
- describing the step count in words of the format text: it is set by the bytecode of the compiler of go.starlark.net, and the text would repeat `internal/compile/compile.go`;
- zero options for the predicate: two dialects for one format, and the predicate would not know `set`, which the specification calls built-in;
- the built-in names of the specification, without `chr` and `ord`: a filter in `module-kit` for the sake of two harmless names;
- the limit "more than N", as in the text of format 0.2, whose "more than 1 000 000" and "at most 100 000 000" are off by a step from how go.starlark.net stops: `module-kit` would set `N + 1`, and a second implementation would be off by a step.

— *Does not decide:* the memory of a computation, which go.starlark.net does not bound: how the Starlark of a third-party module runs from stage 4, in a separate process with a memory limit, is О-9.

— *Consequence:* `format/README.md`; `format/vectors/`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `module-kit`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## Versions of a module

**R89. The rules of the version comparison of a module are in the module format, from version 0.3. The version part is found by the comparison of the new version with each version published below it by semver, the withdrawn ones too, and the author may raise it higher but not lower. Major — when something of what the learner of the previous version had is gone or means something else; in 0.y.z the major is played by y. A new meaning of an entry is a new ID. Eight comparison rules, with the prefix `module-version.`, and the index rule `module-index.version-above` refuse a new version, and the comparison vectors are a new kind, `vectors/versions/`, which `spec` computes by a second implementation. The places of the package that the comparison reads, the format holds in all versions, and `diff` compares across a move of the format too. Text — format 0.3, from line 0.9 of `spec`.** `module-kit`'s side is detailed in its `docs/decisions.md` and its `docs/architecture.md`.
- **The version parts:**
  - major — an entry with a full ID is removed — a skill, a task, a lesson, a trap or a technique —, the audience is narrowed, a skill no longer teaches an anchor skill, the check of a task that stayed has changed, and while the format is v0 — also a move to a new format version;
  - minor — everything as before is in place and means the same, and the module gives more or leads differently;
  - patch — the same entries, checks and path, other words or pictures.

  The table "what changes — part" by the fields of the schemas is normative, in the format text. The rows where the principle leaves a judgement — the mark «Выбор» ("Choice") in `module-kit` — are as `module-kit` proposed; a band added after the last one and a change of a band's grades are minor.
- **What is compared** is packages: the canonical view and the list of the device part, not the author's YAML, so comments, the order of keys and `eval/` do not change the version. A slot check is compared by meaning, as its check kind reads it, and a predicate as a string. The instances of a template are matched by the values of the parameters.
- **0.y.z:** the major is played by y, and the minor and the patch by z; in 0.0.z each version is its own major. "The same major" of `diff` and of `api` is one.
- **A new meaning is a new ID:** a published ID of a skill, a task, a lesson, a trap or a technique does not name another entry of its kind, and a band's ID does not name another band.
- **The comparison rules** have the prefix `module-version.`: they refuse a new version, not a module, as the index rules do. The new version is above each published one; it is the next by one of the parts after the newest and not below the part found; each skill of each published version below is in `skills` or in `retired_skills`; the entries of `retired_skills` of the newest stand in the new one too, and `replaced_by` only expands; a new entry of `retired_skills` names a skill of a published version; an ID that is not in the newest does not come back; `languages` are the same; and the bands: each band of a published version stands in the new one in the same place and with the same ID, and a new band stands only after the last one, while the grades of a band may be changed.
- **The bands** keep their places because the recomputation of `learner-model` reads the place of a band in evidence as written and does not open the packages of earlier versions, and the shift of a band on the module's scale is set by its place. The rule requires no new field, and the scale stays one for all versions of the module. Evidence carries the band's ID too beside the place, so a mapping table of bands can come later, as a field of a next format version, if an author needs to rebuild the scale; it holds only while a band's ID does not name another band. The rule refuses both inserting a band easier than the first and removing a band: otherwise only a new module with a new ID changes the scale.
- **The index rule** `module-index.version-above`: a version that is not in the previous index is above each version of its module in it. It catches a release where CI did not run `diff`.
- **The vectors** are `vectors/versions/<case>/`: the new version as a module folder, `module/`; each published version of the same format version as a module's folder too, `published/<X.Y.Z>/`, whose package the reader builds, and a version of a previous format version as the files of its package that every version keeps, `inventory.json` and `server.json`; and the result, `version.yaml` by the schema `version-vector.schema.json` — the part found or a refusal by a rule. `format-check` computes them by a second implementation, and the CI of `module-kit` passes them all.
- **The places in all versions:** in the inventory — `id`, `version` and `server_part` beside `module_format_version`; the names `inventory.json` and `server.json` of a package as files; a digest — `sha256:` and 64 hexadecimal digits, and the package digest is the digest of the bytes of `inventory.json`; in the canonical view — `manifest.languages`, `manifest.bands` with the IDs of the bands in order, `skill_graph` with the keys `skills` and `retired_skills` with their `replaced_by`, and the keys `tasks`, `lessons`, `traps.traps` and `techniques.techniques`. The format holds them in all versions, v0 too, like the members of the index, and a reader reads them in a package of any version by the places. All of them are in the schemas of 0.2, and without `manifest.bands` among them `diff` would not check the rule of bands across a move of the format.
- **All published versions:** `diff` takes the package of each published version of the module, the withdrawn ones too. The rules about skills, `retired_skills`, IDs and bands go over all of them, and the part found and the immutability of `retired_skills` — over the newest; across a move of the format — by the places above. The packages are given by the CI of `modules`.
- **`retired_skills`** in 0.3 only expands: a wrong entry is not corrected. The recomputation of `learner-model` goes by the table of the current version, so a correction is possible, and loosening the rule later is a minor edit of the format. There are no corrections of an old line, below the newest version.

Normative — format 0.3, from line 0.9 of `spec`: the [format text](../format/README.md), its section on versions of a module and its rules on versions, the index and test vectors; the schema of the comparison vectors, `format/vectors/versions/` and `format-check`.

— *Why:* the primary sources were read on 2026-11-02.
- The rules of `diff` were promised to the format text, which waits for them: "the rules it checks come into this text with it". A new rule is a major edit, and in v0 the next 0.y.
- The version of a module is read by `api` — whether to move the learner to the newest version of the same major —, by `learner-model` and by third-party authors from stage 4. The definition must be one, in the format version, not in a release of `module-kit`, and the vectors hold it, as they hold the verdict.
- 0.y.z — as in Cargo: "Initial development releases starting with "0.y.z" can treat changes in "y" as a major release, and "z" as a minor release. "0.0.z" releases are always major changes" (rust-lang/cargo, `doc/book/src/reference/semver.md`, lines 48–51, branch master, commit 6238f6fd61, read 2026-11-02). semver itself says of 0.y.z only "Anything MAY change at any time" (semver/semver, `semver.md`, line 70, read 2026-11-02).
- All published versions and the places in all versions: comparing only with the newest, and across a move of the format checking only the growth of the version, would miss what is gone. The rule "no entry has gone" holds only skills, and the IDs of tasks, lessons, traps and techniques have no table. A skill that is neither in `skills` nor in `retired_skills` of the current version `learner-model` transfers nowhere, and there is no error then. The CI of `modules` compares with all versions too.
- Places, not the whole previous version: the places are few, all are in 0.2, and the format already holds permanent places for the index.
- The bands: if a new version removes or reorders a band or inserts a new one before the earlier ones, the earlier evidence will fall on another scale, and bands have no mapping table, as skills have `retired_skills`.

— *Rejected:*
- into the format — only the rules of `retired_skills`, while the table of the parts and 0.y.z are rules of `module-kit`: "the same major" would stay without a norm for `api`;
- everything stays with `module-kit`: against the promise of the rules of `diff` to the format text;
- comparison only with the newest published version, and across a move of the format only the growth of the version and the review of `modules`;
- `module-kit` reads the whole previous format version for `diff`: two implementations of the parts already in v0, and the package of types `formatv0` changes in place;
- comparison vectors only by a schema, without a second implementation, as the verdict vectors are not;
- a mapping table of bands now: a field without a reader in the first slice;
- no rule of bands: the scale would be found out about once some module had already changed it.

— *Consequence:* `format/README.md`; `format/schemas/version-vector.schema.json`; `format/vectors/versions/`; `tools/format-check/`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `module-kit`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `learner-model`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## Accessibility

**R90. All UI packages — `app`, `canvas` and `skill-map` — have one accessibility standard: WCAG 2.2 level AA and beyond it two AAA criteria — 2.5.5, targets no smaller than 44 × 44 CSS px, and 2.3.3, motion by `prefers-reduced-motion`. What a package does not meet yet it declares itself, and `app` names it on its page "Accessibility". The caption beside an icon is always visible, but on a closed list of buttons that show an icon alone, each with its caption as its accessible name and a tooltip of the same words. The sheet of `canvas` moves under the hand, with no buttons for it.** How `app` arranges the standard is in `app`'s `docs/architecture.md`; the sources are `app`'s `docs/sources.md`, read by `app` 2026-11-02, and sources 3.13.
- **The standard** — [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), W3C Recommendation 12 December 2024, level AA. Beyond it:
  - 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) — "at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels". `canvas` already has such targets, and children of 6–12 hit with a finger worse than adults;
  - 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions — "Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential to the functionality or the information being conveyed": motion that an action starts is turned off by `prefers-reduced-motion`.

  AAA as a whole — no: "It is not recommended that Level AAA conformance be required as a general policy for entire sites because it is not possible to satisfy all Level AAA success criteria for some content". WCAG 3 is a Working Draft, and the standard does not look at it until it is a Recommendation.
- **Declared nonconformances.** A package names in its documents what it does not meet yet — the criterion, what there is instead and when it goes away —, and `app` gathers them on its page "Accessibility", among its legal pages: its own — among them the answer in handwriting, until a second way of answering (О-25) — and those `canvas` declares in its documents, but for 3.1.2 of the name of the sheet's region when the element has no attribute `lang`, which never happens with `app`, since it always sets the attribute. One of `canvas` is 1.4.12: the printing of the workbook's lines does not take the user's text spacing, for the page rule `format/page.yaml` gives no margin for it.
- **The sheet of `canvas`:**
  - it goes past the task's page, right and down, scrolling in two directions — 1.4.10 allows the sheet a two-dimensional layout —, and its bar's "Zoom in" and "Zoom out" step the page's zoom of it from 50 % to 200 %, as a pinch of two fingers sets it: at 200 % the workbook's print is twice its fit, which meets 1.4.4 by the technique G178;
  - it moves by dragging — with the hand under any pointer, with one finger in pen mode, with two fingers always, with a pen only under the hand, since a pen writes —, by the wheel or the trackpad, and by the keyboard. It has no buttons "Up", "Down", "Left" and "Right", and the tables of icons and of words of `docs/architecture.md` have no rows for them. Dragging with one finger meets 2.5.1, which "does not apply to gestures that involve dragging in any direction"; 2.5.7 Dragging Movements is not met — the sheet's own scrolling is "author-provided", and a keyboard is no substitute, by [Understanding 2.5.7](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements.html), read 2026-10-26 —, so `canvas` declares the nonconformance 2.5.7 of moving the sheet, with no term (Д242), and a single-pointer way without dragging comes back only by a change of this entry. The tracing paper of a task from paper moves by dragging its grip, and by the arrow keys on it, and the strokes Select took move or scale by dragging them or a grip alone, beside their copy and their deletion: `canvas` declares the 2.5.7 of both together with the sheet's;
  - the workbook's lines and boxes are in the accessibility tree; the keyboard enters the sheet and leaves it (2.1.2); the bar of tools does not stick when the window is low (1.4.10, 2.4.11); the frames of `exportWork()` do not change with the theme and forced colors;
  - `canvas` runs its own axe-core in CI: the CI of `app` does not check the subtree of the canvas element.
- **`skill-map`:** a text alternative to the graph, `lang` on a skill's name, mastery not only by color (1.4.1), the keyboard, and moving the map without dragging (2.5.7).
- **An own scroll container** of any package — only with `tabindex="0"`, the role `region` and a name: in Safari a container without focusable content cannot be scrolled from the keyboard (WebKit bug [277290](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=277290)).
- **The caption beside an icon** is always visible, and a button's name is its text (2.5.3), but for a closed list, whose buttons show an icon alone:
  - back — on both screens of a task from paper alone at every width, the screen's name its heading unseen —, close, the previous and the next task (‹ ›), Help, and the tutor's button at the right edge of the screen or in the bottom bar of the page to pick from;
  - the tools of the bar of `canvas` — "Pen", "Eraser", "Hand", "Undo", "Clear", "Zoom in", "Zoom out", and on a task from paper the grid's button, named with its grid, as "Grid: dots";
  - the speaker, one icon for two buttons of `app`: "Voicing", the switch in the head of the tutor's panel, pressed or not, and "Read aloud" at a text — the statement of a task or an example, an explanation;
  - in the head of the tutor's panel on a task from paper, the key of grown-up mode, "Grown-up mode", a switch pressed while the mode is on, and in the dialog of the grown-ups' PIN the delete key of its keypad, "Delete";
  - the grabber of the tutor's sheet on a phone, which takes the sheet to the whole screen and back: "Full screen" or "Half screen", by the sheet's state, its target 88 × 44;
  - the buttons of the paper flow: the camera's "Take photo", its flash, named with its mode, as "Flash: auto", and "Choose from photos"; a frame's "Remove the frame" and "Resize your frame"; the crop's grip "Move the task", and atop the tools "Hide the task" or "Show the task", by the crop's state;
  - at the top right of Home, Subjects and the skill map: "Notifications", a bell, and on a phone the profile menu, its avatar alone, named with the pseudonym, as "Sam, profile menu" — the row of a phone has no room for the name beside the tutor's button and the bell;
  - on a module's card of Subjects, "About the module", ⋯ at its top right, by its title: the manifest's facts and Disconnect, so the card says what the module teaches;
  - on a module's card on Home, "Skill map", at its top right; under the field of the tutor's panel, the microphone, "Voice comes later" while it is off — in a child's profile —, and "Send", and in place of both while an answer is awaited "Stop";
  - the places of the row of places of Home, Subjects and the skill map — Home, Subjects, the cognitive map — from 600 CSS px to 72em, each its icon alone but the place shown, which keeps its words; the cognitive map, shut, has at every width the tooltip "Cognitive map — comes later", its name with why it waits. Below 72em the places' words do not fit one row beside the pills of the top right.
  - where its bar does not fit one row with its words: on the page to pick from, "Remove all frames" and "Retake"; on the solving screen of a task from paper, the tutor's button "Ask" beside Hint; the row is measured, as each language's words differ, and the buttons go below only where icons alone do not fit.

  A button of the list has its caption from the package's table of captions as its accessible name, and a tooltip with the same words on hover and keyboard focus, which can be dismissed, stays while the pointer is over it and hides no content it does not have to (1.4.13). An action keeps its visible caption — Hint, Check, Continue, Done, and "Next" and "Demo" of a worked example, which stand beside "Continue". A phone has no button "More" for the tools of `canvas`: the vertical bar fits a width of 320 CSS px. «…» of the canvas kinds of other authors waits for its screen, with the widgets of third-party authors. A button joins the list only by a change of this entry.
- **The wavy line of "Show where"**, the tutor's mark of a task from paper, holds 1.4.11, 3:1, against the sheet, by the contrast of the interface mockup ([draft/mockup/README.md](../draft/mockup/README.md)); the tick and the cross by each answer of a frame of several tasks hold it against their white halo.

— *Why:* the task screen is put together by `app` and `canvas`, and the screen has one level. `app` cannot oblige another repository, and `spec` can. The standard is chosen by the learners, not by the law: the markets of the beta are not chosen, and what the accessibility laws mean for NovaTrail is П-25. WCAG 2.2 AA covers WCAG 2.1 AA, which the laws name where they name a level, except 4.1.1 Parsing — in 2.2 it is "Obsolete and removed" (`app`'s `docs/sources.md`). The page rule gives no margin for spacing because a margin of 0.12 of the font size per character — more than a fifth of the width of a digit, 0.53 of the font size (`format/page.yaml`) — would shorten the workbook's lines for all learners, and on an area wider than the page the browser's zoom enlarges the printing. 2.5.3 Label in Name does not apply where there is no visible label, and 4.1.2 asks that the name can be programmatically determined, which the caption as the accessible name gives (sources 3.13); the list is closed, so that an icon alone stays where its meaning is common and a word would cover the sheet, the page or the camera's image. The tooltip is the package's own and holds 1.4.13. Four arrows took half of the bar, on a tablet the sheet is moved by the hand, and the two-finger scrolling exists already; a table that named the arrows would send `app` to words and icons no package draws. A grabber is the common sign of a sheet that grows, and a word would cover the sheet's head. `app` already shows a speaker for voicing and for reading a text aloud, and a word beside each text would crowd its card. Buttons wrapped to a second row would cover the photographed page. On the two screens of a task from paper the tutor's button stands in the bottom bar, among the learner's actions, and leaves the right of the page and of the sheet free: on the page to pick from as an icon, beside the selection and Start; on the solving screen with its word "Ask" beside Hint, both of them help, which the learner looks for at one moment, and the word goes, as the top bar's do, only where the row does not fit.

— *Rejected:*
- each package has its own level, and `app` answers for the screen as a whole: `app` would learn of a package's nonconformance last;
- WCAG 2.2 AA without AAA: targets could become 24 × 24 CSS px — 2.5.8, "at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels", — too small for a child's finger;
- a margin for spacing by a new version of `format/page.yaml`;
- for 1.4.4 of the workbook's printing, a scale of the page beyond the fit in `app`'s settings — the bar's zoom gives it on every sheet;
- a list of the nonconformances of all packages in this entry: a package declares them in its documents;
- captions on every icon; dropping the closed list and holding WCAG alone; a visible caption "Tutor" on the tutor's button; a caption "Read aloud" beside each text;
- the buttons "Up", "Down", "Left" and "Right" kept, or behind one button "Move" that opens them in a pop-over — a new button of the list; their rows kept in the tables of icons and of words until `app` takes the release of `canvas` without them;
- a button "More" for the tools of a phone;
- the page to pick from's buttons in a second row, or a breakpoint of width;
- on the screens of a task from paper, the name beside back where it fits — it ran into the pen's popover —; the tutor's button back at the right edge, over the page and the sheet; "Ask" keeping its word always, the bottom bar wrapping on a phone;
- no grabber — the sheet at half the height alone, with no way to the whole screen.

— *Consequence:* `docs/product.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `draft/mockup/README.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

**R91. The rules of translations of the UI packages — `app`, `canvas` and `skill-map` — are shared, and each package has its own tables of translations. The words that more than one package shows are the table of words in `docs/architecture.md`, and `spec` keeps it. The names of anchor skills stay English for now, with their own `lang="en"`.** How `app` arranges translations is in `app`'s `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/architecture.md`.
- **The shared rules:**
  - the language of a package's captions is the attribute `lang` on the element itself, and the element does not read the language of an ancestor;
  - the language in the package's table is looked up by truncating the tag, as the Lookup of [RFC 4647](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647) does, and one not found is English, and the fallback caption has its own `lang`;
  - placeholders are by name, not by concatenating strings: the order of words differs between languages. "Part 2 of 4." is one string with two placeholders, not "Part", a number, "of" and a number;
  - the plural forms are the categories of CLDR, and `other` is always there;
  - a string does not give away the learner's gender and does not speak in the first person of AI;
  - each package carries each interface language — now `en` and `ru`.
- **The table of words** — in `docs/architecture.md`: the value, its words in `en` and `ru`, and the packages that show it. The first rows are the captions of the buttons of the row of `canvas`: the strings of `app` speak of them too. A word that a second package needed enters the table as a row «в реестр spec», like a value of the table of icons, and the words of one package go in its documents.
- **The names of anchor skills** are the English text of the schema `shared-taxonomy.schema.json`. A package sets them with their own `lang="en"`, as `app` does. Whether to translate them into the interface languages and where the translations lie is a question of its own, when it is needed: it touches the shared taxonomy and the format.
- **The examples of `spec`** write what the learner sees, without the first person of AI and without gender: «Прочитано: 6» ("Read:" and the number), not «Я прочитал 6» ("I read" and the number).

— *Why:* a screen that several packages put together must speak the same way, and the table of captions of `canvas` waited for a shared scheme. A package cannot take code from `app`, and `@altnovatrail/spec` lies in a consumer's `devDependencies`, so only the rules can be shared. The table of words is `spec`'s, not in the glossary of `app`: a document of another repository does not oblige the packages, and the shared choice of the UI packages is already held by the table of values of icons. The names of anchor skills are a part of the format, and an anchor skill has no explanation language: their translation would require a place for translations in the format.

— *Rejected:*
- a shared package of the code of translations — one more package with its own release;
- the packages' captions are given by `app`: each consumer would translate the captions, and the samples page too;
- the shared words — by the glossary of `app`: a glossary of another repository would oblige the packages;
- the names of anchor skills are translated into the interface languages already now: that is an edit of the shared taxonomy and of the format without a question of its own.

— *Consequence:* `docs/product.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`.

## Interface language

**R92. The interface languages are `en` and `ru`. A learner's interface language is a field of their profile, which an adult sets, and the screens before a learner is chosen and the section for adults are in the device's language. The contract carries any valid BCP 47 tag, without a list of languages, and texts from `api` `app` requests by naming the language in the request. The interface language does not go into an AI call.** How `app` arranges it is in `app`'s `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/architecture.md`.
- **The languages** are `en` and `ru`, by the recommendation of О-2. A new interface language is a matter of stage 5 of the product, and each UI package carries it.
- **The profile field** "interface language" is set and changed by an adult in the section for adults, and the learner has no switch: an accidental tap would take a child into a language they do not read. No field — the device's language. A tag that the build of `app` does not know it looks up by truncation, then takes the device's language, then English, and does not overwrite the field.
- **The device's language** is for the screens before a learner is chosen — sign-in, choosing the learner, getting started, the failure screens — and for the section for adults: the sign-in screen is seen before the account, and an adult may read in another language than the child. It is the adult's choice on this device, and without a choice the browser's language.
- **The contract** carries the language as a BCP 47 tag, without a list: which languages the build knows is its property, not `api`'s, and a new language does not change the contract. Texts from `api` — the legal texts and the consent — `app` gets by `LegalService.GetLegalTexts`, naming the language in a field of the request, not by the header `Accept-Language`, as the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md) sets it.
- **The legal texts** are in English, and the English text is in force. A text version may have translations into the interface languages, as the part `legal/` holds them — version 2 of `privacy-policy` has one into Russian —, and `GetLegalTexts` gives, beside the English text, the translation into the language the request names, in `translation` and `translation_language`. A translation has no force: a consent names the version, not the translation.
- **To AI** the interface language does not go: the tutor speaks in the module's explanation language. `docs/privacy.md` names the purpose of the field so: in which language the screen speaks with the learner.
- **Before the first attempt** `app` gets the name and the explanation language of the connected modules: the module's card names the explanation language if it is not the screen's language.

— *Why:* the language is in the learner's profile: the learner learns on other devices too, and on a shared tablet each child may have their own. The explanation languages are a question of content, which `modules` writes, so О-2 is resolved only in its part about the interface.

— *Rejected:*
- О-2 is closed whole, and the explanations in the slice are only English: a Russian-speaking child of 6–12 would get tasks in English;
- the interface language is on the device, and `spec` does not know it: all children of a shared tablet would have one language, and on another device the learner would see another one;
- the method of the legal texts only together with the contract of consent.

— *Does not decide:* the explanation languages of the slice's modules and the decimal comma — the format reads `1,5` as two numbers ([format text](../format/README.md)). They stay in О-2, with `modules` and product.

— *Consequence:* `docs/product.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `legal/README.md`.

## The sample file

**R93. The sample file is the message `Sample` of the package `novatrail.eval.v1`, the first message of the eval protocol: one JSON to a sample, without the task's key.
