- `cap_reached`: the account's cap closes platform AI to a learner whose own share is below 100, who would otherwise learn it only from the refusal "quota" of a beginning, which comes with no call of AI and tells as much;
- whole percent, since the share is shown to people and the sum stays hidden; rounded down, so that 100 is the cap reached; the settled spending, so that the share only grows within a day and a reserve that settles lower never shows the cap reached for a moment; `can_view`, since the adult views the share and changes nothing; the service of the account, since the tariff and the counters are the account's.

— *Rejected:*
- a slice without children, where the child's profile is wholly in a later epic;
- a minimum for erasing — sign-in, the list of profiles, "account gone" and deletion —, with the PIN, the key and export written by other tasks;
- the child's profile at once, and learning after consent: the server would store the child's pseudonym before consent;
- interests as a list of codes now: there is no dictionary of codes, and nobody to read them;
- one "create a profile" for the owner and the child: the child's inputs are the age and consent, the owner's — a statement;
- replacing the profile as a whole on a change; `google.protobuf.FieldMask` — in JSON its paths go in lowerCamelCase, and the contract keeps the names of proto;
- the tariff in the response about the account now: there are no tariffs yet (О-14);
- a separate method "is the sign-in fresh": `app` has `authTime` anyway;
- the version of `api` in each response, by which `app` would reload no more than once per version of `api`: rejected before — a contract's version is its package and the tag of `spec`, and within a major package an old build of `app` works with a new `api`;
- the limit of consents before the way out of it, removing a waiting one; no limit; `invalid_argument` without `Refusal` as the contract's response beyond the limit — this is a refusal of the form of the request, and `app` would not say what to do;
- the share of the quota as a field in the responses of other methods; dropping the learner's share from `docs/concepts.md`;
- the share of the profile alone, the account's cap met as a refusal; the larger of the two shares for the learner, by which a child would see what the family spends.

— *Consequence:* `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/account.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/cause.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/attempt.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `api`'s `docs/architecture.md`.

**R99. The path from a module to a task in the contract `app` ↔ `api` is four services of the package `novatrail.api.v1`: `PackageService` — the open views of the manifest, of the skill graph with tiers, of the technique catalog and of the solving steps by the package digest, without a token, and the request about withdrawal; `ModuleService` — the catalog and the connected modules; `LearningService` — the engine choice, the beginning and the open attempt, and lessons by lesson runs; `ProgressService` — the skill map, the adult's progress and the adult's correction of a module's level. An open view is the bytes of the format's JSON with the format version beside them. An engine's choice goes by the route to AI of the request that gives it. The response that closes an attempt says what comes next, and a trap repeats when two closed attempts of the profile have found it.** Normative — [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md).
- **The scope** is both the adult's progress and the state of skills for the map — by the fields that `Read` of `learner-model` gives, before `skill-map` is detailed. What the map needs beyond this comes as a field.
- **The open view** — `OpenView`: the bytes of the format's JSON and beside them `module_format_version`, like the solution of a task. `app` and `api` read it by the format's types `open`, and by the version `app` decides whether it will read the view, or offers to reload.
- **By the digest, without a token** — `PackageService`: `GetManifest`, `GetSkillGraph` — with the tiers `skill_tiers` —, `GetTechniques` and `GetSolvingSteps`, with the level `NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`, Connect GET without headers, by any package that the image of `api` gives. The refusals are "the image does not give the version" and "digest unknown", while a deployment goes on; for a part that the module does not have — a response without a view.
- **The files of the device part** — HTTP GET at the address of `api`, the path `/packages/sha256-<hex>/device/<path>`, without a token and headers: `200`, `404`, `410` and `503` with `Retry-After`. `sha256-<hex>` is as the name of the package's archive in the release of `modules`, and the path is as in the device part of a package as files, by the [format text](../format/README.md). This is a proposal of the plan.
- **Withdrawal** — `CheckPackages`: `app` names the digests it holds, from the account and without the ID of a profile, and for each gets "gives", "no longer gives" or "unknown". It asks at start and after the refusal "the image does not give the version" or the response `410`.
- **Modules** — `ModuleService`, with the right `can_learn`:
  - the catalog — the modules of the pinned index whose current version suits the profile by audience and which the deployment's list of modules names, when it has one; the explanation language does not select;
  - connecting and disconnecting — without a version;
  - the connected modules — with the digest of the current version, and for a module without one — without a digest.

  The open view of the manifest carries `title` and `languages.explanation`: the title and the explanation language before the first attempt `app` takes from it by this digest. A module without a current version has no digest, and so no manifest: `app` names it by the title from the manifest of the previous version, if it has it, otherwise by the ID. This is a proposal of the plan.
- **The engine choice** — `EngineChoice`: the ID of the choice and what it gives — a lesson or a task; or "nothing to give" with the outcome — the quota, the platform's limit or "not admitted", when the AI that checks the tasks is closed to the learner. A choice is given by `ChooseNext`, by the response that closed an attempt outside a lesson, and by the end of a lesson run on request. The choice itself begins nothing.
- **The route of a choice.** A choice goes by the route to AI of the request that gives it — by `ChooseNext`, in `next` of the answers that close an attempt and in the end of a lesson run alike: `ChooseNextRequest` carries `own_key_provider`, as `BeginAttemptRequest` does, empty on platform AI, and `api` judges the engine's pool and "nothing to give" by that route, so that a choice gives nothing that the beginning would refuse. On the own key "nothing to give" comes with `CAUSE_NOT_ADMITTED` alone.
- **The reason code of the choice** is the closed list `ReasonCode`, and only the adult's progress carries it, the field `reason_code` of `AttemptRecord`; `EngineChoice` and the other responses to learning requests carry no code: a child is not told the code, and a field that nobody reads, minimization does not allow.
- **An attempt** — `BeginAttempt`: by the choice of a task, by a segment of a lesson run, or "again" — the same task outside a lesson, on the current version; with the provider of the own key, without the key. The response is the ID of the attempt, the open view of the task and the package digest, and the seed does not go out. `GetOpenAttempt` gives the open attempt on another device too. The choice of a task begins one attempt, and a second request by it gets "already exists", `CAUSE_ALREADY_EXISTS`, — as the choice of a lesson opens one lesson run. The provider at the beginning decides only the checks of the beginning, and each next request goes by its own key, which it carries, — these are proposals of the review.
- **What comes next** — the field `next` in the responses of `SubmitWork`, `ShowSolution` and `Done`, which close an attempt: in a lesson — the place of the next segment or "no more segments", outside a lesson — the engine choice.
- **Lessons:**
  - `OpenLesson` — by a choice, `GetLessonRun` — by the ID of the lesson run, `CompleteLesson` — "lesson passed";
  - the response is `LessonRun`: the ID of the lesson run, the open view of the lesson, the package digest, the places of the task segments that have ended and the open attempt of a segment;
  - the run end reasons — `RunEndReason`: passed, unchecked, not suitable, abandoned. "Early" is no value: the first slice of `engine` has no early end, and the value comes as an addition when one does;
  - `app` keeps the state of a lesson by the key "ID of the lesson, package digest", without the ID of the lesson run, and the contract has it discard the state of another lesson run under the same key;
  - a choice opens one lesson run, and only a new choice begins a new one. This is a proposal of the plan.
- **The profile** — the open attempt and the open lesson runs, `open_attempt` and `open_lesson_runs`: so a device without their state finds the lesson and the attempt.
- **The skill map** — `GetSkillMap`, as a learning action with `can_learn` or an adult action with the right `can_view`, — by two kinds of action:
  - the state of the skills of the current version, as `Read` of `learner-model` reads it: the number of evidence and the time of the last practice, the estimate with uncertainty and retention, the mastery band, the cautious probability and the review date;
  - the state of the anchor skills: knows, does not know or unknown, with the cause and the skills that teach it, and the modules of the catalog that teach it, `teaching_modules` of `AnchorSkillState`: the modules of the index pinned in `api` whose current version suits the profile by audience and names the anchor in `teaches`, except those connected to the profile, by ID, at any state of the anchor. The selection is that of the catalog, `ListCatalog`; the connected modules are left out, since their skills that teach the anchor are already in `teaching_skills`, and the proposal is a connection, `ConnectModule`. The list does not depend on the model, so the field is there at any state of the anchor, at which one to show it `app` decides, and how to show it, `app` and `skill-map`. There is no new kind of data: the profile gets the catalog anyway, `api` has the age category, and the field does not go to the AI;
  - the band of each connected module's level, `level_band`, and when an adult last set it, `level_set_at`, which every learner sees.

  There are no traps on the map: the trap catalog is closed.
- **Progress** — `GetProgress`, with the right `can_view`, by pages:
  - attempts from new to old — the task, the version, the lesson, the close reason, the incorrect answers, the time, and for a task with a rubric — the marks of the criteria;
  - the titles of an attempt, `lesson_title` and `skill_titles`: the title of its lesson whenever `lesson` is set, for an open attempt and a closed one, and the titles of the task's skills for a solved attempt alone, closed by a correct answer, by the solution shown or by "Done". The skills are the primary skills of the task's items, each item's own or else the task's, each once, in the order of the items. Both come from the package of the version the attempt went on, in the module's explanation language, empty when `api` no longer reads that package. Which skills, and the empty titles, are proposals of the executor;
  - repeating traps — on the first page — found in two closed attempts of the profile or more, by the full ID, with `description` and `trap_advice` of the catalog of the version of the last of them, the number of attempts and the time of the last one. Attempts on a version withdrawn as `wrong_key` do not count toward traps — this is a proposal of the plan, and the first page is a proposal of the review;
  - the last correction of each module's level, `level_settings`, on the first page.
- **The correction of a module's level** — `SetModuleLevel`, the third method of `ProgressService`, by an action of an adult with the right `can_manage`, at every profile of the account. It names the profile, a connected module and the band to set the level in — the band next to the band of the level, easier or harder, by the order of the bands of the manifest of the current version, and the lowest band while the level stands below it. A band that is neither the band of the level nor next to it is refused `CAUSE_BAND_NOT_NEXT`, and a request that names the band of the level already appends nothing: it repeats by the state of the profile, with no idempotency key, as the other requests of `ProgressService` do. These are the executor's proposals, made with nobody to ask.
  - **Consent:** a profile whose consent is not confirmed is refused `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT`, and one whose age is to be given again `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED`, as a learning request is: the fact is processing of the learner's data, and a learner whose country raised its age of digital consent may no longer consent alone.
  - **The ends of the scale:** no band comes before the lowest, so at the lowest band "Easier" has nothing to name; the start below it and the guard still put the level there. Above the highest band the band of the level is the highest. A band keeps its place and its ID in every version, by the module format, so the current manifest always names it.
  - **Data:** nothing new beyond the correction itself: the fact, the band set and its time are in `docs/privacy.md` and `docs/dpia.md`, and a level per module is already among the model's outputs there; the device gets the band of the level, which the estimates of the skills on the band scale already show, and the date of the correction, which every learner is to see.
- **Causes** — the values of `Cause`, by the table of causes in `api`'s `docs/architecture.md`: "the image does not give the version", "digest unknown", "no current version", "not suitable", "lesson run ended", "segments not ended", "segment unavailable" and, for the correction of a level, `CAUSE_BAND_NOT_NEXT`. The data of a refusal are the end of the lesson run with a choice and the places of the segments that have ended: so the engine choice and the end of a lesson run lie in `cause.proto`, since the data of `Refusal` carry them and protobuf does not allow a cycle of imports.
- **The version.** The field `teaching_modules`, and for the correction of a level a method, two fields, a message and a value of `Cause`, are only added to `novatrail.api.v1`: `buf breaking` `FILE` lets them pass, the change comes out in any release of the line, an old build of `app` skips the field, and an older one reads the cause by its code.
- **There is no clock offset** at "begin an attempt" and "something else": they do not call the AI, and `api` keeps the family day on the account.

— *Why:*
- the progress and the state of skills for the map in one contract: what the map needs beyond the fields of `Read` comes as a field;
- the bytes of JSON: one schema, the format's, and the solution of a task already goes out so;
- two closed attempts: the traps of the first batch of modules have no `skills`, and the model will not count them by skill, and the rule in the contract text tells `app` what the word by which it captions the list means;
- the catalog by audience: the profile has no languages of the learner, and the module's card names the explanation language precisely for a module in another language;
- tiers with the graph: tiers are a property of the package, not of the learner, and by the digest they are cached together with the graph. So `api` writes too, that `app` takes the graph and the tiers by the digest of the current version;
- one lesson run per choice: the engine chooses a lesson or a task, and an old choice would not begin a new lesson run past it;
- the modules that teach an anchor as a field of the map: `api` proposes such a module, and the device does not read the index, so without the field nobody would see the proposal;
- the route of a choice by its request: a choice that ignored it would give what the beginning of an attempt on that route refuses;
- the skills' titles of a solved attempt alone: on the owner profile the adult and the learner are one person, and an attempt open, left, abandoned or unchecked may be begun again — "again", or by its segment —, so its skills would be a hint. A supporting skill is no skill the task trains, and a module that `api` no longer reads gives no titles;
- the band, not a step, in the correction of a level: "Harder" sent twice would move the level two bands; the band named moves it once, and the second request finds the level in it;
- the band of the level on the map: `app` needs it to offer the two bands next to it, and the learner's screen calls `GetSkillMap`, not `GetProgress`, which the adult alone views: so the learner sees the correction there. `learner-model` gives the band by `Read`.

— *Rejected:*
- the state of skills for the map, and the map and progress, in a later part of the contract after `skill-map` is detailed, so that no field of `v1`, which cannot be removed, is written before it;
- the canonical text of RFC 8785 instead of JSON — this property has no consumer; protobuf messages of its own — a second schema beside the format's schemas; `google.protobuf.Struct` — without types, and numbers are `double`;
- "frequent traps" of the state of a skill of `learner-model`; the threshold of repetition as a constant of `api`;
- the catalog by the interface language; the field "languages" in the profile;
- tiers in the list of connected modules: they would repeat in each response of the list;
- the reason code in `EngineChoice` or another response to the learner;
- `teaches` in `CatalogModule`, with `app` matching it against the map — the matching would go to the device, and the proposal of a module is `api`'s; the connected modules in the list of `teaching_modules` — they would repeat `teaching_skills`; no field until stage 2 — the proposal of a module that teaches an anchor would have no place;
- for the route of a choice: no narrowing for an owner profile, with a refusal at the beginning — `api` cannot know whether the device holds a key; nothing until the own key — `app` needs the field;
- the titles of the skills always, or at every closed attempt; a title of the task, which touches the format, the contract and the modules;
- in the correction of a level: "Easier" and "Harder" as a direction in the request, with an idempotency key — a key `api` records for one fact, where the band makes the repeat safe by itself; the band of the level in `GetProgress` alone — the learner would not see it; a value of `band` for "below the lowest band" — the fact would name no band, and the engine gives the lowest band's tasks there anyway; a repeat held to the first request's level by a key, when the band chosen is what the adult asked for.

— *Consequence:* `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/package.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/module.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/learning.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/progress.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/cause.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/attempt.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/account.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `format/README.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`.

## Format 0.3

**R101. Format 0.3 comes out whole — its text, the second implementation and the vectors at once — and opens the line 0.9 of `spec`. The rules of version comparison are in the [format text](../format/README.md), with the prefix `module-version.`, and the vectors `vectors/versions/`: a published version in them is a module's folder, and a version of the previous format version is a package as files. The parts of the rows «Выбор» are as `module-kit` proposed; a band after the last and the grades of a band are a minor change; an entry of `retired_skills` in 0.3 only expands. The vectors at the boundary of the steps of a predicate and of a solver were given by a measurement on the pinned version of go.starlark.net.** Normative — [the format text](../format/README.md).
- **Whole.** It is more than one check: a new part of the text with a table and eight rules, a second implementation of the comparison, 152 vectors of comparison and the move of the examples and vectors to 0.3.
- **The line 0.9** — a new format version opens a new line of `spec`, and the line 0.8 was already open.
- **The prefix** is `module-version.`: the rules refuse a new version, not a module, and they have vectors of their own, like the rules of the index. Eight rules — `above`, `step`, `retired-complete`, `retired-kept`, `retired-known`, `ids-kept`, `languages-kept` and `bands-kept`: the seven that `module-kit` proposed, and the rule of bands.
- **The vectors of comparison** — `vectors/versions/<case>/`: `module/` is the new version, `published/<X.Y.Z>/` — each published one, and `version.yaml`, by the schema `version-vector.schema.json`, — the `version_part` found or the `refusal`. A published version of the same format version is a module's folder: the reader builds its package, and what changed is seen in the YAML. A version of the previous format version is the files of its package that every version keeps, `inventory.json` and `server.json`; the package was built by the reader of 0.2. The reader of 0.3 will not read a module folder of 0.2, and these files it reads by the places that every version keeps: a later version may change the canonical text and the device part. That there is no `device.json` in the vector is a proposal of the review.
- **The table of parts** — by the fields of the schemas of 0.3, by the table of parts in `module-kit`'s `docs/architecture.md` (`main` 19c33aa). The rows «Выбор» are as `module-kit` proposed, with two changes for 0.3: a band removed, renamed, moved or inserted before the earlier ones is refused by `module-version.bands-kept`, and the refinement of `languages.target`, `es` → `es-419`, by `module-version.languages-kept`.
- **Bands:** a band after the last is minor, the grades of a band are minor. Everything earlier is in its place, and only the starting band of a new learner changes: the module "leads otherwise".
- **`retired_skills`** in 0.3 only expands. A wrong entry could be corrected by loosening `module-version.retired-kept` — by a minor version of the format: the modules of 0.3 would stay valid.
- **The boundaries of steps** — a measurement in the session's folder on go.starlark.net `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d`, in the format's dialect: the predicate through `EvalExprOptions`, the solver through `ExecFileOptions` and `Call`. The harness did not get into the repository.
  - The predicate `value in [n * n for n in range(99997)]` takes 999,990 steps at any value: for 49 — `correct`. With `range(99998)` the count reaches 1,000,000, and the evaluation stops: `unchecked` at any value. These are the verdict vectors `predicate/steps-below-the-limit` and `predicate/steps-reach-the-limit`.
  - A solver with a loop of 9,999,996 turns on one instance takes 99,999,990 steps — 10 at the top level and 99,999,980 for the call —, and with 9,999,997 turns it reaches 100,000,000. These are the template vector `within-the-budget` and the vector `task.template-solver/reaches-the-budget`.
  - A check against `module-kit`'s measurement: a simple predicate is 20 steps. The call of `solve` of the vector `past-the-budget-of-the-template` with 2,000,000 turns is 20,000,020 steps, and the count reaches the budget on the fifth of 64 instances.

  To reach the limit, a predicate needs a list comprehension, and the rule `task.predicate-expression` did not name its variable. So the [format text](../format/README.md) now lets in the names that the expression binds itself.
- **The proposals of the plan:**
  - a new entry of `retired_skills` is a major change, even when the skill is already absent from the newest version: this is a hole in the history before `diff`;
  - `module-version.step` is checked only for a version that passed `module-version.above`, and a change that a rule refuses gives no part of its own: so a case of refusal breaks one rule;
  - "not changed" — the newest published version with the same package digest: the part `none`, and there is no comparison. The same version with another digest is the refusal `module-version.above`, not `module-index.one-package`, as `module-kit` proposed: the rule of the index refuses the build of the index;
  - proposals of the review: `replaced_by` is a set, and its order changes nothing; the text gives the part of a move of the format only while the format is v0, and `format-check` does not count it further; the files of the package of the previous format version are only those that every version keeps;
  - the text pins down what the second implementation counts:
    - items, answer slots and segments of a lesson are compared by place, and a task segment also by the ID of the task;
    - solving steps — by the number and the pairs "what it gives, as a set, — exit condition";
    - age categories and `digit_height` — in the form in force;
    - units — after steps 1–5 and lowercase letters;
    - the skills of a task and of an item — as sets by roles.

— *Why:*
- whole: a merge itself releases, and the text of 0.3 comes out already checked by the second implementation and the vectors. An error of a rule found after the release would be corrected only by 0.4 with the line 0.10;
- a prefix of its own: a part's rule is checked by vectors in `vectors/rules/<id>/`, and a case of comparison is not a module;
- the module folders: the published versions are read the same way as the new one, and a package as files is needed only where the reader will not read the folder;
- the measurement now: without vectors at the boundary, the format's "the count reaches N" would be held by no vector, and the code of `module-kit` begins with them.

— *Rejected:*
- splitting: the text of 0.3 and the line first, and the second implementation and the vectors after, as an editorial change in the line 0.9. The text of 0.3 would come out without the second implementation, and `module-kit` would wait for the second part or move to a tag twice;
- a prefix by parts, as `module-kit` proposed — `manifest.version-above`, `skill-graph.retired-complete`, `module.ids-kept`: such rules would mix with the rules of a module;
- the published versions always as packages of files: the canonical text is one line of JSON, and what changed between versions cannot be read in the vector;
- the grades of a band as a patch: a patch changes only words and pictures. Both changes of bands as major: `api` would not move the learner itself, though nothing of the learner's was lost;
- correcting `retired_skills` by a major version of the module: the rule and the vectors are more complex, and the correction has no reader in the first slice;
- the vectors at the boundary later, by a row «в реестр spec» from the CI of `module-kit`, as an editorial change in the line 0.9.

— *Consequence:* `format/README.md`; `format/VERSION`; `format/schemas/`; `format/vectors/`; `format/examples/`; `tools/format-check/versions.mjs`; `tools/format-check/index.mjs`; `tools/format-check/test/`; `types/formatv0/`; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `README.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `RUN.md`.

## Answers to the format code of `module-kit`

**R102. What the code of format 0.3 of `module-kit` found, `spec` pins down so: without a new version of the format — by a vector, by a refinement that the rules of the text hold, or by a change of the second implementation, in epic E7; and the new rules — the refusal of a character outside the printable set of YAML in quotes, the beginning and the depth of template expressions, the refusal of a previous index that the build will not read — in format 0.4, in epic E6. The schemas at run time `module-kit` keeps as a copy of its own, and the form of calling its commands — in its own documents. The kind `go` of the template gives gopls from a lock file and the Claude Code plugin `gopls-lsp`.** The claims were checked against [YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/), sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4, and [WHATWG MIME Sniffing](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/), 6.2.3, read 2026-11-06, and the divergences of `tools/format-check/yaml.mjs` were shown by a trial on its code. Normative — [the format text](../format/README.md) and [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md).
- **Without a new version of the format** — epic E7, as an editorial change in the line 0.9:
  - **YAML 1.2.2 in `yaml.mjs`** — `tools/format-check/yaml.mjs` reads by YAML 1.2.2 the three places where it diverged from it: the line break CR (5.4) it accepts; `...` at the beginning of a stream it does not count as an empty document; U+FEFF in a plain and a block scalar and in a comment it rejects as "not YAML" — `nb-char` excludes it —, and in quotes it accepts it, as YAML 1.2.2 does. This is a change of the second implementation, not of the format: so YAML 1.2.2 and `module-kit` read it;
  - **The signature of an MP3 without ID3** is four bytes of the frame header, as in WHATWG MIME Sniffing, 6.2.3: "If length is less than 4, return false". The [format text](../format/README.md) says this outright, and the vector `module.media` holds a file `.mp3` of three bytes `FF FB 90`, which the rule rejects. This is a refinement that the rule holds: the text gives the signatures "as WHATWG gives them", and both implementations already require four bytes;
  - **Runs of non-starters** — the [format text](../format/README.md), beside the reservation about the version of Unicode, says that the vectors hold no runs longer than 30 non-starter characters in a row, and the result of normalization on them is a matter of the reader's release: `golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm` goes with the Stream-Safe Text Process ([UAX #15](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr15/), section 13) and after 30 such characters inserts U+034F, and ICU does not;
  - **A unit before the final character** — the verdict vector `number` with the unit `rungs` holds the letter of steps 5–7: `7 rungs .` — outside the notation, and `7 rungs.` and `7 .` — correct;
  - **Frozen globals of a solver** — the [format text](../format/README.md) says that the global values of a solver's program are frozen when its top level has run, as the Starlark specification says ("Immediately after execution of a Starlark module, all values in its top-level environment are frozen", `doc/spec.md` of go.starlark.net 4f4267fb140d), and the vector `task.template-solver` holds a `solve` that appends to a global list and fails. This is the meaning of the language that the text refers to, not a new rule;
  - **`open_view_digest` in the vectors** — the field in the vectors `open-view/` of a task and at the attempts of the vectors `templates/`, for an instance — with the numbers substituted, as the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md) sets it. The CI of `spec` and of `module-kit` check it, and the eval runner of `tutor` will check itself against the vector, not against `module-kit`;
  - **`UNCHECKED_CAUSE_CHECK`** — the cause in `UncheckedCause` of the package `novatrail.eval.v1`: the predicate of the check gave no verdict on a valid observation — it failed on the value, reached the limit of steps or the clock of `module-kit`. The [contracts text](../contracts/README.md) names it beside the others, and the measure "Unchecked" by cause does not blame the model for a flaw of the predicate. A new value only adds to the enum;
  - **A value not in UTF-8** — the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md) names it a condition of an invalid observation: the answer slots of the AI get `unchecked`, and the learner "unchecked", not a refusal of the server. This changes no message of the contract: proto3 carries no such string, and only a Go structure within one process of `api` and `tutor` can meet it;
  - **gopls of the kind `go`** — by the key `devcontainer` of the kind in `repo-template/kinds.json`: it names the folder `repo-template/kinds/go/`, whose `Dockerfile` is the lines of the stage `devcontainer`, before the step of Claude Code, and the rest — the lock file `gopls/go.mod` and `gopls/go.sum` — the copy gets in `.devcontainer/` as it is. The step is the same as at `module-kit`, `engine` and `learner-model`: gopls at the version that `GOPLS_VERSION` in `repo-template/kinds/go/Dockerfile` names and the lock file pins, `go install -mod=readonly tool` and a check of `gopls version` by the whole line. The version is the latest by the Go proxy (`https://proxy.golang.org/golang.org/x/tools/gopls/@latest`) when it was taken: the lock file was built anew by `go get -tool golang.org/x/tools/gopls@vX.Y.Z` on the Go of the toolchain, `GO_VERSION` in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, and matched the lock file of `module-kit` byte for byte. The kind also gives three settings of the Go extension in `devcontainer.json`, and a comment at `context`. `spec` keeps the version of gopls. The version in the lock file and `GOPLS_VERSION` are held to each other by the test of `new-repo` in the files of the kind and by `new-repo-check` in the copy; their own `ci-lint` stays the repositories' business. `_go-modules` in `justfile` does not count the template's lock file as a module of `spec`. A repository's move to a tag is by hand: `.devcontainer/` is taken from what the recipe builds, and the repository's differences are put in again — gopls now comes with it;
  - **The plugin `gopls-lsp`** — by the key `claudePlugins` of the kind `go` the copy loads the Claude Code plugin through `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` in `containerEnv` of its devcontainer, and the plugin runs the gopls that the step above builds.
- **Format 0.4** — in epic E6, together with what the first content of `modules` asked for:
  - **Characters outside the printable set** — the [format text](../format/README.md) names the refusal of a character outside the printable set of [YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/), section 5.1, wherever it stands, in quotes too. The format's YAML rules and both implementations already rejected it as "not YAML", and YAML 1.2.2 tells a processor to accept in quotes all characters outside C0, and by the letter of the text of 0.3 such a file was valid;
  - **The beginning and the depth of a template expression** — a template expression begins with a token and is nested no deeper than 64 levels — a bracket, a unary `-` or `not` —, `format-check` checks the same, and the vectors `task.template-expressions` hold both cases. The limit of 64 is with a margin below what the format's go.starlark.net parses — about 75 brackets —, so every expression of the subset is parsed by the dialect;
  - **A previous index the build will not read** — the build of the index does not read a previous index of a newer format version and a previous index that the schema of its version does not accept: the release fails, as at `module-kit` (`ErrPrevious`), and `index.mjs` does the same.
- **Without a change to `spec`:**
  - **The schemas at run time** — there is no Go package with the format's schemas alone: `module-kit` embeds them as its own copy of `format/schemas/` and holds it by a test byte for byte against `spec.Format`, and each move to a tag updates it. The card of `module-kit` in `docs/architecture.md` names this;
  - **The form of calling the commands** `index`, `diff` and `open` and the file `open-views.json` are kept by `module-kit` — its `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md` —, and `modules` and `canvas` quote it and check the call by their tests of recipes. The cards of `module-kit` and `canvas` give a link to it, and the repository whose move it is writes down as a task of its own the move of `canvas` from the release of `tutor` to the release of `modules` and the manifest of format 0.3 at the element of `canvas`.

— *Why:*
- without a new version — what the text already says or refers to, and the vectors pin down: a third implementation — in `tutor`, in `canvas` — will check itself against them, not against `module-kit`;
- 0.4 — in E6, and not by an epic of its own: every change of the format is a new line of `spec` and a move of every reader, and E6 gives the next 0.y anyway, by the requests of the first content. The format changes once, and `module-kit` moves once. Until then both implementations already rejected everything that 0.4 rejects — except `index.mjs` for a previous index it will not read, which did not hold the refusal until 0.4;
- the unit before the final character — the letter of the text, and its cost is a request to write the answer once more, not an incorrect verdict;
- runs of non-starters — so the format already holds the version of Unicode: a run of 31 marks above one letter is not an answer that a reader gives, nor an option that an author writes;
- the schemas at run time — there is one consumer of the schemas at run time so far, and the copy is held by a test; a package will be needed by a second consumer in Go;
- the form of calling the commands — the form of a call is a contract of the CLI, and whoever executes it keeps it;
- gopls in the kind — so the step is part of what the recipe gives, and the move to a tag stops rolling it back; the check of the versions is needed because CI does not build the stage `devcontainer`.

— *Rejected:*
- characters outside the printable set — accepting them in quotes, as YAML 1.2.2 does: a character that cannot be seen is an error in an author's text; and stating the refusal without a new version — by the letter of the text this is a new strict rule;
- YAML 1.2.2 in `yaml.mjs` — recording the divergence of the second implementation as a debt: on a new vector it would set it apart from `module-kit`;
- the MP3 signature — three bytes, as the text had it: then both implementations would have to be changed against WHATWG, which the text refers to;
- runs of non-starters — the Stream-Safe Text Process in the format with a vector of 31 characters: a new version of the format for the sake of input that does not occur; and keeping silent — the divergence would stay only in `module-kit`;
- the unit before the final character — dropping at step 5 white space before the characters at the end too: this is another verdict on the same value, a new format version;
- `UNCHECKED_CAUSE_CHECK` — not measuring such an answer slot: a predicate that fails on one value is not found by the module's check, and the answer slot would leave the report; writing it with `UNCHECKED_CAUSE_UNSPECIFIED` — this value means "the reading gave a verdict";
- a value not in UTF-8 — keeping silent, or counting it a defect of the caller, an error without a verdict: the learner would get a refusal of the server;
- the template expression — calling the subset what go.starlark.net parses, without a check of `format-check`: the second implementation would not hold the rule; and adjusting `module-kit`: an author does not write a space at the beginning and 76 brackets;
- frozen globals — keeping silent: an implementation on `Program.Init` would accept a solver whose result depends on previous instances; and not freezing — this is the same dependence made a rule;
- `open_view_digest` — separate vectors of the digest: the digest is normative where the view is; and no vector;
- a previous index — reading a previous index of a newer version without the new members and writing the root with its own version: the index would name a version older than the one that already built it; and carrying over the unfamiliar as it is — a build cannot keep "as it was" what it does not know;
- gopls — leaving it a difference of each repository in Go: a move to a tag rolls back the step, and the Go extension without it installs gopls of an unpinned version; a recipe that rewrites a repository's `.devcontainer/` — the task is bigger, and it would overwrite the differences of `tutor` (golangci-lint) on every run; a recipe and a check of CI that `.devcontainer/` is the output of the recipe with a list of differences — a format of the list of differences would be needed at each repository; a check only by a test of `spec` — only its CI would hold the copy;
- everything at once in one epic with 0.4 — then E6 would give 0.5 as well; and everything in E6 — the work without a new version would wait for the first content of `modules`.

— *Consequence:* `format/README.md`; `format/vectors/`; `tools/format-check/yaml.mjs`; `tools/format-check/index.mjs`; `contracts/README.md`; `contracts/novatrail/eval/v1/`; `repo-template/kinds.json`; `repo-template/kinds/go/`; `repo-template/README.md`; `.github/dependabot.yml`; `justfile`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/INBOX.md`.

## The `sim` simulator

**R103. A library's CI takes `sim` by its tag and the SHA of its commit, in a job of its own, and writes `go.work` on the fly without committing it — `sim`, the pull request's code and the other library at the commit from `sim`'s gate file. The CI gate of `modules` is everything the simulator reads from a package, with invariants and absolute thresholds, without bands, and a move of the format changes none of it but the writing in the new format version. The first version of each library is the baseline before the first tag of `sim`, and the gate holds every change after it. `sim` judges the candidates of one library in a round. The simulator reads packages by the types of the canonical view, without `module-kit`, and virtual learners are gathered into populations, not into profiles.** `sim`'s `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/architecture.md` hold the detail.
- **The libraries' gate:** the gate's job runs on every pull request and every commit of `main` of `learner-model` and `engine`, on `ubuntu-24.04`, with `timeout-minutes: 15`, in the `toolchain` stage of the devcontainer of `sim` of the same tag, and holds the merge. `go.work` is not committed, and the simulator's `go.mod` is not edited.
- **The order of releases:** a change that breaks the simulator's API or moves the numbers is first written into `sim` at the commit of its pull request; a tag of `sim` comes out; the library's pull request raises the tag and is merged; after the library's release `sim` raises its `go.mod`. The pair "the threshold 'mastered' and the corridor's target" and a change of `learner-model` that breaks the API of `engine` go in one tag of `sim`: the gate file names both commits, `learner-model` is merged when the pull request of `engine` has passed review, and `api` moves to both versions together. A release of `sim` comes out by itself after green CI on `main`, and the callers' sessions raise the tag in them.
- **The gate of `modules`:** the CI of `modules` runs `sim` when what the simulator reads from a package has changed — `sim` decides this with its command "has it changed" — on the pull request's package, with invariants and absolute thresholds, without bands. A pull request that changes the tag of `sim` runs all the graphs.
- **A move of the format** goes without the simulator: in it `modules` changes nothing of what the simulator reads from a package — neither the graph nor the tasks' bindings — except the entry itself in the new format version, and the review of `modules` holds this. What the simulator reads is changed by a separate pull request, with the simulator, once `sim` has moved to the new tag and to the packages of the new release of `modules`, and `modules` has taken the new tag of `sim` in CI.
- **The first version:** the first version of `learner-model` and `engine` is checked by their own tests — the model's also by the property "the appended equals the recomputed" and by standalone's test vectors — and released signed. `sim` sets up the simulator on it and writes the criterion before the first candidate, the first change after it. The first tag of `sim` comes out after the first versions of both libraries. So in [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md) the first versions of `learner-model` and `engine` come after the moves and the detailing, and the changes of both through the gate after the first tag of `sim`.
- **The judging of a round:** the deciding run is on the last commit of the pull request of each candidate of the round, one judging with all of them, of those that passed the simplest, and the confirmation on held-out learners only of the chosen one. To the first judging `learner-model` brings up to three candidates, each in a draft pull request of its own, and `engine` two or three variants of the corridor; the judging file names the candidates as a list.
- **The simulator's data:** the gate's bands lie in `sim`, in the gate file, which names the commits of `learner-model` and `engine`, the release of `modules` — by its tag and the digest of the index — and the packages by their digests. Synthetic packages `sim` keeps only for its own code and tests, not for judging candidates.
- **Without `module-kit`:** `sim` reads `server.json` by the types `formatv0.CanonicalView` of `spec`'s Go module, as the canonical view and the card of `sim` say, and the window of format versions by the field `module_format_version` of the manifest in the canonical view. Modules and packages through `module-kit` are for `api` and `tutor`, not for `sim`.
- **Populations:** virtual learners are gathered into populations, like standalone's "base population", not into profiles: in the vocabulary a profile is a learner in an account, and a virtual learner has a profile in this sense too — the modules and the runs, the inputs of `engine`. The glossary has "virtual learner" and "population".

— *Why:*
- `go.work` on every pull request keeps the libraries in their separate repositories, and each change passes the simulator and is not merged if it worsens the criterion; the modules' files are not edited meanwhile;
- the gate of `modules` is everything the simulator reads from a package, not just the graph: a pull request that reweighs tasks without touching the graph would otherwise pass by the simulator. Without bands, since the pull request's package has no base to compare them with;
- a review of a move that held only the graph would let a move that reweighs tasks or changes their bindings without touching the graph come out as a release without the simulator — the very case of the gate of `modules`. `modules` writes its review wider than the graph;
- the first version before the gate: without a version of the model the simulator has nothing to import, and the criterion is written before the first run of a candidate, not before the first line of code. Otherwise the order of [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md) would stand in a circle: the libraries' code would wait for the first tag of `sim`, and the first tag needs their first versions;
- the judging of a round is how `sim`'s selection rule works — "of those that passed, the simplest" —, and the held-out learners and the confirmation are spent once per round, not per candidate;
- one term means one thing in every document.

— *Rejected:*
- a gate only on release candidates — it would let a worsening into `main`; the three libraries in one repository — against the split into repositories; `go mod edit -replace` in CI — it edits the simulator's `go.mod` and gives the same as `go.work`;
- a copy of standalone's model in `sim` as the baseline — the model would live in two repositories, and the simulator would measure `learner-model` by someone else's code; the model's code after the first tag of `sim` — a circle;
- a move of the format that waits for a tag of `sim` that reads the new format version and goes with the simulator — every move of the format would wait for `sim`, and `sim` moves to a format version by its tag later than `module-kit`; a review of the move that holds only the graph;
- candidates one at a time, the best by exploration first — each next one needs a held-out set of its own, and the order would choose, not the criterion;
- `sim` through `module-kit` — it would change the rule of the module package and the card of `sim`, and in the build depend on `module-kit` too;
- "profiles of virtual learners" as a second meaning of the word in the vocabulary.

— *Consequence:* `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/INBOX.md`; `sim`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `learner-model`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `modules`'s `docs/architecture.md`.

## The engine's inputs

**R104. The engine chooses a lesson or a task, not an item. Beyond the learner model its input is a summary of issues from `api`, which `api` gathers from its records of choices and attempts, and `Read` of `learner-model` gives for a module whether its trial series has ended and whether the last evidence was still in it. For a skill that the skill map opened, the engine gives a lesson or a task on it.**
- **Not an item:** "item" leaves the list of what the engine chooses in `docs/concepts.md`. Items are a part of a task, and the check, the evidence and the solution belong to the task as a whole; the choice is a lesson, a task or "nothing to give", as `ChoiceKind`.
- **The summary of issues.** The issue of a lesson is the issue of each of its skills.
  - For a skill: the time of the last issue and, if the last closed attempt of the skill was a probe or a repetition, its result as facts — how many items where the skill is primary got a first verdict, at how many of them it is "correct" and whether the solution was shown —, not as a mark "correct": the engine computes "failure".
  - For a module: the number of choices, of a task and of a lesson one each.
  - For a task with a key: when its solution last went to the device. The solution of a task with a rubric, open after "Done", does not count.

  By it the rule keeps the queue "not issued for the longest", the turn of a probe — once in six tasks —, the return of a skill from a pause by a correct answer of a probe and the pause before a task with a seen solution. The types of the summary are its own and simple, like the types of the graph, and the repeat of a choice gathers the summary anew from the records before the choice, which do not change.
- **The trial series:** in a module's trial series the engine does not work through an error and gives no probes, as in standalone's SPEC ([standalone@42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/tree/42b4408)), and the series — the first five answers in the module — is a state of the model. So `Read` gives two marks for a module: whether the trial series has ended, and whether the module's last evidence was still in it — the second is needed so that an error in the series' last answer is not worked through.
- **A skill from the map:** the detailing of `engine` takes the rule "open" of the skill map as an input. For a skill that the map opened and the learner chose, `ChooseNext` gives a lesson or a task on it with the code "the learner chose the skill", if the pool and the lessons hold at least one, and the reachability for "My subjects" may be its own. Such a choice is empty only when `api` has limited the pool to tasks without AI, or, in a choice of a module's tasks, which has no lessons, when the pool holds no task on the skill. The skill the learner chose is the task skill of its module, kept with the connected module, which a choice of the module's tasks reads anew each time.

— *Why:*
- the time of practice from the model is not the time of issue: a task issued without evidence gives no practice, and the rule needs both. `api` keeps the records of choices and attempts anyway, so the summary adds no learner's data, it only hands them to the engine;
- the solution of a task with a rubric, open after "Done", is a sample, not a key;
- the model counts the series, and the engine does not repeat its rules: were it to count by itself by the number of evidence of the module's skills, evidence with several skills would be counted more than once;
- the map's rule rests on the definition of the code "new skill" in the contract, no new field is needed, and the learner's choice gives something wherever the module has a lesson or a task on the skill.

— *Rejected:*
- giving `ChoiceKind` the kind "item" — a change of the contract `app` ↔ `api` and of `api` for a choice the rule does not make;
- a summary only from the model, and in the input only the tasks with a seen solution: a task issued without evidence would not move the queue; a log of the last N issues, like standalone's window `recent` — more learner's data in the call than the rule reads;
- the engine counts the series by itself; a rule without a trial series;
- `engine` decides the reachability by itself, and the map moves to its rule by a field of `GetSkillMap` — the map would wait for the detailing of `engine`, and a field in `v1` cannot be removed afterwards; the map chooses any skill — `skill-map` rejects it.

— *Consequence:* `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/INBOX.md`; `engine`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `learner-model`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `skill-map`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## Production images

**R105. An image that runs in production is a static Go binary on `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13` by the tag `nonroot` and digest: without a shell and a package manager, and not as root. NovaTrail does not use Docker Hardened Images, and it publishes no image: a service's release puts out a signed binary and the `Dockerfile`, and whoever deploys builds the image and keeps it in a private registry of their own.**
- **Which images.** The image that production runs — a Cloud Run service and its jobs:
  - for now only `api` will have such an image: it is one Go process, and its jobs run on the same image;
  - later — `tutor`, when it becomes a service, the services of stage 4 and the self-hosting of `infra`.

  The `toolchain` stage and the devcontainer are not part of this: they are not in production, and NovaTrail publishes neither. The devcontainer is built on every run; CI takes the stage's image from the cache of GitHub Actions and builds it only on a miss. The builds of `app` and `site` are static files of the hosting, they have no image.
- **The build** — in two stages, like the `Dockerfile` of canvas-api ([canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/tree/0901af0)):
  - the build stage is the official `golang` image by exact tag and digest, with the Go version that `go.mod` names and on which the tests run;
  - the binary is built with `CGO_ENABLED=0` and `-trimpath`: it is static, without libc and without the paths of whoever built it.
- **The run** — on `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot@sha256:…`:
  - the base holds only "ca-certificates", "A /etc/passwd entry for a root user", "A /tmp directory" and "tzdata", without a shell and a package manager;
  - the tag `nonroot` runs as the user with uid 65532 (`NONROOT = 65532` in `common/variables.bzl`);
  - distroless tags carry no version — "latest, nonroot, debug, debug-nonroot" — so the image is held by its digest, and the tag names the variant taken. This is what "by tag and digest" in RULES.md means;
  - Dependabot raises the digest: it sees the base image, and the registry is open and asks for no credentials.
- **In the image** — the binary and what its repository put into the image: for `api` these are the module packages. Nothing else — no debugging tools, no `debug` variant.
- **What is in the base.** The image `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot` (index `sha256:25ac8f0c3b2334a9eb05452266bd4697864a8c8ef0ef71e5e6480d7f92868329`, the amd64 variant) was pulled from the registry and taken apart on 2026-11-07. The packages are taken from `/var/lib/dpkg/status.d/`, the licenses from `/usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright`:
  - `base-files` 13.8+deb13u7 — "License: GPL-2+": `/usr/lib/os-release`, `/etc/issue` and the texts of `/usr/share/common-licenses/`;
  - `netbase` 6.5 — "License: GPL-2": `/etc/services`, `/etc/protocols`, `/etc/rpc` and `/etc/ethertypes`;
  - `ca-certificates` 20250419+deb13u1: the certificates are made from `mozilla/certdata.txt` — "License: MPL-2.0", and `debian/*` with the script `update-ca-certificates`, which also lies in the image, — "License: GPL-2+";
  - `tzdata` and `tzdata-legacy` 2026f-0+deb13u1 — "This database is in the public domain";
  - `media-types` 13.0.0 — "Copyright: public-domain".
- **What publishing would mean.** The rule of licenses admits the ASF's category A in what ships with NovaTrail's code and packages. A published image would carry both GPL and MPL-2.0 ([ASF 3rd Party License Policy](https://www.apache.org/legal/resolved.html), read 2026-11-07):
  - GPL is the ASF's category X: "Apache projects may not distribute Category X licensed components, in source or binary form; in ASF source code or in convenience binaries";
  - MPL 2.0 is category B: "Any Category B licensed works may be included in binary-only form in Apache Software Foundation convenience binaries", and with a notice.
- **The release and the deployment:**
  - **A service's release** puts out the binary as a release file, with a signature, and the `Dockerfile` by which the image is built; `api` writes its `Dockerfile` with its code.
  - **NovaTrail's deployment** — the deployment of `infra` — builds the image around the binary that `release-verify` accepted, on the base by digest, by the `Dockerfile` of the service's release, and puts it into its own private registry — the Artifact Registry of `infra`. The image itself needs no signature of its own: it does not leave the private registry, and the release files it is built from are signed.
  - **Self-hosting** builds the same image on its own side, from the same binary and by the same `Dockerfile`.
  - **The example is canvas-api.** Its deployment takes the server from the release, having checked the signature, builds "an image around it" and puts it into its own Artifact Registry (`docs/self-hosting.md` of canvas-api).
  - **NovaTrail's image registry is private:** only the deployment and the platform's own Cloud Run read it. A public registry or an image among the release files is already publication, and it is possible only by a new decision, with a list of the base's packages and their licenses for each digest.
  - **The binary's licenses** are checked by the license checks: "Go / licenses" and `ci-licenses`. The base is not part of them: NovaTrail does not distribute it.
- **Not static Go** — another runtime, cgo, a browser — this decision does not cover. Such an image comes by a change of it, to the same bar: without a shell and a package manager, not as root, by tag and digest.

— *Why:*
- A static Go binary needs only the certificates and tzdata from the base. `static-debian13` gives exactly those: "The smallest distroless image, `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13`, is around 2 MiB". The vulnerabilities that remain are in Go and the dependencies, and govulncheck catches them: `just ci-vuln` and "Go / vuln".
- This path has already gone through production: on this base canvas-api rolled out and rolled back a signed release on Cloud Run on 2026-10-14.
- The base needs no login, and its signature is keyless: "All distroless images are signed by cosign with ephemeral keys (keyless)". The check is `cosign verify $IMAGE_NAME --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com --certificate-identity keyless@distroless.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. This is the same Sigstore model as that of `release-verify`. The project's license is Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`).
- The source is the README, `base/README.md` and the sources of [GoogleContainerTools/distroless](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/distroless), commit c3bf6a1 of 2026-11-02, read 2026-11-07.
- No published image: an image together with its base is a distribution of files under GPL-2 and MPL-2.0, which the rule of licenses does not admit, and a binary under Apache-2.0 with already checked dependencies is not. Self-hosting loses only `docker pull`: instead of it, `docker build` with the same `Dockerfile`. It costs the platform itself nothing: canvas-api has checked this path in production.

— *Rejected:*
- **Docker Hardened Images** — excessive. All read 2026-11-07:
  - on static Go DHI give the same surface: `dhi.io/static` — "A very minimal image that is most useful in the context of running binary executables, such as those built from Rust and Golang" ([the DHI catalog](https://hub.docker.com/hardened-images/catalog/dhi/static)). Beyond it there are only the base's attestations: SBOM, VEX and SLSA Build Level 3 provenance ([the DHI documentation](https://docs.docker.com/dhi/));
  - since 2025-12-17 they are free under Apache 2.0 ([Docker's blog](https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-hardened-images-for-every-developer/)), but the guarantees are paid. "Critical CVE fixes < 7 days with SLA-backed continuous patching" is given by the Select level, "Starting at $5k/repo", and the free one gets "Upstream cadence for Docker-released patches" ([Hardened Images](https://www.docker.com/products/hardened-images/));
  - they can be pulled only after `docker login dhi.io`, and in CI — "authenticate using an organization access token (OAT)" ([Use a Docker Hardened Image](https://docs.docker.com/dhi/how-to/use/)). That would be the first secret in NovaTrail's CI, which a pull request from a fork would not get, and a Docker account for everyone who builds the platform themselves;
  - their signature is checked by Docker's key, without a transparency log: "DHI attestations may not be recorded in the public Rekor transparency log", hence the flag `--insecure-ignore-tlog=true` ([Verify a Docker Hardened Image](https://docs.docker.com/dhi/how-to/verify/)). That is a second model of trust beside that of `release-verify`.
- **`scratch` with certificates from the build stage**, a base of our own without GPL with our own `/etc/passwd` and tzdata in the binary: such a base has neither a signature nor a list of packages of its own, the certificates and tzdata are whatever happened to be in the build image, and the Mozilla certificates in it would still remain under MPL-2.0. Besides, canvas-api has not gone this path.
- **`base-debian13` or `cc-debian13`:** a static binary needs no glibc and libssl — "Statically compiled applications (Go) that do not require libc can use the `gcr.io/distroless/static` image" (`base/README.md`).
- **An Alpine or Debian image without distroless** — that is a shell and a package manager in a production image.
- **Publishing images with an exception in the rule of licenses, counting the base's packages as "the platform".** The ASF calls a platform what a product works with, not what it distributes: "It does not matter, unless the terms for that platform affect the Apache product's licensing". The ASF does not distribute category X in "convenience binaries" either. Besides, a list of packages and licenses for each new digest would be needed, that is, a new check in CI, and Debian's sources, as GPL-2 requires on distribution in the form of object code: "Accompany it with the complete corresponding machine-readable source code" or a written offer to give them (`/usr/share/common-licenses/GPL-2` in the same image).

— *Consequence:* `RULES.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`.

## Deployment

**R106. `infra` rolls out the services and the build of `app`, by one list of exact versions and digests. The deployment of `infra` builds a service's image from the files of its release, by the release's build contract, and starts the jobs of `api` that hold on to a deployment as Cloud Run jobs on the same image as the revision: the check of the configuration and the migrations of both databases before the revision takes requests, and the job that closes the attempts and the lesson runs on packages that have left the image once the revision has taken all the traffic. The deployment facts for the AI admission function and the lowest rung of the rule of admission of models of `api` are kept by `infra`, beside the rollout list, and reach the revision as a file and a variable.**
- **Who rolls out.** `infra`, by a list of exact versions and digests — of both the services and the build of `app`. A component's repository rolls out nothing itself and has no access to production: the projects and Workload Identity Federation for CI are with `infra`.
- **A service's image** is built by the deployment of `infra`:
  1. it takes from the release of the service that the list names the binary and the `Dockerfile` — files of the release — and checks them with `release-verify`;
  2. it builds the image by this `Dockerfile`, on the base by digest. What the service puts into the image beyond the binary, its own code does at the build stage. For `api` these are the module packages by `modules.json`, embedded in the binary, — by the same command with which the first app puts them into a folder. The deployment does not repeat the logic of the packages;
  3. it puts the image into the private Artifact Registry of `infra` and rolls out a Cloud Run revision by the image's digest.

  This is how canvas-api rolled out: the server from the release with a checked signature, "an image around it", a push and a revision by digest ([`docs/self-hosting.md` of canvas-api@0901af0](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/blob/0901af0/docs/self-hosting.md)).
- **The image of `api`** is built by the contract of the release of `api`: the binary `api_<tag>_linux_amd64` is put as the file `api` into the build context `binary`, and the image is built by `docker build --target release --build-context binary=<folder>` by the release's `Dockerfile`; the stage does not read the main context.
- **The jobs of `api`** are commands of its binary, which the release of `api` names, run as Cloud Run jobs on the image of the revision, in this order:
  1. the command that checks the configuration — the facts file by the admission table of this release, and the rung — and serves no requests;
  2. the migrations of both databases, before the revision takes requests;
  3. once the revision has taken all the traffic, the job that closes the attempts and the lesson runs on packages that have left the image.

  The names of the variables and of the commands are written by the epic of the code of `api`.
- **The deployment facts and the rung** are edited in `infra` by a pull request of their own. The revision of `api` gets the facts as a file — a volume on an exact version of a Secret Manager secret, its path in `API_ADMISSION_FACTS_FILE`, like `X_FILE` for secrets —, and the lowest rung by the variable `API_ADMISSION_RUNG` with the code of a rung of `tutor`: `author` or `full`. No file — the platform AI is closed; no rung — "full".
- **The build of `app`** is rolled out by the same list. The rollout checks the archive's signature, writes `/deployment.json` and releases the build, the file and the CSP header in one release of the hosting.
- **A rollback.** `api`, and while the module format is v0 also a build of `app` that has moved to a new format version, roll back only forward. Everything else rolls back by a revert of the list.
- **Self-hosting** takes the same list and the same path of deployment in its own project.
- **Left to `infra`:**
  - the format and place of the list and who edits it;
  - what the rollout checks before the deployment;
  - whether to reject a release of `api` lower than the one rolled out.

— *Why:*
- Access to production stays in one repository. `infra` already has the projects and WIF for CI, and a service's release comes out of a public repository by the shared workflow of `.github`.
- The build path is one — for the platform and for self-hosting. Self-hosting cannot take NovaTrail's private image, and both go through the build in the deployment the same way.
- One place shows what is running. `api` and `app` come out in one list when the open view changes.
- The image's logic stays with the service — in its `Dockerfile` and code — and the deployment only executes what the release signed.
- Only the deployment knows the order "check, migrations, revision, job", and migrations at the service's start would run in each of its instances at once. The image is distroless without a shell, so the jobs are commands of the binary. canvas-api, too, ran a Cloud Run job with the image of the new release before the deployment, as `api`'s `docs/architecture.md` records.
- The check before the migrations: `infra` matches the vocabulary of the facts by the tag of its `spec` submodule, and `api` by the version of the admission table in its binary, and without the check a mismatch would surface after the migrations, when `api` rolls back only forward. The facts are a file, as [the text of the admission table](../admission/README.md) names them.
- The build contract, the facts and the rung are a link between two components, whose summary is the card of `infra`: a contract the other side does not know breaks at the first deployment, and without the card `infra` would not learn that it keeps the facts and the rung.

— *Rejected:*
- **The service's release builds the image** and puts it into the private registry, and `infra` rolls it out by digest. Then each service repository needs access to the production registry, and self-hosting builds its own image anyway — there would be two build paths.
- **Each repository rolls itself out by its release, like canvas-api.** In NovaTrail the releases come out of different repositories, and what is running would be seen only by all of them at once.
- **The code of the deployment of `infra` puts the module packages into the image** — then the logic of `api` would live in two repositories.
- **Migrations at the service's start, and the job after a deployment on a schedule** — migrations in each instance at once.
- **Leaving the task of `infra` that takes this without a row.**
- **The build contract, the facts and the rung only in the documents of `api`** — `infra` would not learn them.
- **The build contract without the check command** — an unknown fact would be found by the revision's start, already after the migrations.
- **The facts as an environment variable with JSON on one line** — against the text of the admission table, which names them a file.

— *Consequence:* `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `run/INBOX.md`.

## The outcome of the detailing of `engine`

**R107. The age category is a filter of `api`, not an input of the engine, and there is no daily goal among the inputs. A skill the learner chose is the task skill of its module: it holds until the learner gives the choice back to the tutor, and the record of the choice keeps it. A task whose solution went to the device is not given again as the next task. `ReasonCode` has a ninth value, `REASON_CODE_ROTATION`, "in rotation". The record of the choice also keeps the skill from the map, the age category and the mark of the engine's modules, and the seed in it is empty: the engine takes no randomness. The summary of issues counts the issues of lessons, the choices of a module and the facts of the last closed attempt. Т-10 is extended with the engine's side and stays open. The checks of identical bits are an option of the shared `go.yml`, wasip1 runs the tests there too, and the test of the code rules is a shared tool of `.github`.** `engine`'s `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/architecture.md` hold the details.
- **The age category**: the modules, the lessons and the pool of tasks `api` already selects by `age_categories` — a module by its audience, a lesson only as a whole, a task only for a learner of its categories —, and the engine gets only what suits the learner. So the category is not among the engine's constraints in `docs/concepts.md`, and `api` keeps it for the pool too, as for lessons. In the record of the choice it stays — for the repeat (below).
- **A skill the learner chose** is the task skill of its module, which the learner sets on the tile of its tasks or on the skill map: it holds until the learner gives the choice back to the tutor. A choice of the module's tasks gives the engine that module alone, with no lessons, and the task skill as `MapSkill`; with none, the engine's rule leads within the module. The record of the choice keeps the skill it was made with and the module it was made in, and `api` calls the engine for `next` in the same module, with its task skill as it is then. Without the field the choice cannot be repeated: the task skill may have changed since.
- **A lesson's band** is the set of the bands of its tasks: a lesson with a verdict suits a skill when the band of its recommended task is in this set; a lesson without tasks suits any band; a lesson of another band does not hold the order.
- **"Not again at once"** for a task whose solution went to the device means "not as the next task", and after how long — `engine` decides. The engine has 24 hours, and when the choice has given nothing, a second pass gives such a task too, after the others, but not the task of the last closed attempt.
- **The daily goal** is neither in the profile nor in the contract ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md)) — only in the prototype ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)) —, and the engine's rule does not read it. It is not among the engine's constraints in `docs/concepts.md` until the product says what it means and where it is kept.
- **"In rotation"**: three places of the rule had no exact code — branch 8 (all the reachable ones are mastered, no dates have come), the queue at "the bottom of the ladder" (no skill is reachable) and a skill "mastered" by the model whose recommended task went above the mastery band: `REASON_CODE_QUEUE` requires "within reach" and "not mastered". They get one value, `REASON_CODE_ROTATION` = 9: "Rotation: a skill given before comes round again, the one not given for longest first, though it does not fit the queue of `REASON_CODE_QUEUE`: it is mastered, or no skill is within reach". Two comments are more precise, and the meaning of their values is as before ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md)): for `REASON_CODE_QUEUE` "not given for longest" is within its module, and for `REASON_CODE_NEW_SKILL` — "whose prerequisites the engine's rule counts as met, or which has none". The rule opens a skill with a prerequisite counted as met, not mastered, too: an anchor "unknown", a cycle, a prerequisite there is nothing to teach with, a prerequisite with `rubric` or `none` counted by a lesson. The words of the code for an adult are written by `app`.
- **The record of the choice**: to repeat a choice without AI, it lacked three fields, and one was superfluous. (1) The field "seed" is empty as long as the engine takes no randomness, and it takes none: that this is so is seen by the version of `engine` in the same record. (2) The record also keeps the skill the learner chose and its module, the profile's age category at the time of the choice, and a mark of which of the digests are the engine's modules, connected and suiting the learner. The category changes at the yearly refinement and at a change of country, the connections at any time, and the digests also name the modules of the log, which only `learner-model` gets. (3) The last attempt and its outcome the repeat derives from the records of choices and attempts before the time of the choice, as it does the summary of issues. This adds no learner's data: the category and the connections are already with `api`.
- **The summary of issues** also counts: (1) the issue of a lesson is the issue of each of its skills: so a lesson moves the queue "not issued for the longest" and the module's time of issue; (2) for a module, the number of choices, of a task and of a lesson one each, not of tasks issued: the tasks of a lesson do not move the counter of the probe's turn, and the turn does not skip; (3) for a skill, the outcome of the last closed attempt if it is a probe or a repetition: a correct repetition of an unreachable skill returns it from a pause, like a correct probe; (4) the result on the skill comes as facts, not as a mark "correct": how many items where the skill is primary got a first verdict, at how many of them it is "correct" and whether the solution was shown. The engine computes "failure" by its own rule, and the rule does not live in `api` as well.
- **Т-10** is extended with the engine's side and stays open. The recommendation is as before — compute on the server. `engine`, like `learner-model`, gives the same choice and the same code on any build of one version, WebAssembly too, is built for the device as it is and checks this in CI from its first code. How it works offline — a computation on the device or a queue the server has chosen in advance — stage 5 decides.
- **The checks of identical bits**: `learner-model` and `engine` both take the runs of arm64 and js/wasm, so as an option of the shared `go.yml` go the runs on the targets — amd64 with GOAMD64 v3, with v1 with `GODEBUG=cpu.all=off`, 386, js/wasm through Node and the wasip1 build, — the differential check of the assembler `fma-diff` and the job on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`. The test of the code rules on `go/types` also becomes a shared tool of `.github` with lists per repository, instead of two copies of `rules_test.go`; until `.github` gives it, `engine` has its own port.
- **wasip1 runs the tests.** "Go / targets" and "Go / arm64" of the shared `go.yml` not only build wasip1 but run its tests: `go test -exec` with an executor of `.github`'s own on `node:wasi` of the Node of the caller's `toolchain` stage, preview1, — as js/wasm runs `go_js_wasm_exec`. The WASI environment is already in the image — Node, `NODE_VERSION` in [.devcontainer/Dockerfile](../.devcontainer/Dockerfile) —, and `go_wasip1_wasm_exec` of Go 1.27 knows only wasmtime, wazero, wasmedge and wasmer. So the executor is our own: the step writes it outside the checkout, like the control of `fma-diff`, and the caller does not have it. The tests of `learner-model` and `detmath`, built by `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go test -c`, are green on it, and a failed test gives a non-zero code (both checked 2026-11-11). `engine` takes the run with a move to the tag of `.github` that has it (Д213).
- **The card of `engine`** in `docs/architecture.md`: the engine's items in "To decide when detailed" are decided, and the items beyond the card are written into its text — the rule of repetition, the anchor skill, a task with a seen solution, lessons, the build for the device; the corridor, the prerequisites and the queue, several modules, the modes and the constraints, the reason codes, the seed and the repeat of a choice, the types. There is no consolidation in a lesson and no early end in the first slice, and `api` does not call the engine at the end of a segment, so the card has no paragraph about them. At the input are runs without the places of the finished segments, and of the attempts with a rubric only those closed by "Done". The items' traps are with the engine's candidate, and `learner-model` needs no change: the graph and the task description cover everything.

— *Why:*
- the category is a filter of `api`: `api` already keeps this rule, and for the engine the category decides nothing. There is as much learner's data in the call as the rule reads;
