- a skill the learner chose holds — so a topic chosen by a person held in standalone: `lesson_topic` in the profile, until it is reset ([standalone@42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/tree/42b4408)). A field of the connected module, and its copy in the record: the module keeps it for the learner, one for each module, and the repeat of a choice sees only the record;
- the band is a set of bands: a lesson has no band field, and `modules` rejected it; the band of the recommended task leads the lesson after the learner as they grow;
- "not as the next" — the key goes to the device after a correct answer too, and the lessons of the first slice hold all the tasks of a skill and band: without the second pass the learner would hear "nothing to give" with a non-empty pool;
- without a daily goal — the rule cannot read it, and the day's goal is what an adult sees;
- one value, not three: the three places have one essence for an adult — the skill came again in rotation, not because it is being worked on. A new value is new words in `app` in all the interface languages, and three values would distinguish what an adult does not need to know. Branch 8 stays: without it, with one module the learner would hear "nothing to give" with a non-empty pool;
- three fields of the record — without them the repeat will not restore the input, and a snapshot of the whole input would keep twice as much learner's data as the rule reads;
- the result as facts — the rule "failure" is one, for the model and for the engine, and a mark from `api` would be its second copy;
- Т-10 is open — offline has a path without computation on the device at all, and stage 5 chooses it;
- shared checks — the two libraries have the same checks, and two copies of the rules test can diverge;
- an executor of our own on Node — the WASI environment is already in the image, and without the run the bits of the build for WASI, one of the two for the device, would not be run;
- the card is a summary, and it must not say what has been decided otherwise.

— *Rejected:*
- a filter by age in the engine — `age_categories` in the task description of `learner-model` and the category in the input;
- a skill the learner chose kept with the module alone, with no copy in the record — the repeat does not see it; a choice from the map for one choice;
- a lesson of only one band; a field `band` of a lesson;
- "at once" as 24 hours without exceptions; more tasks in the pool from `modules` instead of a second pass;
- a daily goal as a field of the profile and an input of the engine — a change of the contract, of `api` and of `docs/privacy.md`, and one more rule;
- three values "all mastered", "the bottom of the ladder", "a new band of the mastered"; removing branch 8;
- a snapshot of the whole input in the record; only the skill from the map in the record — an old choice will not repeat after a change of the category or the connections;
- the summary without these additions: a lesson does not move the queue, the turn of the probe after a lesson shifts by the number of its tasks, a correct repetition does not return from a pause, and "correct" is decided by `api`; the engine computes the summary by itself — it has no input "records of choices";
- closing Т-10 now;
- only options of `go.yml`, and each library has its own rules test; everything its own for each library;
- wasmtime or wazero in the image — one more tool by version and sha256 in each repository for what Node already gives; keeping only the build of wasip1;
- amending only the items "To decide when detailed", and the rest when the code comes; not touching the card.

— *Consequence:* `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/cause.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `run/INBOX.md`; `learner-model`'s `run/DEBT.md`.

## Requests of `modules` to the format from the rest of the port

**R108. The requests of `modules` to the format from the rest of the port go into format 0.4, in epic E6, beside the rules that the code of `module-kit` asked for. A handwritten choice gets an optional mark, `notation: word`: with it the key is one word of letters, and a read word of letters not among the options gets "not yet". A check kind `time` appears — a time `H:MM`, correct when its hours and minutes equal the key's. In the path of a template's picture there are placeholders. A task gets an optional closed leading question: `api` gives it on "Hint" before the first incorrect answer, and the evidence carries it.** The numbers of the handwritten choices and the times are by the tasks of `olympiad-math` 0.1.1 at commit 73c79af of `modules`, counted 2026-11-08: a handwritten choice — in 74 tasks, of them 30 times and 44 words; by tapping — 18 days of the week, 2 months, 6 dates and 3 times in a phrase; and by `modules` at `main` ea2a2ba, read 2026-11-08: options that are phrases — in 29 tasks with a handwritten word of 44, traps with minutes from 60 — in 14 of 30. The numbers of the leading question are by `content/examples/` of [mathtrail-standalone at commit 42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/tree/42b4408), read 2026-11-08: a hint `hint` is in 311 tasks of 753, and in band 5–6 in each of 272. Normative — the [format text](../format/README.md) and the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md).

- **A mark on a handwritten choice.** The mark is optional: the check field `notation: options | word`, and without `word` a handwritten choice stays as it was. With `word` the key and the read value are one word of letters, and the other options and the traps may be phrases; this is a new rule. The value first loses `.`, `!` and `?` at the end. A value of one word of letters that is not among the options gets "not yet" and gives a rung, like an incorrect number. Everything else, as now, is "not in notation" and "unreadable". Traps stay values from the options.
- **The check kind `time`.** The key is a time `"H:MM"`. A value is in notation when after steps 1–5 of the normalization of the [format text](../format/README.md) it is `H:MM` or `HH:MM`, hours 0–23, minutes from 60 too. It is correct when its hours and minutes equal the hours and minutes of the key, so `07:30` is correct with the key `7:30`; the kind does not compute the sum of minutes. The trap values are times in the same notation. The leak search finds the key with a leading zero too. The kind has no parameter of 12 or 24 hours, so `7:30` and `19:30` are different times: where a learner answers by the 12-hour dial, `modules` sets a trap, `9:10` for `21:10`, and the parameter comes by a minor change when content asks for it. Dates, days of the week and months stay a tapped choice.
- **An instance's picture.** In the path of the picture of a template's statement and solution there are placeholders of parameters and derived numbers — `pictures/split-{total}-{parts}.png`. There are no placeholders of the solver's result there: the path is open, and the result stands only in closed fields. An instance has numbers in its path, and its file is held by `task.known-pictures`: the task's rule is checked on every instance anyway. Outside a template there are no braces in a path (`task.placeholders`). The path of each picture of an instance is among the texts in which `task.no-leaks` looks for the task's keys.
- **The leading question.** The optional field of a task `leading_question` is the author's question that breaks the task down, in the module's explanation language. The field is closed. `api` gives it on "Hint" before the first incorrect answer, together with the task's techniques, and records that it gave it, in a field of its own apart from the technique. `task.no-leaks` looks for the task's keys in it, as in `givens`, and in a template there are placeholders in it. It does not change the ladder and the fallback texts.

— *Why:*
- all this is new rules, not a refinement of the text, so they go into 0.4 and E6 with the rules for the code of `module-kit`: the format changes once, and `module-kit` moves once. Each change, by the format's rules of versions, only adds;
- the word mark: an incorrect word is an ordinary error, not an unreadable answer. The word of the answer stands in the question, and the learner copies it. The mark binds the key and the read value, not each option, because in 29 of the 44 tasks with a handwritten word the options are phrases. A full stop at the end is removed: otherwise `Kim.` would get "not yet" for a correct answer, and a false alarm is worse than the absence of a check;
- `time`: all 30 handwritten times are tasks of the skill `time-clocks`, where the time is computed, like "It is 7 o'clock. What time will it be in half an hour?". A choice compares text, and time is computed in hours and minutes. Minutes from 60 are in notation because 14 of the 30 have traps with them. The subject that the recommendation of `modules` waited for already exists;
- the instance's picture: the number of instances is finite, `module-kit` already enumerates them and holds the rule of pictures on each, and the file may be any picture;
- the leading question: before the first error band 5–6 now has only "givens and unknown" and the techniques, and standalone's hints are already written and checked. The field is closed because it hints at the method more strongly than a technique. Its name is different: "hint" in the glossary is the tutor's words, and one term means one thing.

— *Rejected:*
- for the word mark: a mark for any value not among the options, as `modules` proposed — `Kim.` and `07:30` would get "not yet" for a correct answer; a new kind "word" without options — traps have nothing to bind to; leaving it as it is — 44 tasks without rungs for an incorrect answer;
- for `time`: time under the word mark, as `modules` recommended — "not yet" for `07:30`; time by tapping — guessing 1/5; a parameter of 12 or 24 hours now; leaving it — 30 tasks of `time-clocks` without rungs;
- for the picture: a picture that `canvas` draws by the instance's data — already rejected for pictures: 13 schemes and drawers for one module; leaving it — 6 templates are not carried over, and 4 have no picture;
- for the leading question: the field `hint` — the name is taken by the tutor's words; an open field, like `givens`, — it hints at the method; the text of rung 2 — it would change the order of the fallback texts, and before the first error the learner will not see it; merging into `simpler_case` — a simpler case is something else; leaving it — 311 written hints would be lost;
- a change of the decision on the rules for the code of `module-kit` instead of a decision of its own: that one is about the code, and these are requests of content;
- a 0.y of its own before E6: the format and `module-kit` would change twice.

— *Consequence:* `format/README.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/`; `docs/decisions.md`; `run/EPICS.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `run/INBOX.md`.

## The data region

**R109. The platform's data region is the United States, one place for all learners: Cloud Run and everything `infra` keeps in a region — `us-east4` (Ashburn, Virginia), Neon — `aws-us-east-1` (N. Virginia).** `infra`'s `docs/architecture.md` holds the details of `infra`'s side.
- **The region of each resource:**
  - the Cloud Run services and jobs and the Artifact Registry repository — `us-east4`, regional;
  - the Secret Manager secrets — with user-managed replication, at the place `us-east4`, not regional: a regional secret is accessible only from its own region — "Regional secrets can only be accessed by applications or services running within the same location" ([Regional secrets and data residency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/regional-secrets/data-residency), updated 2026-10-26), — and the eval key in Secret Manager is read by CI on GitHub;
  - the log bucket — `us-east4`, and the sink `_Default` is directed into it; `_Required` — in `global`, as long as there is no Google Cloud organization: "Logging automatically creates two log buckets: _Required and _Default, which are in the global location. You can't change the location of existing buckets" ([Regionalize your logs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/regionalized-logs), updated 2026-10-16), and the place of new buckets is set only by an organization setting (О-16);
  - the trace bucket `_Trace` — created in `us-east4` before the first trace: observability buckets have no `global` ([Observability bucket locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/observability/observability-bucket-locations), updated 2026-11-06);
  - Neon — `aws-us-east-1`; Firebase Auth processes data only in the United States in any region, and Firebase Hosting, if `infra` chooses it, is a global service ([Privacy and Security in Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy); sources 4.4).
- **What does not change after creation:** the place of the log bucket, of the Artifact Registry repository — "settings that cannot be changed after the repository is created: … Repository location" ([Create standard repositories](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/repositories/create-repos), updated 2026-11-07), — of a secret with user-managed replication and of the Neon project. The place of `_Trace` only a reprovision changes: "You can't modify the location" ([Update observability buckets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/update-observability-buckets), updated 2026-11-06), and "Reprovisioning is a destructive operation" ([Cloud Trace release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/release-notes), 2026-11-06): the traces are lost in a move.
- **The region of AI calls** is not part of this decision: `tutor` and `docs/privacy.md` decide it, if the author wants. Anthropic has inference only in the United States — `inference_geo: "us"` at a price of 1.1x — and OpenAI has data residency by approval, as `infra`'s `docs/architecture.md` records.
- **The price of the EU later** is a new project, a new Neon project and new buckets with a transfer of the data.

— *Why:*
- the EU gives the first slice nothing: the account owner's sign-in goes through the United States in any region (Firebase Auth), and the slice does not accept learners from the EU and the United Kingdom before the DPIA;
- one place gives the admission function no new input: the region is not its input;
- `us-east4` has Tier 1 prices, and `europe-west3`, near Neon in Frankfurt, Tier 2 ([Cloud Run locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/locations), updated 2026-10-30); `us-east4` and `aws-us-east-1` are both in Northern Virginia.

— *Rejected:*
- **The EU, one place** — Cloud Run `europe-west3` and Neon `aws-eu-central-1`, both in Frankfurt: Tier 2 and no Cloud Run domain mapping, and `europe-west1` and `europe-west4`, with Tier 1 and domain mapping, are not near Neon; Neon `aws-eu-west-2` (London) — without some of the functions ([Regions](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/regions), "Last updated: 2026-10-14"). Domain mapping itself is Preview and not recommended for production, so it does not decide the choice;
- **by learner, both places** — two projects, two Neon databases, two sets of buckets, and the admission function gets a new input, that is, a major version of the admission table.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `run/INBOX.md`.

## Synthetic data and viewing a module's samples

**R110. Synthetic data for a module's tasks is the generator of `canvas` on the module package of the commit where the samples go, and a sample is viewed before a push on the samples page of `canvas`, in the mode "open a file".**
- **Synthetic data:** `synthetic` of `canvas` (`src/eval/synthetic.ts`, the recipe `just synthetic`) takes the open views of tasks from the module package, as `module-kit build` writes it, at the commit where the samples go — the call gives the package — and writes samples with the source `modules`: the module ID, the version and digest of this package and the tag of the newest release of `modules`, since the tag is not checked ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md)); `PURPOSE_EVAL_SET`, Apache-2.0, an ID from the seed, markup. The call names the tasks and seeds, and the seeds are those not yet in the module's eval set, and `modules` puts the files as `eval/<id>.json`. The kinds are those the generator draws: sheets and the workbook; essays — when `canvas` begins to draw them. The code of a sample from a seed stays with `canvas`.
- **Viewing:** the samples page of `canvas` opens a sample file in the same build, without a network: it shows the strokes of the final geometry, the crops and the texts of the markup, changing nothing, saving nothing and calling no AI. So the eval-set organizer and the module's author look in a sample for a name, a signature and contacts before a push, and neither an AI nor an agent looks at it ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md)).

— *Why:* a pull request that changes the open view of a task remakes its samples in the same pull request, by `modules`' own rule, and the runner of stage 2 will check the task on synthetic data at the same time as it changes. `canvas` already reads a sample file with its `src/eval/` and draws these strokes and crops, the page works without a network and calls no AI, and the implementation is one for everyone who contributes samples.

— *Rejected:* synthetic data on the package of a release of `modules` — the synthetic data of a changed task would be lost until the next release; the generator as a library of `canvas`, and the script of the call in `modules` — the code of a sample would split across two repositories; without synthetic data — the module's eval set would hold only people's samples, by the form and with a manual check; viewing by a recipe of `spec` that writes an HTML page, or by a recipe of `modules`' own — a second implementation of what the page of `canvas` already draws.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `run/INBOX.md`.

## The contents of format 0.4

**R111. Format 0.4 holds these contents. The word mark on a handwritten choice is `notation: options | word`: with `word` the key and the read value are one word of letters, and the options stay phrases. The kind `time` admits into notation minutes from 60 too, compares hours and minutes as numbers and knows no 12-hour dial. A worked example on the workbook is in 0.4, with its own leak rule. A list of steps in a lesson's explanation is the part `numbered_list`.** The numbers are by `modules` at `main` ea2a2ba, `canvas` at `main` 73807f2 and `module-kit` at `main` aa7686c, read 2026-11-08. Normative — the [format text](../format/README.md).

- **The word mark.** The check field `notation` of a handwritten choice, `options` or `word`, by default `options` — as it was. With `word` the key is one word of letters, and the value first loses `.`, `!` and `?` at the end. A value that is one word of letters not among the options is "not yet" and a rung, like an incorrect number. A phrase not among the options is "not in notation", as before. Traps stay values from the options, and an option may be a phrase.
- **The kind `time`.** A value is in notation when it is `H:MM` or `HH:MM` after the format text's steps 1 to 5 of numbers, with minutes of two or three digits. The key has hours 0–23, minutes 00–59. A value is correct when its hours and minutes as numbers equal the hours and minutes of the key: `07:30` is correct with the key `7:30`. The kind does not compute the sum of minutes, and minutes from 60 are "not yet", while a trap value may have them. There is no parameter of 12 or 24 hours: `7:30` and `19:30` are different times.
- **A worked example on the workbook.** The `workbook` canvas of an example is the example's lines with boxes, and the demo fills the boxes step by step, on the layout of a workbook's page, `page.yaml`. `lesson.no-leaks` finds a leak when a line of the example with its values equals a line of a task of the lesson with its keys: the example solves the lesson's task. The search for numbers does not see separate numbers of the example's lines.
- **A list of steps.** The part of a lesson's explanation `numbered_list` is texts in order, and the app draws the numbers, and the search for numbers does not see them. The glossary's term is "numbered list" («нумерованный список»).
- **What before v1** — in the row of the epic "Format v1" of table 2, `run/EPICS.md`, not in table 4: what to remove at v1.0 because no module of the first slice uses it, and the questions at the version's boundary.

— *Why:*
- the mark: of the 44 tasks with a handwritten word, the options are one word in 15, and in 29 they are phrases, almost always traps: "It is impossible to tell" — in 27, "Ben and Kim", "red or blue". `modules` rejected rewriting them: a child writes "It is impossible to tell" by hand without trouble. An incorrect word of an answer is a name from the statement that is not among the options: "Maya", "Amy", and where the statement writes "Alice (A)" — "A". The name `notation` is the glossary's term "notation" («допустимая запись»): the mark changes exactly what is in notation. There are no boolean fields in the format, and switches are enumerations with a default value, like `form: any | reduced`;
- `time`: 14 tasks of `time-clocks` have the trap `time-unit-mixup` — "an hour has 100 minutes": `5:60`, `7:70`, `10:100`. With minutes 00–59 alone, as first planned, they would be "unreadable" and lose the trap text, and with a comparison by the sum of minutes 7 of them would equal the key or another trap: `5:60` = `6:00`, `7:95` = `8:35`. The module writes time by 24 hours, "at 18:40… go out?" — `21:10`, and in two tasks of time zones `9:00` and `21:00` are different answers. No trap equals its key modulo 12 hours;
- the example on the workbook: in the lessons of `grade-3-math` there is not a single digit. `lesson.no-leaks` looks in each text of a lesson for the keys of the tasks of its pages, and for division with a remainder the keys are 0–8, for the multiplication table 4–64. With the search for numbers as it was, "17 ÷ 5 = 3 r 2" would be a leak, and no example could be made. An example's leak is a task of the lesson solved in it, not a number in it;
- the list of steps: in all 41 lessons of `olympiad-math` the explanation ends with "How to solve: …" and three steps without numbers: the search for numbers would read "3." as a number. `steps` are the solving steps of a task, and one term means one thing.

— *Rejected:*
- the mark with every option one word of letters, as first planned — it would work in 15 tasks of 44; asking `modules` to rewrite the options — `modules` rejected this; `form: any | word` — it would extend the "form rule" of a fraction; a boolean field — the first in the format, and the format's conventions are silent about booleans;
- `time` with minutes 00–59 alone, as first planned — 14 traps "unreadable"; a comparison by the sum of minutes — `5:60` is correct with the key `6:00`; a parameter of 12 or 24 hours now — no task needs it. Where a learner answers by the 12-hour dial, `modules` sets a trap, `9:10` for `21:10`, and the parameter will come by a minor change when the content asks for it;
- an example on the workbook with the search for numbers as it was — no example could be made; putting the example off until after 0.4 — one more move of all the repositories, and `canvas` cannot do the demo yet and will make it as a task of its own, with 0.4 too;
- `method_steps` — two kinds of steps beside `steps`.

— *Consequence:* `format/README.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/EPICS.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## Legal analysis and the data before the first child

**R112. The platform has no lawyer: legal questions are decided by the author on Claude's analysis. Claude reads the primary sources — the text of a law, a rule or guidance of a regulator, a provider's terms — and gives for each question a quote with the date read, the risks, the options and a recommendation, and the author takes the decision. The analysis is not legal advice, and the risk of an error, in children's law among others, is the author's. So it is everywhere, and at the public launch too.**
- **What the analysis gives:** for each claim about a law or terms — the primary source, a quote and the date read, a record of `docs/sources.md` as every fact that no run of ours checks. What was not confirmed, or where the primary source is silent, is not claimed, but stays an open question with options. Where sources diverge or the text of a law allows two readings, the analysis names both and which one the recommendation chooses.
- **What the author decides:** each question of the registers «П» and «О» that earlier waited for a lawyer — with options and a recommendation, as any open question. The decision is recorded in the log, as the others are.
- **How to read older texts:** «решает юрист», «вопрос юристу», «после ответа юриста», «проверка юристом» in the archives `docs/plan/` and in earlier texts of the log read as the author's decision on Claude's analysis. A document where this sounds like a rule in force is corrected. The deployment fact `minor_safeguards` is declared once the author has decided, on Claude's analysis, that the safeguards are enough, not once a lawyer has said so.
- **The risk** is named plainly: in the law of children's data an error is costly — COPPA, GDPR and the Age Appropriate Design Code punish the operator, not whoever analysed. Claude's analysis may misread a law, may not know a decision of a court or a regulator that is not in open sources, and does not replace the responsibility of a licensed lawyer to a client.

— *Why:* the «П» questions waited for a lawyer for weeks by the calendar, while their primary sources are open, and an analysis of them with quotes and dates is the same work that the documents already do for the providers' terms.

— *Rejected:* Claude's analysis up to and including the closed beta, and a licensed lawyer before the public launch: the closed beta with the children of families we know is already under COPPA and GDPR, but the risk in it is smaller than at the public launch; a licensed lawyer before the first child.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `RUN.md`.

**R113. A learner's works — every work of the profile, the handwriting on a task with a key, an essay and a drawing alike — are stored on the server only if whoever consents for the learner turned this on for the profile; by default storage is off. Storage once on is turned off in one step, and turning it off erases the copies on the server, and the stored works go into the export.**
- **When.** Storing works on the server comes with the essays module, before the first child: otherwise the only copy of a work depends on the browser's rules. Until then, and in a profile where storage is not turned on, the page "This device" in the section for adults warns of the loss; the sign-out erases nothing on the device and warns of none.
- **What is stored** is a stored work, the glossary's term: the work as the device holds it — its history of writing, the context of each submission and its picture, the PNG of the strokes the surface shows —, not the read text and not the words of the feedback; at most 4 MiB, 4,194,304 bytes, counted as the sum of the three. "Artifact" stays the work that is itself the result. Recordings are no stored work: voice input is closed to children (О-6), and a recording comes with its own rules in `docs/privacy.md`. The server does not read a stored work and does not give it to an AI provider: a work is assessed by its picture from the device. Of an essay's attempt the server still stores only the marks of the criteria, and the read text and the words of the feedback are nowhere on the server ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md)); the stored work is not part of the attempt, but a work that whoever consents for the learner asked to keep.
- **Who turns it on:** the account owner, for each profile separately. A learner who gives consent themselves — at the age of digital consent of their country or above — turns storage of their works on and off themselves, in their own profile, and this is their explicit consent; the account owner does not turn it on for them. Any other child neither turns storage on nor turns it off. What the switch says, and on what basis what an essay discloses about health is stored, is the decision on essays as personal data.
- **The switch** is the method `SetWorkStorage`: turning it on is a consent by the text `storage-consent` with its version, by an adult's action, and for a learner who gives consent themselves, by their learning request; the storage consent record lives while the profile lives, and turning storage off writes its date.
- **The methods** are `WorkService` of the contract: a stored work comes to the server, is read back and is erased one at a time, not as a copy of a submission ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md)).
  - `PutWork`, a learning request while storage is on, replaces the work kept of the same attempt; `app` puts it when it writes it to the device, at each submission and when the attempt closes at least. It takes the work's kind from the attempt's task, or from the work kept of it before. A work over the limit gets `CAUSE_WORK_TOO_LARGE`, one put while storage is off `CAUSE_STORAGE_OFF`, and `app` keeps it on the device alone. A digest of the attempt's package that the index of `api`'s image does not know gets `CAUSE_PACKAGE_UNKNOWN`, whatever work was kept before; a withdrawn version, which the image still holds, gives the kind by its task; a version out of the window of formats `api` reads, with no work of the attempt kept before, `failed_precondition` with `CAUSE_VERSION_NOT_GIVEN`, since that code always carries a cause in the contract — `api` still gives it with no `Refusal` (Д246); a message larger than `api` reads — 11 MiB for every method, `api`'s limit —, `resource_exhausted` with no `Refusal`, which `app` reads as `CAUSE_WORK_TOO_LARGE`; a `history_length` below 0, `invalid_argument`.
  - `ListWorks` and `GetWork`, a learning request or an adult's action, restore a work on another device and export it; `DeleteWork` goes by whoever decides the storage, as `SetWorkStorage`.
  - While the profile waits for a consent or for its age, `DeleteWork` goes as switching the storage off goes, and the learner's `ListWorks` and `GetWork` go as the learner's `ExportProfile` goes: erasing one work and exporting are no learning.
- **The export** carries each stored work as the device holds it, by `GetWork`; what `api` takes for it is Д233.
- **What changes in the promises:** "what the learner writes by hand stays on the device" is true while storage is not turned on, and the privacy policy speaks of this choice. With storage on, a child's admission in an essay of harm to themselves or from others lies on the server, but nobody reads it.
- **The DPIA.** The processing and the data are those it rests on: a stored work carries out the consent already given ([docs/dpia.md](dpia.md)).

— *Why:*
- We collect a minimum of data, and storage on the server is an adult's choice, not a default. An adult to whom it matters not to lose works turns it on with one tap.
- Version 1 of `storage-consent`, in force, promises to erase a work, "each work of this profile", and a text in force does not change: a copy of a submission is not the work the text promises, and a handwriting not sent would be lost.
- The limit: the history of a sheet and a picture of it fit in a few hundred kilobytes, and 4 MiB keeps a request of Cloud Run and a row of the database small while no ordinary work reaches it.
- The consent record ends with the profile: after the profile is deleted the works are gone already, and the child consent is proved by its minimal record.
- While the profile waits, a learner who decides the storage could otherwise erase every work at once but not one, and could not export the works the export reads one at a time.

— *Rejected:*
- storage on by default, with the adult turning it off — more children's data on the server without an adult's choice; never — the only copy depends on the browser; always;
- keeping the storage consent record for 5 years after the profile as well — without the profile ID there is nothing to link it to the works, which are gone already;
- a stored work as a copy of the submission; essays only, the rest later;
- no limit — one request could fill the database; a limit per part — three numbers for one promise;
- refusing `DeleteWork` and the learner's `ListWorks` and `GetWork` while the profile waits;
- `failed_precondition` with no `Refusal` for a version out of the window, as `api` gave it.

— *Consequence:* `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/work.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/cause.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `export/README.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

**R114. Development agents — Claude Code, Codex and any others — get no learners' works, no eval samples that lie outside the repositories, no signed volunteers' forms and no records of them, and no scans of signed parental consent forms: the operator keeps those outside the repositories and outside the database of `api`. The provider's training on the agent's data is turned off, and where this depends on the plan, the agent works on a plan where the provider does not train on the data.**
- **What is in the repositories:** synthetic samples and samples that adult volunteers and authors made for eval lie openly in the modules, as the modules themselves do, and the agents see them. There are no learners' works in the repositories: a hard rule every NovaTrail repository shares.
- **Anthropic, Claude Code** ([Data usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage), read 2026-11-09, sources 2.6): "Commercial users: (Team and Enterprise plans, API, 3rd-party platforms, and Claude Gov) maintain existing policies: Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms, unless the customer has chosen to provide their data to us for model improvement"; for the plans Free, Pro, Max and Ultra — "We will train new models using data from Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra accounts when this setting is on", and the setting is [claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls](https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls). So: on commercial terms there is no training; on a plan for individuals the setting is turned off, and `/feedback` and consent to show a session in a quality survey are not given — they pass on the whole session.
- **OpenAI, Codex** ([How your data is used to improve model performance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5722486-how-your-data-is-used-to-improve-model-performance); read 2026-11-09, sources 2.6: the page answers 403, and its copy in the Wayback Machine of 2026-11-01 was read — whether it has changed since was not checked, and the decision turns off both settings anyway): "By default, we don’t use inputs or outputs from ChatGPT Business, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, or our API to improve our models"; for the plans for individuals — "turn off Improve the model for everyone under Settings > Data controls in ChatGPT, or select Do not train on my content in our Privacy Portal. Either option is sufficient for ChatGPT conversations and Codex tasks", and "Codex has a separate Include environments setting in Codex settings for allowing training on full environments. Changing your settings in ChatGPT or the Privacy Portal does not change that setting". So: on a plan for individuals both settings are turned off.

— *Why:* an agent reads everything it was given and gives it to the model's provider; it needs no learners' data to write the platform's code.

— *Rejected:* no restrictions; only a ban on training, without a ban on access — the data would go to the provider with training turned off as well, with its retention periods.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `modules`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

**R115. A self-hosted copy shows the texts of its own operator: the policy, the consents and the operator's name are given by the copy's `api` without a token, and `app` shows them as its own pages, without external links. The platform gives the texts of the part `legal/` of `spec`, and a copy's operator gives their own, from a folder in the part's layout. The controller of a copy's learners' data is its operator, and the platform's author is neither a controller nor a processor, as long as the copy sends them no data and they do not set its purposes: no telemetry from the copies, no hosted service that the copies call.**
- **The texts** — `app` asks `api` for the texts, naming the language in a field of the request. The English text is the one in force, and a consent names the version, not the translation; a text version may have translations into the languages of the interface, files `texts/<id>/<n>.<tag>.md` of the part `legal/`, and `GetLegalTexts` gives the translation into the language of the screen beside the English text. Normative — [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md).
- **Without a rollout of the build** — the texts change without one: the build of `app` is one for the platform and for the copies, and the platform's texts in it would name the wrong one as the operator.
- **A copy's folder** — a copy keeps the texts of its own operator as a folder in the layout of [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md) — `VERSION`, `legal.yaml` and `texts/`, translations too — and checks it with `spec`'s recipe `legal-check-dir`. The copy's `api` reads it by the path from its configuration and does not start if the folder breaks the part's rules, and without a path gives the platform's texts from `spec.Legal`. There are no placeholders in the texts.
- **The operator's name** is the section «Who we are» of the copy's policy in force: the page «Доступность» of `app`, and every page that names the operator, links to it, and the contract has no field for it. The check of the part `legal/` has the rule `legal.operator`, which holds every part, `spec`'s own as well as a copy's folder: the part has a version of `privacy-policy` in force whose day has come — a version in force alone is not enough —, and every version of it, drafts too, has a heading of the second level that reads exactly `Who we are`, not required in a translation. So `legal-check-dir` fails a copy without it.
- **The controller.** GDPR Art. 4(7): the controller is whoever "alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data". EDPB [07/2020](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2023-10/EDPB_guidelines_202007_controllerprocessor_final_en.pdf), v2.1, read 2026-11-09 (sources 3.3): para. 67 — choosing another's tool "for its own purposes" may be a joint decision on the means, and footnote 29 — "The provider of the system can be a joint controller if the criteria mentioned above are met, i.e. if the provider participates in the determination of purposes and means"; para. 68 — there is no joint control "where the processing they carry out is separable and could be performed by one party without intervention from the other". So the platform's code sends a copy's data neither to the author nor to the platform.

— *Why:* the text that an adult accepts names whoever is responsible for the data — the operator of this copy; and the build is one for all and signed, so the texts must come not from it but from the `api` of the copy whose operator wrote them.

— *Rejected:*
- the operator's name and contact in `deployment.json`, and the texts in the build — the build would carry texts that do not suit another copy;
- the texts in the build, and a copy rebuilds `app` — a copy would take not the same signed build as the platform;
- a field of the contract for the operator's name — a second place of the same truth, which can part from the text; and no rule for the name at all.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `legal/README.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

**R116. The lawful basis under GDPR: an adult's own learning data — contract, Art. 6(1)(b), and the data of a learner under 18 — consent, Art. 6(1)(a): below the age of digital consent of the country it is given by a parent (Art. 8), and under 13 also the verifiable parental consent under COPPA; at this age and above — by the learner themselves. Verifiable parental consent is a signed form, named by a request code, whose scan the parent uploads in `app` and the operator checks; whether a card transaction with a notice to the holder comes by the public launch is П-28. Consent is withdrawn as easily as it is given. What is mandatory in a consent is given briefly in the interface language, and the full text, the one in force, in English.** Read 2026-11-09 (sources 3.3): GDPR — [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679); the EDPB guidelines [05/2020 on consent](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/files/file1/edpb_guidelines_202005_consent_en.pdf), v1.1, and [2/2019 on Art. 6(1)(b)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sites/default/files/files/file1/edpb_guidelines-art_6-1-b-adopted_after_public_consultation_en.pdf), v2.0; WP260 rev.01 on transparency, endorsed by the EDPB; COPPA — 16 CFR 312 as amended by the FTC's 2025 rule ([90 FR 16918](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-04-22/html/2025-05904.htm), published 2025-04-22, in effect from 2025-06-23, compliance from 2026-04-22; the text of the part by the eCFR API as of 2026-11-05, the eCFR page answers with a bot check); ICO — the pages on children and UK GDPR by copies of the Wayback Machine of 2026-04-28, the site answers 403.
- **An adult's basis is contract.** Art. 6(1)(b): "processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party". An adult's learning is exactly what they ordered: the learner model, the choice of tasks and the checking do not work without them (EDPB 2/2019, para. 26 — the contract, its validity and necessity). Improving the service cannot be justified so (para. 49), and the platform does nothing of the kind on this basis.
- **The basis under 18 is consent.** A contract on behalf of a child is not taken: Art. 6(1)(b) requires a contract to which the data subject themselves is a party, EDPB 2/2019 para. 13 refers to national law on children's legal capacity, and the ICO writes of a parent's contract on behalf of a child: "you should again take legal advice". Legitimate interest is rejected: Art. 6(1)(f) — "in particular where the data subject is a child". Art. 8(1) applies, "Where point (a) of Article 6(1) applies, in relation to the offer of information society services directly to a child", and a service for all ages with children's profiles the ICO considers offered to children directly: "when any age restrictions in place allow users under the age of 18". The age of digital consent is by country, by the table of [`consent-age/`](../consent-age/README.md): GDPR — 16, a country may lower it to 13 (Art. 8(1)); UK GDPR — 13 ([Art. 8](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2016/679/article/8), read 2026-11-09). EDPB 05/2020 paras. 147–149: the learner confirms, changes or withdraws the parent's consent on reaching the age of digital consent, and the platform tells them of it. **A learner at this age and above gives their own consent themselves, in their own profile in `app`, before the first work, and withdraws it there too;** the profile is created by the account owner, but they do not give consent on behalf of a learner at or above the age of digital consent. In the same way a child who has reached this age confirms the parent's consent or withdraws it at the yearly update of the category.
- **The method of verifiable consent.** COPPA §312.5(b)(1): the method "must be reasonably calculated, in light of available technology, to ensure that the person providing consent is the child's parent". From the list of §312.5(b)(2) — (i) "a consent form to be signed by the parent and returned to the operator by postal mail, facsimile, or electronic scan", the method now, and (ii) "in connection with a transaction, to use a credit card, debit card, or other online payment system that provides notification of each discrete transaction to the primary account holder", which is П-28; EDPB 05/2020 gives the same argument for Art. 8(2) — "a payment of €0,01 … via a bank transaction" (footnote 68), and para. 137: "In low-risk cases, verification of parental responsibility via email may be sufficient. Conversely, in high-risk cases, it may be appropriate to ask for more proof". A child's work goes to an AI provider, so the risk is not low.
- **The form and its scan.** The form does not ask for the child's name: it names the request code — 10 characters of Crockford base32 in two groups, `ABCDE-FGHJK`, which `api` gives, unique among the waiting ones. The parent uploads the scan in `app` (`SendConsentForm`), and `api` puts it into the private bucket of this record, where the operator checks it against the code with their command of `api` and confirms the consent or does not accept the form; the scan of a withdrawn waiting consent is erased with it. The scan is kept while the consent is in force and 5 years after the deletion, as the minimal record of a consent, and then erased. Development agents do not get the scan. COPPA: what was obtained from the parent at consent the operator keeps confidential (FAQ, A.8, a copy of the Wayback Machine of 2026-10-13); GDPR: the proof of consent — no longer than needed (EDPB 05/2020 para. 107).
- **The scans' bucket** — outside the repositories and outside the database of `api`: a bucket of its own, `<project>-consent-forms`, in the project `infra`, region `us-east4`, with the settings of the operator's private bucket, under the prefix `consent-forms/`. Only the operator reads and lists it, and `api` creates and erases objects under the prefix, reading none; `api` takes the bucket and the prefix by its variables and changes nothing. Before the first child, the bucket moves to a project of the operator's own, where CI of `infra` holds nothing (Д240).
- **Email plus and text plus** (§312.5(b)(2)(viii), (ix)) — only for an operator to whom "discloses" of §312.2 does not apply. An AI provider that only reads the work for the platform's service and for nothing else is "support for the internal operations", not a third party (§312.2, the definitions "Disclose" and "Third party") — Claude's reading, the rule does not name AI providers expressly. A provider that trains models on the data is a third party, and a disclosure to it requires a separate consent: the FTC in its commentary to the rule — "Disclosures of a child's personal information to third parties … to train or otherwise develop artificial intelligence technologies, are not integral … and would require consent". So email plus would hold only while no provider has crossed this line — and it is rejected.
- **Withdrawal.** Art. 7(3): "It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent"; EDPB 05/2020 para. 114 — by the same interface, without a fee and without losing the service.
- **The notice to the parent** (§312.4(c), (d)): what is collected and why, to whom it is disclosed and why, the retention policy (§312.10), how to give consent and how to withdraw it, the parent's rights — the texts of `legal/` for adults and for the family say this.
- **The language.** WP260 rev.01, para. 13: "A translation in one or more other languages should be provided where the controller targets data subjects speaking those languages", and the interface of `app` is in Russian too (footnote 15: "where the controller operates a website in the language in question"). Art. 12(1) — "clear and plain language", EDPB 05/2020 para. 70 — "A controller must assess what kind of audience it is". What is mandatory in a consent — who the operator is, which data and why, to whom they go, how to withdraw — `app` shows briefly in the language of the screen, as the "bite-sized" explanations of AADC std 4, and the full text, the one that is accepted and that is in force, in English. The translation is a text of the set `legal/`, not the interface dictionary. Full translations are taken for the policy: version 2 of `privacy-policy` has a translation into Russian, without force, as Connecticut's law asks (sources 3.9).

— *Why:* one basis per age that holds under both GDPR and COPPA: parental consent under COPPA is needed under 13 on any basis, and a contract with a child rests only on the country's law. A UUID of 36 characters copied by hand onto paper is copied with errors, and the upload in `app` is one path to the bucket, without the operator's mailbox. Listing a bucket cannot be narrowed by the name of an object (sources 10.2 infra), so in a bucket shared with the organizers they would list the scans' names — the consent's ID and the time of the upload.

— *Rejected:*
- consent for all — withdrawing an adult's consent would mean the end of the service, and consent suits poorly what the service cannot exist without; legitimate interest; email plus;
- a verification service — knowledge questions or a document with a face (§312.5(b)(2)(vi), (vii)) — it collects more data than needed (EDPB 05/2020 para. 145), and costs money;
- for the language — a full translation of a consent — it would have to be kept in step in all languages; English only — the consent of a parent who reads Russian may be deemed uninformed;
- the ID of the consent record on the form; a letter to the operator — one more processor and retention period, which are hard to keep; paper by post — slow, and the operator's address is needed; choosing a payment provider now — the public launch is far off;
- the scans under a prefix of the operator's shared bucket.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `infra`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

**R117. The minimal record of a child consent — a parent's, or the own consent of a learner under 18 who gave it themselves —, the record's ID, the date, the method of verification and the date of deletion, without the account and profile IDs, the pseudonym, the age category and the country, is kept for 5 years after the deletion of the account or the profile, or after the withdrawal, and erases itself. An adult's consent and a consent "waiting" are deleted whole. The period is in the written retention policy and in the privacy policy.**
- GDPR Art. 7(1): "the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented"; Art. 5(2) — accountability; Art. 17(3)(e) — erasure does not apply while the processing is needed "for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims". EDPB 05/2020 para. 107: "After the processing activity ends, proof of consent should be kept no longer then strictly necessary for compliance with a legal obligation or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims" (sources 3.3).
- COPPA sets no period for the consent record. §312.10 requires a written retention policy with the purposes, the need and the time of deletion, and a child's data "may not be retained indefinitely". The record holds no child's data, and what was obtained from the parent at consent the FTC tells to keep confidential (FAQ, A.8, a Wayback copy of 2026-10-13).
- The period is by the statute of limitations: 28 U.S.C. § 2462 ([Cornell LII](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/2462), read 2026-11-09) — "shall not be entertained unless commenced within five years from the date when the claim first accrued". That this general period holds the FTC's penalties under COPPA too is Claude's reading, not the text of the rule.
- The record can be linked to a family only through the export file held by the owner and the scan of the signed form held by the operator, which is kept for the same period.
- A learner's own consent: the withdrawal deletes the profile, and the learner's consent needs proving just as the parent's consent does (Art. 7(1)).

— *Why:* without the record the platform has nothing to prove the consent with after the deletion, and with a record longer than the statute of limitations it has nothing to justify the retention with.

— *Rejected:* 3 years — shorter than the statute of limitations; erasing it together with the account — nothing to prove the consent with; keeping it indefinitely — against §312.10 and Art. 5(1)(e).

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

**R118. The account owner's adulthood is their statement "I am 18" with a date, and for a child's profile the signed form of consent confirms it too; voicing on Android and Linux is a choice of the system that the adult makes; the device's clock offset is not geolocation but account data, of which the policy speaks.** Read 2026-11-09 (sources 3.3).
- **The owner's adulthood.** EDPB 05/2020 para. 135: "In some low-risk situations, it may be appropriate to require a new subscriber to a service to disclose their year of birth or to fill out a form stating they are not a minor"; AADC std 3: "if you provide a logged-in or subscription based service, you may allow the main (confirmed adult) account holder to set up child profiles" (a Wayback copy of 2026-09-26). The signed form confirms also that the consent is given by an adult. Whether a card transaction comes by the public launch is П-28, and the texts in force do not promise it. A country where the law requires more than a statement `api` closes before the attempt.
- **Voicing on Android and Linux.** Chromium sets `is_local_service = !voices[i].remote` (`speech_synthesis_impl.cc`), and on Android and Linux gives a voice only `native = true` (`tts_android.cc`, `tts_linux.cc`; [chromium.googlesource.com](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src), branch `main`, read 2026-11-09): every system voice there is given to the page with `localService` true, and the page cannot tell the network synthesis of the system's engine. Android lets only the app itself know this — `Voice.isNetworkConnectionRequired()` ([Android Developers](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/speech/tts/Voice), read 2026-11-09). The text is given to the synthesis engine by the browser by the adult's choice, as to their screen reader, and the platform has no agreement with the engine's provider.
- **The clock offset.** COPPA §312.2 names as personal information "Geolocation information sufficient to identify street name and name of a city or town"; an offset from UTC in minutes names a time zone, not a city. The ICO's code, std 10 — "data taken from a user's device which indicates the geographical location of that device, including GPS data or data about connection with local wifi equipment" — is silent on time zones (a Wayback copy of 2026-10-04). The offset is tied to the account, so it is account data (§312.2, para. 11), and the policy speaks of it.

— *Why:* none of the three needs more than is decided already: the statement and the method of consent — the EDPB and the ICO allow them at low risk, and for children's profiles the confirmation is given by the method of consent; voicing and the offset the platform does not turn into geodata or a disclosure by its own actions.

— *Rejected:* for adulthood — an age verification service; for voicing — no voicing on Android and Linux for children; for the offset — a time zone that the adult chooses: an extra step.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

**R119. A DPIA — before the first child, wherever they live, and before the first learner from the EU or the United Kingdom, if one comes earlier — by the ICO's template; the DPIA is [docs/dpia.md](dpia.md).** The ICO's code, std 2: "Undertake a DPIA to assess and mitigate risks to the rights and freedoms of children who are likely to access your service … Take into account differing ages, capacities and development needs", and the code applies to a service outside the EEA if "you offer your service to users in the UK … The code applies if that service is likely to be accessed by children" ("Services covered by this code"; copies of the Wayback Machine of 2026-09-26 and 2026-10-30, the site answers 403). GDPR Art. 35 requires an assessment when the processing is "likely to result in a high risk". The ICO: "A data protection impact assessment should help you to decide what steps you need to take to verify age and parental responsibility" — so the DPIA records too why the methods of consent and of age verification are proportionate to the risk.

— *Why:* the platform is open to children of any country, and a child's work goes to an AI provider; an assessment before the first child is cheaper than reworking after them, and the legal texts on children and on samples rest on it.

— *Rejected:*
- a DPIA at stage 3, by the beta and the public launch — a closed beta with children of the United Kingdom would go outside std 2;
- a DPIA only before the first learner from the EU or the United Kingdom — the earlier recommendation, made before the ICO's code was weighed;
- a DPIA within the analysis of consent and the account — it would not know the outcomes of the analyses of the AI providers and of samples and eval sets.

— *Consequence:* `docs/dpia.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/product.md`; `RUN.md`.

## The eval key in CI

**R120. The platform's keys for eval lie in the Secret Manager of `infra` — a secret per AI provider, `eval-key-<provider code>`: `eval-key-anthropic` and `eval-key-openai` —, and the CI of `modules` and `tutor` reads them through Workload Identity Federation, by its own pool `github-eval`, with no long-lived copy in GitHub. The pool admits only the job of the GitHub environment `eval` of these two repositories and does not admit Dependabot; it and its provider `github` are made by `bootstrap.sh` of `infra`, apart from its CI pool with the deployment accounts, which stays only with `infra`, and the OpenTofu module of `infra` makes the secrets and the rights to them. On a pull request from a fork and from Dependabot the eval job fails and names the reason, and a maintainer carries a Dependabot change over into their own branch and opens their own pull request from it.** The primary sources were read 2026-11-09.
- **The place.** The Secret Manager of the project `infra`, with user-managed replication, with the location `us-east4`, and not a regional secret: "Regional secrets can only be accessed by applications or services running within the same location" ([Secret Manager, Regional secrets and data residency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/regional-secrets/data-residency), updated 2026-10-26), and a GitHub runner is not in this location. A secret with user-managed replication "has its payload data replicated to a user configured set of locations" ([Choosing a replication policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/choosing-replication)). The values are put in by the author — `gcloud secrets versions add` —, not by code: no secret lies in a repository. Each key has its own spending limit at the provider, set by the author, and the price of a run is named before the first launch. A new eval provider is a new secret in the module of `infra`, by the provider code of the admission table.
- **The own pool.** The pool `github-eval` and its provider `github` are made by `bootstrap.sh` of `infra`, separate from its CI pool: that pool admits only the tokens of `infra`, `bootstrap.sh` at each run returns its provider's condition to its own, and in it are the production deployment accounts. The pool is not in the OpenTofu module: there it would require for `infra-config` a role on the project's pools, and IAM conditions do not narrow pools — `iam.googleapis.com` is not among the services with resource attributes (Google Cloud, IAM Conditions, resource attributes, updated 2026-11-07). With such a role `infra-config` could change the condition of the pool through which it enters itself, and it borrows the deployment accounts already. In the pool `github-eval` there is nothing but access to the eval secrets. The mapping is `google.subject=assertion.sub`, and the provider's condition is `assertion.repository_owner_id=='344507087' && (assertion.repository_id=='1425775415' || assertion.repository_id=='1425813274') && assertion.environment=='eval' && assertion.actor!='dependabot[bot]'`: the numeric IDs of `altnovatrail`, `modules` and `tutor` (the GitHub API, read 2026-11-09), because "Using "name" fields like repository and repository_owner increases the chances of cybersquatting and typosquatting attacks … use the numeric *_id fields instead" ([Workload Identity Federation with deployment pipelines](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines), updated 2026-11-07), and "Always add an Attribute Condition to restrict entry into the Workload Identity Pool" ([google-github-actions/auth](https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth), README, branch `main`).
- **The sign-in.** Direct Workload Identity Federation, without an intermediary service account: "Without this input, the GitHub Action will use Direct Workload Identity Federation" (the README of `auth`; the latest release v3.0.0 of 2025-08-28, the tag on 7c6bc770dae815cd3e89ee6cdf493a5fab2cc093), and Google advises the same: "we recommend that you grant direct resource access to the principal" (ibid.); Secret Manager supports direct access — "No known limitations" ([Supported services](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/federated-identity-supported-services)). Each eval secret gets `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` for two principals of the pool `github-eval`: `principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/<project number>/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-eval/subject/repo:altnovatrail@344507087/modules@1425775415:environment:eval` and the same with `tutor@1425813274`. The immutable `sub` is already turned on for `modules` and `tutor` (`use_immutable_subject: true`, the GitHub API `actions/oidc/customization/sub`, read 2026-11-09).
- **Who reads — the environment `eval`.** "The subject claim includes the environment name when the job references an environment" ([GitHub Docs, OpenID Connect reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc)), so the key goes only to a job with `environment: eval`, and other jobs of the same pull request do not get it. The environment's branch rule is "Selected branches and tags": `main` and `refs/pull/*/merge`, because "The deployment branch or tag rule is matched against the `GITHUB_REF` of the workflow run. … Adding another branch rule for `refs/pull/*/merge` would also allow workflows triggered by `pull_request` events to deploy to the environment" ([Deployments and environments](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments)); without it a pull request's job does not enter the environment. The environment has no reviewers: eval runs on every pull request, and the spending is held by the key's limit at the provider.
- **A fork.** `modules` and `tutor` are public. For a pull request from a fork "the permissions are adjusted to change any write permissions to read only" ([Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)), and `id-token` — "This requires `id-token: write`" (ibid.), so it has no OIDC token; the exception is the setting "Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests", and it exists only for "forks of private repositories" ([Managing GitHub Actions settings for a repository](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/enabling-features-for-your-repository/managing-github-actions-settings-for-a-repository)).
- **Dependabot can get an OIDC token:** "By default, GitHub Actions workflows triggered by Dependabot get a `GITHUB_TOKEN` with read-only permissions. You can use the `permissions` key in your workflow to increase the access for the token" ([Troubleshooting Dependabot on GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/troubleshooting-dependabot/troubleshooting-dependabot-on-github-actions)). So two places hold it back: the provider's condition refuses a token whose `actor` is `dependabot[bot]`, and the first step of the eval job fails and names the reason if the pull request is not from a branch of the repository itself (`github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository`) or was opened by Dependabot (`github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'`) — by the pull request's author, not by `github.actor`, which names whoever started the run.
- **A Dependabot change.** A maintainer reads it, puts Dependabot's commit into their own branch of the repository, opens their own pull request from it — the job runs in their name —, and closes Dependabot's pull request. There is no Dependabot secret with a copy of the key: "Secrets are populated from Dependabot secrets. GitHub Actions secrets are not available" ([Dependabot on GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-on-actions)), and it would be a second long-lived copy.
- **What each does:**
  - `infra`: `bootstrap.sh` — the pool `github-eval` and the provider `github` with the condition above, its CI pool unchanged; the OpenTofu module — the secrets `eval-key-anthropic` and `eval-key-openai` without values, with user-managed replication in `us-east4`, and the `secretAccessor` bindings to the two principals; tests;
  - `modules` and `tutor`: the environment `eval` with the branch rule `main` and `refs/pull/*/merge`, without reviewers; the eval job — `environment: eval`, `permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }`, the first step is the check of the fork and of the pull request's author, then `google-github-actions/auth` by SHA, with the `workload_identity_provider` of the pool `github-eval` and without `service_account`, and the reading of the secrets;
  - the author: the values of the keys, their spending limits at the providers, and before the first run — the price.

  What is still to do is Д149.

— *Why:* the key is one per provider and lives in one place, and GitHub gets only a token for ten minutes — "the resulting token has a maximum lifetime of 10 minutes" (the README of `auth`); the own pool separates the pull requests of the two repositories from the production deployment accounts, and the environment separates the eval job from the other jobs of the same repositories. Made by `bootstrap.sh`, the pool keeps the same boundary, and `infra-config` gets no rights over its own door.

— *Rejected:*
- an eval environment secret in each repository — a long-lived copy of the key in GitHub in two places;
- a Dependabot secret — one more copy;
- the shared CI pool of `bootstrap.sh` with a widened condition: the production pool with the deployment accounts would open to the pull request jobs of the two repositories, and only the precision of the bindings would separate them;
- the pool in the OpenTofu module, with a role on the pools for `infra-config` — it could change the condition of its own door;
- a separate Google Cloud project for eval — a second project with a bootstrap, a state and a budget, while the own pool gives isolation too;
- a binding by `sub` without the environment — any job of any workflow would get the key;
- a condition by `job_workflow_ref` — the workflow file is edited in a branch, so the boundary is the same, and there is no setting visible in GitHub;
- one JSON secret with all the keys — changing one key would change them all;
- a maintainer's commit into Dependabot's branch — after it Dependabot stops rebasing the pull request, and the check by the pull request's author would not let the job in anyway.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `.github`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `infra`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## AI providers

**R121. The processor agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic enter their terms by themselves, and for OpenAI the author also signs a copy by a form; zero data retention the author asks of both now. For learners under 18, while the provider has approved neither it nor the exclusion of content from the abuse monitoring logs, the fact `minimal_retention` does not hold and platform AI is closed to them; for `adult` the fact is no condition: the cell of platform AI opens with `data_processing_agreement` alone, at Anthropic and at OpenAI, and the privacy policy names what the provider keeps. `tutor` calls only the paths that zero data retention covers, and the models of Anthropic that need retention of 30 days are outside the list of models admitted for learners' works. What zero data retention does not lift the privacy policy names.** Read 2026-11-09.
- **OpenAI's DPA.** Services Agreement, §5.3: "If Customer uses the Services to process Personal Data, OpenAI and Customer will comply with the DPA, which is incorporated by this reference into the Agreement"; the DPA — "supplements, and is incorporated into, the OpenAI Services Agreement", "Updated: December 1, 2025", "Effective: January 1, 2026", and §1.1 — "OpenAI acts as a Data Processor on the Customer’s behalf". On the DPA's page there is the link "Execute Data Processing Agreement", an Ironclad form, for a signed copy. openai.com answers 403: copies of the Wayback Machine were read — the [Services Agreement](https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement) of 2026-11-07 and the [DPA](https://openai.com/policies/data-processing-addendum) of 2026-10-28. The DPA does not speak of children.
- **Anthropic's DPA.** The [Commercial Terms](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms), "Effective Jun 17, 2025", section C: "Data submitted through the Services will be processed in accordance with the Anthropic Data Processing Addendum ("DPA"), which is incorporated into these Terms by reference"; the [DPA](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum), "Effective Feb 24, 2025": "Customer is the controller and Anthropic is Customer's processor"; section B: "Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services". Neither speaks of children.
- **OpenAI's zero data retention** ([Data controls in the OpenAI platform](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data), no date): "these controls are subject to prior approval by OpenAI and acceptance of additional requirements", the application — "Get in touch with our sales team". Covered are `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions`, where "the store parameter … will always be treated as false", and `/v1/files`, `/v1/conversations`, `/v1/assistants`, `/v1/vector_stores` and `/v1/batches` are not. It does not lift: "Image and file inputs are scanned for CSAM content upon submission. If the classifier detects potential CSAM content, the image will be retained for manual review", and "Safety Retention" — "we may retain and human review customer content when using these models that our classifiers detect as potentially violating our Usage Policies". Without zero data retention — "abuse monitoring logs are generated for all API feature usage and retained for up to 30 days", and Responses keeps the state for 30 days unless `store` is `false`.
- **Anthropic's zero data retention** ([API and data retention](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention), no date; [Zero data retention](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/8956058), updated 2026-10-15): "To request ZDR for your organization, contact the Anthropic sales team", "subject to Anthropic's approval"; covered are Messages and Token Counting, while Batch — "29-day retention", the Files API and the Console are not. It does not lift: "Anthropic still retains User Safety classifier results", and "if a chat or session is flagged, Anthropic may retain inputs and outputs for up to 2 years" and the classifiers' scores — "for up to 7 years" ([7996866](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866), updated 2026-07-01). The models "Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, and Claude Mythos 5: These models require 30-day data retention and are not available under ZDR unless expressly authorized by Anthropic" ([Covered Models](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15425695), updated 2026-09-01); the Covered Models are also Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, designated 2026-11-09, which keep content "at least 30 days" (sources 2.9). The pages on default retention diverge — 30 days in 7996866 and "not retained by default" in API and data retention —, and the decision does not rest on this: the fact is held by an approved zero data retention.
- **What `tutor` does:** at OpenAI — Responses with `store: false` and the picture in the body of the request, without `/v1/files`; at Anthropic — Messages, without the Files API and Batch; the Covered Models are outside the list of models admitted for learners' works, for `adult` too ([`admission/models.go` of `tutor` at 8ec7e91](https://github.com/altnovatrail/tutor/blob/8ec7e91/admission/models.go) names `claude-opus-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5`), until Anthropic permits them under zero data retention: they keep content longer than the privacy policy names.
- **The admission table** takes this into the descriptions of the facts: `data_processing_agreement` holds when the agreement is in force — signed or part of terms the platform accepted — and nothing in it excludes requests of learners of the declared categories; the date the terms were read is 2026-11-09 for each cell but the cell of platform AI of `adult` at Anthropic: when it opened, Anthropic's row was read again whole, and the cell has 2026-11-15, while OpenAI's row was read again then but for its Usage Policies, so its cell keeps 2026-11-09 (sources 2.9).
- **What the privacy policy names for `adult`**, in its version in force from 2026-11-28: what the provider keeps — Anthropic deletes within 30 days, OpenAI keeps its abuse monitoring logs up to 30 days.
- **The author's step:** sign a copy of OpenAI's DPA by the Ironclad form and submit applications for zero data retention to the sales of OpenAI and Anthropic — the texts of the applications are written by Claude. The price and the "additional requirements" are not published: before signing anything, the author names them. For children the application still stands: the cells under 18 need it.

— *Why:* without zero data retention a child's work lies at the provider for 30 days, and OpenAI requires it for under 13; the application is the only path, and it is worth submitting before it is needed.

— *Rejected:*
- an application to one provider first — without the second, two readers of different providers cannot be assembled;
- the paths that zero data retention does not cover — the Files API and Batch.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `admission/admission-table.json`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`.

**R122. An own key is only for a profile of the category `adult`; to a learner under 18 it is closed at all providers.** `api` does so already (О-4).
- The key's owner is the provider's "Customer". OpenAI: the Services Agreement is for "customers who are businesses and developers", and by §3.3(c) the Customer does not allow "minors to use OpenAI Services without consent from their parent or guardian"; zero data retention for under 13 — only by the approval of sales, which a family's key does not have. Anthropic: "individuals and hobbyists are welcome to use the Claude API. However … use of the API is subject to our Commercial Terms of Service, regardless of whether you are an individual or representing a company" ([8987200](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8987200), updated 2026-03-16), and "Customer is responsible for all activity under its account" (Commercial Terms, D.5). With an own key a family would become an organization serving minors, with the measures the providers require of one, which it will not carry out.

— *Why:* the obligations to the provider would fall on the family, and the platform cannot carry them out for it.

— *Rejected:* opening the own key to a learner of 13–18 at or above the age of digital consent, with the platform's measures — by the terms the key's owner is obliged to keep the measures anyway; a learner exactly at that age consents themselves, and the rejection holds for them too.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `RUN.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

**R123. The measures for minors that OpenAI and Anthropic require the platform keeps as a list per provider, with the status of each; to the provider's measures it adds its own — an adult's "report a problem" at the tutor's answer and an escalation path with the operator, with a review period of 3 days —, and it does not monitor the content of works itself. When all of a provider's measures are met, the author decides by analysis that they are sufficient, and only then does the operator declare `minor_safeguards`.**
- **OpenAI** ([Under-18 API guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-checks/under-18-api-guidance), read 2026-11-09, no date): "Providing age-appropriate disclosures to minors about AI tools and how to use them responsibly", "Implementing age-appropriate content filters", "Implementing reasonable monitoring and reporting mechanisms, including escalation paths for high-risk interactions", "Where required or otherwise appropriate for your use case, using age assurance systems"; and "OpenAI reserves the right to audit organizations for compliance with this policy. Customers who fail to demonstrate compliance may receive warnings and, in cases of repeated or serious noncompliance, may be subject to suspension or termination of API access". The [Usage Policies](https://openai.com/policies/usage-policies), "Effective: November 20, 2026", a copy of the Wayback Machine of 2026-11-06: "Keep young people safe", and among the prohibitions — "inference regarding an individual’s emotions in the workplace and educational settings, except when necessary for medical or safety reasons" and "automation of high-stakes actions in sensitive areas without human review … education".
- **Anthropic** ([Guidelines for organizations serving minors](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9307344-responsible-use-of-anthropic-s-models-guidelines-for-organizations-serving-minors), updated 2026-03-16): "Age verification systems", "Content moderation and filtering", "Monitoring and reporting mechanisms to identify and address potential issues", "Educational resources and guidance for minors", "a child-safety system prompt, which organizations serving minors should implement", COPPA and a statement about it on the site, "Organizations must disclose to their users that they are interacting with an AI system rather than a human"; and "Anthropic will periodically audit organizations for compliance with these safeguards". The [Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup), "Effective Nov 12, 2026": "Products serving minors … must comply with the additional guidelines outlined in our Support article and all applicable laws", and "We define a minor or child to be any individual under the age of 18 years old, regardless of jurisdiction".
