- An image in base64, beside the history as JSON: the owner gets the picture and can build the strokes again.
- A file for each work and each page keeps every answer within one file, read with no library; a work changed between `ExportProfile` and `GetWork` would make the export say two things of it.
- The pages are `app`'s to write: the photo, the crops and the work stay on the device. The open attempts of tasks from paper are what `api` keeps of the learner, so the owner gets them; the model's hidden solution and answer never leave the server, where they would name the answer.
- `export.case`: a file system that does not tell case apart would make two files or folders of the export one when it is unpacked, one lost without a word.
- `correction_id`: a correction is no attempt, and the log stays one sequence by `seq`.
- A reload is how `app` already meets a contract newer than its build, with no new field; an export stays whole.

— *Rejected:*
- one JSON file into which `app` inserts the part of `api` — fragile, and the part of `api` would become a string inside a string; both bytes and JSON in the export — two forms of one value to keep in step; only bytes — not readable without a protobuf library; a proto package `novatrail.export.v1` for the records — such formats are normative parts, the way of `deployment/`;
- an image as a file of its own — a file of the export that is not JSON; the picture alone, without the history — the owner could not build the strokes again; holding the size to the work's file — the size counts the bytes `api` keeps, which the JSON value of the history does not give back;
- a reader of one version bound to read the earlier ones too — the part's check would carry two versions of its schemas;
- `ExportProfile` and `ExportAccount` naming the version `app` writes, and `api` giving either — a new field and two writers in `api`; no export and no word why until the build reloads; after the third new beginning, an export of the works as `GetWork` gave them — the rule and the manifest would change; `api` refusing `PutWork` of the profile while an export goes on — a new cause and a new state in `api`;
- `file_id` in small letters alone, with `api` held to them — it would narrow the form of the IDs `api` gives beyond what the clash needs;
- a correction's ID in `attempt_id`; the corrections as a list of their own in the profile's file — the log would no longer be one sequence by `seq`;
- the hidden solution and answer of an open attempt of a task from paper in the export — they would name the answer; the attempts of tasks from paper left out of `api.zip` — the owner would not see what `api` keeps.

— *Open:* `api` and `app` write the export by the current version — the stored works listed without bytes and fetched one by one by `GetWork`, the restart and the reload (Д233).

— *Consequence:* `export/`; `tools/export/`; `spec.go`; `types/exportv<version>/`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/account.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`.

**R136. The consent contract: confirmation of parental consent by a signed form, the scan of which `app` uploads by the request code; a learner's own consent and its withdrawal in their profile, and a teenager's withdrawal of the consent a parent gave; cancelling a waiting one and the limit of "waiting" consents; age and country anew; storage of works as a consent; the text version in each consent record; "report a problem" with storage for a year after handling.**
- **Who gives consent** — by the category: for a learner below the country's age of digital consent — a parent, at it and above — the learner themselves, for their own profile — the owner. `ChildConsent` and `ProfileConsent` name this by the field `giver`, and `ProfileConsent.need` names what the profile waits for before the next work: the learner's own consent, a parental consent or the age; while it waits, a learning request gets `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT` or `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED` ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md)).
- **Parental consent** is a signed form `parent-consent` with the request code: 10 characters of Crockford base32, `ABCDE-FGHJK`, unique among the waiting ones. A scan, a photo or a PDF up to 10 MiB the adult uploads in `app`, `SendConsentForm`; `api` puts it into the private bucket of the consent forms, and the operator checks it against the code with its command and confirms the consent or does not accept the form, and then a new one is sent. A card transaction — by the public launch (П-28).
- **A learner's own consent** — `GiveOwnConsent` by the text `teen-consent`, in their profile, before the first work: the profile of such a learner `CreateChildProfile` creates at once. With it too a learner who has grown to the age confirms the consent that a parent gave.
- **Withdrawal** is deletion of the profile with everything in it, with the minimal record of the consent: parental consent — `DeleteProfile`, one's own — `WithdrawOwnConsent`, by a learning request. A teenager who has grown to the age of digital consent under a parental consent also withdraws it: `WithdrawOwnConsent` is valid at a profile that waits for the learner's own consent, `CONSENT_NEED_OWN`, and deletes the profile, as `DeleteProfile` does; `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED` — only at a profile whose consent an adult gave and which does not wait for the learner's own consent. A learner who gave consent themselves also exports before the withdrawal themselves: `ExportProfile` with `ACTION_LEARNING`. Neither `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT` nor `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED` refuses requests about the consent itself — `GiveOwnConsent`, `WithdrawOwnConsent`, the learner's export, turning storage off and `ReportProblem` —, nor `DeleteWork`, which goes as turning the storage off goes, nor the learner's `ListWorks` and `GetWork`, which go as the learner's `ExportProfile` goes. The profile of a learner who gave consent themselves is deleted by an adult's `DeleteProfile` too: the account is the owner's, and `app` says so before that. Deletion leaves problem reports until their period, without an ID. `GetAccount` does not show what was withdrawn or cancelled: of them only the minimal record remains, without the account ID.
- **Cancelling** — `CancelChildConsent`, at a consent without a profile: a waiting one is erased whole, with the scan, and a confirmed one is cancelled as a withdrawal — with the minimal record and the scan for their period; neither counts toward the limit any more. The limit is `CAUSE_TOO_MANY_CONSENTS`, `resource_exhausted`, without data; the number is set by `api`, and a retry with the same key gets the same consent even at the limit.
- **Age and country anew** — `RestateAge`, by an adult action: when the country raised the age of digital consent (`CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED`), at the yearly confirmation, which `Profile.age_check_due` marks a year later, and with a change of country. A category that needs another consent leaves the profile waiting for it: the learner's own consent or a parental consent with a new code.
- **Storage of works** — `SetWorkStorage`: turning it on is a consent by `storage-consent` of whoever consents for the learner, and for a learner who gives consent themselves — by their own learning request; the wrong kind of action gets `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED` or the new cause `CAUSE_LEARNER_DECIDES`. The record lives as long as the profile lives. Storage that an adult turned on `app` offers to the teenager after the confirmation, on a separate screen: the consent is the teenager's `SetWorkStorage`, which, for storage turned on by an adult, is not a repeat but a record of their own consent in place of the adult's; a refusal turns storage off and erases the copies, and `app` offers the export before that.
- **Text version** — `LegalTextRef`, which the request that gives consent takes from `GetLegalTexts`; one not current — `CAUSE_TEXT_NOT_CURRENT`. `RequestChildConsent` and `RestateAge` always name `parent-consent` while the text has a version in force: who gives consent only `api` computes, and it writes the version only into a parental consent.
- **"Report a problem"** — `AttemptService.ReportProblem`, by a learning request from the task screen (to whom `app` shows the button — П-26): which answer and rung, the words as `app` showed them, a word of the closed set and a text; the answer is an ID and the review period, 3 days. `api` stores it until the review and a year after.
- **The operator's commands** — to confirm or not accept a form, to read and close a report — are `api`'s to set.
- **Export** — the part `export/` carries all this, from its version 1.

— *Why:* without these methods the operator has nothing to confirm consent with, a teenager nothing to give their own with, and an adult nothing to withdraw and cancel a waiting one with; the first child waits for the consent contract, by what must hold before the first child in the DPIA, and `api` and `app` wait for it, to come out in one release (Д169). A teenager who grew to the age withdraws the parent's consent as well as confirming it, since the rule of the lawful basis and the texts promise "confirm or withdraw", and the separate screen of storage, since New York's law requires a teenager's separate consent to what learning does not need (GBL §899-ff; sources 3.8).

— *Rejected:* a mail to the operator with a scan, and paper by post; `consent_id` on the form; the repeated question of age as a task of its own — `api` would wait for it longer; version 2 of the export for these records; only an adult exports; report periods of 90 days and 3 years; choosing a payment provider now; for a teenager who grew to the age — only confirming the parent's consent; for storage an adult turned on — leaving it on, or turning it off at once.

— *Consequence:* `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/account.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/attempt.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/cause.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/legal.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `export/README.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `legal/`; `run/DEBT.md`.

**R137. The NovaTrail operator in the texts is ALT EdTech LLC, the author's company, formed in Texas: the address, telephone and email are the company's; the terms are governed by the law of Texas, and a dispute is heard by the courts of Bexar County, Texas, — without mandatory arbitration and without a waiver of class actions.**
- **The operator is the company**, not the author personally: the liability is on the company. Rejected: the author personally — they would be liable themselves, and changing the operator later means new versions of all texts and a transfer of data.
- **The data** — in the section "Who we are" of [the policy](../legal/texts/privacy-policy/1.md): ALT EdTech LLC, 12828 Willow Centre Dr, Ste D, Houston, TX 77066-3043, USA; +1 224 933 2890; `altedtech.info@gmail.com`, as code. This is asked for by COPPA — "The name, address, telephone number, and email address of all operators collecting or maintaining personal information from children through the website or online service" (16 CFR §312.4(d)(1), [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-312/section-312.4), read 2026-11-10) — and by GDPR Art. 13(1)(a). These are the data of a company, not of a person: they stand in the public repository and in every release. The email is a consumer Gmail, without a processor agreement with Google, for families with children too, and the policy names Google as its recipient under Google's own terms.
- **The address is the company's.** The rule does not name the kind of address, and the FTC's FAQ, C.2, repeats its words ([Complying with COPPA: FAQ](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions), the live page, read 2026-11-10; before, the site answered 403, sources 3.3); where the FTC needs a kind, it names it — ""Valid physical postal address" means the sender's current street address, a Post Office box the sender has accurately registered with the United States Postal Service, or a private mailbox…" (16 CFR §316.2(p), CAN-SPAM, [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-316/section-316.2), read 2026-11-10). Whether a mailbox is fit for COPPA neither the rule nor the FAQ says — Claude's reading, — and the company's address removes this question. Rejected: a mailbox — not confirmed; a home address — forever in a public repository.
- **Law and court** — in the section "Law and disputes" of [the terms](../legal/texts/terms-of-use/1.md): the law of the State of Texas; the state courts in Bexar County or the federal court of the Western District of Texas, San Antonio Division, which Bexar belongs to — "The San Antonio Division comprises the counties of Atascosa, Bandera, Bexar, …" (28 U.S.C. §124(d)(4), [LII](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/124), read 2026-11-10), — unless the law of the user's country or state gives them the right to sue where they live; the consumer's rights under the law of their country the terms do not take away anyway. The court is chosen apart from the address: Houston is in Harris County, the Southern District of Texas. Rejected: mandatory arbitration with a waiver of class actions — a longer text and stricter to the family.
- **The state of formation** is not analysed: it is a question of taxes and residence, not of learners' data. Of the laws of Texas, what concerns the platform is the rules for a small business (§541.002) and the breach procedure of §521.053; beside them, the laws of New York, Connecticut, Colorado, Montana and Arkansas on minors, Rhode Island's rule on the controller and the biometrics laws of Colorado and Washington, each fulfilled for all learners from the US (sources 3.8). The breach laws of the other states the operator follows all, by the strictest, for every learner from the US — a letter no later than the 30th day, and each authority whose law and threshold are not ruled out; the operator's state of formation does not limit them, since many bind whoever holds data of their residents (sources 10.1).

— *Why:* without the operator and the law neither the policy nor the terms come into force (COPPA §312.4(d)(1); GDPR Art. 13(1)(a)), and the first deployment of `app`, with adults, waits for them.

— *Consequence:* `legal/texts/privacy-policy/1.md`; `legal/texts/terms-of-use/1.md`; `legal/legal.yaml`; `docs/privacy.md`.

**R138. The texts for adults — `privacy-policy`, `terms-of-use` and `storage-consent` version 1 — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions they rest on; the operator's mail is consumer Gmail, `altedtech.info@gmail.com`, for families with children too, and the policy names Google as its recipient under Google's own terms, without a processor agreement, and asks not to write a child's data in letters; people's letters to the operator are kept a year after the letter or the last answer to it.**
- **The reconciliation.** The drafts were written before the consent contract, with the changes it made to the rules it rests on, and the operator were set, and the reconciliation before the approval found 31 discrepancies — 21 of them such that the text in force would have said something other than what was decided —, all corrected before the approval: a version in force does not change by a byte (`legal.in-force-unchanged`):
  - parental consent — a form with the consent request code, the upload of a scan in `app`; a check by card is not promised, it is П-28;
  - a teenager: the profile — at once, their own consent, they decide the storage of their work and the export themselves, withdrawal deletes the profile;
  - the age asked anew — every year, with a change of country and when the country raised the age; the country's age by which the category is given;
  - what remains after the withdrawal and the removal of consent, and the scan of a removed waiting consent;
  - disclosure — "to nobody, except as the law requires", and the basis when life is threatened, Arts. 6(1)(d) and 9(2)(c);
  - the problem report and the letters to the operator — in what is collected, and in the retention periods;
  - the providers of the samples and who sees the IP address of the samples page; the volunteer's form — kept without a time limit while the samples are published;
  - the terms name ALT EdTech LLC and do not accept learners from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom until there are representatives; the storage consent — who stores, where and why, and the consent record.
- **The mail** is the company's consumer Gmail, for good and for families with children too, and the policy says so plainly: in "Who receives data" — a separate table of the recipients not under a processor agreement, in "Who we are" and "Children" — a request not to write a child's data in letters, to do the export, deletion and withdrawal in the app, and to write from the sign-in address, naming nothing about the child; the texts for the family ask the same. There is no processor agreement for Gmail, and none will be taken for the mail: the Cloud Data Processing Addendum covers "an Agreement for Google Workspace or Cloud Identity" ([Google](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum), read 2026-11-10), not Gmail, and Workspace is not paid for. *Cost:* Google keeps people's letters as it decides itself, not under an agreement with the operator. A letter in which a parent did write about a child is kept by Google without the written assurances that COPPA requires before someone keeps a child's data for the operator — "obtain written assurances that such entities will employ reasonable measures to maintain the confidentiality, security, and integrity of the information" (16 CFR [§312.8(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-312/section-312.8), read 2026-11-10); whether Google's consumer terms count as such assurances has not been checked —, and without an agreement under GBL §899-gg (sources 3.9); for learners from the EU and the United Kingdom, GDPR Art. 28 requires a processor under an agreement. The [DPIA](dpia.md) holds this as a risk, which the author accepts. *Rejected:* a mail service with a processor agreement — Google Workspace on the company's domain, under the Cloud Data Processing Addendum, Zoho Mail, Fastmail or Proton Mail (sources 3.9): each is a new processor and paid for, and Workspace and Zoho need a domain of one's own, which there is not.
- **The retention of letters** — a year after the letter or after the last answer to it, whichever is later: to show what the operator answered to a request about rights and when (GDPR Arts. 5(2), 12(3)) — the same year as for the problem report. Rejected: 30 days after the answer — there would be nothing to show that the request was fulfilled; 3 years — a child's data in letters would live longer.
- **The basis of letters and problem reports** — the legitimate interest in answering, in protecting learners from harm and in showing that an answer was given (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)); an answer to a request about rights is also an obligation under the GDPR (Art. 6(1)(c)). This is Claude's reading: nothing had set it, and the reconciliation found that Art. 13(1)(c) asks for the basis of each purpose.
- **The age boundary** — "from this age", not "above it": a learner exactly at the age of digital consent of their country consents themselves.
- **The mail at Google** is in data centers of Google's choosing: the policy does not promise where Gmail keeps the letters.
- **The approval** — the author reads the final texts and writes «утверждаю» ("I approve"). `in_force_since` is the day from which a version applies, which for a text whose place is `app` may be later than the day of this word; for the three versions here the two days are one.

— *Why:* the first deployment of `app`, with adults, waits for the policy and the terms in force: while no version is in force, `GetLegalTexts` gives an empty list.

— *Consequence:* `legal/`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

**R139. The text sets of the samples page `measure` and `eval-set` version 1 — the notices `measure-notice` and `eval-set-notice`, the forms `measure-form` and `volunteer-form` — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions; the controller of the samples and the forms is ALT EdTech LLC, and the organizer acts for it, on its instructions; an eval-set sample can always be withdrawn: before it is entered into the module's repository, it is erased, and after that it leaves the next version of the module and its tests, while the released versions and others' copies remain; the organizer takes no volunteers from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom until the representatives are named.** The approval is the author's.
- **The controller** is the operator, ALT EdTech LLC: each of the four texts names it and its contacts, as GDPR Art. 13(1)(a) requires, while before they said only "the operator". The organizer — the maintainer of `modules` or of the measurement, now the author — acts for the operator, on its instructions: there is one controller. Rejected: the organizer on their own — a second recipient or a joint controller, whom the texts would have to name, and an agreement between them.
- **Withdrawal** — by a letter to both the organizer and the operator, by the writer code in the measurement (Art. 7(3)); one who lost the code — by the name and the date of the form; for an eval-set sample — by the name and the date of the form, within 30 days: one not yet entered into the module's repository is erased, and one entered leaves the next version of the module and its tests, while the released versions and others' copies under Apache-2.0 remain; the form lives while the sample is in the repository or in a released version. The basis stays consent (Art. 6(1)(a)), as in the policy in force, and a withdrawal under Art. 7(3) stops what the platform itself does. Rejected: withdrawing nothing after publication — against Art. 7(3); the basis being a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)) — the policy in force says "consent", and its version 2 would have been needed before the sets.
- **Volunteers from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom** — as with learners: until there are representatives under Art. 27, the organizer does not take their forms, and the form asks to declare this. Rejected: accepting them — Art. 27 requires a representative for them too.
- **Model training** — the platform trains no model of its own on eval-set samples, but after publication under Apache-2.0 anyone takes them, as the license allows, for training too: the former "not for training a model" promised what cannot be held to.
- **The reconciliation** found other things too, now corrected: the writing history — with the pointer and with what was erased, which stays in it ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md)); the basis — Arts. 6(1)(a), 9(2)(a), 7(1) and 17(3)(e); the runner's reports are erased with the samples; the scan of the form — by the same upload link; iCloud Drive in the forms too; "runner" — "NovaTrail's program that measures the reading"; a link to the rights in the policy; the gist names the operator and the way to withdraw.
- **Discrepancies with the policy.** The policy in force says of the page's samples "never on our server or in a repository", while eval-set samples are published in the module's repository, and of a sample given to a module "this cannot be withdrawn", while now a withdrawal takes it out of the next version. The version in force does not change: both phrases are corrected by version 2 of the policy.
- **The writer code** links the samples to each other, and only the measurement form at the operator links them to the name: the former "never to your name" was wrong.

— *Why:* the large measurement on the samples of adult volunteers waits for the approved sets, and without a named controller and a way to withdraw, consent on the page is not informed (Arts. 7, 13).

— *Consequence:* `legal/`; `docs/privacy.md`.

**R140. The laws of the US states: the platform knows the learner's country, not the state, so a requirement of a state law that concerns it is fulfilled for all learners from the US; what concerns it now — with no threshold or below one — is the small-business rules of Texas, the laws of New York, Connecticut, Colorado, Montana and Arkansas on minors, Rhode Island's rule on the controller, the biometrics laws of Colorado and Washington and, by the strictest of them, the breach laws of all the states; the measurement takes no volunteers from Colorado and Washington.** Read from the primary sources 2026-11-10 (sources 3.8).
- **The scope** — all the states' children's laws, the biometric laws and those on educational data, the general privacy laws by their thresholds, the breach laws of all the states, and all the laws of Texas, the operator's state; the other general laws — as a list for "when the platform grows". Rejected: all the laws of all the states — longer, and most general laws do not concern a small operator; only Texas.
- **Fulfilled across the whole country.** The learner's state is a new kind of data, which `api` does not know and does not ask for. The exception is the measurement's volunteers: the form asks them to declare that they do not live in Colorado or Washington (below). Rejected: asking for the state and closing states — new data and a change of the contract; for now only Texas.
- **The operator is a small business by the SBA's standards** under any fitting code (13 CFR 121.201): Texas and Nebraska (§541.002, 87-1103) and Minnesota (325M.12) require of it only the ban on selling sensitive data without consent, and the platform sells nothing.
- **What concerns it now and what is missing:**
  - New York, GBL §899-ff: for a teenager of 13–17 — only what is strictly necessary for the service, or a separate consent with refusal as the most prominent choice and without asking again for a year; the storage of work is such a consent (Д201); a notice when the learner stops being a minor, and device signals (§899-hh, 899-ii; Д201); processor agreements with deletion within 30 days (§899-gg) — open question П-30;
  - Connecticut, Colorado, Montana: care for minors, no advertising, no selling, no features that stretch out use — this is already so: no notifications, no mailings, and for children no timers and no competitions; the risk assessment for minors is the DPIA, and the learner model is profiling, which the DPIA assesses too. The DPIA is checked against the assessments of the three states from their texts (sources 3.12): it weighs the benefits against the risks, is kept, and assesses the impact of profiling; it names and signs whoever approves it, by Colorado's Rule 8.04(A)(13), and the learner model is evaluated for fairness by a criterion of `sim`, by Rule 9.06(F)(10). Consumer rights with an appeal — in Connecticut, which applies the whole law to the processing of sensitive data, — version 2 of the policy; in Colorado and Montana the general rights apply only above their thresholds;
  - Montana: MCA 30-14-2803(2) applies its section on minors' assessments, 30-14-2819, with no threshold to "persons that conduct business in this state or deliver commercial products or services that are intentionally targeted to residents of this state", read 2026-11-13 (sources 3.12); whether a Texas operator that serves the whole country, by invitation and for free, does either is not verified, and it is taken to apply;
  - Arkansas, Act 952: the right to correct data — by a request to the operator, by version 2 of the policy;
  - the breach laws: the procedure is the strictest of all the states' — the letter no later than the 30th day after discovery, by California's form, and each authority whose law covers what was reached and whose threshold the number reached does not rule out is told; the learner's state is still not asked (sources 10.1; Д249);
  - Rhode Island: the controller is named — ALT EdTech LLC, in the texts.
- **The volunteers' biometrics.** Colorado, C.R.S. 6-1-1314, counts as biometrics also behavioral data that "can be processed" for identification, with no threshold; Washington, RCW 19.373, — "keystroke patterns or rhythms" and the like, with a private right of action. The measurement's writing history may fall under them, and it may not. While there is no public biometric policy, the organizer takes no volunteers from Colorado and Washington, and the form asks to declare this, in version 2 of the set `measure`. Rejected: meeting their requirements now — a public policy, a protocol and a review once a year for the sake of a few volunteers; the measurement without the writing history — the measurement's samples carry it, with the volunteer's explicit consent.
- **Not checked against the primary source, and named so in [docs/privacy.md](privacy.md):** whether Montana's no-threshold rule reaches an operator that serves by invitation and for free; "commercial purposes" for a free service in Arkansas; Rhode Island's "commercial website"; whether Colorado and Washington apply to the writing history; part of the dates and signatures, read from copies in the Wayback Machine and from indexes.
- **To watch:** entering an app store — Texas SB 2420 is in effect, Utah and California AB 1043 will come; selling to schools — the laws on educational data; Vermont, the design code, from 2027-01-01, if the platform gets online revenue; the thresholds of "when the platform grows".

— *Why:* the operator is in the United States, the first child from the US waits for what the states' laws require, among what must hold before the first child, and the states' laws on children apply to a small operator too.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

**R141. The texts for the family — `parent-consent`, `teen-consent`, `child-notice` and `teen-notice` version 1 — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions and the state laws; with them come version 2 of `privacy-policy`, with the US consumer rights, and its translation into Russian, for which the part `legal/` gets translations of versions, by its version 2; and version 2 of the set `measure`, where a volunteer declares that they do not live in Colorado or Washington. The operator's mail stays Gmail for families too, and a teenager who has reached the age of digital consent can also withdraw the parent's consent.** The author approves the texts.
- **The reconciliation.** The drafts were written before the decisions on consent, the operator, the texts for adults, the samples page and the state laws, and the reconciliation found 24 discrepancies, 10 of them such that the text in force would have said something other than what was decided. All were corrected before the approval:
  - not one text for the family named the controller and its contacts — now there is the section "Who we are", as in the text sets of the samples page, and in the texts for the learner the company's name;
  - not one named the basis — now there is the section "Why we may": Arts. 6(1)(a) and 8, the check under COPPA, the record after deletion — Arts. 7(1) and 17(3)(e);
  - what remains after withdrawal was incomplete: the scan of the form, the problem report and the letters to the operator remain too;
  - `child-notice` said "Nobody else can see it", while the operator reads a problem report with the tutor's words — now this is said too;
  - `teen-consent` did not say that an adult can delete the profile too, did not name the recipients, and reduced "what remains" to the consent record;
  - the gist of `parent-consent` and of `teen-notice` said less than the text;
  - small things: the age asked anew — once a year, with a change of country and when the country raised the age; for an essay, the text read goes to the AI; deletion — after a new sign-in; the form — the consent of ALT EdTech LLC; the data — in the US.
- **The mail is Gmail for good, and for families with children too:** there will be no processor agreement for the mail. The texts for the family and the policy ask not to write a child's data in letters; what the app can do — in the app; the rest — by a letter from the address one signs in with, naming nothing about the child: by the sign-in address the operator finds the account. The risk is risk 18 of the DPIA, which the author accepted. *Rejected* — the services with a processor agreement, by their sites, read 2026-11-11: [Fastmail](https://www.fastmail.com/pricing/) — $5 a month when paid for a year, an address without a domain of one's own, [an agreement](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/dpa/) with erasure within 14 days after closing; [Proton Mail Plus](https://proton.me/mail/pricing) — $2.49 a month, but its [agreement](https://proton.me/legal/dpa) sets no erasure period; Zoho Mail Lite and Google Workspace — only with a domain of one's own, which there is not (О-16), and Google's Cloud Data Processing Addendum gives erasure within up to 180 days.
- **A teenager who has reached the age of digital consent under the parent's consent** confirms it by `GiveOwnConsent` or withdraws it by `WithdrawOwnConsent`: the texts, the policy in force and the lawful basis of a learner's own consent (EDPB 05/2020, paras. 147–149; sources 3.3) promise "confirm or withdraw", and withdrawal is as easy as consent (Art. 7(3)). *Rejected:* only confirming, while an adult can delete the profile, — the promise would have to be taken back.
- **The storage of work turned on by the adult, after the teenager's confirmation** — `app` asks the teenager about it on a separate screen, a refusal turns storage off and erases the copies on the server, and `app` offers the export before that: the New York law requires a separate consent of a teenager to what learning does not need (GBL §899-ff, sources 3.8). *Rejected:* leaving it on — there is no consent of the teenager to it; turning it off at once — it erases what the teenager may have wanted.
- **At 18** the texts say only that `app` will tell the learner that the protection the law gives minors no longer applies to them (GBL §899-hh(2): "shall provide notice to such user that such user is no longer covered by the protections and rights provided under this article", [NY Senate](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-HH), read 2026-11-11). What then happens to the profile of an adult in someone else's account — a move to their own account or a new consent — is open question П-31. *Rejected:* deciding the move now — a change of the contract and the decisions, more than the texts need.
- **Requests about a child that the app cannot handle** — correction (Arkansas, A.C.A. §4-88-1503(b)(3)–(4)) and access beyond the export: by a letter from the sign-in address, without the child's data, and a method of its own for the request in the app is open question П-32, by the public launch. *Rejected:* a method now — a change of the contract before the first child, with no need for it.
- **The US consumer rights in version 2 of the policy.** The Connecticut law with amendment PA 25-113 has been in effect since 2026-07-01 also for whoever "control or process consumers' sensitive data" (CGS §42-516(2)), and the data of a known child are sensitive (§42-515(39)(D)), with no threshold and no small-business exemption ([2026 Supplement, ch. 743jj](https://www.cga.ct.gov/2026/sup/chap_743jj.htm), read 2026-11-11). As every state requirement that concerns the platform, this is fulfilled for everyone in the US:
  - the rights of §42-518(a): to know and to see — with inferences, that is with the learner model; to correct; to delete; a copy; to opt out of targeted advertising, of sale and of profiling with significant effects; to contest such profiling; the list of buyers — the platform does none of these things, and says so;
  - the answer — 45 days, and another 45 with a notice within the first 45 (§42-518(c)(1)); free of charge once in 12 months, (c)(3); the check that it is the owner who asks — by a letter from the sign-in address, (c)(4), and no new account is needed (§42-520(c)(1));
  - the appeal — by the same way, an answer in writing within 60 days, and with a refusal, how to complain to the attorney general of Connecticut (§42-518(d)) — by the form of that office, subject "Consumer Data Privacy" ([CT AG](https://portal.ct.gov/ag/common/complaint-form-landing-page), read 2026-11-11);
  - the notice of §42-520(b)(1): there are no sales and no targeted advertising; a statement on the training of large language models, (H); the month and year of the last change, (I);
  - Arkansas, Act 952 (from 2026-07-01): correction at the request of a parent or of a teenager of 13–16 ([Act 952](https://www.arkleg.state.ar.us/Home/FTPDocument?path=%2FACTS%2F2025R%2FPublic%2FACT952.pdf), read 2026-11-11);
  - Texas: a small business does not owe the rights of the TDPSA (Bus. & Com. Code §541.002(a)(3)) — the policy says so, and gives the rights anyway;
  - New York, §899-ff, -hh, -ii: a separate consent screen for what is optional, with refusal as the most prominent choice and without asking again for a year; a notice at 18; a device signal counts as a refusal ([NY Senate, §899-II](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-II), read 2026-11-11);
  - the heartbeat of the sign-in SDK — in the row "Signing in" and in the retention periods; the two phrases about samples — as the text sets of the samples page have them.
- **The translation of the policy into Russian.** CGS §42-520(b)(2) requires the notice "in each language in which the controller … provides any product or service", and `app` speaks `en` and `ru`. The translation comes with version 2 of the policy. The part `legal/` gets translations of versions, by its version 2: the field `translations` of a text version and the file `texts/<id>/<n>.<tag>.md`, which the rules `legal.files`, `legal.markdown` and `legal.in-force-unchanged` hold too; `GetLegalTexts` gives the translation into the language of the screen, in the fields `translation` and `translation_language`; the types are `types/legalv2`, and the npm package from line 0.15 on has `./legalv2` instead of `./legalv1`; the part's version starts line 0.15. A translation has no force: the English is in force, and a consent names the version, not the translation. *Rejected:* the translation as a task of its own — without it the policy in force would not fulfill the Connecticut law for a Russian screen; a Russian interface not for the US — a change of `app` and О-2.
- **The set `measure` version 2** — `measure-notice` and `measure-form` version 2: the organizer takes no forms from those who live in Colorado or Washington, and the form asks to declare this.
- **The set `child-sample`** is not here: the operator has no bucket for it yet (Д156), and texts in force would describe a storage that does not exist. It comes into force when `infra` creates the bucket.
- **П-30 is checked** against GBL §899-gg by the primary sources 2026-11-11 ([§899-GG](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-GG)): the law requires an agreement with instructions, help with deletion, information and audits, notice of new processors, erasure on the operator's instruction with the instruction passed on, and a confirmation of erasure within 30 days of the request. All four — [OpenAI](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/openai-data-processing-addendum.pdf), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum), [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum) with Firebase and [Neon at Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/sites/default/files/legal/dpa-20230721.pdf) — lack the confirmation of erasure within 30 days and the passing of the instruction to their own processors; OpenAI and Anthropic lack erasure on instruction too, Google erases within up to 180 days, Neon only on a written request. П-30 stays open: the operator asks each of them for an addendum, before the first child.
- **Not checked against the primary source:** "commercial purposes" for a free service in Arkansas; whether a SOC 2 report is enough for §899-gg(5)(d); the web page of OpenAI's agreement gave 403, and the PDF on its CDN was read; the rules of the New York attorney general under the child data law are not final.

— *Why:* `app` E3 waits for the texts for the family, and the first child from the US waits for what the state laws require of the policy, among what must hold before the first child.

— *Open:* in `app`, the teenager's withdrawal of the parent's consent and the separate screen for the storage of work (Д204); the operator's written procedure for rights requests under version 2 of the policy (Д206).

— *Consequence:* `legal/`; `contracts/README.md`; `types/legalv2`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

**R142. The measurement of E10 weighs the spending of Claude Code sessions by the prices of Anthropic's API, not by shares of the subscription's limit; the weight was checked once, over the whole trial of code map tools, against the share of the limit that `/usage` shows, and the measurement converts the weight into shares of the limit by that check.**
- NovaTrail's sessions run on the author's subscription, and Anthropic does not publish how the subscription counts spending: the help names the five-hour and the weekly limits and what spending depends on, but there is no formula that would turn cache reads, writes and output into a share of the limit (sources 2.12).
- The weight of a call is by Anthropic's API prices (measurements 1.2), which `tools/tokens/prices.mjs` holds; `just tokens-report` prints it in dollars.
- **The check.** `/usage` cannot be read from `claude -p` — neither by a field of its JSON nor by a command —, so the share of the limit was read once, before and after the whole trial of code map tools. The share of the limit over the window — +66 p.p. of the five-hour limit and +11 p.p. of the weekly one. The weight of all the sessions of this machine by API prices over the same window — ≈ $53–72 (measurements 1.4). So 1 p.p. of the five-hour limit of Max is no more than ≈ $0.8–1.1 at API prices, and of the weekly one ≈ $5–6.5. The weight by the prices stays, and the measurement of E10 converts it into shares of the limit by these numbers.

— *Why:* the prices are published by the primary source, and the measurement can be repeated in any repository without the author, while `/usage` is read only by a session that is signed in. *Rejected:* always measuring by the shares of `/usage` — they cannot be restored from the transcripts, and `spec`'s baseline (measurements 1.3) could not be recomputed; only tokens, without weights, — they would add cache reads to output, which for Opus 5.5 is 100 times dearer: $0.20 against $20 per million.

## Claude Code sessions

**R143. A session's tokens are saved by the order of its work and the structure of the documents, not by code-map tools: one task is one session, compaction at 400 thousand tokens, a thin CLAUDE.md, no claude.ai connectors, the body of a done task in the archive at once, the plan's tables and the records of sources and measurements in files of their own, `docs/` in English for the session that reads them, and a long run waited for without polling. gopls serves the diagnostics of Go code. How the savings are kept — budgets of size, a measurement and a new analysis by a threshold — is an entry of its own.**
- **One task is one session.** A task's planning and execution run in one session; the next task starts in a new session or after `/clear`, and the inbox triage runs in the session it was started in. The hook `UserPromptSubmit` of `tools/session/`, which `.claude/settings.json` of `spec` and of the template runs, stops a prompt that starts another task than the one the session has led, and names `/clear`. A task starts by RUN.md's phrases and the forms the author writes — «делай», «сделай», «делаем», «выполняй», «реализуй», «спланируй», «начинай», «приступай к реализации», «продолжай» —, each a whole word, with the task's number right after it or after «задачу», «задачи» or «реализацию»; a number followed by «.» or «-» and a digit, `T6.1`, or by a question mark, `делаем T42?`, starts nothing. «Сделай эпик E…» and its forms but planning start an epic, which the orchestrator's session leads as one task; «планируй эпик E…» starts nothing, and a Cyrillic «Т» or «Е» is no number. «Разбери входящие» names no task and goes on. An executor's run of the orchestrator is one task: a fresh `claude -p` is its `/clear`, `--resume` goes on with its own session, the hook runs in `-p` too ([headless](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md)), and the numbers of `NOVATRAIL_RUN_TASKS` count as one task, so a run whose executor wrote its task under another number is resumed under either.
- **Compaction at 400 thousand tokens**, by `autoCompactWindow` of `.claude/settings.json` of `spec` and of the template, which holds in a cloud session too, not by a variable of `containerEnv`.
- **A thin CLAUDE.md.** The checks of each part are its rule in `.claude/rules/`, with `paths`, loaded when the session reads or edits a file of the part and dropped by compaction; CLAUDE.md names the rules, and CI holds every check (measurements 1.8).
- **No claude.ai connectors**: `disableClaudeAiConnectors` in the project settings of every repository. The setting does not turn off the skills of plugins.
- **The archive at once.** A done task's body and its gist sentence go to its epic's archive in `docs/plan/` at once, and table 1 keeps its row; the tables of the plan other than table 1 are files of `run/`, of which a task reads the rows it and its files name.
- **Sources and measurements** are files of their own, `docs/sources.md` and `docs/measurements.md`, which `docs/architecture.md` does not hold; what a record is and how a claim cites it is the rule of citations. In `spec`, the sections of sources of `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/privacy.md` and `docs/product.md` and the section of Claude Code sessions of `docs/repositories.md` point to them, for the links of the log and the archives; the DPIA keeps its sources, since it is handed over whole.
- **The reader of `docs/`** is a Claude Code session that acts for an engineer, a module author or a lawyer without asking what was meant: the bar of RULES.md holds, the structure is chosen for reading in parts, and the texts people read are those the bar names.
- **`docs/` are in English** in every repository: a quote of a source keeps its language, the prefixes О-, П-, Т-, Д and В stay Cyrillic, and the numbers of entries and sections do not change. A translation is no rewrite. `translation-check` compares it with its original at a commit, unit by unit — a heading of the same level and number, a paragraph, a list item at its depth, a cell, a block of code —, and in each pair the citations, links, numbers, code, quotes of English text and the fixed words of the log (`tools/translation/vocabulary.mjs`) match; a citation or a number gone into another unit is an error. A fresh subagent that did not translate reads a sample chosen by the hash of the commit before, a tenth of the document, and names every difference of meaning. The order of a translation, by subagents of Opus, is [tools/translation/README.md](../tools/translation/README.md).
- **A long run** — tests, a simulation, a build, CI — goes to the background in a session a person leads, which waits for its notification or a Monitor of its condition, never a loop of `sleep` in the foreground; the orchestrator's executor waits in the foreground instead, by its contract.
- **gopls.** The kind `go` of the template loads the plugin `gopls-lsp`, for the diagnostics after an edit, not for savings: by the key `claudePlugins` of `repo-template/kinds.json`, `new-repo` adds `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`, `${containerWorkspaceFolder}/spec/claude-plugins/gopls-lsp`, to `containerEnv` of the copy's devcontainer. `claude-plugins/gopls-lsp/` holds the plugin's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `LICENSE` byte for byte from commit `e37d307` of Anthropic's marketplace, Apache-2.0; the plugin runs the gopls the kind builds from its lock file, and its version is the tag of `spec`. `new-repo-check` finds each folder the variable names inside the workspace, and refuses in `.claude/settings.json` a marketplace in a local folder, a plugin turned on from `novatrail` and one the variable already loads. A plugin of the variable replaces a marketplace plugin of the same name ([Plugin loading](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md)), so a repository with the variable and the old keys starts one gopls; on a copy whose `spec` is a tag whose template still writes the marketplace, `new-repo-check` says to take a newer tag of `spec`, whose devcontainer loads the plugins. In a cloud session the language server does not start ([Code intelligence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/code-intelligence.md)). The trial is measurements 1.10.

— *Why:*
- A session's spending is set by what it has gathered: it starts at 41–45 thousand tokens, and a call's context averages 218–294 thousand. One session per task would have cut the context of the main sessions of E4 and E9 by 51%; both ran in one session though the plan asked for new ones, so the hook holds the rule. Compaction overlaps with it; the thin CLAUDE.md saves 5,090 tokens a call, ≈ 2%; the connectors and the list of skills carry ≈ 10 thousand tokens a call (measurements 1.5).
- The hook takes the forms the author writes: «делай» stands before a task number in 157 of the author's prompts, more than «выполни задачу», and none of the 230 prompts the forms add only names a task (measurements 1.7).
- The structure of the documents is second order, ≈ 4.4% of what is carried: the archive ≤ 1.9% across 13 repositories, table 4 in a file ≤ 3.9% for `spec`, the sources ≤ 0.8% (measurements 1.6). One file of records for all the documents is simpler than one for the architecture alone, and `docs-check` checks a record's number without new code.
- `docs/` are written for the agent, and English is 11.4% cheaper in tokens on seven sections (measurements 1.6). Without a check by machine a translation loses a link, a number or a condition unseen; unit by unit is the strictest check without a model, and it keeps the structure citations rely on.
- Each turn of a polling loop rereads the whole context: a session of `learner-model` waited so in 76 main calls, $3.08 of the session's $14.62 (measurements 10 learner-model); one sentence every session reads costs far less.
- The plugin's version is the tag of `spec`, with neither network nor installation. The variable is one container's environment and `${containerWorkspaceFolder}` its own path, so no session depends on which container ran before it or on the trust of its folder, while a marketplace is recorded in `~/.claude`, which all NovaTrail containers share, by the path of the container that recorded it last ([Plugin loading](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md); [Dev Containers](https://containers.dev/implementors/json_reference/)).

— *Rejected:*
- code-map tools — Serena, graphify, claude-context, repomix, ast-grep, aider's map: on the trial none is cheaper than `grep` and `Read`, LSP is +9%, graphify +25% on code and +32% on documents, and the graph of `spec`'s documents takes 69 minutes and ≈ $7–25 (measurements 1.4);
- a consolidation of the decisions in force beside the log — 0.5–0.7% for a second copy that every change drags after it (measurements 1.6); a change rewrites the entry in its place instead (measurements 1.14.5);
- a file per section, an entry per file, a table of contents of the log, shorter cards of the components — reads are partial anyway, and anchors and links break (measurements 1.6);
- a cheap model for subagents — Haiku was right 0 times of 3; a map of the repository in the rules — 0.65%; skills in `.claude/skills/`; a shorter output of checks — 0.1%; a shorter MEMORY.md — 0.7%; compaction at 300 thousand — −61% instead of −51%, but 18 compactions instead of 11 and more details lost (measurements 1.5);
- `docs/` left in Russian, though the translation gives ≈ 0.8% in all, for ≈ $65 and an edit of every line: `docs/` are written for the agent;
- the sources of the architecture alone; the DPIA's sources moved too; a register of records of its own, «И-…» — new code and Cyrillic in English text; a link to an anchor — it breaks when a heading is edited or translated; the measurements left in `docs/repositories.md`;
- a translation compared by sections — a link gone into another unit would pass; a link gone away accepted — the translation would change the structure; a back-translation instead of the blind reading — twice as dear, and its own errors hide differences; a sample chosen by the translator; Sonnet 5 — slower and worse in terms on the pilot;
- RUN.md's phrases alone in the hook — the author writes otherwise, and such a session passed; forms the author does not write, «сделаем», «начинаем», which ask in Russian; a verb a few words before a number — `делай как в T24` only names one;
- the rule of long runs in the RUN.md of `spec` and of the template — two homes; the description of the Bash tool alone — it did not hold in that session of `learner-model`;
- `gopls-lsp@claude-plugins-official` — its `ref` takes no commit, the marketplace updates itself, and `"version": "1.0.0"` keeps the copy in the cache by Anthropic's choice; `settings` with `git-subdir` and `sha` — it pins the commit, but fetches the plugin over the network, and each clone needs `claude plugin install`; a marketplace of `spec` — a relative `directory`, `github` or `git` at a tag — its record in the shared `~/.claude` holds one container's path, a project's `enabledPlugins` installs nothing from an external source, and a tag would pin twice ([Marketplace reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/marketplace-reference.md); [Plugins for an organization](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/org.md); [Plugin loading](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md)); `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` per container — it moves the whole plugin root, and the folder would still need trust; the variable in `env` of `.claude/settings.json` — Claude Code does not take it there; gopls in `spec`'s devcontainer — its Dockerfile is the base of every kind; `typescript-lsp`; no plugin — the trial showed the diagnostics.

— *Consequence:* `.claude/settings.json`; `tools/session/`; `CLAUDE.md`; `.claude/rules/`; `docs/sources.md`; `docs/measurements.md`; `tools/translation/`; `claude-plugins/`; `repo-template/kinds.json`; `tools/new-repo/`; `RULES.md`; `docs/repositories.md`.

## Account deletion and the Google sign-in

**R144. Account deletion also removes the "Sign in with Google" connection in the owner's Google account: `app` revokes the Google access token that the fresh sign-in by the window before the deletion gives, and `api` does not get this token.**
- **What was found.** Deleting the user at the sign-in service does not remove the connection: after `DeleteAccount` the user is gone, but the dev project's connection stayed among the author's connected apps. Google's help says nothing about this (sources 4.6; measurements 4.1).
- **How.** Deletion requires a fresh sign-in, and the sign-in by the window gives the Google access token. After the answer "deleted", `app` revokes it at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke`, and the revocation removes everything the owner granted the project ([OAuth 2.0 for Client-side Web Applications](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/javascript-implicit-flow), "Token revocation"; sources 4.6). The token lives only in the memory of `app`.
- **What `app` decides** (`run/DEBT.md`, Д221): how to send the request — Google's documentation prescribes a form, without CORS (sources 4.6), while the trial of 2026-11-12 saw CORS in the response (measurements 4.1); what to add to `app`'s `csp.json`; what the screen says if the revocation failed.
- **The texts.** The policy of version 2 does not name the connection among what remains. With the revocation the connection is not there, and no new version is needed. The DPIA does not change: the connection is data of the adult owner in their Google account, and the DPIA's description of the processing and its measure "sign-in only through the Google window" are the same.

— *Why:* deletion requires a fresh sign-in anyway, the token is already in the memory of `app`, and a connection the policy is silent about would contradict the honest retention periods the privacy principles promise. *Rejected:* only writing down that the connection stays — version 3 of the policy would be needed; the revocation on the server — `api` would hold a Google token it does not need, against minimization. — *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## Keeping the token savings

**R145. The savings of a session's tokens, by the order of its work and the structure of the documents, are kept by three levels, from the cheapest: budgets of size in `docs-check` on every pull request, without a model; a measurement by `tokens-report --row` at each epic's archive and once a month; and a new analysis only by a threshold, not by the calendar. The budgets are in bytes, in `tools/docs-check/budgets.json`, and a repository is checked by them once its root holds `docs-budgets.json`.**
- **Budgets.** `docs-check` measures each whole file named, each rule of `.claude/rules/`, each entry of the decision log, the own text under each heading of a document cited by name — to the next heading, numbered or not — and above its first heading, and each row of a table of the files named. A limit is in KB of 1,024 bytes; `sections` gives a numbered section a limit of its own, and `entries` an entry, by its number, `{"R18": 56}`, `R4` being `R04`. Over the limit is an error that names the file, the size, the limit and the file the limit came from; raising a limit is an edit of that file, seen in review. A wrong file of budgets — an unknown key, a limit that is not a whole number of KB, a limit for a file, a section or an entry that does not exist — is an error, not a check turned off. A limit is set at the largest of its kind plus 10–20% (measurements 1.9), but for `entry`, 12 KB in `spec`: an entry longer keeps a limit of its own in `entries`, its size rounded up to the KB, until a task rewrites it as its text in force alone and drops that limit. `format/`, `legal/` and the archives of `docs/plan/` have none. The same file holds the switch `"comments": true`, by which `docs-check` checks the numbers of decisions in comments of code.
- **Another repository.** The block `repository` holds its limits, read from its `spec/` submodule, and its `docs-budgets.json` names what differs, `{}` when nothing does. Without that file `docs-check-repo` does not measure, so a move to a tag does not turn red before the repository writes the file by its own numbers; the template carries it from the start. Every repository has it now, and the check without it goes by Д276. The block holds `entry` 12 and `"comments": true`, as `spec`'s does, and a repository's entries longer than 12 KB keep their own limits in `entries` until a task rewrites them as their text in force. A limit of the block `repository` for `run/TASKS.md`, which a repository with no open task outside an epic lacks, is no error there; a limit of its own file for a file it does not have is one, and so is a limit of the block `spec` in `spec`.
- **The measurement.** At the archive of an epic, the repository's session runs `tokens-report --since <the first day of the epic> --row` and adds the row to its measurements; once a month a session of `spec` measures the folders of transcripts of all 13 repositories on this machine, from the window of the last row, and adds a row for each to measurements 1.9. The transcripts are on the machine where the work ran, so the measurement is a session there, not a cloud task on a schedule. `just inbox` prints the date of the monthly measurement and of the quarterly check once it has come, from measurements 1.9; it runs on the author's word or once every task of the current epic is done, so a monthly row may come later than its date. Beside the context of a main call, `tokens-report` prints that of the main calls among the first 80 of each session, in its report, its `--json` and the last column of `--row`, so that a table that has not taken the column keeps the others in place.
- **The threshold.** A task of analysis goes into `run/TASKS.md` when the context of a main call is more than 25% above the repository's reference, over at least 300 main calls; or when a budget was raised three times since the last analysis, by `git log` of the file of budgets; or when a quarter has passed since the last check of Claude Code's changelog — what new means of saving it brings. A raise is a commit of a file of budgets that raises one limit or more, counted once; a repository's first `docs-budgets.json`, a limit held only until a translation and a lowering are none. An analysis by the first condition starts from the context of the first 80 calls: at the reference or below it, the excess is the length of tasks, which the plan's rule of splitting a task larger than one review answers. Its planning decides whether an epic is needed. The references, the last analysis and the dates are measurements 1.9.

— *Why:*
- An analysis reads the documents of 13 repositories, so a weekly one spends what it saves, and frequent restructuring breaks the structure the sessions rely on; it goes by occasion, like the review of the DPIA.
- Bytes, since the check runs in CI, which has no key, and the lower bound of bytes per token (measurements 1.6) keeps a limit in bytes from letting more tokens through than meant.
- A repository by its own file: the other repositories' documents were far over `spec`'s limits — RUN.md up to 228 KB, `docs/architecture.md` up to 791 KB (measurements 1.6) —, and the limits would have made their move to the tag red.
- An entry with dated amendments keeps its size until a task touches it and rewrites it as its text in force, and one long entry would raise `entry` for every entry of its log: `.github` raised it to 50 KB for one entry, `sim` to 90 for one.
- `entry` 12 KB, not the largest plus a margin: an entry holds its text in force alone, and all but 42 of `spec`'s 160 entries fit it; a margin over the longest would let each new entry grow to 40 KB.
- Every repository's first file set limits measured after its restructuring — `tutor`'s six, `app`'s eight —, before any document grew, and counted as a raise it would call an analysis that finds nothing.
- Epic E8 of `learner-model` was 35% above its reference while its first 80 calls were 4.5% below it: the whole excess was three long sessions (measurements 10 learner-model).

— *Rejected:*
- a weekly analysis with restructuring — the reasons above;
- counting tokens through the API — a key in CI, a call over the network on every run, and a check that turns red when the tokenizer changes; through `claude -p` — money on every pull request;
- `spec`'s limits in every repository at once, `entry` 12 and the comments too — a move to the tag would turn red before the task that rewrites the repository's entries and comments;
- only `spec` measured monthly, reminded by the rule alone — the rule rests on the session's memory, and the other repositories would have no "before";
- one `entry` for every entry of a log, with no limit of an entry's own;
- a repository's first file as one raise — two more edits would call an analysis in `tutor` and `app`; each limit raised as a raise;
- the threshold by the context of the first 80 calls — a text read late in a session would no longer reach it; no such number — each analysis would count it by a script of its own;
- a check in `docs-check` that a decision that changes another rewrites it too — without a model it cannot tell an entry that changes another from one that cites it, and it would only add noise; review keeps the rule;
- a check that a consolidation of the decisions is lossless, and that tables of contents are fresh — the decision on saving tokens took neither.

— *Consequence:* `tools/docs-check/budgets.json`; `tools/docs-check/budgets.mjs`; `tools/docs-check/comments.mjs`; `tools/docs-check/config.mjs`; `tools/docs-check/main.mjs`; `tools/docs-check/test/`; `tools/tokens/`; `tools/inbox/due.mjs`; `docs/measurements.md`; `RUN.md`; `repo-template/files/docs-budgets.json`; `repo-template/files/RUN.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `.claude/rules/tools.md`.

## Checks without the author

**R146. The executor runs the checks of a task without the author: the path in the browser — with Playwright in the devcontainer, signed in on a local build by a custom token of a conventional user; the paid calls of AI — on a stub of `tutor` in the dev mode of `api`, and a real call only where the task checks the model's words, every paid run of eval among them, under a spending limit the author sets once at the provider and a cap the task names; and on real devices nothing: the three engines in CI are the check. The plan's rule that a step outside the repository or one that costs money waits for the author's confirmation gets that exception, in `spec` and in the template.** The author walks nothing by hand: no path, no confirmation of each call, no device.
- **The path.** The scenario lives in the repository whose screens it walks, `app`, and runs in its devcontainer, where the browser is. A local build of `app` signs in by `signInWithCustomToken` with a token that a tool of `api` issues for a conventional user on the dev project, as `api` does for `dev-check`; a release build has no such sign-in. `api` is reached by its name in the network of Docker. The Google window stays for the deployment.
- **The calls of AI.** A run of the path calls the stub of `tutor` in the dev mode of `api`, which `api` refuses outside that mode, as it refuses the emulator of Firebase Auth. A real call goes only where the task checks the words of the model, and that covers every paid run of eval: what it measures is what a model answers — the words, the reading of a sheet or an assessment by a rubric. Such a call goes on a key that has its own spending limit at the provider, set once by the author — a dev key, or for a run of eval an eval key whose workspace has it, as each eval key has —, and under a cap in the task's text; the executor starts it itself, and the task's «Сделано» names what was spent. What a run of eval may send stays what its eval set admits — its samples, their consents and the providers of admission. Anything else that costs money still waits for the author's confirmation by the plan's rule.
- **Devices.** Chromium, WebKit and Firefox in CI are the check of the engines. What only a device shows — the pen, the voices of the device, VoiceOver and TalkBack, the Home screen — the executor does not check, and `app` keeps it as its debt until the author decides otherwise.

— *Why:* a check that waits for the author does not run: the walks of `app` by hand passed only part of the path. A token signed by Firebase checks the real path of the sign-in, revocation included, and needs no change to `api`'s refusal of the emulator; a stub costs nothing and calls no provider with a learner's work; a limit at the provider holds even when a session miscounts. A paid run of eval measures what a model answers, and `tutor` already lets the executor start such runs within a task's cap: reading "the model's words" as the words alone would put each run of reading or of a rubric behind the author's confirmation, which this decision rejects. *Rejected:*
- for the sign-in — the emulator of Firebase Auth: it does not verify a token's signature, and `api` refuses to start with it; Playwright in the author's browser over CDP — the profile would hold the author's sign-in; walks by hand;
- for the calls — a cap held by the executor alone, a limit at the provider alone, a confirmation of each call;
- for the runs of eval — the runs of words alone, with the author's «да» for each run of reading or assessment;
- for devices — a farm of devices now: its price and what it can do were not read from primary sources, and a Google sign-in on a farm needs an account of its own; walks by hand.

— *Consequence:* `RUN.md`; `repo-template/files/RUN.md`.

## The DPIA's approver and the fairness of the learner model

**R147. The DPIA names whoever approves it — Aleksandr Riazanov, Staff Software Engineer, the author —, and the author signs the PDF of an approved version, which the operator keeps outside the repository: until the first child one version alone, the one in force before the first child, and from the first child on each new version before the processing goes on by it. The learner model is checked for fairness by a criterion of the learner simulator: virtual learners of the same skill but different grades come to the same estimate and the same kind of task within a number of attempts written down before the first run, and the result goes into the DPIA's impact assessment of profiling. The base does not hold the criterion, and none of the 48 sets of the model's constants tried brings it there: until 100 children no long runs fit them, and at 100 children the criterion is evaluated again. The first child, from any country, waits for three rules built and checked by a short run of `sim`, for the legal texts that name the adult's correction and for that signature; the author has accepted the residual risk with the round's numbers.** Colorado's rules ask a data protection assessment for "names, positions, and signatures of the individuals responsible for the review and approval" (4 CCR 904-3 Rule 8.04(A)(13)) and a profiling assessment for "How the Profiling system is evaluated for fairness and disparate impact, and the results of any such evaluation" (Rule 9.06(F)(10)); read 2026-11-13, sources 3.12.
- **The name and the position** are in the DPIA's sign-off, with the dates of its review log: "Aleksandr Riazanov, Staff Software Engineer"; the operator is the author's company, ALT EdTech LLC.
- **The signature.** A version is approved when the author signs its PDF, with the version and the date; the operator keeps the PDF outside the repository for as long as the DPIA itself is kept, and gives it to an Attorney General on request. The `Signed-off-by` of a commit is the Developer Certificate of Origin, not an approval, and does not stand for a signature. Until the first child the author signs one PDF more, that of the version in force before the first child, as a condition before the first child; the versions in between need no signature, and `spec`'s git history keeps them; the PDFs signed already, of version 1 and others, stay as they are. The acceptances the DPIA records, each with its date, stay the author's decisions, and that signature approves them with the rest of its version. From the first child on, the author signs the PDF of each new version before the processing goes on by it. That a learner from the EU or the United Kingdom, an adult, may come before the first child, under versions that no signature approves, is open (Д268).
- **The criterion of fairness** is the simulator's, in `sim`, which holds the criteria and the gate, and not `learner-model`'s: the library is measured, it does not measure itself. It compares populations that differ only by the grade, which sets the start band. The age category is not in it: neither the model nor the engine reads it, and `api` limits the pool by it on purpose, by the module's `age_categories` — content unsuitable for an age, which the DPIA's impact assessment of profiling assesses as a design choice. The numbers — how many learners, how many attempts, what "the same" means — `sim` writes down before the first run, as for each of its criteria.
- **The result.** The criterion of `sim`, written down before its first run, ran on `learner-model` v0.1.8 and `engine` v0.1.6, in `evaluations/fairness-1/` of `sim`, and its result is in the DPIA's impact assessment of profiling since version 19: the base does not hold it. Grades 1 and 5 come to the estimate of grade 3 by the 50th answer for 0.812 and 0.5525 of the learners, below the bound 0.90, while the kind of task holds; a model that starts above the truth leaves it most slowly. The round of `learner-model` aimed at the fairness by the grade ended with its exit: of 48 sets of constants, none brings grade 5 above 0.853 of the bound 0.90, and each one checked fails other cells.
- **The first child**, from any country, waits for three things. First, three rules, built and checked by a short run of `sim`: the estimate starts low, an adult corrects the level, and a guard lowers the level after N failures in a row. Second, the versions of the legal texts that name the adult's correction (Д259). Third, the signature above. The author has accepted the residual risk of the disparity by the grade, with the round's numbers, in version 24 of the DPIA. No long runs fit the model's constants until 100 children, and at 100 children the criterion is evaluated again.

— *Why:*
- Colorado's element 13 needs a name and a signature, and a public DPIA with a name stays whole, while the signed copy is what the Attorney General gets; the simulator already decides every variant of the model by a criterion written in advance, so a run gives the "results" the rule asks for without new data of learners.
- This decision and Colorado's Rule 9.06(F)(10) ask for the results whatever they are; a disparity found is a risk to a child of any country, not only one from the US; children wait for much else before the first one comes, so the condition costs nothing now, and the author accepts a residual risk knowing the round's numbers.
- One signature until the first child: only the author learns, codes to other adults come no earlier than 2026-11-28, and the platform processes no child's data. The laws of Connecticut, Colorado and Montana bind a controller that offers its service to users it knows are minors (sources 3.12). Colorado's signatures, Rule 8.04(A)(13), are read here as belonging to the assessment that the processing of a minor's data goes by: the version in force when the first child comes. That is Claude's reading of the law: sources 3.12 quotes no rule on when the signature is due, and Rule 8.05(E) keeps the prior versions, which git does.

— *Rejected:*
- for the approver — the name and the signature only in the PDF, outside the public DPIA; "the author" as it is, which leaves the element unmet;
- for the evaluation — an argument in the DPIA without a run; no evaluation; the age category in the criterion — the difference it makes is by design; the criterion in `learner-model` — the simulator and its gate are `sim`'s;
- for the result — the residual risk accepted without a round aimed at the disparity — `sim` had already called it a risk to children; the condition only for a child from the US — the disparity does not depend on the country; holding the criterion with no way to accept the risk — a round may end in an exit;
- for the signature — a signed PDF of each approved version until the first child, which is paperwork with no processing behind it while versions follow one another several times a day; no signature at all, which leaves Colorado's element 13 unmet once it applies.

— *Consequence:* `docs/dpia.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

The first slice is for a phone, a tablet and a computer; the sign-in is Google's alone.** Where the mockup's files and its claude.ai canvas are, and which version, is in [draft/README.md](../draft/README.md) and the README of `draft/mockup/`.
- **The mockup** is the look: the sources in `draft/mockup/` and their README — screens and states, the style, the sizes and the rules between them, the contrast and the differences from the documents. "Who's learning?" opens the owner profile without the PIN while the account holds no profile of another category.

- **The style** keeps the system font of `app`: the mockup's Inter and Caveat are not taken. The quota shows a share, as `GetQuota` gives it, not a number of calls. Strings do not speak in the first person of AI, and each is in `en` and `ru`. The gist of a legal text is the `summary` of its version in force in `legal/legal.yaml`, word for word. The tooltip is white on an opaque `#1d1d1f`, and every package draws it so.

Their words and icons are shared, by the table of words in `docs/architecture.md` and the one set of icons: the map and the legend show them.
- **The lesson and the task screen** of a module are the mockup's, on both sizes. The lesson's segments open in a pop-over from the line under its title; a worked example's "Next" and "Demo" stand in one row with `app`'s "Continue"; the end has no score. A task of a module is solved on the screen and sheet of a task from paper, its statement on the tracing paper and the options of a choice buttons on it, with no "Show the solution"; an essay with a rubric has "Done" in the row, its feedback drawn by the rubric. A mark of the tutor is a frame beside the learner's work, never over it. What of the screen the mockup does not draw, `app` draws by its rules of style; the canvas note `t155` names each by the key of its string.
- **A task from paper** is the mockup's paper flow, with the behaviour the documents give a task from the learner's paper: the camera, the page with every task the AI found picked and a frame drawn by hand, and each picked task on a sheet of the learner's grid under its crop as tracing paper, with no switch of kinds. Its row is "Ask" · Hint · Check, with no "Show the solution" and no option buttons. "Show where", the profile's hint mode set in Settings, draws its wavy line under the place of the first mistake.
- **The tutor's panel** opens at the side, from the tutor's button and by Hint, not by a verdict; it belongs to the app, not to a canvas. One component on every screen, it has Hint, "Explain differently" and the speaker of voicing, on a task from paper too, and a field — for a request about the frames on the page to pick from, for a question on a task from paper, its microphone an adult's —: elsewhere its line is buttons. To an adult the tutor is neutral — no name, no fox (О-13). The verdict is the program's: a line in the panel while it is open, a card above the row while it is closed. "Report a problem" stands under each of the AI's words to an adult. At the quota's end the quota's line comes instead of the AI's words, and the task's own hints stay.

  - *Closed:* a submission is read in the deployment's reading mode and gets the program's verdict, as the card. `app` asks neither `GetRungWords` nor `GetCorrectAnswerWords`: no analysis of the course of solution, no tutor's mark, no words. The rung is the program's and grows with the wrong answers.
  - *The opening* asks once for the words of the last submission of the task on screen that gave "not yet" or "correct", when they were not asked: after "not yet" the rung's words, with that submission's work and its number of wrong answers, and the frame they bring; after "correct" the correct answer words, with the work. A later submission "unreadable" or "unchecked" leaves the number of wrong answers as it was, and the words of the "not yet" before it are still current. An earlier "not yet" whose words were not asked gets none, and another opening for the same submission asks nothing again: the panel shows the words it got. `app` holds that submission's work in memory while the task's screen is open, and asks nothing once the learner has left the screen or begun another attempt.
