The mockup's highlighter is not taken: a new tool is behaviour.
- **Buttons without a visible caption** are the closed list of the shared accessibility standard, each with a tooltip of its accessible name.
- **The devices** of the first slice are a phone, a tablet and a computer. The mockup is drawn in two sizes — an iPad in landscape, 1194 × 834 CSS px, and a phone in portrait, 390 × 844 —, by one `Main.dc.html` whose prop `device` is `ipad` or `phone`, the phone on its board `Phone.dc.html`: the same screens, states and logic, laid out by rules of style of its own. The sign-in, its sky filling the window, is drawn for a computer too, on `Desktop.dc.html`. An iPad in portrait and a computer's other screens follow the rules of the README of `draft/mockup/`, and a width of 320 CSS px reflows, the sheet in two dimensions (WCAG 1.4.10). On a phone the tool bar is the same vertical bar at the left edge, with no "More"; the tutor's panel is a sheet from the bottom, half the height with the task in view, which its grabber takes to the whole screen and back, and while it is open the row and the tool bar hide; a pop-over is a sheet from the bottom; the legend of the skill states is behind "What the marks mean"; the sheet of a canvas is as wide as the screen and two screens tall.
- **The sign-in** is Google's alone, as the mockup and `docs/architecture.md` have it. Apple is the question Т-41.

— *Why:*
- The documents describe behaviour and the mockup a look, and a session that reads both needs to know which wins. A screen the mockup lacks — the legal pages, the failure screens — `app` draws by the mockup's rules of style; Settings, the section for adults, is a device's settings, where an adult already looks. A child's screens are behaviour that waits for the children.
- One rule of the skill states in one package keeps the card and the map from parting.
- The app is to work on a phone, not only on a tablet and a computer. The size of 390 × 844 is chosen without a table to follow: Apple's guidelines no longer give a table of screen sizes (sources 5.5). One logic keeps the two sizes from parting, and a lesson is drawn once for both; the same bar keeps the panel of `canvas` one shape and fits a width of 320 CSS px without "More"; the sheet keeps the task in view.
- Small buttons and pop-overs keep the sheet clear; one caption for one button in `app`, the mockup and the documents.
- The theme stays `app`'s and the bar's accessibility the element's, and the mockup has one row for "Next", "Demo" and "Continue".
- A hidden tutor is not to analyse what the learner solves on the sheet, and an open one is; and the cost: on `novatrail` on 2026-11-17, by a count of the calls — not a measurement of `docs/measurements.md` —, the tutor's words of an hour of the author's lessons, by Opus 5.5 · `high`, cost about $0.10 for 5 calls, and the reading by one Haiku about $0.003 for 6. With the panel closed, less of the learner's work goes to the provider too. The verdict stays without the panel: it is the program's, and the learner goes on by it.

- A task from paper needs no choice of kinds; the learner turns its grid.

— *Rejected:*

- only rules of style, with snapshots in a pull request; drawing every screen of `app` into the mockup; the mockup as sources and a README alone, without its runtime — a session would not see it;
- Pip for everyone; a persona of the adult's choice in the presentation style — a new field, which runs into О-23;
- captions on every icon; dropping the closed list and holding WCAG alone; a visible caption "Tutor" on the tutor's button;
- Apple in the first slice — a new provider of sign-in, a new version of `deployment/` and tasks of `api`, `app` and `infra`;
- the panel drawn by `app` — an edit of the contract `types/canvas` in both repositories, and the panel's accessibility moved to `app`; the bar as `::part(tools)`; colours fixed in `canvas`; two rows on a worked example, and "Next" and "Demo" drawn by `app`;
- only a tablet and a computer; a phone of 375 or 360 CSS px; a `Phone.dc.html` of its own; the sign-in's card at a computer window's edge; a horizontal bar at the bottom with "More"; the tutor over the whole screen at once; the legend always under the modules;
- for the skill states — a third view of `<novatrail-skill-map>` that draws the card's bar inside the card of `app`, and the rule repeated in `app`;
- helplines in the adult's Help;
- the section for adults as cards of buttons — untidy;
- the options as a static list over the sheet; the rubric's feedback left to a later task of `app`; the caption "Explain it differently", with `app` changed to it;
- the words only from a new Check after the opening — the analysis of an error already made would be lost; a button "Analyse" in the panel — a step more;
- the mockup's tooltip at 0.92, the fill of `canvas` recorded as its difference — two tooltips on one screen, and `app` left to check the contrast over the canvas alone.

— *Open:* whether a child who solves with the tutor's panel closed has passed the hint ladder, to settle with the children's screens of epic E4 of `app` (О-26).

— *Consequence:* `docs/product.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `draft/README.md`; `draft/mockup/README.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## AI on the deployment

**R149. NovaTrail is not used without AI: on the deployment `novatrail` platform AI is open — `api` runs at the rung "author", declares the facts `data_processing_agreement` and `minimal_retention` at Anthropic for `adult`, as the first app did, and calls Anthropic by the platform's key. For adults the rung "full" is no condition of admission: it stays the target of quality, measured on the samples of adult volunteers. Only the author learns there until `infra` withdraws `minimal_retention` on a deployment whose `api` reads table 0.4, in which the cell of platform AI of `adult` needs `data_processing_agreement` alone, as version 4 of the privacy policy, from 2026-11-28, says what the provider keeps, and not before 2026-11-28; and until each entry of `tutor`'s list admitted without an eval passes one, leaves the list or the author decides anew. Children stay closed, and a deployment that declares facts for any cell under 18 names the rung "full".**
- **What it opens.** A module's task of handwriting works on https://novatrail.web.app as it was meant to: the learner solves it on the canvas, presses "Check", the AI reads the work, a program gives the verdict by the task's key, and "not yet" shows where the error is. The module «Ознакомительный блок», `novatrail/check-board`, whose tasks have no options and no key that holds a free solution, is solved on the sheet of a task from paper instead, a model judging the work as it judges a task from paper's. The way is all there already: reading only on "Check"; one reader, Haiku 5.5 · `medium`, in the deployment's reading mode `single`, and a program's verdict; and after "not yet", while the tutor's panel is open or once the learner opens it, a frame round the first error from the words of the rung, `MARK_KIND_FRAME` of [the contracts](../contracts/README.md). With the panel closed, "not yet" shows what was read and the program's verdict. Only the admission kept it closed: the rung "full", which no model has passed, the refusal of "author" on a deployment, no facts and no key.
- **The mode `single`** holds for every learner of `novatrail`, not only for the author: an adult who comes by a code of `api invite` is read in it too, and so would a child be, at any rung.
- **Who learns.** Nobody but the author uses `novatrail`: the second adult who had come by a code of `api invite` does not learn there. The operator gives a code of `api invite` to another adult only after `infra` has withdrawn `minimal_retention` on a deployment whose `api` reads table 0.4, and from 2026-11-28; and before that first code, each entry of `tutor`'s list admitted without an eval — `CallWorkbook`, `CallEssay` and `CallRubric` at the rung "author" — passes an eval on Haiku 5.5 or leaves the list, or the author decides anew: the rung "author" that `novatrail` runs at would otherwise give them that adult's work too. Before the rollout `infra` checks that the database holds no account but the author's, and brings any it finds to the author, deleting none.
- **`api`**: on a deployment it accepts the rung "author", and the providers open to an adult's own key follow the rung, as `tutor` admits them. A release.
- **`infra`**: the platform's key of Anthropic as a secret of Secret Manager, mounted as a volume, `API_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE`; the facts `{"anthropic": {"data_processing_agreement": ["adult"], "minimal_retention": ["adult"]}}`; the rung "author"; the new pair by the rollout list. Before the key goes in, the author sets the spending limit of the provider's workspace; the adapters of `tutor` take no address from the environment.
- **The fact is declared untruthfully**, as the first app declared it: the organization at Anthropic has retention "On · 30 days". The author's work is the author's data, and the author, an adult, decides where it lies. The cost is written here, not hidden. The untruthful fact ends when `infra` withdraws `minimal_retention` on a deployment whose `api` reads table 0.4.
- **Children** are closed: an own key to every learner under 18, and platform AI until a provider's measures for minors are met and judged sufficient. A deployment that declares facts for any cell under 18 — `data_processing_agreement` or `minimal_retention` for `under_13`, `from_13_to_consent` or `from_consent_to_18` — names the rung "full". `tutor`'s list selects its entries by the deployment's rung, not by the learner's category, so at the rung "author" the entries admitted without an eval would read a child's work. Until then the entries read the author's own work alone — the workbook in `just dev-app` of `api` too, as its synthetic child —, and a real child's workbook or essay stays closed by the facts the table needs. No code of `tutor` holds this: it is a condition of the deployment, and the DPIA names it among what must hold before the first child.

— *Why:* the AI that reads the work on the canvas is what the platform is for, and without it the site shows a module that cannot be begun. The same exception had been weighed for the first app, where only the author learned, and the same holds on `novatrail` now.

— *Rejected:*
- AI only for accounts the operator marks: the program has one rule for everyone who uses it;
- the rung "author" by the adult's own key: a key on each device, and the same rung;
- waiting for the rung "full" on volunteers' samples: the site would have no AI for months;
- solving the module only locally, by `just dev-ai` of `api`: the platform is shown on the site;
- `Table.Select` taking "full" for every category but `adult`, whatever the deployment names: code of `tutor`, and it closes the workbook with models in `just dev-app`;
- no entry of `tutor`'s list for the workbook for now.

— *Consequence:* `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `COORDINATION.md`.

**R150. The catalog of a deployment is the list of modules its operator names: a setting of `api` lists the IDs of the modules whose current version the catalog may give, and with no setting the catalog gives the whole pinned index. On `novatrail` the list is `novatrail/olympiad-math`, `novatrail/check-board` and `novatrail/english-essays`.**
- The setting hides a module from the catalog of this deployment, and nothing else: the module, its versions, the index and the format stay as they are, and so does the first slice's goal of two modules of two subjects. A connected module that the list leaves out stays connected, but the catalog does not give it and the engine chooses none of its lessons and tasks; an attempt or a lesson run already open on it goes on to its end on its package. This is a proposal of the plan.
- `api` reads the setting at its start, and an ID that the pinned index does not hold is an error, as a fact that [the admission table](../admission/README.md) does not name is: a typo would hide a module without a word.
- What the setting is called and how it is read is `api`'s. `infra` sets it for `novatrail`, as `api_catalog_modules`, by the same path as the deployment facts.
- **The essays** are on `novatrail` so that reading an essay and assessing it at the rung "author", which `tutor`'s list admits without an eval, reaches a module there. An essay's two calls, its reading and its assessment, cost $0.0008 with Haiku 5.5 · `medium` (measurements 3.11 tutor). The next version of `english-essays` drops "Do not write your name…" from its five assignments, since `app` on `novatrail` shows it before each submission of a whole work to AI (Д152).

— *Why:* "not on this site" is a deployment's choice, and neither a withdrawal nor the format can say it. The withdrawal has three reasons — a wrong key, an answer leak, unsuitable content ([the module format](../format/README.md)) —, and "not on this site" is none of them; a hidden flag in the manifest would be a change of the format, with `api` and `app` after it.

— *Rejected:* taking a module out of the first slice — the first slice's goal would change; leaving it, with each learner turning it off in "My subjects"; the list on `novatrail` without the essays, with the entries of `tutor`'s list for an essay waiting for a deployment whose catalog has them — on `novatrail` they would reach nothing.

— *Consequence:* `docs/concepts.md`; `COORDINATION.md`.

## Stored works in the export

**R151. A profile's stored works reach the export as files of their own beside `api.zip`, not inside it: `app` reads each by `GetWork`, one at a time, and writes it into the ZIP, and the profile's file of `api.zip` names them only — the attempt, the kind, when it was kept and the size. This is version 3 of `export/`.**

— *Why:* the export is one unary answer, and Cloud Run gives an answer over HTTP/1 at most 32 MiB without chunks or a stream (sources 4.7); `api` holds a work five or six times in memory while it builds the answer, so a profile of a few works of 4 MiB with pictures that do not compress may not export at all. By files, every answer stays within the 4 MiB of a work, no method is new, and `app` already builds the ZIP of what the device holds.

— *Rejected:* a stream of the part — a method that streams, which the contracts forbid, every method being unary ([contracts/README.md](../contracts/README.md)); a link to a temporary object of a bucket — a new copy of every work outside the database, a new place of learners' data beside those [docs/privacy.md](privacy.md) names, and a task of `infra`; a limit on the sum of a profile's works — version 1 of `storage-consent`, in force, promises each work, and a text in force does not change; keeping version 2 — `v0.17.0` is out and `api` gives version 2.

— *Open:* the work of `api` and `app` on version 3 of the export (Д233).

— *Consequence:* `export/`; `docs/repositories.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

**R152. The breach laws of the US states: the operator follows them all, by the strictest, for every learner from the US. Whoever's data a breach reached hears of it from one letter by email no later than the 30th day after discovery, whatever the harm, with the total number reached and no number by state; where the laws of the District of Columbia, New York or North Carolina cover what was reached, the operator gives the substitute notice they name. Each authority whose law covers what was reached and whose threshold the number reached does not rule out is told, Maryland's before the letters and Vermont's by the 14th business day; nobody is asked for their state, and the privacy policy does not change.** Read 2026-11-15, sources 10.1–10.57: from the legislatures' sites and the official codes, and where those did not open, from Wayback Machine copies of the official pages or from the session laws — for California, Connecticut, Illinois, Indiana, Georgia, Alabama, Arkansas, Tennessee, Mississippi, New Mexico and Oklahoma, as each record names; the law of the U.S. Virgin Islands was not read (sources 10.55).

- **The scope** — the breach laws of all 50 states, the District of Columbia and the territories that have one. Rejected: by thresholds — a breach law has no threshold for people, and the authority's threshold counts residents of the state, which the operator does not know; Texas alone — §521.053(b-1) lets a resident of another state be told by that state's law, and many laws bind whoever holds data of their residents, without "conducts business in" (sources 10.1).
- **What of the platform's data they cover:** a stored work that concerns health — Texas without a name, New York and the District of Columbia with any identifier, eighteen more with a name; the writing history, where the definition of biometric data is not limited to what the holder authenticates by — Iowa, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Washington, Maryland, Florida, New York, Connecticut, North Carolina and, from 2027-01-01, Vermont; a name with a signature on a scanned form — North Dakota and North Carolina. The server holds no names, but a work can carry one and an email address often does, so the order takes a name as reached. The platform keeps no password and no security question: Google signs in, and an email alone is in no law. Taken to apply, not verified: whether writing history is "biometric" in those laws; whether the laws of Arizona, Indiana, Ohio and Pennsylvania, which find a resident by the mailing address in the records, reach an operator that has none.
- **The letter.** The shortest deadline is 30 days after discovery — California, New York, Washington; Colorado and Florida from the determination. No threshold of harm is relied on: California, Illinois, Texas and North Dakota have none, and Vermont wants a decision of no harm sent to its attorney general. Encryption excuses nothing: Wyoming has no exception for it, and Texas none for data about health. One letter fits all the laws that the platform's data reaches: California's form — "Notice of Data Breach" with its five headings, plain language, at least 10-point type — and what the laws whose rules on it were read ask, which [docs/privacy.md](privacy.md) lists — with the total number reached, which Rhode Island asks, and no number by state, since Illinois, as read, forbids the number of its residents, which the operator does not know anyway. The rules of Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Nebraska, North Dakota and Texas on the letter were not read, and the template is checked against them first (Д249). Massachusetts forbids the nature of the breach and the number, while California and Rhode Island ask for them; Massachusetts covers only a social security number, a licence or a financial account, which the platform does not hold, so the two do not meet. The operator's toll-free number, which Wyoming asks (sources 10.52), is set up in the breach and not before (Д249).
- **By email.** Alabama, Arizona, Florida, Wyoming and others take an email letter as it is; Maryland, Colorado, Vermont and others when the business works through the Internet or by email; 26 others only "consistent with" E-SIGN, 15 U.S.C. §7001(c), which needs the person's consent, and the operator asks none. Most of these deem whoever notifies by their own written procedures within the law's timing to comply — `BREACH.md` of `infra` is written as such procedures, and whether it counts is not verified, as the platform has no lawyer. New York's text was not checked word for word beyond whom it binds and its 30 days (sources 10.34), and the rest of what this entry says of it is checked before the first letter (Д249). The District of Columbia, New York and North Carolina have no such clause: where a breach reaches data their laws cover, the operator gives the substitute notice those laws name — the same letter by email, the notice posted on a page of the platform's site (of `app` or of the hosting of `infra`), a message to major media of the District of Columbia, New York and North Carolina, and to New York's attorney general the word that the operator has neither the postal addresses nor the consent; no new text and no new data.
- **The authorities.** Each authority whose law covers what was reached and whose threshold of residents is not above the total number reached, since any of them may live there: the attorney general of Maryland before the letters; of Vermont, a preliminary description by the 14th business day after discovery; those that want it no later than the letters — Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Illinois, Montana, Nebraska, New York — its attorney general, department of state and state police —, North Dakota and Oregon; those of the 30th day — Texas, Colorado, Florida and Washington; and by their own terms — Rhode Island without delaying the letters, Missouri and North Carolina without unreasonable delay, Iowa 5 business days after the letters, California's sample copy 15 days after them, Alabama and Arizona — with its department of homeland security — by the 45th day; the thresholds and terms are in [docs/privacy.md](privacy.md). An authority that asks for the number of its residents gets the total and the word that the state is not known. Over 500 notified, the nationwide consumer reporting agencies — Rhode Island's threshold, the lowest among the laws reached.
- **Nobody is asked for their state.** The policy in force says "We do not ask which state you live in", and the order needs no state: it is the same for every learner. Rejected: asking for the state in a breach — a new kind of data, a new version of `privacy-policy`, since a text in force does not change, and a letter that waits for an answer.
- **The GDPR** stays as it is: Arts. 33 and 34 wait for the first learner from the EU, the EEA or the United Kingdom, as [BREACH.md `infra`](https://github.com/altnovatrail/infra/blob/main/BREACH.md) has it.
- **To watch:** a law reached by data the platform does not hold now — Puerto Rico tells its consumer affairs department within 10 days, and New Jersey its state police before the people, both for a social security number, a licence, an account or a username with its password; Massachusetts, above; Vermont's definitions from 2027-01-01; Hawaii's SB 3016 (2026), whose fate was not read; the U.S. Virgin Islands, whose law was not read (sources 10.55).

— *Why:*
- The platform does not know a learner's state, and the deadline of Texas — 60 days — is twice that of California, New York and Washington; the first child from the US and 250 learners — the threshold at which `infra` reviews its procedure — wait for this, and the DPIA lists it among what must hold before the first child.
- The laws themselves name the substitute notice where there is neither an address nor the consent — North Carolina names the lack of consent outright (sources 10.35) —, and the texts in force do not change; one letter answers the words of both Rhode Island and Illinois (sources 10.15, 10.41).

— *Rejected:*
- a letter per state's law — the operator does not know who lives where;
- reading a state's law in the breach, as [BREACH.md `infra`](https://github.com/altnovatrail/infra/blob/main/BREACH.md) does now — the day of a breach is no day to read 56 laws;
- a consent to notices by email under §7001(c) — a new legal text or a version of `terms-of-use` with the statements (B) and (C), a screen of `app` and a record of the consent in `api`, and New York forbids making it a condition, so those who refuse still get the substitute notice; it is the option once the platform's growth makes messages to the media frequent;
- the letter alone — the three laws may count the notice as not given; a letter with no number — Rhode Island unmet; deciding with a lawyer in the breach — the day of a breach is no day to decide it.

— *Consequence:* `docs/sources.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## The work plan's files

**R153. RUN.md holds only what the tasks need — its rules and the current epic —, and tables 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the work plan are each a file of their own in the folder `run/` at the root, each opening with its rules: `run/EPICS.md`, `run/QUESTIONS.md`, `run/DEBT.md` — the former `DEBT.md` — and in `spec` `run/INBOX.md`; the open tasks outside an epic are a file of `run/` too. A done task's gist sentence goes to the archive with its body. Every other repository has the same layout, from the template or by its move to a tag of `spec`, and the checks read the tables only from `run/`.** The names of the folder and of the files are the executor's.
- **The files.** Each table moved verbatim, under its heading in English — «Table 2. Epics for later», «Table 3. Questions to the author», «Table 4. Technical debt», «Table 5. Rows of other repositories recorded in spec» —, so `table 3` and `Д173` in older texts still name it; only its relative links lead from `run/`. The file opens with the table's rules — what a row holds, when it leaves, who reads the file — and its next free number, with no record of what closed; `run/INBOX.md` also with how the inbox triage goes. The files are in English, as RUN.md is. The records the openings of tables 4 and 5 held are in `docs/plan/E12.md`; the archives that have the section «Начала таблиц 3, 4 и 5 RUN.md» keep it under its name, and an epic's archive gets no such section. A citation such as `RUN.md, table 2` or `table 5 of RUN.md` in an older text or an archive reads through the opening of RUN.md, which names each table's file; an entry of the log whose text says where a table is names its file.
- **RUN.md.** The rules say the same in fewer words and point to RULES.md, CLAUDE.md and the log for what they repeated; the opening links the files of `run/`. Its limit in `budgets.json` is 96 KB: an epic's planned bodies live in it until they are done.
- **The gist sentence.** When a task is done, its body and its gist sentence go to the archive together: the sentence is a list item without a heading at the start of the section that receives the body — «T… — сделана <дата>: <итог одной фразой>» —, and RUN.md keeps neither; the row of table 1 stays.
- **The checks.** `docs-check` reads the register «В» only from `run/QUESTIONS.md` and «Д» only from `run/DEBT.md`, in every repository; a table left in RUN.md or `DEBT.md` beside the one read is a second copy, an error. The block `repository` of `budgets.json` names the files of the layout, `DEBT.md` not among them; of its limits only that of `run/TASKS.md`, which four repositories have not, is optional, while a limit of a repository's own `docs-budgets.json` for a file it does not have is an error. `just inbox` reads table 5 from `run/INBOX.md`, and table 3 of each other repository at a commit from its `run/QUESTIONS.md`; a pull request counts when it changes it. A fingerprint is of the cells alone, so a move changes none.
- **The other repositories.** `repo-template/` has the layout — `run/EPICS.md`, `run/QUESTIONS.md` and `run/DEBT.md`, and a RUN.md with its rules and epic E1 —, so a new repository starts with it, and every existing one holds its tables in `run/`.

— *Why:* every task reads RUN.md, and on 2026-11-15 tables 2, 3 and 5 and the gist sentences were 32 KB of its 55 — read by the triage, by the planning of an epic or by a task that cites a row, not by each task —, while its rules repeated RULES.md and CLAUDE.md; with them moved and the rules cut, RUN.md went from 55,192 bytes to 16,523. The name `run/` sits beside RUN.md and reads as its tables; `plan/` would be confused with `docs/plan/` in grep and in links. Each file is named by what it holds, in capitals like RUN.md, and `DEBT.md` keeps its name. The checks read only `run/`, as every repository holds its tables there.

— *Rejected:* a folder `plan/`; keeping `DEBT.md` at the root while the other tables move — two layouts in one plan; a heading in RUN.md that points to each table — bytes for each task, where the opening's list says the same; the gist sentence in RUN.md until the next epic's archive.

— *Consequence:* `run/`; `RUN.md`; `docs/plan/` — the links of the archives to `run/DEBT.md`; `docs/plan/E12.md`; `tools/docs-check/` — `config.mjs`, `registers.mjs`, `budgets.mjs`, `budgets.json`, the fixtures and the tests; `tools/inbox/`; `repo-template/files/` — `RUN.md`, `run/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`; `tools/new-repo/`; `RULES.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `README.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `consent-age/README.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `justfile`; `tools/translation/`.

**R154. The work plan's files — RUN.md, the tables of `run/` and `COORDINATION.md` — are in English and written for the Claude Code session, not for people: terse rules and tables, no history. In Russian stay the bodies of tasks in table 1 and in `run/TASKS.md`, the section «Порядок» of `COORDINATION.md`, the epic archives `docs/plan/` and the reports to the author. Commit messages and a pull request's title and description are in English and terse too. `COORDINATION.md` keeps only its rules and «Порядок», and a closed row is deleted. "No history" holds beyond the plan too, for the documents under `docs/` and the comments of code.**
- **English.** The rules of RUN.md and of `COORDINATION.md`; the openings, columns and rows of the tables of `run/`; the headings — «Rules», «Epics», «Table 1. Current epic — …», «Tasks outside an epic» of `run/TASKS.md`, «Table 2. Epics for later», «Table 3. Questions to the author», «Table 4. Technical debt», «Table 5. Rows of other repositories recorded in spec». The rules keep their numbers, so `rule 13 of RUN.md` and `rule 4 of COORDINATION.md` in older texts still name them; «Как пользоваться» in older texts and in [the DPIA](dpia.md) is Rules, «Как устроен план» and «Как устроен план: эпики» are Epics.

The archives are not translated: they are read a task at a time.
- **No history.** A table's opening holds its rules and its next free number: which rows closed and when is in the «Сделано» of the task that closed it, or in the triage's commit. The records the openings of tables 4 and 5 held are in `docs/plan/E12.md`. RUN.md names only the last done epic, where table 1 has none, for the archive that receives a done task outside an epic.
- **`COORDINATION.md`.** Rules, then «Порядок»: one line of the plan's goal, and the items of the order in which the repositories appear, in `docs/repositories.md`, with their open rows and next free numbers.
- **The checks.** `docs-check` and `just inbox` read a table under its English heading alone — `isTableHeading` of `tools/docs-check/markdown.mjs` —; a table under a Russian heading «Таблица N.» is read nowhere, and beside `run/`, in RUN.md or `DEBT.md`, it is a second copy, an error. `tools/docs-check/budgets.json` holds `COORDINATION.md`, `run/DEBT.md` and `run/INBOX.md` to limits of their own, so that what was cut does not grow back unseen.

— *Why:* to save tokens: every task reads RUN.md, a task that cites a row reads `run/`, and the coordinator reads `COORDINATION.md` whole. English is cheaper than Russian by 8–14% of tokens for the same text (measurements 1.6), and the files were written for a person — narrative, history, repeated context — while their reader is the session. On 2026-11-15 RUN.md went from 16,523 bytes to 9,534, `COORDINATION.md` from 73,343 to 17,280, `run/DEBT.md` from 77,203 to 32,305 and `run/INBOX.md` from 9,855 to 5,522. The author reads the bodies of tasks, «Порядок» and the reports, and they stay in Russian. The same holds for the documents and the comments of code (measurements 1.14).

— *Rejected:* translating the archives `docs/plan/` — 2.2 MB read a task at a time, for little saving; keeping the closed rows of `COORDINATION.md` in a section of the file — the coordinator reads them at every run, and the commit keeps them for whoever cites one; translating the bodies of tasks — the author writes and checks them; an English mark beside «в реестр spec» — two marks to read, for a few bytes a row.

— *Consequence:* `RUN.md`; `run/`; `COORDINATION.md`; `docs/plan/E12.md`; `tools/docs-check/` — `markdown.mjs`, `registers.mjs`, `config.mjs`, `budgets.json`, the fixtures and the tests; `tools/inbox/`; `repo-template/files/` — `RUN.md`, `run/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`; `tools/new-repo/`; `RULES.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `README.md`; `.bestpractices.json` — `english_justification` and `know_secure_design_justification`; `tools/translation/README.md`; `docs/measurements.md`.

**R155. The open tasks outside an epic are a file of their own, `run/TASKS.md`, of which a session reads only the body of its own task; RUN.md keeps its rules and the current epic.** The name of the file is the executor's.
- **The file.** It opens with its rules — never read whole: `grep -n '^#### T' run/TASKS.md` lists the tasks, `awk '/^#### T117\./{p=1;print;next} /^#### /{p=0} p' run/TASKS.md` gives one body —, then the section «Tasks outside an epic» with the bodies, in Russian, as every task's body is. A new task outside an epic, a new analysis of the savings of tokens among them, goes there; a done one goes to the archive with its gist sentence. A task is found by `grep -n '^#### T03\.' RUN.md run/TASKS.md docs/plan/*.md`.

— *Consequence:* `RUN.md`; `run/TASKS.md`; `run/INBOX.md`; `repo-template/files/` — `RUN.md`, `run/TASKS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`; `tools/new-repo/`; `tools/docs-check/budgets.json`; `tools/docs-check/budgets.mjs`; `RULES.md`; `CLAUDE.md`; `README.md`; `docs/repositories.md`; `docs/measurements.md`.

## The orchestrator

**R156. An epic across repositories runs by itself: the author says «Сделай эпик E…» in a session of `spec` opened in its second devcontainer configuration, `.devcontainer/orchestrator/`, which sees the host's Docker. That session — the orchestrator — runs each task of the epic as one fresh `claude -p "Выполни задачу Txx из RUN.md"`, by `docker exec` in the container of its repository, in parallel wherever the graph allows; gathers every executor's questions to the author into one queue and continues the same executor session with the answers; and merges each pull request once its checks are green, without the author's review. The same container also runs a task across repositories: one session, which the author leads, writes in the clone of every repository the task names, in `.epics`. The code and the procedure are `tools/orchestrator/`.**
- **Where.** `.devcontainer/orchestrator/devcontainer.json` mounts the host's socket `/var/run/docker.sock`; spec's documents container stays without it. Access to the socket is root on the host ([Docker Engine security](https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/553482ce632f00c6e7faabab863422b4916e7c18/content/manuals/engine/security/_index.md), "Docker daemon attack surface"): no code but NovaTrail's own is opened in that container. It mounts spec's folder — the folder the documents container opens too, whose branch a task of spec switches — and `.epics`: so the orchestrator runs from its own clone of spec's `main`, which `sync` makes or moves forward and nobody edits, on the volume `novatrail-claude`, beside the folders of its runs and epics ([tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md)).
- **The executor.** A task is one run of `claude -p` by `docker exec` in the container of its repository's clone, found by the labels `devcontainer.local_folder` and `devcontainer.config_file` together — spec's folder has two configurations ([`singleContainer.ts`](https://github.com/devcontainers/cli/blob/a190a3f86fe20b582c25c4dcb7bbf5fdb739ab26/src/spec-node/singleContainer.ts) of devcontainers/cli at a190a3f). It is a fresh session, as one task is one session, with every permission, `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. It works by the contract [tools/orchestrator/executor.md](../tools/orchestrator/executor.md), which the orchestrator copies into the run's folder from its own clone when the run starts and gives by `--append-system-prompt` on every attempt, the first and each `--resume`: a session keeps its first request's system prompt through `--resume` only until it is compacted, and then takes the later launch's ([CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference.md)). By it the executor does the task by its repository's RUN.md, puts a question for the author into that repository's table 3 and returns `waiting`, carries the task to a pull request planned for the fewest pull requests and rounds of CI and never merges it, and returns `done` only once every check of the pull request has finished, its report in Russian in the status. `NOVATRAIL_DEVCONTAINER` is `1` there by `containerEnv`, so the run is inside the devcontainer as RULES.md requires; git pushes by `gh auth git-credential`, since the container's own helper is VS Code's and has no window under `docker exec` (measurements 4.4). The run's status and cost come from its `stream-json` and its `result` (measurements 1.19), as the README says. spec's `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, which every repository's copies, sets `"shutdownAction": "none"`, so closing a window of VS Code does not stop a container under a running executor (the [devcontainer.json reference](https://github.com/devcontainers/devcontainers.github.io/blob/0778f35686d362a165105c9d117b4ae4b33f9e6d/_implementors/json_reference.md), `shutdownAction`).
- **The procedure** of «Сделай эпик E…» is in the README, beside the commands it calls, and the hook of `tools/session/` counts the phrase as one task. E… is spec's current epic, table 1 of the clone's RUN.md; its graph is the epic's own open tasks of spec, run in spec's documents container, and the open tasks of the rows of «Порядок» it names, read from each repository's `main`. The state is the epic's folder, `epic.json` and `questions.json`, from which a compaction or a new session takes the epic. The orchestrator edits no file of spec's working tree: it names the rows done, and a task of spec deletes them. The graph is the session's, not a loop in code; a loop comes only by the trigger of Д258, with a rewrite of this entry.
- **The merge.** The orchestrator merges each pull request itself — `gh pr merge --merge` — once CI, `codecov/patch` and SonarCloud are green, SonarCloud's issues of the pull request read by its API, since a green check can hide them. Nobody reviews it, the legal texts, the DPIA and the log included: the author reads the orchestrator's report, which carries each executor's in gist. A draft is a task's product and is not merged; a red `main` is the author's, never mended by the orchestrator; after a merge that changed `.devcontainer/` the orchestrator rebuilds the repository's container itself ([README](../tools/orchestrator/README.md)).
- **Questions.** The executor never decides for the author. The orchestrator keeps one queue of all executors' questions, pauses only the node that waits on one, asks the author in its own session — in its window or from the Claude app by Remote Control — one at a time, with options and a recommendation, and continues the same executor session with all of a run's answers at once (`--resume`). A small technical question inside one repository, which no document reserves for the author, it decides itself and names in its report. A question across repositories is still a row «в реестр spec» of its repository's table 3 ([README](../tools/orchestrator/README.md)).
- **Plans.** The author approves neither an executor's plan nor the plan of an epic in a repository: the plan goes into the report, in Russian, and into the pull request's description, in English.
- **The latest tag of spec first.** Wave 0 moves each repository of the epic that is not on spec's latest release to its tag, by the repository's own open task of a move, with a prompt that names the tag, or by `tools/orchestrator/tasks/spec-tag.md`.
- **Parallelism and limits.** One repository runs one task at a time; different ones run in parallel, with no limit on the executors at once. The subscription's limit is one for every session of the account, a window of five hours and a weekly ceiling, and no document names a limit on sessions at once (sources 2.12). A limit reached pauses every start until its reset, and then the limited runs continue; how `-p` shows a limit is measurements 1.19. The orchestrator never turns on usage bought beyond the subscription, so a run stops at the limit rather than going on at API prices (sources 2.12). A task has a ceiling of cost, by measurements 1.12: `--max-budget-usd` does not count a resumed run's earlier spend, while `total_cost_usd` reports the session's whole total ([CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference.md); measurements 1.19), so the orchestrator gives each attempt only what is left; over the ceiling — a question to the author. A failed run, a red check or an issue gets two attempts in the same session, then goes to the author ([README](../tools/orchestrator/README.md)).
- **The subscription.** The runs use the author's own sign-in to Claude, not an API key. Anthropic's Consumer Terms forbid access "through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise" except by an API key "or where we otherwise explicitly permit it", and its documentation of Claude Code offers a token of the subscription "for CI pipelines, scripts" ([Authentication](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md)), runs a `-p` session on the sign-in unless `--bare` is given ([headless](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md)), and assumes "ordinary, individual usage" for the advertised limits (sources 2.12). The author reads `claude -p` as such a permission: it is Claude Code's own mode, under the author's own sign-in, in the author's own repositories, not a product of a third party that routes others' credentials. `--bare` is to become the default of `-p` in a later release, and bare mode does not use the sign-in ([headless](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md)): each raise of Claude Code's version checks it, by Д251.
- **The model.** Every run, the executors' and the orchestrator's own, is Opus at effort `high`, unless the author's word or a measurement says otherwise.
- **A task across repositories** runs in this container too, as one session the author leads in its window of VS Code — no executor of `claude -p`; one task, one session —, on the epic's branch in the clones of `.epics` of every repository its body names. The session edits them with its own tools and runs each repository's checks and servers in that repository's container, by `docker exec`, through `xrepo`. The task's `spec` is its clone in `.epics` too, its bookkeeping there; the container opens spec's folder, whose rules the session reads, so no task of spec runs in that folder while it does. Each finished change is pushed to the epic's branch; the pull requests, their merges and releases follow the author's «да», by `xrepo ship`.
- **The rules.** RULES.md says that «Сделай эпик E…» is the word on each task it runs — the executor commits, pushes and opens the pull request, the orchestrator merges it —, that the devcontainer rule holds for each executor in its own repository's container, and that a session of a task across repositories writes in every repository the task names, from spec's orchestrator container, and pushes each change. RUN.md's rules and the opening and rules of COORDINATION.md say that the orchestrator is the coordinator's role carried to the end, in the orchestrator's container. The template's RUN.md names the contract.

— *Why:* an epic across repositories is to run in one session, with no task started by hand: each task of each repository waited for the author to open its container, type its phrase, review, commit and merge, while the coordinator only named the next one. A fresh `claude -p` is one task in one session; each task runs in its own repository's container, with its own toolchain, as the devcontainer rule holds; and the context lives in files — RUN.md, table 3, the log, the epic's folder. The questions stay with the author, since decisions are the author's, and only they stop the run. The checks a pull request meets — CI, `codecov/patch`, SonarCloud — are the bar of a merge; the author reads what was done in the report. The limit is shared by every session anyway (sources 2.12), so a pause at the limit is the one brake needed. A repository behind the latest tag of spec lacks the plan's layout and language and the line of the contract in its RUN.md. In the pilot (measurements 1.13) four runs returned before CI or SonarCloud had reported, so `done` waits for every check. A task across repositories is one session that holds the whole change and reaches every repository's container, with its toolchain, and the author sees it work end to end before any pull request.

— *Rejected:*
- the Docker socket in spec's ordinary container — every session on documents would be root on the host; a repository of its own for the orchestrator — a change of the list of repositories, its own CI and tags, and it would read spec's plan past its own tag;
- for the executors, Remote Control and messages between sessions — nobody can type `/clear` into another session, and the end of a task is not seen (Remote Control is the author's channel to the orchestrator); cloud sessions — no devcontainer; all repositories in one container — their toolchains differ; the Agent SDK — the same terms as the CLI's (sources 2.11), but as a package of `tools/` it would enter NovaTrail's code and its lock file, while the CLI is a development tool that never ships, already in every image;
- a review of the legal texts, the DPIA and the log, or of each pull request;
- every question to the author; deciding everything but the log itself; a board of questions on claude.ai, or another channel such as Slack;
- approving each executor's plan, or the plans of epics;
- up to three executors at once, or one at a time; and, on the terms of the subscription, a cap on executors at once to stay "ordinary", an API key for the executors — the terms are plain, but every token is paid —, or a question to Anthropic's support first;
- the status's schema as a part in `types/` — a normative part, with its version, examples and vectors, in the Go module and the npm package and a new line of the release; it is `tools/orchestrator/status.schema.json`;
- a `git worktree` for the orchestrator's copy — it shares `.git` with the working tree —, or the working tree with no copy;
- a ceiling of $50, or none by default;
- the procedure in the Rules of `COORDINATION.md` — every coordinator's session would read it, and the file is at its budget; the orchestrator closing rows of «Порядок» itself — spec's working tree may be on any branch, and its clone is never edited;
- the default `shutdownAction`, `stopContainer`, with which an attempt is lost and paid again from where it stopped; `none` only for the repositories of an epic, by hand, which a repository joining one forgets;
- for a task across repositories: an executor of `claude -p` in each repository's container, the host's clones mounted, no such task at all.

— *Consequence:* `RULES.md`; `RUN.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `repo-template/files/RUN.md`; `tools/new-repo/`; `CLAUDE.md`; `.devcontainer/orchestrator/devcontainer.json`; `tools/orchestrator/README.md`; `tools/orchestrator/executor.md`; `tools/orchestrator/tasks/spec-tag.md`; `tools/session/`; `docs/sources.md`; `docs/measurements.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## The fairness of the learner model until 100 children

**R157. Until 100 children learn on NovaTrail, no long runs fit the learner model's constants on `sim`. What stays is `sim`'s fast gate in CI and one-off analyses of how the model works. In place of calibration come three rules, checked by a short run of `sim`: the estimate of a new learner starts a band below the band of the grade, an adult sets a module's level a band easier or harder in one step, and three failures in a row of a module lower its level by a band. The rules are the measures of the residual risk of the disparity by the grade, which the author accepts, low, with the numbers of the round of `learner-model`. The first child waits for the rules built and checked by that run, for the versions of the legal texts that name the adult's correction (Д259) and for the author's signature on the PDF of the version of the DPIA in force before the first child. At 100 children the criterion of fairness is evaluated again (Д261).**
- **The round's numbers.**
  - *The base.* `learner-model` v0.1.8 with `engine` v0.1.6. By the 50th answer, 0.812 of grade 1's learners and 0.5525 of grade 5's come to grade 3's estimate, against the bound 0.90.
  - *The asymmetry.* A start 2.5 above the truth comes down in 83.33 answers on average; a start below comes up in 32.52.
  - *The cause.* The engine gives the trial series' tasks a band higher when the start is higher, so the series cannot tell a start a band too high from the truth. The step of θ after the series is slow to close that gap.
  - *The constants.* 48 sets were screened, and none brings grade 5 above 0.853. Each of the 12 sets checked against "no worse" fails 10 to 23 checks of the other cells. The bound is not reached by fitting constants, and the round ended with its exit once the exploration of `learner-model` had finished its decisive run.
- **The rules** answer the cause rather than fit around it. `engine` does not change.
  - *The start*, `learner-model`'s: the estimate of a new learner starts a band below the band of the grade. A start below the band errs on the side the model leaves quickly.
  - *The adult's correction*: "Easier" and "Harder" in the section for adults of `app`, a band in one step, by a method of `ProgressService`, which `api` appends to the evidence log as a fact for `learner-model`. An adult who sees the child sets the level in one step. The adult of the account corrects every profile, a learner who gives consent themselves too, and every learner sees that an adult set the level, and when.
  - *The guard*, `learner-model`'s: three failures in a row of a module lower its level by a band. It bounds how long a child meets tasks that are too hard.
- **"Checked"** is a short run against the base by a criterion `sim` writes before the run: grade 5's `M11.same` by the 50th answer above 0.5525; the guard lowering the level of at most 5 % of the learners under grade 3; the adult's correction better against the truth than none; and no cell worse by `fair` but `M11.band` of grade 1, which the author accepts as part of the residual risk. The DPIA's measure against the disparity, "no candidate may make the disparity worse", has this one exception. The run's numbers go into the DPIA's impact assessment of profiling.
- **The short run** is done, on `learner-model` df338e5, the commit of its pull request #84 that came out as v0.1.13, with `engine` v0.1.6, against the base v0.1.8, by criteria `sim` wrote before each run.
  - *Grade 5's* `M11.same` by the 50th answer is 0.812 [0.795; 0.829] against 0.5525, grade 1's 0.909 [0.8965; 0.9215] against 0.812.
  - *The guard* lowers the level of 0.0005 [0; 0.0015] of grade 3's learners.
  - *`fair`* holds 5 of its 6 checks and fails `M11.band` of grade 1 — 0.0177 [0.0146; 0.021] against the base's 0.0067, worse by at most 0.0142 against the tolerance 0.01, within the bound 0.05 of `sim`'s criterion of fairness —, since the start a band below the grade's puts grade 1 below the lowest band.
  - *The adult's correction*, measured against the truth, brings 0.56 [0.54; 0.581] of grade 1's learners within 0.5 of it by the 50th answer, against 0.351 [0.3295; 0.372] without, a difference of 0.209 [0.185; 0.233]. Measured against grade 3's estimate, the difference is −0.497 [−0.519; −0.475], which is not the correction's measure.
  - *The gate.* The bands of `sim`'s gate are recorded on df338e5, in `sim` v0.1.28, in the order a library's change takes through the gate: the short run on the commit of its pull request, a tag of `sim`, then the library's merge and release.
- **The DPIA.** The author accepted the residual risk of the disparity by the grade, low, in version 24 of the DPIA, with the rules as its measures, before the rules were checked. Version 28 holds the short run's results in its measures, its sign-off, its conditions before the first child and its impact assessment of profiling.
- **What stays.**
  - `sim`'s gate on every pull request of the model and of the engine;
  - a one-off analysis, when a change asks why;
  - `sim`'s criterion of fairness and its judgement `model-fair-1`. The judgement is deferred, and so are the round's remaining tasks in the plans of `learner-model` and `sim`, which stay `[?]` there until 100 children.
- **At 100 children.** The evaluation of fairness stays a commitment of this decision and of the DPIA's sign-off, but no plan of it is kept until then: the round of `learner-model` and the judgement of `sim` are run/DEBT.md, Д261, not rows of COORDINATION.md, whose git history keeps those rows. When 100 children learn, the evaluation is planned afresh from `sim`'s criterion of fairness and the model of that day.

— *Why:*
- NovaTrail is a prototype, and the round's learners are synthetic: their bands and answers are the assumptions of `sim`'s criterion of fairness, not children's.
- Below 100 children, no difference between grades in real learners could be told from noise. A criterion calibrated on synthetic cells promises what nobody can check.
- A decisive run took one and a half to two and a half hours, and the exploration found the bound out of reach of constants.
- The rules remove the asymmetry by construction, and a short run can show that they do.
- The author accepts a residual risk knowing the round's numbers, as the DPIA's evaluation of fairness allows when a round ends in its exit.
- 100 children are a year off, and by then the round's plan will hardly hold.

— *Rejected:*
- carrying the round on to the bound 0.90, with more decisive runs, the round's further tasks of `learner-model` and the judgement of `sim`;
- stopping the exploration of `learner-model` before its decisive runs, which leaves no numbers for the risk;
- the rules alone, with no risk accepted: the rules are no measurement of fairness, and the evaluation of fairness asks for its results whatever they are;
- the risk alone, with no rules: the asymmetry would reach the first children untouched;
- the risk accepted only once the rules are checked;
- the start in the trial series of `engine`, which would leave the model's start where the asymmetry is; a guard in `engine`, which reads no failures of its own;
- the correction silent to the learner, against standard 11 of the ICO's code as the DPIA's measure reads it: a child is told that the adult sees their progress;
- the correction of a learner who gives consent themselves left to that learner alone;
- for `M11.band` of grade 1, a cell within the bound of `sim`'s criterion of fairness: a start not below the lowest band, with a new candidate and a new run, which reopens the choice of the start a band below the grade's; the bands of the gate held until the condition of fairness before the first child is decided;
- the round's rows kept `[?]` in «Порядок» of COORDINATION.md, which every reading of the plan carries for a year; the rows deleted with nothing in their place, which drops the commitment of the DPIA's sign-off.

— *Consequence:* `docs/dpia.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `COORDINATION.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## The orchestrator away from VS Code

**R158. Away from VS Code the author drives the orchestrator's session through Remote Control, in the Claude app on the phone: the questions are AskUserQuestion, as in the window, with a push to the phone, and the answers and free text come from the app, typed or by its dictation. NovaTrail builds no channel, board or voice layer of its own. A question with no answer waits, and stops only its node. Free text from the app is the author's word in the session. After its own merge of a pull request that changed `.devcontainer/`, the orchestrator rebuilds the repository's container itself, and it creates the container a repository never had, both by the Dev Containers CLI in a helper container.**
- **The channel.** `/remote-control` in the orchestrator's session in the VS Code extension puts the session in the Code tab of the Claude app, while the host is on and the session's `claude` runs ([Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md); [Claude Code on mobile](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mobile.md)). The author turns it on before the first run, and in `/config` "Push when actions required", for the questions, and "Push when Claude decides", for PushNotification, by the steps before the first run in [tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md).
  - PushNotification reaches the phone only with Remote Control on, and without it is a notification on the computer alone ([Tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md)). In the pilot it was off, so no push reached the phone.
  - The answers to AskUserQuestion and free text reach the session from the app, as the author has seen (sources 2.13): no probe checks it again.
- **Voice** is the app's dictation in the same session: speech becomes text, and the reply is text. In Claude Code "dictation is available but voice mode isn't" (sources 2.13), so nothing is read aloud. No rules of "by voice at once / from the screen" and no task of hands-free voice are made.
- **A question with no answer waits.** No time-out decides it: only its node stands, the rest of the graph goes on, and nobody decides for the author.
- **The author's word away from VS Code.** Free text from the app — a new task ("do … in parallel too"), a change of order, the stop of a node — is the author's word in the session, as typed in the window. The orchestrator takes it into the graph, `epic.json`, stops a run where the word asks, and answers what it did. The hook of `tools/session/` stops a phrase that starts a task by its number right after the verb, so a new task is said otherwise, as `добавь T45 api в граф` in [tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md).
- **The containers.** The orchestrator rebuilds a repository's container after its own merge of a pull request that changed `.devcontainer/`, once CI of `main` on the merge is green, and creates the container of a repository of the graph that has none, from its `main` with CI on it green. The commands are `rebuild` and `create` of `tools/orchestrator/`; RUN.md names both in its exception, with no confirmation, for «Сделай эпик E…». Only NovaTrail's repositories, `altnovatrail/*`, are built: the socket is root on the host ([Docker Engine security](https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/553482ce632f00c6e7faabab863422b4916e7c18/content/manuals/engine/security/_index.md), "Docker daemon attack surface"), and the CLI builds what the repository's `.devcontainer/` names.
  - *The helper.* The CLI's `devcontainer up` needs the clone at the host's path: Docker mounts by the host's paths, not the container's (the feature `docker-outside-of-docker`, [NOTES.md](https://github.com/devcontainers/features/blob/b6877129e0a264b8e83a63e8b93de29077132e5b/src/docker-outside-of-docker/NOTES.md)), and the host's folder is the container's label `devcontainer.local_folder` ([`singleContainer.ts`](https://github.com/devcontainers/cli/blob/a190a3f86fe20b582c25c4dcb7bbf5fdb739ab26/src/spec-node/singleContainer.ts) of devcontainers/cli at a190a3f). For each `rebuild` or `create` the orchestrator runs `docker run --rm` of its own container's image, in the stage `orchestrator`, with the host's socket; the host's network, so that a repository's `initializeCommand`, which Dev Containers runs on the host (the [devcontainer.json reference](https://github.com/devcontainers/devcontainers.github.io/blob/0778f35686d362a165105c9d117b4ae4b33f9e6d/_implementors/json_reference.md), `initializeCommand`), reads the host's routes for its network's MTU; and the host's folder that holds the clone at the same path, where git makes a new clone and the same command makes `.epics` beside the clone on the host, where the container's bind needs it (Docker's [Bind mounts](https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/747e4c7528c703b357b1ae83cbbf411229ce59d2/content/manuals/engine/storage/bind-mounts.md)). The orchestrator's own container sees spec's folder and `.epics`, never the host's clones. Seen 2026-11-17: `.github` rebuilt in 15 s, a temporary clone's container made in 9 s (measurements 4.6).
  - *A new clone* lies beside spec's on the host, in the folder that holds the orchestrator's own folder by its label. git in the helper clones it from `main` on GitHub, with spec as its submodule. A folder already there is used as it is, by the checks below.
  - *What is built.* Only a clone whose origin is `altnovatrail/<repo>` on GitHub, by HTTPS or SSH, and whose `.devcontainer/` is that of `main` on GitHub, unchanged in the working tree, so the CLI builds what `main` names. The clone's `.git/` is writable from the repository's own container, which has no socket, so git in the helper never runs with the clone's configuration, whose hooks and fsmonitor would run there: `main` is a fresh clone in the helper's own folder, and nothing of the clone is written. A repository with two containers on the same labels is not rebuilt: the CLI removes the one it finds. The orchestrator's own container is never rebuilt: the author rebuilds it.
  - *A window of VS Code* is not looked for. The rebuild is refused only while Claude Code runs in the container — an executor, or a session in a window —, which `docker top` lists (measurements 4.6). A window without it loses its container, and the author reopens it by «Reopen in Container». The author keeps the windows of the epic's repositories closed while it runs.

— *Why:* the pilot (measurements 1.13): 4 of 9 questions waited for the author's morning, one of `skill-map` from 06:08 to 14:23 UTC, and most repositories waited twice for a rebuild by hand, at night until the morning. Remote Control already gives the questions, the answers and the push in the session the orchestrator runs, and the author has seen it work: whatever NovaTrail built on top would be code to keep and a probe to run for what is already there. A rebuild after a green merge is a step the author only did by hand, with nothing to decide. The helper leaves the orchestrator's configuration as it is and builds from what `main` names, never from a working tree an executor could have changed.

— *Rejected:*
- a board of questions, an artifact on claude.ai with its database, which the orchestrator polls: an artifact is a static page with no backend, and a comment reaches the session only while its watch lasts ([Artifacts](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/artifacts.md)), so the board is code and a probe that Remote Control spares;
- hands-free voice, by the voice mode of a chat or by a messenger a phone reads aloud in the car: Claude Code has no voice mode, and no page read says whether the app's pushes reach CarPlay or Android Auto (sources 2.13);
- Slack, Channels — Telegram, Discord, iMessage — and the like: one more service outside, with its own sign-in and terms, and Channels are in research preview and run on Bun ([Channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md));
- a time-out after which the recommendation is taken: the executor and the orchestrator never decide for the author;
- a rebuild before CI of `main` on the merge is green, or of a repository outside NovaTrail;
- the host's folder of the clones mounted in the orchestrator's container at the host's path: it mounts whatever else lies beside the clones, as `${localWorkspaceFolder}/..` mounted whole would for `.epics`. That the container could then write every clone is no reason: the socket is root on the host anyway, and every container mounts `~/.claude`;
- a window found by the process of Dev Containers with `VSCODE_REMOTE_CONTAINERS_SESSION`: no document names it, a probe found it, and a version of Dev Containers may drop it; a question to the author before each rebuild.

— *Open:* the helper builds by the legacy `docker build`, with no buildx in the stage `orchestrator` (Д269).

— *Consequence:* `tools/orchestrator/main.mjs`; `tools/orchestrator/devcontainers.mjs`; `tools/orchestrator/test/`; `tools/orchestrator/README.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## The executor's waits and its rounds of CI

**R159. A task is planned and ended for the fewest pull requests and rounds of CI: what can run locally runs before the pull request, and CI confirms rather than finds. Tasks of one repository in a row, none waiting on another, run as a batch on one branch with one pull request; a task across repositories runs on one branch of one name in each repository it touches. The orchestrator's executor waits on a long run in the foreground — the wait under `timeout 590` in its own command and Bash's `timeout` of 600000 ms, the call repeated until the run is done —, never by `run_in_background`, Monitor or `ScheduleWakeup`; the background that the shared rules give a long run is for a session a person leads. It commits a task's bookkeeping — «Сделано», the archive, the mark — before it waits on CI, so that a push after a green CI is only for what a check found, and after a fix that follows a finding of CI, SonarCloud or the review it runs the local recipe of CI that covers the changed files before it pushes, not one file.** The waits, the bookkeeping and the local recipe are the executor's proposal, which the author has not yet checked; a different choice rewrites this entry.
- **A batch.** One branch `<epic>-<repo>`, as `e16-spec`, from the up-to-date `main`. Each task of the batch is one commit with its bookkeeping, its «Сделано» naming «ветка …» for the pull request not opened yet, pushed, with no pull request and no checks. The last task runs every local check of the parts the batch changed and `/code-review high` over the batch, opens the one pull request, writes its number into every «Сделано» of the batch, and waits on CI. The orchestrator merges it by a merge commit, so that each task keeps its commit, and each task of the batch is done by that merge. The batch closes early, with its own pull request, at a task whose release another node needs, one whose change of `.devcontainer/` needs the container rebuilt before the next task, or one that waits on the author. A single task has a branch of its own.
- **A task across repositories.** One branch of the same name in every repository it touches, all its code there. Such tasks are spec's: they stand in table 1 of spec's RUN.md, each naming its repositories, with no row of `COORDINATION.md` and no task in those repositories' RUN.md. One session, led by the author in spec's orchestrator container, writes into every repository the task names; one task is one session. Its clones, wiring, stand and gate are those of `xrepo` of `tools/orchestrator/`, and its pull requests go in the order of their dependencies.
- **Where.** `RULES.md` — the principle; `RUN.md` — the grouping of a plan; [tools/orchestrator/executor.md](../tools/orchestrator/executor.md) — the waits, the bookkeeping, the local recipe and the batch; [tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md) — the nodes of a batch and their prompts. The code of `tools/orchestrator/` needs no change for these: a status `done` without a pull request is valid, and `next` counts a branch with no pull request.

— *Why:*
- A task took 30.4 minutes, of them 7.7 on GitHub's checks and 3.7 on the local checks, around a change that is often small (measurements 1.15.1). On one branch, the five tasks before the last of a batch of `spec` took 4–8 minutes and $1.3–6.8 each, and the batch's six tasks 62.6 minutes and one round of CI, against 20.8 minutes a task of E16 (measurements 1.15.7).
- Under `claude -p --json-schema` a turn that ends to wait in the background is made to give its status at once. Before the orchestrator's prompt asked for the foreground, 59 of 301 attempts ended with the background command stopped after their last status, 49 of them a wait on CI; with it, 0 of 17 (measurements 1.15.4).
- A call of the wait in the foreground reads the context from the cache, about $0.03, once each ten minutes at most; a task of `learner-model` waited by short loops in 76 calls (measurements 1.15.4).
- 40 pushes of bookkeeping after the pull request opened, in 38 tasks, were followed by 251 minutes of waiting on CI: 1.1 minutes a task, 6.6 in a task that did it (measurements 1.15.2).
- In a task of `app` a fix that only CI checked cost 27 minutes (measurements 1.14.3).
- `[parallel]` would shorten a full `just ci` of `app` by at most 38%, under 0.8 minutes a task of `app`. The container sat under one core in 79% of its samples, waiting on the model or GitHub (measurements 1.15.3). It is debt, Д273.
- A task across repositories is one change: one session that sees every repository writes it and wires it as one, and the author sees it work end to end before any pull request.
- A pull request whose CI builds against a tag or `release-verify` of another repository cannot pass before that release; opened after it, it passes in its one round.

— *Rejected:*
- a pull request and a round of CI for each task: a task's overhead is mostly its checks and its bookkeeping, and a batch shares them;
- the repositories of a task across repositories one after another, each merged and released before the next is written: nobody sees the change work end to end before its first release;
- an executor of `claude -p` for each repository, in its own container, on the shared branch, each taking the others' work by their pushed commits: the clones share one folder instead, `.epics`, and one session holds the whole change; no task across repositories, a task in each, merged and released in turn;
- every pull request at once, the dependent's CI failing until the release; CI built against another repository's branch, by a commit;
- starting the executor with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` and without Monitor and `ScheduleWakeup`: a task of `tools/orchestrator` and a trial on 2.1.280, while the word of the prompt alone held in 17 attempts of 17; it comes back if a run breaks the rule;
- the word in the orchestrator's prompt alone: RULES.md would go on saying the opposite;
- only the bookkeeping, or no change: each rule is a line of the contract, and neither costs a round;
- `[parallel]` now, by a row of `COORDINATION.md`: the gain is under a minute a task, and engines run at once share their cores with the other executors;
- the executor leaving CI to the orchestrator: a failure would resume the session and write its context to the cache again, $0.7–1.2 against $0.03 a call of the wait (measurements 1.15.5);
- a shorter interval of polling: the executors poll every 20–30 s, so it gives seconds a round.

— *Consequence:* `RULES.md`; `RUN.md`; `tools/orchestrator/executor.md`; `tools/orchestrator/README.md`; `run/DEBT.md`.

## Texts without history

**R160. A text holds the current state, not its history, in the documents and the comments of code of every NovaTrail repository: each fact has one home; a decision is its text in force, and a change rewrites it in its place; a comment says only what the code cannot; a done task writes one line of «Сделано» with its pull request. Every other repository takes the rule with its move to a tag of `spec` that has it, by its row of `COORDINATION.md`.** Which lines a move to a tag changes is the executor's proposal, which the author has not yet checked; a different choice of the author rewrites the item «Decisions».
- **One home.** The current state lives where it is set: a version in `deploy/*.json`, the `spec` submodule, `package.json` or an `ARG` of the Dockerfile, a release in its tag, what a task did in its pull request. A document names the file to look at, not the value, and keeps no chronicle of versions, statuses or raises; the history is git, the releases and the archives `docs/plan/`. A fact is written once, and the other texts name where it is.
- **Decisions.** An entry is its text in force: what was decided, why, what was rejected and where it is described. A change rewrites the entry in its place, under its number, and every entry it changes too, in the same change, instead of an amendment that restates it; git keeps the old text, and the commit says why. The dated amendments of every log are folded into their entries in epic E22, by each repository's own task, rather than entry by entry as tasks touch them: the readability of the logs and the measurement of their citations weigh for it (measurements 1.18). A repository's move to a tag of `spec` is its commit, which says why, with the lines of its CLAUDE.md and RUN.md that name the tag, and no entry of the log; its README names no tag. A rewrite keeps what the entry rejected and the quotes of sources it gives itself.
- **Comments.** A comment of code says what the code and its names cannot: why, a constraint, a pitfall, the contract of an exported API. It never retells the code, its history or its task, and cites no task, no decision and no section of a document: its reason stands in words, without the log.
- **A done task.** «Сделано» is one line: what was done and its pull request, which says how it was checked — where the author commits after review, the report says it. What stays open is rows of `run/QUESTIONS.md` and `run/DEBT.md`, not text of the body. The gist sentence and the archive stay, and so does the report to the author, their way into the work. The architecture describes the current design, without retelling a decision.
- **Outside the rule** is `docs/measurements.md`, whose entries are dated by nature — a record of `docs/sources.md` holds its current reading, by the rule of citations —; the normative texts for authors — `format/`, `contracts/`, `admission/`, `deployment/`, `legal/`, `consent-age/` and `export/` —, whose versions are their content; the `.proto` files and the descriptions of schemas that code is generated from; the archives `docs/plan/`. A task that changes one of them writes its new text by the rule.
- **Where it is said.** `RULES.md`; the openings of `docs/decisions.md` and of the template's; RUN.md's rule of a done task, and the template's; the openings of `run/QUESTIONS.md` and `run/DEBT.md` and of the template's; `run/INBOX.md`; the opening of [docs/sources.md](sources.md). The work plan's own "no history" holds for `docs/` and comments too, and what a text may cite is the rule of citations.

— *Why:*
- The documents are 26% of the context of an executor's main calls and 23% of their output; the rule saves about 2–3 minutes and $0.51–0.85 of a session's 28.8 minutes and $5.72 (measurements 1.14.5).
- None of the three tasks traced needed a chronicle: the session takes a version from where it is set, while 9 of the last 20 pull requests of `infra` rewrote its status paragraph, which none read (measurements 1.14.3, 1.14.4).
- Amendments are 7–45% of a log: one entry of `infra`'s log, 25.9 thousand characters, holds about one paragraph in force (measurements 1.14.4). A session reads a whole entry to find what holds and writes amendments that restate another entry, and the author cannot read the logs.
- 42% of the comment blocks sampled retell the code; 2 of 8 numbers of decisions checked in comments were wrong, which no check saw (measurements 1.14.4).
- A task wrote one fact six to nine times — the decision, amendments, the architecture, «Сделано», the gist sentence, the commit, the pull request, the report —, and the review and the next task read each copy again (measurements 1.14.4).

— *Rejected:*
- one line of the current version, rewritten by each raise: a version written twice goes stale;
- a log kept append-only, without the amendments that only restate or raise: it keeps the history in the file and saves about half as much;
- the decisions in force consolidated beside the log: a second copy that every change drags an edit after (measurements 1.6). Rewriting in place keeps one copy, and for it weigh that the logs are 6.5% of the executors' context, not the 2.6% of the earlier sample, that the amendments that restate cost output and review, and that the author cannot read the logs (measurements 1.14.5);
- a «Сделано» of several lines and a part «Открыто» in the body: they restate the pull request and the rows;
- a move that changes the submodule alone, CLAUDE.md and RUN.md naming no tag: a session would run `git -C spec describe --tags` to know it; a line of the README that names the tag: a README names no version.

What a session stops knowing — why and when a decision changed — is in git (`git log -p`, `git log -L`), read when a task asks; an earlier «Сделано» as a precedent is better a short recipe in the rule of the part; an entry rewritten keeps what it rejected.

— *Consequence:* `RULES.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `RUN.md`; `run/QUESTIONS.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `run/INBOX.md`; `repo-template/files/` — `docs/decisions.md`, `RUN.md`, `run/QUESTIONS.md`, `run/DEBT.md`.

**R161. The statement of a task stands on the tracing paper of the sheet of a task from paper, never in a card of `app` above `<novatrail-canvas>`: a task from paper's is its crop, a task of a module's the picture `app` draws from the module's text and its picture of the task. The element's own statement and its boolean attribute `statement-hidden`, which left that statement out while `app` drew a card, stay members of `CanvasElement`, unused.**

— *Why:* one canvas of solving for every task, its statement the one difference, and one picture that the screen and the Check both see. A member of an agreement stays, unused, so that no reader of the types breaks.

— *Rejected:*
- `app`'s card above the element, with its picture, its speaker and a fold to one line with «Show all» on a phone: a second screen of solving beside the sheet of a task from paper, which goes with all its code;
- `canvas` drawing such a card, its speaker raising an event that `app` answers with its voicing: the layout of a phone and the voice would be split between two packages.

— *Consequence:* `docs/architecture.md`; `types/canvas/index.d.ts`; `COORDINATION.md`.

## Tasks from the learner's paper

**R162. A task from the learner's paper is the app's main feature, open to every profile in the first slice. The learner photographs a page of their own book or worksheet; the AI finds the tasks on the whole page, each found one picked, and the learner frames by hand one it missed. Each picked task is solved on a dotted sheet of its own, under the task's crop as tracing paper. "Check" is one call of AI, in which a model judges the work: each answer's verdict, "Correct" or "Not yet", with no mark that a model gave it, the place of a mistake, the tutor's words and a ladder of hints. Such a task shows no solution but to a grown-up who asks the tutor for it in grown-up mode, behind the PIN, and its attempts are the profile's history on the device, not evidence of the learner model.** A frame round several tasks is the most common case, and each of its tasks is checked; the look is the interface mockup ([draft/mockup/README.md](../draft/mockup/README.md)).
- **For whom.** Every profile, of every age category, with no setting that closes it: the card "Take from my paper" on home is open. It is in the first slice of the product.
