- **Stop.** While the answer to the question sent is awaited, by `AskTutor` or in grown-up mode by `AskGrownUp`, Stop stands in the field in place of the microphone and Send: it calls the request off, which `api` sees as its context cancelled — the model's call is cut short, the call's reserve of the quota settled and the key's record of the request going dropped —, takes the question out of the conversation and puts it back in the field with the line "Stopped: your question is back in the field — change it and send it again.", and the question sent again goes under a new key. An act already being drawn has no Stop: it takes 3 s at most.
- **Voice.** The microphone of the field, for a learner of the category `adult` alone, starts the browser's `SpeechRecognition` in the language of the screens, asking for recognition on the device where the browser offers it. While it listens the head says "Listening…" with Stop; then its text stands in the field with "From your voice: read it, correct it, then send.", and nothing goes before Send: a question said is a question typed. `app` keeps no audio and sends none to `api`. The browser decides where recognition runs, and may send the audio to its maker's service, on that service's terms (sources 5.6): which browser does what, and what the privacy policy says of it, is П-35. A browser without recognition, or a refusal of the microphone, leaves the field to typing. The microphone serves the request on the page to pick from too. A child's microphone stays off, "Voice comes later", until П-5.
- **Grown-up mode.** While it is on, the field's request is the grown-up's and goes by `AskGrownUp`, the drawing, which may give the whole solution and act on the sheet; Turn off or another task brings back `AskTutor` and its limits.
- **Admission.** The recognition is the browser's, not a call of AI of `tutor`, so the admission table does not change; its rule of `voice`, open to `adult` alone, is the microphone's rule too. The text it gives is a question as any.

— *Why:* the author wants one tutor everywhere: panels built apart for each screen drifted, each with its own buttons and field. A question in one's own words is what a tutor is for, and on a task from paper the words already have their call, their cascade, their leak check and their form check: a question is one more request of the same prompt, with no new capability, provider or processor. The browser's recognition needs no key, no processor of NovaTrail and no contract for audio, and the learner sees and corrects the text before anything goes, so a misheard word is never sent unseen.

— *Rejected:*
- a panel of its own on each screen, as before: the same parts built several times, drifting apart;
- a provider's speech-to-text now, through `api` or `tutor`: a new processor and its terms, a contract for audio and the audio on NovaTrail's servers, for what the browser does;
- voice for children now, while П-5 is open; a question sent straight from speech, with no reading before Send;
- the server keeping the question or the conversation, so that `app` need not send it: a new kind of kept data, with a name perhaps in it;
- a capability of its own for a question, with its own prompt and eval set: the words of a task from paper already speak as a tutor under the leak check, and their eval set is still to come, as it is;
- a question with no Check, from the statement alone: there would be no hidden answer for the leak check;
- a question that cannot be stopped once sent: a grown-up who changed their mind waits up to five minutes for an answer they no longer want;
- the field on a task of a module and on Home now: no request takes a question there, and a module's words are admitted by eval, which a question has not had.

— *Consequence:* `docs/product.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `docs/sources.md`; `contracts/README.md`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/attempt.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/account.proto`; `draft/mockup/README.md`; `run/EPICS.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `tutor`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## Grown-up mode of the tutor

**R174. On a task from paper and on a task of a module alike the tutor's panel has a grown-up mode, behind the grown-ups' PIN: while it is on, the tutor has none of its limits — it may give the whole solution — and acts directly on the sheet as the grown-up asks: it writes the solution in handwriting strokes, strikes a line out, underlines, circles, hatches a region or erases strokes. One call of AI, `drawing`, reads the crop of the work and the strokes it shows, by their IDs and points, and answers with ready strokes and the IDs of the strokes to take off, which the program only applies. Turned off, or on another task, the limits are back. An attempt it acted on gives no evidence.** The states `solve-grown-pin` to `solve-grown-off` of [the interface mockup](../draft/mockup/README.md) draw it.
- **The key.** A key button in the head of the tutor's panel on the sheet of a task opens the dialog of the grown-ups' PIN. For now the PIN is a static 5555, which `app` checks and the dialog names (run/DEBT.md, Д305); once a page of all the settings sets the account's PIN — `api` holds `SetPin`, `VerifyPin`, `ChangePin` and `ResetPin`, of 4 to 6 digits —, the key checks that one. While the mode is on, a band says "Grown-up mode · No limits, up to the full solution · Turn off". The mode is the tab's, for the task alone, kept nowhere: Turn off, another task or a reload ends it.
- **The request.** The grown-up asks in the panel's field, and `AttemptService.AskGrownUp` sends the request, the conversation on the task before it, the work as it stands, `paper` alone — its crop the part of the sheet in sight that the grown-up sees free, with room to write in, by `exportForDrawing()` of `<novatrail-canvas>`, since the Check's crop ends at the strokes and an empty sheet has none — the canvas's bar of buttons and the panels of `app` over the sheet, the tutor's among them, left out, so that the tutor writes nowhere they hide —, how many of its pixels make a millimetre of the task's page — the page's 1000 units taken as the 210 mm of A4 —, by which a request in millimetres, as a grid every 2 mm, is drawn, and the strokes that crop shows, `SheetStroke`: each its ID and its points in the crop's pixels, thinned by `app` to at most 128, with no time and no pressure — 3000 strokes of 128 points stay within the size of a message beside the two crops, in the order of the sheet. The request and the conversation go to the model between tags as data, never as instructions.
- **The answer** comes whole, not as a stream: the tutor's words about what it did, in the language of the screens, the strokes to write, each its points in the crop's pixels, its colour and its width, the IDs to take off, the outcome, and `repeated` for a repeat. `api` holds the act to its schema — each stroke of at least two points, a colour `#rrggbb`, each ID to take off one the request named. There is no leak check and no form check: the solution is what the grown-up asked for, and the words speak to the grown-up.
- **The act on the sheet.** `canvas` puts it on as one event `tutor` of the history: its strokes, of the pointer "tutor", on the tracing paper while it is shown, else on the sheet, and the strokes it takes off. It draws the strokes one after another at the speed of a hand, but all within 3 s, and at once under reduced motion; one undo takes the act back whole. Turned off, the mode leaves the tutor's strokes on the sheet: they are the sheet's as any stroke, and a Check after it judges the sheet as it stands.
- **The call** is `drawing`, a capability of the admission table open to every age category: the same work goes to the same provider as the Check's, and the PIN, not the age, keeps the mode from the child. Its prompt is its own, version 1, and it is the first call of `tutor` by tool use: one tool, `draw`, with `tool_choice` `auto`. Its cascade asks Haiku 5.5 · `medium`, then Sonnet 5.5 · `medium`, of one provider, the next when the one before gave no act the program holds; each with `max_tokens` 64000, a constant until a setting of the parent sets it (run/DEBT.md, Д306). The two are admitted at the rung "author" by the author's word, without a run of eval, until 2027-01-17, as the other calls of a task from paper are; the eval set of `drawing` is to come (run/DEBT.md, Д307). The debug mode logs the call as `DEBUG_CALL_KIND_DRAWING`.
- **The rights and the time.** `AskGrownUp` is an adult's action, with the right `can_manage`, on an open attempt of a task from paper or of a task of a module alike. It reserves the quota as `AskTutor` does, and has a time budget of its own, 300 s, `API_GROWN_UP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` of `api`: `app`'s client waits as long, and `api`'s server and Cloud Run's request timeout of `infra` hold it.
- **Kept nowhere.** The server keeps neither the request, the strokes nor the answer, in no log and no record of the idempotency key, so a repeat gets `repeated` alone. The act is part of the history the device keeps, as any stroke, and a sample file never holds one: the tutor's strokes are no learner's writing.
- **What goes to AI.** The strokes' points are the one place where they reach AI, and only here, at a grown-up's request behind the PIN: they let the model end a line on a curve or bound a region by it, which the picture alone does not place exactly. They carry no time and no pressure and nothing erased, but they keep the sheet's order and each stroke's direction, which the final geometry of a sample drops; whether that makes them more than the final geometry in law is П-36, and what the legal texts say of the mode, П-37.
- **No progress.** An attempt of a task from paper gives no evidence anyway, and one of a task of a module that the mode acted on gives none either, its verdict still shown: the act, the solution with it, moves no learner model, no skill map and no engine, so the grown-up's solution counts for nothing. The attempt stays open, as before.

— *Why:* A grown-up beside a child at homework wants to show how it is done on the child's own sheet, or to check a solution by striking out and writing over — what a tutor's limits forbid. The PIN keeps it the grown-up's, and Turn off brings back the tutor that does nothing for the learner. The model sends ready strokes because only it knows the geometry: a program that drew by commands — "hatch this region", "circle that line" — would have to know every figure, region and notation. The strokes' points make the drawing exact: on a sheet with the graph of x·sin x + 1, Haiku 5.5 · `medium` and Sonnet 5.5 hatched the area under the curve on a 2 mm grid that ends on the curve, computed from the points (measurements 5.1). Haiku · `medium` first keeps the price at about a cent; Sonnet takes over where Haiku gives no act. 64000 tokens because Haiku at `high` spent 32000 on thinking alone and gave nothing; 300 s because Haiku · `medium` drew in 102 s and at `high` in 177 s. The answer is whole because the act is one event that one undo takes back. On a task of a module the grown-up's strokes would pass for the learner's own, so its attempt gives no evidence once the mode acted on it.

— *Rejected:*
- the program drawing by the model's commands: the program would have to know everything;
- the mode on a task from paper alone: the author wants the one sheet whole on every task; an attempt of a module it acted on as evidence: a grown-up's solution would count as the learner's;
- the model's picture alone, with the program erasing a region it names: imprecise;
- the solution as a card in the tutor's chat: the grown-up wants it on the sheet, where the child works;
- Opus 5.5 in the cascade: as precise as Sonnet at more than twice its price; Haiku · `high` — 177 s, and with 32000 tokens no act; Haiku · `low` — it drew vertical lines alone, no grid;
- `max_tokens` 32000; the 90 s of the other calls of a task from paper;
- the leak check and the form check in the mode: they would refuse what the grown-up asked for;
- the strokes with time and pressure: nothing of the drawing reads them;
- the answer as a stream, or the act stroke by stroke from the server: an undo would take back a part.

— *Consequence:* `RULES.md`; `docs/decisions.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `docs/measurements.md`; `admission/`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/attempt.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/debug.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `types/canvas/index.d.ts`; `export/schemas/paper.schema.json`; `legal/`; `draft/mockup/README.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `tutor`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## Every task of a module on the sheet

**R175. Every task of a module is solved on the screen and the sheet of a task from paper, all of it — the tracing paper, the grid, the tools, the row of debug, Ask, Hint and Check, the tutor's one panel and its grown-up mode —, and only its statement comes otherwise: from the module, as its text and its media, not from a photo. There is no other screen of solving: no statement card above the canvas, no solving steps, no solving mode, no "Show the solution" and no page of a workbook. How a task is chosen and checked stays the module's: the check board, `novatrail/check-board` «Ознакомительный блок», is a page of tasks that a model judges, with no evidence; every other module gives one task at a time, chosen by the engine in the module's task skill, its verdict a program's by its key and its attempt evidence of the learner model; a task with a rubric gets feedback by its criteria.** The mockup's states `board`, `module-task`, `module-choice`, `module-long` and `essay-sheet` draw it ([draft/mockup/README.md](../draft/mockup/README.md)).
- **The page.** Solve on the tile of the module's tasks — its card has no other — opens `#/paper/module/<module>`. A module `ConnectedModule.on_sheet` names is a page: `app` begins its tasks by `BeginPaperAttempts` with `module_id`, a new `page_id` each time, and `api` begins an attempt of each task of the module's current version that suits the learner, by the order of their IDs, at most 20, with the counter and the list of a page from paper; `api` names such modules, by their IDs, in its code, the check board alone, and the engine chooses none of their tasks. Every other module is one task: `app` asks `LearningService.ChooseNext` with the module's ID and begins its attempt by `BeginAttempt`; "Next task" after a verdict asks again. The pill of the module's task skill stands where the counter stands on a page, and opens the same choice as the tile on Home.
- **The statement.** `app` draws the statement's text as a picture — dark on white, left-aligned, wrapped —, with the module's picture of the task under it, which `canvas` lays as the tracing paper, `PaperTask.source` `"module"`, under the sign «Задача модуля», "Task of the module". A module's text needs no Recognise and has no Original.
- **A choice.** The options of an answer slot bound `choice` are buttons on the tracing paper under the statement, `PaperTask.options`: `canvas` draws them as a part of the tracing paper, not as a component of its own, and tells `app` which was tapped; `app` holds the choice and sends it as `TappedChoice`. The sheet stays the learner's to work on beside them.
- **The Check.** On the check board a task from paper's — one call of AI in which a model judges the work, the statement's picture as `PaperWork.statement`, so that the screen and the model see one picture. On every other module `AttemptService.SubmitWork` with `SheetWork.crop`, the strokes without the tracing paper, and the tapped options: a model reads the answer, the program compares it with the key, and an option tapped needs no model. A task with a rubric is written on the lined sheet and sent by `SubmitEssay` with the same crop; Done in the row, between Hint and Check, ends it by `Done`, and the marks by the criteria go to an adult.
- **The tutor.** The panel gives the task's hints, "Explain differently" and "Report a problem"; on a task of a module it has no field of a question but in grown-up mode, as the mockup draws it. Grown-up mode stands on a task of a module as on a task from paper, by `AskGrownUp` on its attempt: an attempt it acted on gives no evidence, its verdict still shown.
- **What is kept.** A page of the check board is the tab's: the profile's history on the device keeps the pages from paper alone, and the export holds none of a module's page. An attempt of any other module is `api`'s, as before, and the history keeps its verdicts by the attempt.

— *Why:* the author's word: one canvas of solving, well worked out with all its tools, the same for a task from paper and for every task of a module, its statement the one difference; the old screen of a task, with its own steps, mode and card, goes with all its code. The check board's tasks have no options and no key a program could hold an answer of the learner's own to, so a model judges them, as it judges a task from paper; a program by its key stays where a task has one, as olympiad maths has, and its attempts stay evidence. Options on the tracing paper keep the statement and its answers in one place, and an extension of the tracing paper keeps one component, no second copy of its code. A picture of the text keeps the check board's Check the one of a task from paper, its prompt held by its fingerprint in the admission. The practice inside lessons goes into the lessons, which are remade.

— *Rejected:*
- the olympiad tasks on the old screen of a task, with its statement card, solving steps and modes "by steps" and "on my own": the author wants one canvas, and the old one goes with all its code;
- the options as `app`'s pop-over over the row, or as a component of `canvas` beside the tracing paper: away from the statement, and a second component of the same picture;
- every module's tasks judged by a model, as the check board's: a program decides every verdict where a task has a key, and a model's verdict is no evidence;
- a field of the module format that says a module is a page: a version of the format and of every reader of it, `module-kit`, `api` and `app`, for one module;
- the statement as text to the Check: a new call and a new prompt beside the pinned one of a task from paper;
- the text laid out by `canvas` on the tracing paper, as after Recognise: the Check takes a picture all the same, and two drawings of one statement could differ;
- the check board's page in the profile's history on the device: a new kind of page in the store and in the export format, for one module.

— *Consequence:* `docs/decisions.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/attempt.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/paper.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/module.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/account.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/learning.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/package.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `types/canvas/index.d.ts`; `draft/mockup/`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `canvas`'s `docs/decisions.md`.

## The module's card: its lesson and its tasks

**R176. Each module's lessons and tasks start from its own card on Home, and Home has no "Next up". The card has two tiles. The tile of its lesson is shut, grey under «Soon», while the lessons are remade: its row and Continue are shut, and "The lessons are being remade" stands in place of its steps. The tile of its tasks, green, has Solve — a task of this module alone, never a lesson, on the sheet of a task from paper — and the row that names the skill its tasks train, which opens the choice of it. The check board, a page of tasks, has the tile of tasks alone. The task skill is the module's own, chosen by the learner on the tile or on the skill map among the skills the map opens, and kept with the connected module until the learner gives the choice back to the tutor. The page of lessons lists the module's lessons in the author's order, each with its state, and opens any of them; with no lesson begun, the tile names the next one in the author's order. After a task of a module, Next task stays in it; at the end of a lesson come the next lesson and Solve; "Something else" goes. On the card "Tasks from my paper", "From a file" stands beside "Open camera", and "History", the solving history, in place of "Your pages".** The mockup's states `home`, `home-tasks`, `home-tasks-own`, `lessons`, `board-home` and `pick-file` draw it ([draft/mockup/README.md](../draft/mockup/README.md)).
- **The tile of the lesson** is shut while the lessons are remade, and so is the way from it to the page of lessons: the lessons hold only their explanations and worked examples, and their tasks are gone. `ListLessons`, `OpenLesson` and the page stay for the lessons remade, whose tile names the lesson `ListLessons` gives as `tile_lesson`: that of an open run, the one begun last when there are several; else the first in the author's order not passed; else the first. Its bar shows the lesson's steps by the place the device keeps, or else by the task segments of the run that have ended. It names no "lesson N of M": the lessons of a group have no order between them. Continue opens it — the open run, or a new run by `OpenLesson` with its full ID.
- **The tile of the tasks** says "The tutor picks the skill", or names the task skill. The choice opens under the row: the tutor, which gives the choice back, the skills suggested first, then every skill of the module by its tier, each locked one shut, as on the map. Solve asks `ChooseNext` with the module and opens its task on the sheet of a task from paper. The profile's open attempt of a task of this module Solve opens again, rather than closing it; one of another module it closes, after `app`'s warning, as a choice does. On the check board Solve opens its page on the sheet.
- **The task skill** is set by `ModuleService.SetTaskSkill` and comes back in `ConnectedModule.task_skill`. The skill map's Practise sets it too, and Solves: the learner has one skill of their own for a module, in one place. `api` holds only that the skill is in the graph of the module's current version: which skills are open is the rule of `skill-map`, and the engine gives a task on any skill of the pool anyway. A module disconnected loses it, and a new version that no longer has the skill reads as none.
- **A choice of a module's tasks** gives the engine that module alone, with no lessons, and its task skill as the skill chosen, `REASON_CODE_SKILL_CHOSEN`; with none, the engine's rule leads within the module; a task skill with no task in the pool gives nothing. The record of the choice keeps the module and the skill, and `next` after its task keeps the module, with the task skill as it is then. The end of a lesson run gives a choice of the lesson's module, of its tasks alone: Solve beside the next lesson. `ChooseNext` without a module, the choice among all the modules connected, stays in the contract, and `app` asks it no more. The engine does not change: `api` narrows its input.
- **The page of lessons**, `#/module/<module>/lessons` in `app`, lists what `ListLessons` gives, a look that writes nothing, ends no run and makes no choice, so the tile and the page cost nothing at every visit to Home. Its order is the engine's — by the skill graph, a lesson after those whose skills its own need, then by tier and by ID —, which `engine` exports with the place of each lesson's group, so that one rule orders the lessons; a group of more than one stands as "In any order", with no numbers. A lesson tapped opens by `OpenLesson` with its full ID, which records a choice of its own, `REASON_CODE_LESSON_CHOSEN`, so every run names a choice, as the summary of issues and the adult's progress read them; its record holds what an engine's choice would then, and a replay does not run the engine for it. A lesson passed opens a new run. The lesson of an open run that the current version no longer lists stands after the others, so the tile names only lessons of the page.
- **Home** has the cards of the modules and "Tasks from my paper", across the width: no open lesson or task above them and no "What's next". An open lesson goes on from its module's tile, and an open task by Solve.
- **The task screen and the end of a lesson.** Next task is the choice `next` gave, in the module; with none in hand, `ChooseNext` with the task's module. There is no "Something else": Home leads to another module. The end of a lesson offers the module's next lesson — the tile's lesson once the run has ended — and Solve, the choice the end gave, and Home.
- **"From a file"** takes a picture from the device's files to the page to pick from, as a photo comes from the camera, with no camera; back from that page goes Home. **"History"** is the list of the pages the device keeps, under its new name: what it holds and how long are as before.

— *Why:* the author's word: lessons and tasks start from each module on its own, and the card on Home, not the engine across the modules, is where a learner chooses what to do. A learner who asks for a module's tasks gets them, not a lesson nor another module's task. A skill for each module, as a topic of each subject: one skill for the profile would lead the choice in a module it is not in, and a card could not say which skill its tasks train. A look that writes nothing, for a tile shown at every visit, where a choice would close the open attempt. A choice of its own for a lesson the learner chose keeps every run linked to a choice, as the records and the export have it, with no second kind of run. One rule of the order of lessons, the engine's, not a copy in `api`. A lesson's tasks would need a screen of a task in the lesson, which there no longer is; their practice goes into the lessons when they are remade, and the tile stays shut until then.

— *Rejected:*
- one skill chosen for the profile, carried in the chain of choices — a skill of one module would lead another's, and no card could show it;
- Solve giving lessons as well — the lesson has a tile of its own, and the learner chooses it there;
- "Next up" beside the cards — two ways into one lesson, and the engine's choice across the modules the author no longer wants on Home;
- the list of lessons from the package on the device — the states of the lessons are the server's runs, and the device holds no open view of lessons it has not opened;
- "lesson N of M" on the tile — the lessons of a group have no order;
- the order of lessons computed in `api` — a second copy of the engine's rule, which could drift;
- a run of a lesson the learner chose with no choice — a link that may be empty, and a run the summary of issues and the progress do not see;
- `api` refusing a locked skill — it would need the rule "open", which is `skill-map`'s, for a skill `app` never offers;
- the page of lessons as a stub — the author wanted it drawn first, and all of it comes in one release;
- the lessons open while remade, with their explanations and examples alone — the author wants them back whole, their practice in them.

— *Consequence:* `docs/decisions.md`; `docs/concepts.md`; `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/product.md`; `docs/privacy.md`; `docs/dpia.md`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/module.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/learning.proto`; `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/cause.proto`; `contracts/README.md`; `export/`; `draft/mockup/`; `engine`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `api`'s `docs/decisions.md`; `app`'s `docs/decisions.md`.
